tests.title: Inner Fire
tests.subtitle: Drive, ambition, self-direction
tests.description: Measures your intensity, ambition and how strongly you push your own path.
tests.whatYouLearn: How intense your inner drive is and how it shows up in decisions.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Pairs better when intensity levels are compatible (calm vs fiery).

options.text: Running something of my own

Good at my job and home by seven

options.text: Play for fun. Nobody said you had to be good

options.text: Light up. You have an answer, and a plan

Turn it around: “You first. Tell me yours.”

options.text: Feel it for a day, then get back to work
Ask your boss what it would take next time
Sigh a little, then carry on as usual
Shrug. There’s more to life than designations

tests.measures: how strongly you set your own direction and push toward your goals

VeryHigh.label: The Full-Throttle Soul
summaries: You don’t wait for life to happen. You book a meeting with it.

You were the kid with a plan and you’re the adult with three. Standing still makes you restless, and a big goal makes you come alive. People borrow your energy when theirs runs out, and you rarely notice how much you carry.
behaviors: Your dream couple is two people building big things side by side.
You plan surprises with the same energy you plan your career.
You need someone who won’t ask you to shrink your dreams to fit.
strengths: When you decide something will happen, it usually does.
weaknesses: You can treat love like another project to win, and forget to simply enjoy it.
realLife: On a first date: You’re pitching your startup idea by the second chai, and somehow it’s charming.
In a fight: You want to fix it right now. They may need a night before they can talk.
tips: Ask about their dream before you share yours. The best teams listen first.
match: Best with: A fellow builder, or a calm soul who grounds you without slowing you down.
Green flag: They have dreams of their own and chase them with the same hunger.
Careful with: Someone who only loves the version of you that’s winning.

High.label: The Five-Year Planner
summaries: You have a plan, a backup plan, and a vision board.

You like knowing where you’re going, and you enjoy the work of getting there. Goals give your days a shape, and progress, even a little, puts you in a good mood. You’re not a machine, you just feel most like yourself when you’re building something.
behaviors: You want someone with their own goals, not just a calendar to fill.
You’ll ask about their career plans by the third date, with real interest.
Your love shows up as effort: planned trips, remembered deadlines, practical help.
strengths: You make things happen, for yourself and for the people you love.
weaknesses: Rest can feel like falling behind, so you sometimes skip it.
realLife: On a first date: You arrive straight from a meeting, phone on silent, and ask what they’re building.
In a fight: You go straight to solutions. Ask “do you want advice or a hug?” first.
tips: Put one lazy day a month in your calendar like it’s a meeting. Love needs time that isn’t productive.
match: Best with: Someone with their own fire who’s proud of yours, not threatened by it.
Green flag: They celebrate your wins as loudly as their own.
Careful with: Someone who keeps asking you to choose between them and your goals.

Moderate.label: The Seasonal Hustler
summaries: Full throttle when it matters, feet up when it doesn’t.

You can grind with the best of them when something lights you up, and let go completely when it doesn’t. Your drive comes in seasons, not every single day. That makes you good company for the workaholic and for the person on their third chai of the afternoon.
behaviors: In crunch weeks you go quiet, then come back with a long-weekend plan.
You can be their hype person and their “log off now” person.
You want a life with big goals and lazy Sundays in it.
strengths: You know when to push and when to rest, which is rarer than it sounds.
weaknesses: In a busy season you can disappear without saying it’s just a phase.
realLife: On a first date: You’re fully present, unless it’s quarter-end. Then you suggest a Sunday instead.
In a fight: You listen, then offer a fix. Sometimes they just want to be heard first.
tips: Tell them when a busy season is starting. A simple “crazy two weeks ahead” saves a lot of worry.
match: Best with: Someone with their own rhythm who doesn’t panic when yours changes.
Green flag: They ask “busy week?” instead of taking your quiet personally.
Careful with: Someone who only likes you in your high-energy seasons.

Low.label: The Work-to-Live Type
summaries: You work hard enough, then you log off and live.

You do your job well and you don’t let it eat your evenings. You have goals, just sensible-sized ones, and you’d rather enjoy the road than sprint down it. People love how unbothered you stay while everyone around you chases the next thing.
behaviors: Your weekends are for them, not for catching up on work.
You’d pick a calm life together over a flashy one.
You cheer for their ambitions without needing to match them.
strengths: You have time for people, and it shows.
weaknesses: When a big chance comes, you can talk yourself out of it as “too much effort”.
realLife: On a first date: You leave the office on time for once and are fully there, phone in your bag.
In a fight: You stay calm and fair, but you can wait too long to say what you need.
tips: Pick one thing a year that scares you a little and go for it. Your easy pace will be waiting when you get back.
match: Best with: Someone who values evenings and holidays as much as you do.
Green flag: They close the laptop when they’re with you.
Careful with: Someone who keeps calling your balance “no ambition”, as a joke, again and again.

VeryLow.label: The Hammock Philosopher
summaries: Life isn’t a race, and you refuse to run it like one.

You know something busy people forget: a good life is made of good days, not just big goals. You’re relaxed, easy to be around and hard to rattle with talk of five-year plans. Ambition isn’t missing in you, it’s just not in charge.
behaviors: You’re the one who says “let’s just stay in” and makes it the best night of the week.
You never make love feel like another item on a to-do list.
Their big plans impress you less than how they treat the waiter.
strengths: You make people feel they can finally exhale.
weaknesses: A driven person can read your calm as not caring about the future.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest a long walk and a chai stall. No reservation, no rush.
In a fight: You want to drop it and order food. Sometimes it needs talking first.
tips: Say one thing you’re quietly hoping for out loud. Being easygoing doesn’t mean you can’t want something.
match: Best with: Someone who loves slow mornings, or a go-getter who needs a soft place to land.
Green flag: They can do nothing with you all day and call it a great day.
Careful with: Someone who keeps trying to “fix” your pace into theirs.

tests.title: Calm Presence
tests.subtitle: How steady you are under pressure
tests.description: Measures emotional steadiness, patience, and your ability to stay grounded when life is messy.
tests.whatYouLearn: Whether you bring calm or intensity into stressful moments.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Calm + calm is peaceful; calm + intense can work if both respect each other’s style.

questions.text: Your flight is cancelled at the gate. Your first move…

options.text: Breathe, find the desk, sort it out
Panic-text five people at once
Argue with the poor staff at the counter
Rant on the family group, then rebook

questions.text: In a crisis, people come to you because…

options.text: They know you’ll feel it right along with them
You stay calm when they can’t

questions.text: Stuck in Bengaluru traffic, forty minutes late for something important. You…

options.text: Text ahead, then sit with it
Honk at everything, including the signal
Put on a podcast. Honking won’t move the cars
Check the map every thirty seconds, sighing

questions.text: The person you’re seeing texts “We need to talk.” Then goes offline for two hours. You…

options.text: Assume it’s about the weekend plan, carry on
Replay every chat from the last week
Feel a knot, but wait to hear it
Reply “Sure, call me when you’re free”

questions.text: Big presentation in ten minutes, and the laptop won’t connect to the projector. You…

options.text: Restart everything twice, heart racing
Feel your face go hot and your mind go blank
Joke about it and start without slides
Sweat a little, call IT, keep smiling

questions.text: Mum calls, upset: an aunty said something rude about her at a wedding. You…

options.text: Get angry on her behalf, ready to call the aunty
Stay calm on the call, then rant to your sibling
Tell her the aunty isn’t worth her sleep
Listen, help her laugh about it, move on

questions.text: When you’re angry, people usually…

options.text: Hear about it later, calmly, in full sentences
Know right away. It’s all over your face

questions.text: Your food order arrives wrong at 11 pm and you’re starving. You…

options.text: Feel like the whole night is ruined
Complain in the app, eat it anyway
Spend twenty minutes arguing with chat support
Eat it. Food is food

tests.measures: how steady, patient and grounded you stay under pressure

VeryHigh.label: The Human Anchor
summaries: Storms come and go. You stay exactly where you are.

You stay steady when plans crash, people shout and phones light up with bad news. It isn’t that you don’t feel things, you just don’t let them push you around. People call you first in a crisis, because your voice slows their heartbeat down.
behaviors: You’re the calm voice when their exam, job or family drama hits.
Fights with you rarely get loud, because you won’t match the volume.
You show love by staying, not by making speeches.
strengths: In a crisis you get clearer, not louder.
weaknesses: You can be so steady that nobody notices when you’re hurting too.
realLife: On a first date: It starts pouring, and you’re the one who says, “Let’s find chai and wait it out.”
In a fight: You stay calm, which helps. Just don’t let calm turn into silence: say what you need.
tips: Let people see you rattled once in a while. Anchors are lovely, but anchors need looking after too.
match: Best with: Someone who brings colour and feeling, and trusts your calm to hold them.
Green flag: They check on you too, not only when they need your calm.
Careful with: Someone who mistakes your calm for a sign that you’ll put up with anything.

High.label: The Cool Head
summaries: When everyone panics, you’re already looking for the fix.
You rarely lose your balance, and when you do, it doesn’t last. You’ve learnt that most problems shrink when you don’t add drama to them. People feel safer around you, even when they can’t say why.
behaviors: Your calm voice is what they need when their day falls apart.
You don’t blow up over small things, so big talks feel safe with you.
Sometimes they’ll wish you looked a little more upset, just to know you care.
strengths: You lower the temperature of every room you walk into.
weaknesses: Your calm can look like not caring when they want you to feel it with them.
realLife: On a first date: The cab cancels twice and you still arrive smiling, with a funny story about it.
In a fight: You stay level and listen. Remember to say how you feel too, not just what’s fair.
tips: Show your feelings a bit more than feels natural. “That hurt” from a calm person lands with real weight.
match: Best with: Someone warm and expressive who finds your steadiness a relief.
Green flag: They tell you how they feel instead of hoping you’ll guess.
Careful with: Someone who creates chaos and leans on you to clean it up.

Moderate.label: The Count-to-Ten Type
summaries: You feel the wave, then you ride it.

Things do get to you, you just don’t let them drive. You feel the irritation, take a breath and choose what to do with it, most days. On a bad day you snap a little, and you’re quick to notice it and own it.
behaviors: You can stay calm through their bad day, mostly. Ask again on a bad week.
You’d rather take a walk than say something you’ll regret.
You’re steady enough to lean on and real enough to have your own moments.
strengths: You can feel strongly and still think clearly, most of the time.
weaknesses: When you’re tired or hungry, your fuse is shorter than you admit.
realLife: On a first date: The waiter spills water on you. You wince, then make a joke about it.
In a fight: You take a breath, but sometimes the sharp line slips out first. Then you come back and own it.
tips: Know what shortens your fuse: hunger, no sleep, Monday mornings. Don’t start a big talk when any of them is on.
match: Best with: Someone who can handle your rare snaps and gives you room to reset.
Green flag: They say “let’s talk after dinner” when things get heated.
Careful with: Someone whose moods swing so much that you’re always the one calming things down.

Low.label: The Pressure Cooker
summaries: Calm, calm, calm, then one loud whistle.

You hold it together longer than people think, until it all comes out at once. You care a lot, so stress lands on you hard, and it shows. Once the steam is out, you’re soft, clear and ready to fix things.
behaviors: You can swallow small annoyances for weeks, then one sock on the floor sets off the whistle.
You need a minute to vent before you can think about solutions.
When you say sorry after a blow-up, you say it properly.
strengths: You feel things fully, which makes your love warm and your loyalty fierce.
weaknesses: Saving up small irritations means the big blow-up is never really about the sock.
realLife: On a first date: You’re nervous and chatty for ten minutes, then perfectly lovely once you settle in.
In a fight: You hold back, then say everything at once. Say the small thing the day it happens.
tips: Let the steam out in small puffs: say “that annoyed me” the same day, while it’s still small.
match: Best with: Someone patient who checks in early: “Something’s bugging you, na?”
Green flag: They notice the steam building and ask before the whistle.
Careful with: Someone who keeps a list of your bad moments and brings it out later.

VeryLow.label: The Firecracker
summaries: You feel it fast, say it fast, and forget it fast.

Your feelings don’t queue, they arrive all at once and loudly. That same quick spark makes you passionate, funny and impossible to ignore. You flare up fast and you usually cool down just as fast, often before the other person has finished being shocked.
behaviors: They will never have to guess how you feel about anything.
A late reply or a cold tone can light your fuse before you know the reason.
You apologise as quickly as you flare up, and you mean it.
strengths: Total honesty: nothing festers inside you, it all comes out and gets sorted.
weaknesses: Words said in the first hot minute can stay with someone long after you’ve cooled.
realLife: On a first date: The restaurant loses your booking. You’re furious, then laughing about it by dessert.
In a fight: You go off in the first minute. Try a glass of water and ten slow breaths before the first sentence.
tips: Make a ten-minute rule: when you’re upset, write the message, wait, then send the kinder version.
match: Best with: Someone steady who loves your fire and doesn’t take every spark personally.
Green flag: They stay calm when you’re loud and come back to talk when you’re ready.
Careful with: Someone who pokes you just to watch you react.

Undecided.label: The Count-to-Ten Type

weaknesses: When you’re tired or hungry, your fuse is shorter than you admit.

tests.title: Social Energy
tests.subtitle: Your level of outgoing energy
tests.description: Shows whether you recharge around people or need solitude to feel good.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your natural social battery and preferred social rhythm.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Prevents mismatch: extro energy vs intro energy needs different pacing.

options.text: Say yes, then secretly hope it gets cancelled
“Where? I’m coming.” Already changing
Reply “next time” and order in
Go for an hour, then home to bed

questions.text: Your perfect birthday:

options.text: A big party with everyone I know
Dinner with my two favourite people

questions.text: Your cousin’s wedding, day three of five. By now you…

options.text: Have claimed the one quiet corner in the hall
Still dancing, with longer chai breaks
Need an hour alone in the room with your phone
Are leading the sangeet dance practice

questions.text: Your office says coming in is optional. You go in…

options.text: Never. My desk, my rules, my pyjamas
Every day. Home alone all day is too quiet
Two days a week, for lunch and gossip
Most days. The chatter keeps me going

questions.text: A stranger at a house party starts chatting with you. You…

options.text: Smile, nod, and drift towards the snacks
Talk a little, and feel tired after
Chat for a bit, then find your own people
Know their whole life story in ten minutes

questions.text: After a whole day out with people, you feel…

options.text: Buzzing. Who’s up for dinner?
Happy, then quiet for the evening
Like you need a full day alone now

questions.text: A holiday with the person you’re seeing:

options.text: Just us two in the hills, phones off
A group trip with their people and mine

questions.text: You’ve had the flat to yourself all weekend. By Sunday night you…

options.text: Have called three people just to hear voices
Feel brand new
Enjoyed it, and you’re glad Monday has faces
Spent half of it on the group chat anyway

tests.measures: how much energy you get from social interaction versus alone time

VeryHigh.label: The Human Disco Ball
summaries: You walk into a room and it gets louder, in a good way.

You come alive around people, and the more the merrier. Small talk with strangers, a five-day wedding, a house party that runs till 3 am: you’re still going. A quiet evening alone is nice once in a while, but by Sunday you’re texting everyone.
behaviors: Meeting their people early isn’t scary for you, it’s the fun part.
Your love life comes with a full calendar and lots of new faces.
You need someone who’s proud to walk into a party next to you.
strengths: You can make a stranger feel like an old pal in five minutes.
weaknesses: A quieter person can end up feeling like a plus-one in your life instead of the main plan.
realLife: On a first date: It starts as coffee for two and ends as dinner with people you met that evening.
In a fight: You want to talk it out now, out loud. Give them a quiet hour first.
tips: Make time for just the two of you: no group, no phones. Your sparkle is lovely, but they want you to themselves too.
match: Best with: Someone who loves a crowd, or a calmer soul who enjoys your sparkle from the sofa.
Green flag: They let you shine at the party and still find you at the end of the night.
Careful with: Someone who makes you feel guilty for having so many people in your life.

High.label: The Group-Chat Starter
summaries: If there’s a plan, you probably made it.
People are where your energy comes from. A good evening out sends you home buzzing, and a quiet weekend has you texting everyone by Sunday. You like your alone time, just in small amounts.
behaviors: You’ll want to meet their people early, and you’ll want them to meet yours.
Your dates often turn into group plans, and you love it when they do.
A whole weekend at home together sounds lovely for exactly one day.
strengths: You make people feel included, and you’re the reason the group still meets.
weaknesses: A quieter person can feel crowded by how many plans you fill their week with.
realLife: On a first date: You pick a lively place, chat with the waiter, and know the next table by the end.
In a fight: You want to talk it out now, face to face. They may need some quiet first.
tips: Plan one quiet date for every two busy ones. Some people only open up when the room is small.
match: Best with: Someone social enough to come along and secure enough to let you go without them.
Green flag: They’re warm with your people and happy to bring theirs.
Careful with: Someone who wants you all to themselves and frowns at every group plan.

Moderate.label: The Dimmer Switch
summaries: Life of the party on Saturday, phone on silent by Sunday.

You can light up a room and you can disappear into a book, and both are really you. You read your own battery well: you know when you want people and when you need peace. People never quite know which version they’ll get, and they like both.
behaviors: One weekend it’s brunch with their gang, the next it’s a movie on your sofa.
You can keep up with their social life without needing to lead it.
You’ll tell them when your battery’s low, mostly in time.
strengths: You fit in at the loud party and at the quiet dinner, and you enjoy both.
weaknesses: Your plans change as your battery does, and people can’t always keep up.
realLife: On a first date: Dinner, then you decide on the spot whether it turns into drinks with their gang.
In a fight: You can talk it out right away or take space, depending on your battery. Tell them which.
tips: Give them your battery like a weather report: “Low today, big plans Saturday.” It turns your changes into something they can plan around.
match: Best with: Someone flexible who’s fine with a big Saturday and a silent Sunday.
Green flag: They ask “in the mood for people tonight?” instead of assuming.
Careful with: Someone who wants you at full volume all the time, or never.

Low.label: The Quiet Regular
summaries: Same three people, same café, no complaints.

You enjoy people, especially the ones you’ve known forever, but big crowds wear you out fast. You choose your plans carefully and you’re loyal to your small circle. One good evening out a week is plenty; the rest belongs to you.
behaviors: You’ll introduce them to your two closest people, and that means everything.
You like a mix: a dinner out, then a quiet night in to recover.
You leave parties early, and they’ll learn it’s not about them.
strengths: Your people know you’ll always show up for the plans that matter.
weaknesses: You can say no so often that new people stop asking.
realLife: On a first date: Your favourite little place, where they already know your order.
In a fight: You need some time alone first, then you’re ready to talk it through properly.
tips: Say yes to one plan a month you’d normally skip. Some of the best people are at the parties you almost missed.
match: Best with: Someone with a small, close circle who loves nights in as much as nights out.
Green flag: They’re happy to leave a party early with you.
Careful with: Someone who needs a packed weekend calendar to feel happy.

VeryLow.label: The Blanket Burrito
summaries: Plans cancelled? Best news of the week.

Your best evenings involve a blanket, your own playlist and nobody needing anything from you. You’re not shy or cold: you like people, just in small, quiet doses. Time alone is how you refill, and you come back from it kinder and sharper.
behaviors: Your idea of romance is two people reading on the same sofa, not talking.
You’d rather have one long, real conversation than a night of small talk.
Letting someone into your quiet time is your biggest compliment.
strengths: When you do show up, you’re fully there, listening like nobody else in the room.
weaknesses: A social person can read your need for space as you pulling away from them.
realLife: On a first date: A quiet café, a corner table, and a conversation that runs three hours.
In a fight: You need to go away and think. Say “I need an hour” so they don’t feel shut out.
tips: Tell them early: “When I go quiet, I’m recharging, not leaving.” It saves them a lot of guessing.
match: Best with: Someone who loves quiet nights in, or a social soul who doesn’t need you at every party.
Green flag: They can sit in comfortable silence with you and call it a good evening.
Careful with: Someone who sulks every time you skip a party.

tests.title: Openness
tests.subtitle: Curiosity, novelty, new experiences
tests.description: Measures curiosity, willingness to try new things, and openness to different ideas.
tests.whatYouLearn: Whether you seek novelty or prefer the familiar.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Matching improves when lifestyle pace (adventurous vs stable) is compatible.

Mostly new finds, a few old songs to sing along

tests.measures: how curious and open you are to new ideas and experiences

VeryHigh.label: The Collector of Firsts
summaries: Same old is your least favourite thing in the world.

You collect experiences the way other people collect things. A new city, a strange dish, a stranger’s opinion that flips your thinking: that’s your idea of a good day. You’re happiest at the edge of the map, and you bring the people you love along.
behaviors: Your dream relationship is a long list of firsts together.
You change your mind when you learn something new, and you’re proud of it.
You need someone who sees your restlessness as a gift, not a warning sign.
strengths: You can find something new and exciting in any city, any day, any person.
weaknesses: Calm, regular days can feel like a cage to you, even when they’re a gift.
realLife: On a first date: A cooking class, a night market, or a street neither of you has walked down.
In a fight: You want to try something new to fix it. Make sure you’ve actually heard what’s wrong.
tips: Learn to love the ordinary days too. A slow Sunday with the right person is its own kind of new.
match: Best with: Someone just as curious, who packs a bag when you say “let’s go”.
Green flag: They grow with you, not just alongside you.
Careful with: Someone who wants you to settle down by settling for less.

High.label: The Curious Cat
summaries: If you haven’t tried it, it’s already on your list.

New food, new places, new ideas: you’re pulled towards them like a magnet. You learn things just because they’re interesting, and your phone holds a hundred saved reels of places to go. Routine is fine in small doses; too much and you get restless.
behaviors: You suggest a new date idea every weekend and get excited about each one.
You fall for people who can teach you something you didn’t know.
You get bored when love turns into the same three plans on repeat.
strengths: You keep life, and love, from ever going stale.
weaknesses: Chasing the next new thing can make a steady person feel left behind.
realLife: On a first date: You pick a place neither of you has been, because that’s half the fun.
In a fight: You want to try a new way to solve it. Sometimes they just want the old peace back.
tips: Keep one ritual with them that never changes. It makes all your new adventures feel safer to them.
match: Best with: A fellow explorer, or a grounded person who loves your sense of wonder.
Green flag: They say yes to your strange ideas, at least once.
Careful with: Someone who mocks your curiosity or calls it a phase.

Moderate.label: The Weekend Explorer
summaries: Routine on weekdays, a little adventure on weekends.

You like a life with a solid base and a few surprises sprinkled on top. You’ll try the new restaurant, and you’ll also keep your Sunday ritual. New ideas interest you when they make sense, not just because they’re new.
behaviors: You’ll say yes to their odd hobby once, and maybe stick with it.
You like a mix of favourite date spots and new places to try.
You bring both stability and fresh energy to whoever you’re with.
strengths: You make adventure feel safe and routine feel fun.
weaknesses: You can sit on the fence until the moment for trying something has passed.
realLife: On a first date: A new café near a place you both know, so there’s an easy escape route.
In a fight: You can see both sides, which helps. Just pick one when it’s time to decide.
tips: When you’re torn between the usual and the new, pick the new once a month. You can always go back.
match: Best with: Someone with a bit of explorer in them and a love of home too.
Green flag: They mix your old favourites with new ideas, without pushing.
Careful with: Someone who never wants to try anything, or never wants to stay put.

Low.label: The Comfort Classic
summaries: You’ll try the new thing, then fly back to your old favourite.

You like your routines and your known places, and you’re not against something new now and then. You need a little warm-up before change, and you like to know what you’re getting into. Once you’ve tried something and liked it, it becomes part of home.
behaviors: You’ll try their favourite cuisine, then quietly order your usual next time.
Surprise trips make you a bit nervous; a heads-up makes you happy.
You fall in love slowly and stay in love steadily.
strengths: You can make any new place feel like home within a month.
weaknesses: You can say no to new things before you’ve really thought about them.
realLife: On a first date: A place you know well, maybe one new dish if they recommend it.
In a fight: You want the old peace back. Hear out what they want changed first.
tips: When you feel a no coming, try “let me think about it” instead. Half your best memories will come from those.
match: Best with: Someone who brings small adventures and gives you time to warm up.
Green flag: They share plans in advance and respect your favourites.
Careful with: Someone who springs huge changes on you and calls it being spontaneous.

VeryLow.label: The Same-Order Loyalist
summaries: You found what you love. Why would you keep looking?

You know your favourite dish, your favourite song and your favourite people, and you’re loyal to all of them. New things don’t scare you, they just rarely beat what you already love. Your steadiness makes you the person everyone comes home to.
behaviors: Once you love someone, you don’t keep looking around.
Your idea of romance is a ritual: same café, same table, every Saturday.
Big changes take you time, and you get there in your own way.
strengths: Deep loyalty: to people, to places and to promises.
weaknesses: “We always do it this way” can quietly close doors they want open.
realLife: On a first date: You take them to the place you’ve loved for years and know exactly what to order.
In a fight: You want things back to normal fast. Make sure the problem is solved, not just buried.
tips: Try one tiny new thing together each month: a dish, a route, a film. It keeps the familiar feeling fresh.
match: Best with: Someone who values routine and home, or an explorer who loves coming back to you.
Green flag: They build little rituals with you and keep them.
Careful with: Someone who calls your comfort zone boring and keeps pushing you out of it.

Undecided.label: The Weekend Explorer
summaries: Routine on weekdays, a little adventure on weekends.

You like a life with a solid base and a few surprises sprinkled on top. You’ll try the new restaurant, and you’ll also keep your Sunday ritual. New ideas interest you when they make sense, not just because they’re new.
behaviors: You’ll say yes to their odd hobby once, and maybe stick with it.
You like a mix of favourite date spots and new places to try.
You bring both stability and fresh energy to whoever you’re with.
strengths: You make adventure feel safe and routine feel fun.
weaknesses: You can sit on the fence until the moment for trying something has passed.
realLife: On a first date: A new café near a place you both know, so there’s an easy escape route.
In a fight: You can see both sides, which helps. Just pick one when it’s time to decide.
tips: When you’re torn between the usual and the new, pick the new once a month. You can always go back.
match: Best with: Someone with a bit of explorer in them and a love of home too.
Green flag: They mix your old favourites with new ideas, without pushing.
Careful with: Someone who never wants to try anything, or never wants to stay put.

tests.measures: how consistently you follow through on commitments and routines

VeryHigh.label: The Human Calendar
summaries: Gym at 6, inbox clear by 10, in bed by 11. Every day.

Your life runs like a well-kept train timetable, and you like it that way. You keep habits for years, finish what you start and save money without trying. Self-control comes so naturally to you that you sometimes forget how hard it is for others.
behaviors: You plan anniversaries months ahead and never forget a birthday.
You need someone who keeps their word, every single time.
A last-minute change of plans can throw off your whole day.
strengths: You build a life step by step, and it actually gets built.
weaknesses: You can hold people to your standards and forget they run on a different clock.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve read the menu online, booked the table and planned the route home.
In a fight: You want the facts and a fix. Leave room for feelings that don’t follow rules.
tips: Let one small plan go wrong on purpose and see what happens. Being easy on little things makes you easier to love.
match: Best with: Someone equally steady, or a free spirit who loves being looked after.
Green flag: They respect your routine, and sometimes join it.
Careful with: Someone who mocks your discipline or keeps breaking plans.

High.label: The Checklist Hero
summaries: You said you’d do it. It’s already done.

You like your days to have a shape, and you keep your promises, big and small. Habits come easily to you because you can see how small things add up. You’re the one people trust with the plan, the money and the spare keys.
behaviors: You show love by showing up: on time, every time.
You remember the date, the booking, and that they hate coriander.
Broken plans bother you more than you let on.
strengths: When you say you’ll do something, people stop worrying about it.
weaknesses: Their spontaneous ideas can feel like a threat to your carefully planned week.
realLife: On a first date: You arrive five minutes early and already know what you’re ordering.
In a fight: You want a clear fix and a plan. Sometimes they need you to listen before you solve.
tips: Leave one evening a week unplanned and say yes to whatever they suggest. Love grows in the gaps too.
match: Best with: Someone reliable who respects your routines and brings a little fun to them.
Green flag: They keep small promises, which tells you everything about the big ones.
Careful with: Someone who keeps cancelling last minute and calls it being chill.

Moderate.label: The Flexible Planner
summaries: A plan, a backup, and room for a surprise.

You keep your life mostly on track without being a robot about it. Bills get paid, deadlines get met, and you’ll still skip the gym for a good chat. Your habits come and go in seasons, and you always find your way back to them.
behaviors: You remember the important dates, mostly without a reminder.
You’ll plan the trip, but leave one day completely open.
You can be counted on without being rigid about it.
strengths: You’re reliable enough to trust and relaxed enough to enjoy.
weaknesses: When life gets busy, your good habits are the first thing you drop.
realLife: On a first date: You booked the place, but you’re happy to walk somewhere else if it looks nicer.
In a fight: You solve it practically, then you come back and actually follow through.
tips: Pick one habit that matters to you both, like a weekly date night, and protect it like a meeting.
match: Best with: Someone who likes some structure and some surprise, just like you.
Green flag: They keep their word and don’t mind changing plans now and then.
Careful with: Someone who never plans, or plans everything without asking you.

Low.label: The Last-Minute Legend
summaries: Deadlines are when your brain finally wakes up.

You get things done, just rarely early. Pressure is your fuel and the night before is your natural habitat. You’re flexible, quick on your feet and calm in chaos, because chaos is where you do your best work.
behaviors: Your gifts are thoughtful, and sometimes bought on the way there.
You’re great at a last-minute plan, less great at booking ahead.
You keep the big promises and forget the small ones, like texting when you land.
strengths: In a sudden crisis, you’re the one who can make a plan in five minutes.
weaknesses: People who plan ahead can feel stressed just watching you leave it all to the end.
realLife: On a first date: You book the table on the way there, and somehow get the best seat.
In a fight: You say you’ll fix it, and you will. Name a day, so they know when.
tips: Do the small things the moment you think of them: the text, the booking, the reply. Two minutes now saves a lot of hurt later.
match: Best with: Someone patient with your timing who enjoys a bit of spontaneity.
Green flag: They give you a gentle reminder without making you feel like a child.
Careful with: Someone who needs every plan locked a month ahead and panics when it isn’t.

VeryLow.label: The Free Spirit
summaries: Plans are suggestions. Life is happening right now.

You live by feel, not by schedule, and some of your best stories began with “let’s just go”. Rules and routines feel like a tight collar to you. You’re fun, flexible and brilliant in a surprise, even if your to-do list has been waiting since March.
behaviors: You’re the one who suggests a midnight drive for no reason at all.
Remembering dates and plans is harder for you than feeling things deeply.
You love hard and freely, without needing it all mapped out.
strengths: You can turn any boring day into a story worth telling.
weaknesses: A missed promise feels small to you and big to the person who was waiting.
realLife: On a first date: It was meant to be coffee. It became a street food crawl and a sunset.
In a fight: You want to move on fast. Make sure the thing that hurt them actually gets fixed.
tips: Pick the three promises that matter most to them, like calls, dates and birthdays, and set reminders. Keep the rest of life free.
match: Best with: Someone organised enough to hold the calendar and fun enough to jump in the car.
Green flag: They love your spark and gently help you keep the promises that matter.
Careful with: Someone who tries to run your life like a timetable.

Undecided.label: The Flexible Planner
summaries: A plan, a backup, and room for a surprise.

You keep your life mostly on track without being a robot about it. Bills get paid, deadlines get met, and you’ll still skip the gym for a good chat. Your habits come and go in seasons, and you always find your way back to them.
behaviors: You remember the important dates, mostly without a reminder.
You’ll plan the trip, but leave one day completely open.
You can be counted on without being rigid about it.
strengths: You’re reliable enough to trust and relaxed enough to enjoy.
weaknesses: When life gets busy, your good habits are the first thing you drop.
realLife: On a first date: You booked the place, but you’re happy to walk somewhere else if it looks nicer.
In a fight: You solve it practically, then you come back and actually follow through.
tips: Pick one habit that matters to you both, like a weekly date night, and protect it like a meeting.
match: Best with: Someone who likes some structure and some surprise, just like you.
Green flag: They keep their word and don’t mind changing plans now and then.
Careful with: Someone who never plans, or plans everything without asking you.

tests.measures: how much creative and imaginative energy you carry

VeryHigh.label: The Technicolour Mind
summaries: Your head is a film festival that never closes.

You see the world in colour and stories. A waiting room becomes a novel, an empty wall becomes a mural, a dinner becomes an experience. Making things isn’t a hobby for you, it’s how you breathe, and life feels grey when you can’t.
behaviors: You write the card, design the date and pick the playlist, all yourself.
You fall for minds before faces, and for stories before plans.
You need room to create, even when you’re deeply in love.
strengths: You make ordinary moments feel like scenes from a film.
weaknesses: Bills, dates and the boring bits of life can slip right past you.
realLife: On a first date: You turn a normal dinner into a story they’ll still be telling years later.
In a fight: You feel it all in colour. Say it in plain words too, so they can follow.
tips: Let one practical person into your life without trying to change them. They’re the frame that makes your painting hang straight.
match: Best with: A fellow dreamer, or a grounded soul who loves your colour and helps with the admin.
Green flag: They protect your time to create and ask to see what you made.
Careful with: Someone who treats your art like a waste of time.

High.label: The Idea Machine
summaries: Give you a blank page and you’ll fill three.

Your mind is always making something: a plan, a story, a better way to do it. You notice beauty in small things and you love putting your own spin on everything. Boring answers bore you, and people come to you when they’re stuck.
behaviors: Your gifts are handmade, or so personal they could only be from you.
You turn a normal Tuesday into a date with a theme.
You need someone who enjoys your ideas instead of rolling their eyes.
strengths: You see possibilities everyone else walked right past.
weaknesses: Ten new ideas can mean none of them gets finished.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest something unusual: a gallery, a street-art walk, a cooking class.
In a fight: You come up with ten ways to fix it. Pick one and stick with it.
tips: Finish one idea all the way, even a small one. It’s the finished things that people remember.
match: Best with: Someone who loves your ideas and helps you finish one or two.
Green flag: They get excited about your ideas instead of asking “but why?”
Careful with: Someone who keeps telling you to “be realistic”, in that tone.

Moderate.label: The Practical Dreamer
summaries: One foot in the clouds, one on the ground.

You can dream big and still check the budget. You enjoy making things, from a good playlist to a nicely plated dinner, and you also like things that work. People come to you for ideas that are fresh but doable.
behaviors: You plan dates with a creative twist that still run on time.
You can enjoy a deep talk about dreams and a sharp talk about rent.
You keep love interesting without making it complicated.
strengths: You make creative ideas actually happen.
weaknesses: You can hold back your wilder ideas in case they sound silly.
realLife: On a first date: A pottery class with dinner booked after, because you plan for fun too.
In a fight: You can see a creative way out. Just make sure they feel heard first.
tips: Share the idea you think is too silly. The ones you hold back are often the ones they’ll love.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys a bit of art and a bit of logic, like you.
Green flag: They get excited about your ideas and help you make them real.
Careful with: Someone who laughs at your imagination, or wants nothing but chaos.

Low.label: The Useful-Gift Giver
summaries: Thoughtful, sensible, and one step ahead of the problem.

You have taste and you have ideas, you just like them to be useful. You’ll pick the gift they’ll actually use and the plan that will actually work. Creativity, for you, is about solving things smartly, not putting on a show.
behaviors: Your gifts get used every single day, and they remember who gave them.
You enjoy their creative side, as long as the bills still get paid.
You plan dates that run smoothly, with one small personal touch.
strengths: You make good ideas real, without the drama.
weaknesses: You can dismiss a fun idea too quickly because it isn’t useful yet.
realLife: On a first date: A good, reliable place, plus a small surprise you thought of on the way.
In a fight: You look for the fix. Let them feel it out before you hand over the solution.
tips: Let one plan be about how it feels, not how it works. A little impractical joy goes a long way in love.
match: Best with: Someone creative who’s happy to have you as the grounded half.
Green flag: They notice the thought behind your practical choices.
Careful with: Someone with big ideas who expects you to do all the work for them.

VeryLow.label: The No-Nonsense Fixer
summaries: You don’t dream up a bridge. You build one.

You like things that work, plans that make sense and answers you can check. While others are still brainstorming, you’ve already found the simplest way to get it done. Your mind is clear and grounded, and people bring you their messes because you actually fix them.
behaviors: You show love by fixing things: their laptop, their CV, their leaking tap.
Grand romantic gestures matter less to you than someone who simply shows up.
You need someone who sees practical care as real love.
strengths: You turn chaos into something that works.
weaknesses: A dreamy person can feel unheard when you go straight to “but is it practical?”
realLife: On a first date: You’ve checked the parking, the menu and the weather. Smooth from start to finish.
In a fight: You go straight to fixing it. Ask first whether they want a fix or a listen.
tips: Once in a while, say yes to an idea before asking if it’s practical. Some of the best things in life aren’t.
match: Best with: Someone grounded, or a creative soul who loves having a steady builder beside them.
Green flag: They value your help and don’t need everything to be a grand gesture.
Careful with: Someone who calls you boring because you don’t do drama.

Undecided.label: The Practical Dreamer
summaries: One foot in the clouds, one on the ground.

You can dream big and still check the budget. You enjoy making things, from a good playlist to a nicely plated dinner, and you also like things that work. People come to you for ideas that are fresh but doable.
behaviors: You plan dates with a creative twist that still run on time.
You can enjoy a deep talk about dreams and a sharp talk about rent.
You keep love interesting without making it complicated.

weaknesses: You can hold back your wilder ideas in case they sound silly.

In a fight: You can see a creative way out. Just make sure they feel heard first.
tips: Share the idea you think is too silly. The ones you hold back are often the ones they’ll love.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys a bit of art and a bit of logic, like you.
Green flag: They get excited about your ideas and help you make them real.
Careful with: Someone who laughs at your imagination, or wants nothing but chaos.

tests.measures: how quickly you bounce back after setbacks and emotional difficulty

VeryHigh.label: The Unsinkable One
summaries: Life throws lemons. You’re already selling nimbu paani.

You’ve learnt that most bad days are just days. Failure, rejection and chaos knock on your door, and you let them in, make them chai and show them out. You’re not in denial, you just believe in tomorrow so firmly that today’s mess can’t hold you.
behaviors: You don’t let one bad week shake your faith in a good relationship.
Rejection doesn’t make you bitter, it makes you curious about who’s next.
You’re the calm hope at home when everyone else is worried.
strengths: No setback is big enough to stop you for long.
weaknesses: You can bounce back so fast that you skip the lesson, or miss someone else’s pain.
realLife: On a first date: It rains, the bike won’t start, and you’re laughing harder than anyone at the bus stop.
In a fight: You want to fix it and move on within the hour. Let them take the time they need.
tips: Let yourself be sad sometimes, out loud. Bouncing back is your gift, but feeling it first makes you whole.
match: Best with: Someone with steady hope of their own, or a deep feeler who needs your light.
Green flag: They lean on you and also let you lean on them.
Careful with: Someone who needs you to always be the cheerful one.

High.label: The Comeback Kid
summaries: Knock you down and you’re already planning the comeback.

Setbacks sting, and then they turn into fuel. You take a moment, find the lesson and get moving again, often with a funny story about it. People around you feel braver, because you make failure look survivable.
behaviors: A bad fight doesn’t mean a bad relationship to you.
You can laugh about a disaster date by the next morning.
When they’re down, you’re great at reminding them it won’t last.
strengths: You turn bad luck into a story and a plan.
weaknesses: You can move on so fast that the other person feels left behind in the hurt.
realLife: On a first date: The café is shut and it’s raining, and you still call it the best evening of the month.
In a fight: You’re ready to move on before they are. Ask if they are too.
tips: When someone you love is hurting, don’t rush them to the bright side. Sit in the dark with them for a bit first.
match: Best with: Someone who can match your bounce, or who loves being lifted up by it.
Green flag: They face problems with you instead of blaming you for them.
Careful with: Someone who stays stuck in every bad mood and expects you to carry it.

Moderate.label: The Bamboo Soul
summaries: You bend in the storm. You don’t break.

Hard things shake you, and you let yourself feel them, but they don’t knock you over for long. A few low days, a talk with someone you trust, and you’re slowly upright again. You’re honest about it: not falsely cheerful, not stuck.
behaviors: After a fight, you need an evening, then you’re ready to make up.
You can hold their bad week without falling apart yourself.
You say so when you’re not okay, and then you get okay again.
strengths: You stay honest about pain without letting it run your life.
weaknesses: In a really bad week, you can go quiet instead of asking for help.
realLife: On a first date: The plan falls through and you suggest plan B, a little disappointed, still fun.
In a fight: You need a night to reset, then you come back ready to fix it.
tips: Ask for help a day earlier than you think you need it. Bending is easier with someone to lean on.
match: Best with: Someone steady who sits with you on bad days and laughs with you after.
Green flag: They ask “do you want to talk, or do you want food?” and mean both.
Careful with: Someone who brings a new crisis every week and leaves no room for yours.

Low.label: The Slow Mender
summaries: Knocked down, you take your time, then stand up stronger.

Setbacks knock the wind out of you for a while, and you don’t hide that. You need time, a few good people and a bit of quiet to find your feet again. But you always do, and you come back with lessons you don’t forget.
behaviors: After a fight, you need a day before things feel normal again.
Rejection lands hard, so you choose carefully who you open up to.
You remember who stood by you on your slow days.
strengths: You learn deeply from every fall, so you rarely make the same mistake twice.
weaknesses: You can stay in a low mood longer than the problem deserves.
realLife: On a first date: You’re careful about what you share, but your warmth shows through anyway.
In a fight: You go quiet and take it hard. Say “I need a day” instead of disappearing.
tips: Give the low feeling a time limit: two days to sulk, then one small step forward. It gets lighter faster than you expect.
match: Best with: Someone warm and patient who reminds you how far you’ve come.
Green flag: They give you space and still check in.
Careful with: Someone who makes you feel weak for taking your time.

VeryLow.label: The Deep Feeler
summaries: You feel every hit fully, and you heal at your own pace.

When something hurts, it doesn’t bounce off you, it goes deep. You think about what went wrong, you feel it for a long time, and you rarely pretend you’re fine. That depth makes you gentle with others who struggle, because you know how heavy things can get.
behaviors: A fight or a cold week can stay with you long after it’s over.
You love with your whole heart, so heartbreak takes its time to leave.
You need someone who stays gentle on your slow days.
strengths: You understand pain like few people do, and others feel safe falling apart near you.
weaknesses: On low days, one bad moment can feel like the whole story of your life.
realLife: On a first date: You’re a little guarded at first. By the end, you’ve shared something real.
In a fight: It stays with you for days. Tell them you need time, so they don’t read it as anger.
tips: Keep one small routine for hard days: a walk, a call, a hot meal. Small steps carry you further than you think.
match: Best with: Someone patient and steady who doesn’t rush you to be okay.
Green flag: They check in on you a week later, not just on the day it happened.
Careful with: Someone who says “just get over it” when you’re hurting.

Undecided.label: The Bamboo Soul

tests.subtitle: Warmth, generosity, empathy

tests.howItHelpsMatch: Matching improves when kindness level and emotional softness align.

tests.measures: how naturally warm, generous, and gentle you are in daily life

VeryHigh.label: The Human Hug
summaries: Strangers tell you their life stories in the queue.

Kindness isn’t something you do, it’s how you’re made. You feed the street dogs, stand up for whoever’s being roasted, and still tip the waiter who spilled dal on you. People feel lighter after talking to you, and you rarely notice how much you give.
behaviors: You love loudly and gently at the same time.
You forgive quickly, sometimes before they’ve even said sorry.
Their family loves you within a week, and so does their dog.
strengths: You make people feel seen, heard and safe, sometimes in five minutes.
weaknesses: People who take more than they give can find you very easily.
realLife: On a first date: Before dessert, you’ve won over the waiter and helped an aunty with her bags.
In a fight: You apologise first, even when it wasn’t your fault. Say how you feel too.
tips: Kindness to yourself counts too. Say one no this week without explaining, and notice who stays.
match: Best with: Someone just as warm, who protects your soft heart instead of using it.
Green flag: They’re kind to you when nobody’s watching.
Careful with: Someone who only turns up when they need your help.

High.label: The Chai Maker
summaries: First to notice, first to put the kettle on.

You notice when someone’s off, and you do something about it. You give people the benefit of the doubt and you’re gentle with their feelings, even on your own bad days. People feel safe with you, and they tell you things they tell nobody else.
behaviors: You remember their stressful day and check in on it that evening.
You show care in small, steady ways: food, notes, a hand on the shoulder.
Even in a fight, you try not to say the thing that would really hurt.
strengths: You make people feel looked after, often before they ask.
weaknesses: You can give so much that you forget to ask for anything back.
realLife: On a first date: You notice they’re cold before they say it, and offer your jacket.
In a fight: You soften fast and want to make up. Make sure your side gets said too.
tips: Let someone look after you for a change. Being cared for is part of love, not a debt.
match: Best with: Someone who notices your kindness and gives it back.
Green flag: They make you the chai on the days you’re the one who needs it.
Careful with: Someone who takes your care and never asks how you are.

Moderate.label: The Kind Realist
summaries: Warm, fair, and nobody’s doormat.

You care about people and you show it, but you also know where your limits are. You’ll help a stranger, check on a friend and still say no when someone takes advantage. Your kindness has a spine, and people respect it.
behaviors: You’re caring without losing yourself in the other person.
You’ll go out of your way for them, and you expect the same effort back.
You’re gentle in a fight, but you won’t pretend you’re okay when you’re not.
strengths: You’re kind without being a pushover, which is rarer than it sounds.
weaknesses: When you’re tired, your kindness can switch off faster than you’d like.
realLife: On a first date: You’re warm with them and with the waiter, and you split the bill without a fuss.
In a fight: You stay fair and kind, and you still say what you need.
tips: Say no kindly and early, not late and annoyed. Your kindness lasts longer when it has edges.
match: Best with: Someone fair and warm who gives as much as they take.
Green flag: They respect your no as much as your yes.
Careful with: Someone who mistakes your kindness for unlimited favours.

Low.label: The Inner-Circle Guard
summaries: Polite to everyone, devoted to a chosen few.

You’re polite with strangers and fiercely warm with your people. You don’t give your energy away easily, because you know what it’s worth. Your kindness is practical: you turn up with help, not with speeches.
behaviors: They’ll feel your care through what you do, not what you say.
Once they’re in your circle, you’ll fight anyone for them.
You need time and trust before you show your softer side.
strengths: When you’re on someone’s side, you’re on it completely.
weaknesses: People outside your circle can read you as cold before they know you.
realLife: On a first date: You’re polite and watchful, then you warm up once they make you laugh.
In a fight: You can get blunt when you’re hurt. Soften the first sentence and the rest goes better.
tips: Say the warm thing you’re thinking. Your people know you care, but hearing it means more than you know.
match: Best with: Someone warm who’s happy to earn your trust and doesn’t take your caution personally.
Green flag: They’re kind to the waiter, their mum and you, all in the same way.
Careful with: Someone sweet to your face and harsh about others behind their backs.

VeryLow.label: The Coconut
summaries: Hard shell, soft inside. Few people get to the inside.

You don’t hand out your warmth to everyone, and you have your reasons. Maybe life taught you that people take more than they give. But the few who make it past your shell find someone fiercely loyal, honest and quietly soft.
behaviors: It takes a while before you show your soft side, and they have to earn it.
Your care shows in actions, like fixing things, rarely in sweet words.
Once you trust someone, you protect them like family.
strengths: Your loyalty, once earned, is unbreakable.
weaknesses: Your shell can keep out good people along with the bad ones.
realLife: On a first date: You’re polite, a little reserved, and you notice everything they do.
In a fight: You put up walls and go cool. Say “I’m guarding myself” so they know it isn’t hate.
tips: Try one small soft thing a week: a compliment, a thank-you, a “that was sweet”. Let one safe person see the inside.
match: Best with: Someone patient and consistent who doesn’t push, just keeps showing up.
Green flag: They keep small promises and never use your soft side against you.
Careful with: Someone who pushes for closeness fast and sulks when you need time.

Undecided.label: The Kind Realist

You care about people and you show it, but you also know where your limits are. You’ll help a stranger, check on a friend and still say no when someone takes advantage. Your kindness has a spine, and people respect it.

You’ll go out of your way for them, and you expect the same effort back.
You’re gentle in a fight, but you won’t pretend you’re okay when you’re not.

In a fight: You stay fair and kind, and you still say what you need.
tips: Say no kindly and early, not late and annoyed. Your kindness lasts longer when it has edges.
match: Best with: Someone fair and warm who gives as much as they take.
Green flag: They respect your no as much as your yes.
Careful with: Someone who mistakes your kindness for unlimited favours.

tests.measures: how comfortable you are with bold decisions and uncertainty

VeryHigh.label: The Fearless Wildcard
summaries: Your life story uses the word “suddenly” a lot.

You’ve quit jobs, moved cities on a hunch and said “why not” to things most people only think about. Risk doesn’t scare you; a boring, safe life does. You live with your whole chest, and people around you can’t look away.
behaviors: You’ll say “I like you” first, probably on the first date.
You fall fast and love boldly, and you want someone who can keep up.
Love with you is never boring, though sometimes it’s a little dizzy.
strengths: Fear just doesn’t get the final word in your life.
weaknesses: Your big leaps can land on the people you love, too.
realLife: On a first date: Coffee turns into a last-minute road trip, and somehow they say yes.
In a fight: You want to fix it with a big move right now. Try a small, honest talk first.
tips: Before each big jump, ask one person who loves you what they think. Not for permission, for the view you can’t see.
match: Best with: A fellow adventurer, or a steady soul who loves your fire and keeps the first-aid kit.
Green flag: They match your courage and still ask the hard questions.
Careful with: Someone who dares you into things just to watch you do them.

High.label: The One-Way Ticket
summaries: If it scares you a little, it’s probably worth doing.

You’d rather try and fail than wonder for the rest of your life. Uncertainty makes you curious, not nervous, and you’ve made a few jumps people called crazy. Most of them worked out, and the ones that didn’t make great stories.
behaviors: You say how you feel early, because waiting feels worse than a no.
You plan trips and dates with a bit of adventure built in.
You can get restless when love starts feeling too predictable.
strengths: You make things happen while others are still thinking about it.
weaknesses: A careful person can feel run over by how fast you decide.
realLife: On a first date: You pick a place neither of you knows, then a second place nobody planned.
In a fight: You want a bold move to fix it. Sometimes they just want a slow talk.
tips: Before a big leap, tell them first and listen to their worries. Bold is better when the person you love is on board.
match: Best with: Someone brave enough to jump with you, or calm enough to check the parachute.
Green flag: They say yes to your adventures and tell you honestly when one is too much.
Careful with: Someone who wants to clip your wings so they can feel safe.

Moderate.label: The Calculated Leaper
summaries: Brave enough to jump, smart enough to check first.

You’re up for a risk when it makes sense and happy to play safe when it doesn’t. You’ll go paragliding, just not with the cheapest operator. You weigh things quickly, decide clearly and rarely regret it either way.
behaviors: You’ll make the first move, once you’ve read the signs a little.
You like a mix of safe plans and the occasional wild weekend.
You’re steady enough to trust and bold enough to keep things alive.
strengths: You know which risks are worth taking, which is a rare skill.
weaknesses: You can talk yourself out of a good leap by calculating for too long.
realLife: On a first date: Something a little different, like a climbing wall, with a known café as backup.
In a fight: You weigh both sides and look for the fair middle.
tips: When the odds are good and your heart says yes, stop calculating. You’ve already done the maths.
match: Best with: Someone who’s bold in some ways and careful in others.
Green flag: They take your caution and your courage equally seriously.
Careful with: Someone who’s reckless with your money or your heart.

Low.label: The Fine-Print Reader
summaries: You’ll jump. After you’ve checked how deep the water is.

You’re not scared of change, you just like to read the fine print first. You take risks when the numbers make sense and the plan is solid. People call you before every big decision, because you ask the questions they forgot.
behaviors: You move at a steady pace and like knowing where things are going.
You’ll take a chance on someone once you’ve seen they’re consistent.
You’re the one who plans the trip and checks the weather twice.
strengths: Your decisions age well.
weaknesses: Too much checking can kill the thrill of a good, spontaneous yes.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve read the reviews and checked the parking, and you still enjoy every minute.
In a fight: You want facts before feelings. Let their feelings count as facts too.
tips: Next time your gut says yes, give yourself a day, not a month. Some chances don’t wait for the fine print.
match: Best with: Someone a little bolder than you who respects your homework.
Green flag: They explain their big ideas instead of rushing you into them.
Careful with: Someone who makes big decisions for both of you without asking.

VeryLow.label: The Power-Bank Person
summaries: Prepared for everything, surprised by nothing.

You think three steps ahead, and you’ve probably got a backup plan for the backup plan. You don’t gamble with your money, your time or your heart, and that’s exactly why you rarely crash. People feel safe around you because you’ve thought of what they forgot.
behaviors: You take your time before you open up, and once you do, you’re all in.
You want to know where things are going before you invest your heart.
Surprises are lovely to you, as long as someone warned you about them first.
strengths: You avoid disasters before anyone else even sees them coming.
weaknesses: Waiting until you’re completely sure can mean the moment passes.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve checked their profile twice, picked a busy café, and told someone where you’ll be.
In a fight: You want to think before you speak. Ask for an evening instead of going silent.
tips: Pick one small risk a month: say the thing, book the trip, send the text. Most worst cases never happen.
match: Best with: Someone steady and honest who never makes you guess where you stand.
Green flag: They’re consistent: their words and their actions match.
Careful with: Someone who keeps telling you to “just live a little”, in that tone.

Undecided.label: The Calculated Leaper
summaries: Brave enough to jump, smart enough to check first.

You’re up for a risk when it makes sense and happy to play safe when it doesn’t. You’ll go paragliding, just not with the cheapest operator. You weigh things quickly, decide clearly and rarely regret it either way.
behaviors: You’ll make the first move, once you’ve read the signs a little.
You like a mix of safe plans and the occasional wild weekend.
You’re steady enough to trust and bold enough to keep things alive.
strengths: You know which risks are worth taking, which is a rare skill.
weaknesses: You can talk yourself out of a good leap by calculating for too long.
realLife: On a first date: Something a little different, like a climbing wall, with a known café as backup.
In a fight: You weigh both sides and look for the fair middle.
tips: When the odds are good and your heart says yes, stop calculating. You’ve already done the maths.
match: Best with: Someone who’s bold in some ways and careful in others.
Green flag: They take your caution and your courage equally seriously.
Careful with: Someone who’s reckless with your money or your heart.
