tests.measures: how much playful, light-hearted humor you bring to relationships

VeryHigh.label: The Resident Comedian
summaries: If the room’s too quiet, you take it personally.

You see the funny side of everything: weddings, traffic, even your own heartbreak. Making people laugh is how you love them, cheer them up and feel at home anywhere. The room gets brighter when you walk in, and everyone knows it.
behaviors: You’ll have them laughing so hard on the first date they forget to be nervous.
Your love comes in bits, nicknames and voice notes full of impressions.
Sometimes jokes are your armour, and only someone close gets past them.
strengths: You can make anyone laugh, anywhere, even on their worst day.
weaknesses: Joking about everything can hide what you really feel.
realLife: On a first date: You do impressions of the waiter, the weather and yourself, and they’re crying with laughter.
In a fight: You crack a joke in the first minute. Sometimes it helps, sometimes it makes things worse.
tips: Say one serious, true thing without a joke after it. Let it sit. It’ll mean more than a hundred funny lines.
match: Best with: Someone who’s a great audience and an even better heckler.
Green flag: They laugh at your jokes and still ask how you really are.
Careful with: Someone who only wants the funny you, never the real one.

High.label: The Meme Dealer
summaries: You have a meme for every situation, and you will send it.

Laughter is your favourite way to connect. You tease the people you like, send memes as love letters and find something funny in the worst Monday. You can be serious, you just think life is lighter with a joke in it.
behaviors: Your flirting is mostly teasing, with a compliment hidden inside.
You make up inside jokes within a week and use them for years.
You need someone who can laugh at themselves, and at you.
strengths: You turn strangers into pals and bad days into stories.
weaknesses: A joke at the wrong moment can make someone feel you’re not taking them seriously.
realLife: On a first date: You roast the menu, they roast you back, and you know it’s going well.
In a fight: You want to joke the tension away. Check they’re ready to laugh first.
tips: When they bring up something serious, put the jokes down for ten minutes. They’ll trust your laugh more after.
match: Best with: Someone who laughs easily and teases you right back.
Green flag: They send memes back, and they know when to stop joking.
Careful with: Someone who takes every tease as an insult.

Moderate.label: The Read-the-Room Type
summaries: Jokes at dinner, serious at 2 am. You know which is which.

You can trade banter with the best of them and switch to serious in a second when it matters. You read the room before you joke, which is why your jokes rarely land wrong. People enjoy you at a party and trust you in a crisis.
behaviors: You can tease them on Monday and hold their hand through bad news on Tuesday.
You know which topics are safe for jokes and which aren’t.
Your playful side grows as you feel safer with someone.
strengths: Timing: you know exactly when a laugh helps and when it hurts.
weaknesses: Reading the room all the time can stop you from just being silly.
realLife: On a first date: Easy laughs over starters, a real conversation by dessert.
In a fight: You stay serious until it’s sorted, then a small joke tells them you’re okay.
tips: Don’t wait for the room to feel safe before you play. Start the silliness sometimes, and let others follow.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys both banter and depth, and can switch with you.
Green flag: They laugh with you and also sit with you through the serious stuff.
Careful with: Someone who can only do one: all jokes or all heavy.

Low.label: The Dry Wit
summaries: One perfectly timed line a night. That’s all you need.

You’re mostly serious, and then you say one dry line that makes the whole table lose it. You don’t perform or chase laughs, you just notice what’s funny and say it quietly. People who get your jokes feel like they’re in on a secret.
behaviors: Your funny side shows up slowly, somewhere around the third date.
You like someone who catches your quiet jokes, not just the loud ones.
You can be playful, but you keep the big talks serious.
strengths: Your rare jokes land harder because nobody sees them coming.
weaknesses: Your straight face can leave new people unsure whether you’re joking.
realLife: On a first date: You’re calm and a bit reserved, then one line makes them choke on their coffee.
In a fight: You stay serious and steady. A small dry joke at the end can help you both reset.
tips: Let people see your funny side earlier. That joke you’re saving for the fifth date? Say it on the first.
match: Best with: Someone who catches your quiet jokes and doesn’t need constant entertainment.
Green flag: They laugh at your deadpan line a second after everyone else.
Careful with: Someone who uses jokes to dodge every real conversation.

VeryLow.label: The Old Soul
summaries: Small talk bores you. Real talk is where you shine.

You take life, people and words seriously, in the best way. You’d rather have one honest conversation than an evening of banter, and people trust you with things they’d never joke about. You do laugh, just not at everything, which makes your laugh worth earning.
behaviors: Your affection shows in deep questions and full attention.
Teasing can sting you more than people realise.
You fall for someone who’s serious about the things that matter.
strengths: People feel truly taken seriously around you.
weaknesses: A playful person can feel you’re judging their jokes, even when you’re just thinking.
realLife: On a first date: You skip the small talk and end up on family, fears and dreams.
In a fight: You want it taken seriously. Tell them a joke right now would feel dismissive.
tips: Let yourself be silly with one safe person. A shared laugh can say “I trust you” as loudly as a deep talk.
match: Best with: Someone thoughtful, or a gentle joker who knows when to stop.
Green flag: They can laugh, and they drop the jokes the moment you need it.
Careful with: Someone who laughs off every serious talk.

Undecided.label: The Read-the-Room Type
summaries: Jokes at dinner, serious at 2 am. You know which is which.

You can trade banter with the best of them and switch to serious in a second when it matters. You read the room before you joke, which is why your jokes rarely land wrong. People enjoy you at a party and trust you in a crisis.
behaviors: You can tease them on Monday and hold their hand through bad news on Tuesday.
You know which topics are safe for jokes and which aren’t.
Your playful side grows as you feel safer with someone.
strengths: Timing: you know exactly when a laugh helps and when it hurts.
weaknesses: Reading the room all the time can stop you from just being silly.
realLife: On a first date: Easy laughs over starters, a real conversation by dessert.
In a fight: You stay serious until it’s sorted, then a small joke tells them you’re okay.
tips: Don’t wait for the room to feel safe before you play. Start the silliness sometimes, and let others follow.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys both banter and depth, and can switch with you.
Green flag: They laugh with you and also sit with you through the serious stuff.
Careful with: Someone who can only do one: all jokes or all heavy.

tests.title: Warmth & Care
tests.subtitle: How you show affection
tests.description: Shows how naturally you express care, tenderness, and emotional warmth.
tests.whatYouLearn: How openly you show affection and how comfortable you are with emotional warmth.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps match people who prefer similar levels of affection and emotional reassurance.

questions.text: They’ve had a rough day and go quiet over dinner. You…

options.text: Give them space, but stay close by
Say “Bad day? Come here,” arms already open
Order their favourite dessert without a word
Act normal so they don’t feel watched

questions.text: You’ve started really liking someone. Can the people around you tell?

options.text: Not unless I tell them
Instantly. I’m smiling at my phone all day

questions.text: Saying “I miss you” first feels…

options.text: Like jumping off a cliff
Easy. If I feel it, I say it
Fine, once I know they feel it too
Awkward, so I send a song instead

questions.text: First time meeting their college gang. How does your affection show?

options.text: Proud looks and inside jokes, in full view
It doesn’t. That’s for when we’re alone
Small things: saving them a seat, refilling their glass
A smile across the table now and then

questions.text: Pet names like “baby” or “jaan”:

options.text: One, maybe, once things are serious
Cringe. Their real name is lovely
Only teasing ones, like “boss”
Love them. I’ll have three for you by week two

questions.text: A close friend is moving to another city. At the send-off you…

options.text: Help them pack. That’s my goodbye
Hug them too long and maybe cry a bit
Say “Will miss you, yaar,” and mean it
Crack jokes so nobody gets emotional

questions.text: People who meet you usually say you’re…

options.text: Warm from the first minute
Hard to read at first

questions.text: Three months in. How often do they hear how you feel?

options.text: They know. I don’t need to keep saying it
On special days, and when it hits me
All the time, in a hundred small ways
More through what I do than what I say

tests.measures: how naturally you show affection, care, and emotional warmth

VeryHigh.label: The Walking Sunshine
summaries: Your affection has no off switch and no disguise.

You greet people like you haven’t seen them in years, you hype them up and you remember their small wins. Love, for you, is meant to be seen and felt every day. Holding it in feels almost like lying, so you don’t.
behaviors: Everyone in your life knows when you like someone, often before they do.
Pet names, long hugs, good-morning texts: all of it from week one.
You turn ordinary days into small celebrations of them.
strengths: You make people feel like the best thing that happened to your day.
weaknesses: Someone reserved might feel flooded before they feel loved.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve laughed at all their jokes, told them they have a great smile and hugged them goodbye twice.
In a fight: You want to hug it out in five minutes. Give them the hour they need first.
tips: In the early weeks, let your warmth move at their speed. It isn’t too much; it just needs the right pace.
match: Best with: Someone who loves being loved out loud, or a quiet one who melts slowly.
Green flag: They’re affectionate back in their own way, even if it’s quieter.
Careful with: Someone who soaks up all your warmth but keeps their own locked away.

High.label: The Open Heart
summaries: You feel it, you show it, you mean it.
Affection comes out of you naturally: a hug, a “proud of you”, a check-in when you sense a bad day. You believe love should be felt, not guessed. People open up around you because you go first.
behaviors: You say “I miss you” first and never keep score.
A bad day for them means a call from you, then their favourite snack at the door.
You love telling them what you like about them, out of nowhere.
strengths: Nobody near you ever wonders whether they’re cared for.
weaknesses: When your warmth isn’t returned the same way, you can take it personally.
realLife: On a first date: You compliment their laugh, ask about their family and hug goodbye without thinking twice.
In a fight: You want to fix it with a hug and a talk, ideally on the same night.
tips: Learn how they show love too. A quiet person’s cup of chai can be their “I love you”.
match: Best with: Someone who receives warmth easily and gives it back in their own style.
Green flag: They light up when you’re affectionate instead of going stiff.
Careful with: Someone who enjoys your warmth but never gives any back.

Moderate.label: The Steady Glow
summaries: Warm, easy, and turned up when it matters.
You’re affectionate without making a show of it. You read the room: soft when someone needs it, light when they don’t. People feel comfortable around you because your warmth is steady, not dramatic.
behaviors: You’ll hold their hand at the movies and keep it cool in front of their parents.
Your “I miss you” comes when you mean it, not on a schedule.
You notice when they’re off and ask, without turning it into a big talk.
strengths: Your warmth is easy to be around: never too little, never too much.
weaknesses: Very expressive people may want more from you, and you might not notice.
realLife: On a first date: Easy laughs, a warm goodbye, and a “that was fun, let’s do it again” text on your way home.
In a fight: You stay kind even when you’re upset, and you reach out first once you’ve cooled down.
tips: Every now and then, say the warm thing you’re thinking instead of saving it for later.
match: Best with: Someone who likes warmth that feels natural, not performed.
Green flag: They tell you what makes them feel cared for, so you don’t have to guess.
Careful with: Someone whose affection is loud in public and missing in private.

Low.label: The Secret Softie
summaries: Cool on the outside, pure mush for your chosen few.

To most people you seem calm and a little reserved. The few who get close see the softie: the one who saves their voice notes and checks if they’ve eaten. You let warmth out slowly, because you want it to land with the right person.
behaviors: You’re sweeter in private than anyone at your office would believe.
You crack a joke when a moment gets too emotional, then text something kind later.
Once you trust them, the pet names and the long hugs start appearing.
strengths: Your warmth feels special, because it’s clearly not for everyone.
weaknesses: In the early weeks, your calm face can look like low interest.
realLife: On a first date: Cool and a little quiet for an hour, then suddenly you’re telling them about your childhood dog.
In a fight: You crack a joke to cool things down. Follow it with the real thing: “That hurt me.”
tips: Let them see the softie a little earlier than feels safe. The right person won’t waste it.
match: Best with: Someone warm and steady who gives you time to open up.
Green flag: They make you laugh until your guard drops on its own.
Careful with: Someone who teases you for being soft once you finally are.

VeryLow.label: The Locked Locket
summaries: Deep feelings, kept close, shown in quiet ways.

You feel a lot more than you show. Affection lives inside you like something precious, and you open it for very few people. Somewhere along the way you learnt that loyalty and turning up say more than big words, and you still believe it.
behaviors: You remember exactly how they take their chai, but “I miss you” takes you weeks.
Your love shows in loyalty: you turn up, you stay, you don’t switch off.
Someone has to read your small signs, and the right person will love decoding them.
strengths: Your rare sweet words land like gold, because nobody ever doubts them.
weaknesses: Someone who needs warmth out loud may feel alone, even while you care deeply.
realLife: On a first date: You listen more than you talk, and the next day you text “Had a good time.” From you, that’s a lot.
In a fight: You go still and polite. Try one honest line instead: “I’m upset, give me an hour.”
tips: Pick one small way to say it out loud each week. A “glad you’re here” costs you nothing and means everything to them.
match: Best with: Someone patient who reads small signs and doesn’t need constant words.
Green flag: They notice your quiet gestures and thank you for them.
Careful with: Someone who calls you cold in week one without trying to know you.

Undecided.label: The Steady Glow
summaries: Warm, easy, and turned up when it matters.
You’re affectionate without making a show of it. You read the room: soft when someone needs it, light when they don’t. People feel comfortable around you because your warmth is steady, not dramatic.
behaviors: You’ll hold their hand at the movies and keep it cool in front of their parents.
Your “I miss you” comes when you mean it, not on a schedule.
You notice when they’re off and ask, without turning it into a big talk.
strengths: Your warmth is easy to be around: never too little, never too much.
weaknesses: Very expressive people may want more from you, and you might not notice.
realLife: On a first date: Easy laughs, a warm goodbye, and a “that was fun, let’s do it again” text on your way home.
In a fight: You stay kind even when you’re upset, and you reach out first once you’ve cooled down.
tips: Every now and then, say the warm thing you’re thinking instead of saving it for later.
match: Best with: Someone who likes warmth that feels natural, not performed.
Green flag: They tell you what makes them feel cared for, so you don’t have to guess.
Careful with: Someone whose affection is loud in public and missing in private.

tests.title: Quality Time
tests.subtitle: Presence, attention, shared moments
tests.description: Measures how much being fully present matters to you (time together, attention, shared activities).
tests.whatYouLearn: Whether attention and presence is your main love-language.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps avoid mismatch where one wants time together and the other prefers independence.

questions.text: You’re telling them a story and they say “hmm” while scrolling. You…

options.text: Finish it anyway. They’re half listening
Laugh: “Phone down, this is the good part”
Don’t mind. I scroll while I talk too
Save the story for when they’re free

questions.text: A free weekend together. You’d pick…

options.text: A day out together, then a lazy day apart
A little trip, only us two
Whatever comes up, with whoever’s around
Lazy days at home, just the two of us

questions.text: They’re swamped at work for two weeks and can barely meet. You…

options.text: Enjoy the extra me-time, honestly
Drop by with dinner, even for twenty minutes
Ask for one proper evening, no matter what
Get it. We’ll make up for it later

questions.text: Which date would you still talk about years later?

options.text: The time they surprised me with the perfect gift
A gig where we danced and barely spoke
A long walk where we talked till the shops shut
A cooking disaster at home that we laughed through

questions.text: They take a six-month project in another city. What keeps you close?

options.text: A video call every night, even a sleepy one
Knowing we’re solid. Distance doesn’t worry me
A few long calls a week
Texts through the week, a visit every month

questions.text: A fixed weekly date night sounds…

options.text: Like homework. We see each other enough
Nice, but not every single week
Perfect. Phones in a bowl, just us

questions.text: At a big family wedding together, you’d rather…

options.text: Split up, mingle, find each other at dinner
Stay side by side all night

questions.text: After a long, bad day, what do you want from them?

options.text: A call on the way home, a proper one
Just sit with me. No phones, full attention
Some alone time first, then maybe a chat
A plan for us this weekend to look forward to

tests.measures: how much focused, shared time matters to your feeling of love

VeryHigh.label: The Present Tense
summaries: Time together is how you know you’re loved.

Gifts and grand words are nice, but nothing reaches you like someone choosing to spend their time on you. You remember conversations word for word and walks street by street. You live for the moments when the world goes quiet and it’s just the two of you.
behaviors: You’d take a whole lazy day together over an expensive dinner.
You remember exact conversations from your first month.
Cancelled plans hurt you more than you usually admit.
strengths: You make people feel chosen, every single time you’re together.
weaknesses: When life gets busy for them, you can feel forgotten even when you’re not.
realLife: On a first date: Coffee becomes dinner becomes a walk, and you both notice the café shut an hour ago.
In a fight: You want to talk it through tonight, together, not leave it for tomorrow.
tips: When they’re busy, ask for one small fixed thing, like a ten-minute call each night. It keeps you close without asking for the world.
match: Best with: Someone who loves long evenings, slow walks and phones on silent.
Green flag: They make time for you in busy weeks, not only in free ones.
Careful with: Someone who keeps cancelling with a sweet text instead of a new plan.

High.label: The Phones-Down Type
summaries: Your attention is your love, and you want theirs.
For you, love lives in attention: eye contact, a real conversation, a walk with no agenda. You give your full presence and you notice when it isn’t returned. Busy is fine; distracted is not.
behaviors: You notice the third time they check their phone at dinner.
A long evening of talking feels better to you than any gift.
You plan dates that leave room to actually talk.
strengths: When you’re with someone, they feel like the only person in the room.
weaknesses: A busy week on their side can feel like a step back to you.
realLife: On a first date: A café with good chairs and no loud music, so you can talk for three hours.
In a fight: You want to sit face to face, not argue over text.
tips: Ask for time out loud, like “can Thursday be just ours?”, instead of feeling hurt when it doesn’t happen.
match: Best with: Someone who loves long conversations and protects time together.
Green flag: They put their phone face down without being asked.
Careful with: Someone who is always “just replying to one message”.

Moderate.label: The Good Company
summaries: Time together is a joy, not a requirement.

You enjoy shared time, and you’re easy company whether it’s a long date or an errand run. You don’t count hours and you don’t need every evening. When you’re together you’re actually there, and when you’re apart you’re fine.
behaviors: Grocery shopping with them can be as fun as a fancy dinner.
You’re happy with a mix: some planned dates, some lazy evenings, some days apart.
You put your phone away when it matters, without making a rule of it.
strengths: You make ordinary time together feel easy and light.
weaknesses: Someone who needs a lot of time might wish you asked for more of it.
realLife: On a first date: An easy walk that turns into dinner, because neither of you wanted it to end.
In a fight: You’d rather sit down together and talk it out than fight over text.
tips: Ask for the time you want, now and then. Being easygoing doesn’t mean you can’t have wishes.
match: Best with: Someone relaxed about time who enjoys simple plans.
Green flag: They’re present when you’re together and secure when you’re not.
Careful with: Someone who is always there in person and somewhere else in their head.

Low.label: The Sunday Special
summaries: Busy all week, all theirs on the weekend.

Your weekdays belong to work, the gym, your people and your own plans. Time together matters to you, but it fits into a rhythm: a good Sunday, a long call on Wednesday. You’d rather have a few great hours than many half-present ones.
behaviors: Your weekdays are packed, but Sunday brunch with them is sacred.
You’re happy with a few good meets a week rather than daily plans.
When you’re together it’s good time, and you also like going home.
strengths: You keep a full life and still show up for the hours that count.
weaknesses: Your rhythm can feel like a timetable to someone who wants spontaneous time.
realLife: On a first date: Saturday afternoon, planned a week ahead, and you’re fully there for it.
In a fight: You’d rather sort it properly on the weekend than in rushed weekday texts.
tips: Throw in one unplanned weekday evening now and then. Surprise time feels extra special.
match: Best with: Someone who also has a busy week and loves a good weekend.
Green flag: They respect your routine and make the weekends fun.
Careful with: Someone who wants you to drop every plan for theirs.

VeryLow.label: The Cutting Chai
summaries: Love in small, strong doses, and that’s plenty.

Like a cutting chai, you don’t need a full cup to feel it. A ten-minute call, a quick meet, a meme at lunch: that’s enough to keep you close. You have a full life of your own, and you love people best when nobody is counting hours.
behaviors: You don’t need to meet every weekend to feel sure of someone.
A fifteen-minute chai break with them can make your whole week.
You stay steady through long work phases and busy seasons.
strengths: Busy weeks and long distances don’t shake you.
weaknesses: Someone who feels loved through time may read your full calendar as low interest.
realLife: On a first date: A one-hour coffee that you end on time, happily, with a plan for the next one.
In a fight: You’re fine to pause and talk it over next week. Check that they are too.
tips: Now and then, give them one proper, phone-free evening on purpose. To some people, that says more than anything.
match: Best with: Someone with a busy, happy life of their own.
Green flag: They make the time they do have count, without guilt-tripping you about the rest.
Careful with: Someone who tracks how many evenings you spent with them this month.

Undecided.label: The Good Company
summaries: Time together is a joy, not a requirement.

You enjoy shared time, and you’re easy company whether it’s a long date or an errand run. You don’t count hours and you don’t need every evening. When you’re together you’re actually there, and when you’re apart you’re fine.
behaviors: Grocery shopping with them can be as fun as a fancy dinner.
You’re happy with a mix: some planned dates, some lazy evenings, some days apart.
You put your phone away when it matters, without making a rule of it.
strengths: You make ordinary time together feel easy and light.
weaknesses: Someone who needs a lot of time might wish you asked for more of it.
realLife: On a first date: An easy walk that turns into dinner, because neither of you wanted it to end.
In a fight: You’d rather sit down together and talk it out than fight over text.
tips: Ask for the time you want, now and then. Being easygoing doesn’t mean you can’t have wishes.
match: Best with: Someone relaxed about time who enjoys simple plans.
Green flag: They’re present when you’re together and secure when you’re not.
Careful with: Someone who is always there in person and somewhere else in their head.

tests.title: Physical Touch
tests.subtitle: Closeness through touch
tests.description: Shows how important hugs, touch, and physical closeness are for your feeling of love.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your need for physical affection and comfort.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps match people with similar physical closeness needs.

options.text: Smile and see if they take it
Keep walking. I’m not a hand-holder
Take it. Obviously

questions.text: Meeting the person you’re seeing, a month in. Hello is…

options.text: A smile and a “hi”, that’s plenty
A hug, every single time

questions.text: Bad day. What helps you most?

options.text: Talking it out over chai
A long hug, no words needed
Being left alone for a while
Someone sitting close, a hand on my back

questions.text: Movie night on the sofa. Where are you?

options.text: My own corner, my own blanket
Close, shoulders touching
Under one blanket, curled up together
Legs across their lap, both on our phones

questions.text: They’re a hugger. Every hello, every bye, sometimes in between. You…

options.text: Finally, someone who gets it
Need a breather now and then
Would ask them to tone it down
Love it, just not during my work calls

options.text: Their favourite meal, made by me
A high five and a silly dance
A tight hug or a squeeze of the hand
A look across the room

options.text: Dozing on their shoulder on a long bus ride
Long, honest talks
Hugs and holding hands

options.text: Like it for a minute, then it’s too much
Melt. Please never stop
Gently move away. It distracts me
Enjoy it, if we’re alone

tests.measures: how important physical closeness and touch are for your feeling of love

VeryHigh.label: The Koala
summaries: Cuddly, cosy, and always within arm’s reach.

For you, closeness is something you need to feel, not just know. Hugs, a head on a shoulder, a hand in yours: they settle you like nothing else. You love with your whole self, and touch is how it shows.
behaviors: Movie night means one blanket and zero personal space.
You hug hello, hug goodbye, and sometimes hug for no reason in between.
A long day without a single hug leaves you feeling a little homesick.
strengths: You make people feel safe and wanted with one hug.
weaknesses: When someone needs space, it can feel like rejection to you.
realLife: On a first date: You hugged hello, sat close, and had to stop yourself from holding their hand by the second chai.
In a fight: You want a hug before the talk is even over. Let the talk finish; the hug will mean more.
tips: When they pull back, ask instead of guessing. Needing space is often just a mood, not a message about you.
match: Best with: A fellow hugger who finds your hugs as calming as you find theirs.
Green flag: They pull you in for a hug before you even ask.
Careful with: Someone who gives affection as a reward and holds it back as a punishment.

High.label: The Hand-Holder
summaries: Fingers laced, wherever you go.

Touch is how you feel close: holding hands, an arm around the shoulder, a hug that lasts a second longer. You feel calmer when your person is within reach. A day without a single hug feels a little off to you.
behaviors: You reach for their hand in the auto, at the mall, in the queue.
A hug is your fix for most bad days, theirs and yours.
You sit on the same side of the table whenever you can.
strengths: Your touch calms people faster than any pep talk.
weaknesses: Someone who needs space may feel crowded before they say so.
realLife: On a first date: You noticed exactly when their hand was close enough to hold, and waited for the right moment.
In a fight: You want to make up with a hug. Ask first; they might need a minute.
tips: Ask early how they feel about touch. Moving at the same pace makes every hug feel welcome.
match: Best with: Someone who loves affection and isn’t shy about giving it.
Green flag: They reach for your hand first, sometimes.
Careful with: Someone who goes cold and distant as a way to punish you.

Moderate.label: The Shoulder Leaner
summaries: Easy closeness, when the moment is right.

You enjoy touch without needing it every minute. A lean on the shoulder during a film, a hand held on a long walk, a hug when they get home: it comes naturally when you’re relaxed. Busy or in public, you’re just as happy with a smile.
behaviors: You lean on them during movies without even thinking about it.
You hold hands on evening walks, then let go to point at a street dog.
You enjoy cosy Sundays on the sofa and space on busy weekdays.
strengths: You’re easy to be close to: warm, relaxed, never clingy.
weaknesses: A very touchy person might want more than you think to give.
realLife: On a first date: A hug hello that’s a little awkward, and a much better one at goodbye.
In a fight: You need to talk first, then a hug seals it.
tips: When you feel warm, let your hands show it. A touch on the arm can say “we’re fine” in one second.
match: Best with: Someone who likes affection that feels natural and unforced.
Green flag: They read your mood and know when a hug is welcome.
Careful with: Someone who uses a hug to skip talking about real problems.

Low.label: The Rare Hugger
summaries: Rare hugs, real hugs.

You’re not very touchy, but when you do hug someone, you mean it completely. You save touch for moments that matter: a goodbye at the airport, good news, a bad day. It feels more special to you when it isn’t constant.
behaviors: You hold hands on special walks, not on every walk.
A long hug from you after a hard day says more than any speech.
You warm up to touch as trust grows, slowly and surely.
strengths: Your hugs feel like an event, because they are.
weaknesses: A touch-loving person may feel you holding back in the early days.
realLife: On a first date: A warm smile hello, a quick hug goodbye, and you think about that hug later.
In a fight: You’d rather talk it out first. A hug feels right only once things are settled.
tips: Offer one small touch more than feels natural: a hand on the arm, a hug hello. Small things say a lot.
match: Best with: Someone affectionate but patient, who lets you set the pace.
Green flag: They notice when you reach out and make it feel safe.
Careful with: Someone who jokes about you being stiff instead of giving you time.

VeryLow.label: The Personal Bubble
summaries: Close at heart, with plenty of elbow room.

You love people in many ways, and touch just isn’t the main one. You feel close through talks, jokes, plans and loyalty, and you like your personal space intact. It isn’t coldness; you simply feel most like yourself with room to breathe.
behaviors: You’d rather sit across the table than squeeze in on the same side.
A hug is lovely now and then, and you like to choose the moment.
You show affection through a well-timed text, a plan, a favourite snack.
strengths: Your affection never feels pushy, so people relax around you.
weaknesses: Someone who feels love through touch may read your space as distance.
realLife: On a first date: A friendly wave hello, great conversation, and no awkward goodbye hug.
In a fight: You need distance to calm down. Say “I need ten minutes” so it doesn’t feel like a rejection.
tips: Tell them what does make you feel close. Pointing to the yes is kinder than only saying no.
match: Best with: Someone who shows love through words, time or effort more than hugs.
Green flag: They ask before they hug, and don’t sulk if the answer is “later”.
Careful with: Someone who keeps pushing for closeness after you’ve asked for space.

Undecided.label: The Shoulder Leaner
summaries: Easy closeness, when the moment is right.

You enjoy touch without needing it every minute. A lean on the shoulder during a film, a hand held on a long walk, a hug when they get home: it comes naturally when you’re relaxed. Busy or in public, you’re just as happy with a smile.
behaviors: You lean on them during movies without even thinking about it.
You hold hands on evening walks, then let go to point at a street dog.
You enjoy cosy Sundays on the sofa and space on busy weekdays.
strengths: You’re easy to be close to: warm, relaxed, never clingy.
weaknesses: A very touchy person might want more than you think to give.
realLife: On a first date: A hug hello that’s a little awkward, and a much better one at goodbye.
In a fight: You need to talk first, then a hug seals it.
tips: When you feel warm, let your hands show it. A touch on the arm can say “we’re fine” in one second.
match: Best with: Someone who likes affection that feels natural and unforced.
Green flag: They read your mood and know when a hug is welcome.
Careful with: Someone who uses a hug to skip talking about real problems.

tests.title: Words of Affirmation
tests.subtitle: Love through words and praise
tests.description: Measures how much loving words, compliments, and verbal reassurance matter to you.
tests.whatYouLearn: How important words are for your emotional security.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Pairs better when both value words similarly (or can learn each other’s language).

questions.text: You nailed a big presentation at work. What would mean most from them?

options.text: Dinner out to celebrate, no speech needed
A long message on how proud they are
My favourite lunch, delivered to my desk
“So proud of you,” said over dinner, eye to eye

questions.text: Which one stays with you longer?

options.text: Something kind they once did
Something sweet they once said

questions.text: A year in, they still say “I love you” every night. You think…

options.text: Never too much. Say it again
It means more when it’s rare
Sweet, as long as they show it too
Lovely, though I’m more of a “me too” person

questions.text: You feel low about how you look before a cousin’s wedding. What helps?

options.text: One honest compliment, said once
Them helping me fix my outfit and hair
Them saying “you look stunning” till I believe it

questions.text: Your sister lands a new job. Your message in the family group:

options.text: A whole paragraph and five emojis
Nothing there. I’ll take her out for dinner
“Congrats! 🎉” and a call later
A 👍 there, a big hug at home

questions.text: After a fight, what makes it feel truly over?

options.text: A long talk about what happened
Them making me chai the next morning
Hearing a real “I’m sorry, I was wrong”

questions.text: Their texts are dry, but they always show up when it counts. You…

options.text: Fine. I can read love between the dry lines
Would miss the words. I need to hear it too
Am happy. Showing up is the message
Love it, but I’d want a sweet line now and then

questions.text: They write you a handwritten letter. You…

options.text: Smile, then wonder where to keep it
Love it and tell them straight away
Find it sweet, if a little filmy
Keep it forever and reread it on bad days

tests.measures: how much verbal reassurance and kind words affect your emotional security

VeryHigh.label: The Screenshot Keeper
summaries: You keep every sweet message, and you reread them.

Kind words reach you somewhere deep, and you never forget them. You save sweet messages, remember compliments from years ago and write the kind of birthday notes people keep. For you, love that isn’t said can feel like love that isn’t there.
behaviors: You have a folder of screenshots that nobody else will ever see.
Hearing “I love you” never gets old for you.
Your birthday messages are paragraphs, and you quietly hope theirs are too.
strengths: Your words make people feel truly seen.
weaknesses: A quiet day without kind words can feel like a cold day to you.
realLife: On a first date: You told them three things you liked about them, and screenshotted their “reached home, had fun” text.
In a fight: You remember the exact words said in a fight. Ask for the kind ones you need afterwards.
tips: Ask for words directly: “tell me one thing you like about us.” It isn’t too much to ask; it’s just clear.
match: Best with: Someone who says what they feel, out loud and often.
Green flag: They tell you why they like you, not just that they do.
Careful with: Someone whose words turn careless or cruel when they’re upset.

High.label: The Hype Person
summaries: Your words lift people, and theirs lift you.

You’re the one who says “you’re brilliant” before the interview and “I’m proud of you” after it. Words matter to you both ways: you give them freely and you feel them deeply. One kind line from the right person can change your whole day.
behaviors: You tell them what you love about them, often and specifically.
A sweet good-morning message sets your whole day right.
A careless word from them can sting more than you show.
strengths: People feel braver after talking to you.
weaknesses: If someone shows love quietly, you might miss it while waiting for the words.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve told them their laugh is great and that their dadi story is the best thing you’ve heard all week.
In a fight: Words cut you deep, so you need a clear sorry, not just a hug.
tips: Tell them, early and kindly, that words matter to you. Most people give them happily once they know.
match: Best with: Someone expressive who likes saying what they feel.
Green flag: They notice your effort and tell you so.
Careful with: Someone who uses sharp words when angry and calls it honesty.

Moderate.label: The Well-Timed Word
summaries: Kind words when they count, actions the rest of the time.

You like both: a sweet message and a person who shows up. You say kind things when they matter, like before an interview or after a bad day, and you enjoy hearing them too. Neither words nor actions alone convince you; together, they do.
behaviors: You send a “you’ve got this” right before their big meeting.
You like hearing “I’m proud of you”, but you don’t need it daily.
You notice when words and actions don’t line up, and it bothers you.
strengths: Your words arrive exactly when someone needs them.
weaknesses: Someone who needs daily reassurance may want more than your well-timed lines.
realLife: On a first date: You compliment one thing you actually noticed, and keep the rest for date two.
In a fight: You say sorry clearly, then show it by changing something.
tips: Add a few ordinary-day compliments. Kind words feel just as good on a random Tuesday.
match: Best with: Someone whose words and actions say the same thing.
Green flag: They tell you what they love about you, and their actions back it up.
Careful with: Sweet texts that disappear the moment things get hard.

Low.label: The Rare Compliment
summaries: Few words, and every one of them meant.

You’re not a gusher. You say kind things rarely and only when they’re true, so they land hard. You’d rather show love through effort, but you’ve learnt that the right line at the right time can mean the world.
behaviors: Your once-a-month “you look good” gets screenshotted.
You’d rather say it in person than in a long paragraph.
You trust their actions more than their words, and that mostly works for you.
strengths: When you praise someone, they know it’s real.
weaknesses: Your silence on good days can feel like nothing to someone who needs words.
realLife: On a first date: You give one compliment, carefully chosen, and they think about it all the way home.
In a fight: You go quiet and fix things with actions. Add one line: “I’m sorry, this matters to me.”
tips: When you think something nice about them, say it. A true sentence doesn’t need perfect timing.
match: Best with: Someone who values quality over quantity in what you say.
Green flag: They mean what they say, even when they say little.
Careful with: Someone who showers you with compliments and never follows through.

VeryLow.label: The Show-Don’t-Tell
summaries: Your love comes with receipts, not speeches.

You trust what people do far more than what they say, and you love the same way. Sweet words come cheap to you; turning up at 6 am with a spare charger is the real thing. You’ve probably heard “say it sometimes” more than once.
behaviors: You’ll fix their geyser long before you’ll say “I adore you”.
Compliments make you squirm a little, giving them and getting them.
You judge love by who turns up, not by who types the most.
strengths: Your love is solid proof, never empty talk.
weaknesses: Someone who needs to hear it can feel unloved while you’re busy showing it.
realLife: On a first date: You arrive early, pick a good table and walk them to their auto. Compliments: one, maybe.
In a fight: You want to fix the problem, not talk feelings for an hour. Say one sentence about how you feel first.
tips: Say one kind thing out loud every day, even if it feels unnecessary. To some people, words are the proof.
match: Best with: Someone who reads actions as fluently as you do.
Green flag: They keep small promises without needing reminders.
Careful with: Lovely words that never turn into plans.

Undecided.label: The Well-Timed Word
summaries: Kind words when they count, actions the rest of the time.

You like both: a sweet message and a person who shows up. You say kind things when they matter, like before an interview or after a bad day, and you enjoy hearing them too. Neither words nor actions alone convince you; together, they do.
behaviors: You send a “you’ve got this” right before their big meeting.
You like hearing “I’m proud of you”, but you don’t need it daily.
You notice when words and actions don’t line up, and it bothers you.
strengths: Your words arrive exactly when someone needs them.
weaknesses: Someone who needs daily reassurance may want more than your well-timed lines.
realLife: On a first date: You compliment one thing you actually noticed, and keep the rest for date two.
In a fight: You say sorry clearly, then show it by changing something.
tips: Add a few ordinary-day compliments. Kind words feel just as good on a random Tuesday.
match: Best with: Someone whose words and actions say the same thing.
Green flag: They tell you what they love about you, and their actions back it up.
Careful with: Sweet texts that disappear the moment things get hard.

tests.title: Acts of Service
tests.subtitle: Love through actions and help
tests.description: Shows whether doing helpful things is how you give/feel love (support, effort, reliability).
tests.whatYouLearn: How strongly you value practical support and effort.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Matching improves when both value effort similarly (otherwise one feels unappreciated).

questions.text: You come home exhausted. The flat is clean and dinner is waiting. You feel…

options.text: Grateful. A lovely bonus
Happy, but what I wanted was a hug
Loved. Nothing says it better
Spoilt, in the best way

questions.text: They’re down with fever. You…

options.text: Text “get well soon” and let them rest
Order medicines to their door and check in
Turn up with soup, medicines and a charger
Call and keep them company for a bit

questions.text: Your idea of a romantic gesture:

options.text: They plan a surprise evening out
They refill my water bottle before I notice

questions.text: Their flight lands at 5 am. You…

options.text: Am at arrivals, half asleep, with chai
Text “landed?” when I wake up
Book their cab and track it till they’re home

questions.text: They promised to book the movie tickets and forgot. Again. You…

options.text: Shrug. It’s just tickets
Book them myself, a little annoyed
Feel hurt. Small promises are big to me

questions.text: You’re shifting flats this Saturday. What would you love from them?

options.text: Pizza and company once the boxes are in
Taking the day off to carry boxes with me
Nothing. Moving is my thing to handle
Coming over after work to help unpack

questions.text: When words feel hard, how do you show you care?

options.text: I make time, even just to sit with them
I say it anyway, awkwardly
A bit of both: a hug and a small favour
I do something: cook, fix, carry, sort

questions.text: They notice your bike making a weird noise and quietly get it serviced. You…

options.text: Wish they’d asked me first
Melt. That’s the most romantic thing ever
Feel cared for, and a bit embarrassed

tests.measures: how much practical help and effort matter to your feeling of being loved

VeryHigh.label: The Airport Pickup
summaries: 5 am flight? You’re already at arrivals.

For you, love is a verb with an alarm clock. You show it by turning up: the 5 am pickup, the medicine run, the form filled in on time. And nothing makes you feel more loved than someone who does the same without being asked.
behaviors: You remember their errands better than your own.
Someone taking a chore off your plate feels like flowers to you.
A forgotten promise, even a tiny one, stays with you for days.
strengths: You make people feel completely looked after.
weaknesses: You might keep giving until you’re drained, quietly hoping they notice.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve already checked the parking, the menu and the route home for them.
In a fight: Unkept promises are what hurt you most. Say that clearly, not just “it’s fine”.
tips: Tell them how you feel loved, in plain words: “when you help without me asking, I feel so cared for.” Nobody can guess it.
match: Best with: Someone who shows love by doing, as naturally as you do.
Green flag: They notice what needs doing and just do it.
Careful with: Someone who takes your effort for granted and never offers any back.

High.label: The Quiet Fixer
summaries: You say it with a full fridge and a fixed tap.
When you love someone, your hands get busy. You fix, carry, cook, sort and remember. Words feel thin to you next to effort, and the person who shows up for the boring stuff wins your heart.
behaviors: You’ve set up their new phone, booked their doctor and found their lost charger.
When they do something for you without being asked, it means a lot.
Broken promises hurt you more than forgotten compliments.
strengths: Life gets easier for anyone you love.
weaknesses: You might fix someone’s problem when they only wanted to be heard.
realLife: On a first date: You arrive early, check their route home and make sure they got back safe.
In a fight: You try to fix the issue right away. Ask first: “Do you want help, or just a hug?”
tips: Let people help you too. Being cared for is part of love, not a debt.
match: Best with: Someone reliable who keeps their small promises.
Green flag: They do what they said they’d do, on time.
Careful with: Someone who says sweet things but never lifts a finger.

Moderate.label: The Fair Teammate
summaries: You share the load and notice who carries it.

For you, love includes the boring parts: groceries, bills, remembering to book the gas cylinder. You like a fair split and you notice effort, without keeping a strict score. Help is one of the ways you feel loved, not the only one.
behaviors: You’ll do the dishes if they cooked, without being asked.
You notice when they quietly handle something that was stressing you.
You like a relationship that runs like a good team.
strengths: You make shared life feel fair and easy.
weaknesses: Fairness can quietly turn into counting when you’re tired.
realLife: On a first date: You split the bill naturally, with no awkward dance about who pays.
In a fight: You want to sort out who’s doing what, calmly, like a plan.
tips: Ask for help before you’re tired and annoyed. “Can you take this one?” is easier than a fight later.
match: Best with: Someone who pulls their weight and says thanks.
Green flag: They step in when you’re swamped, without a speech about it.
Careful with: Someone who needs a reminder for everything, every time.

Low.label: The I’ve-Got-It Type
summaries: Thanks for offering. You’ve got this.

You’re capable and you know it, so help feels like a nice extra rather than a need. You’re the one who carries your own bags and fixes your own Wi-Fi. You appreciate effort, but you’d rather someone stood beside you than did it for you.
behaviors: Your first answer to “need help?” is “no, it’s fine”, even when it isn’t.
You notice their effort and it touches you, just quietly.
You help others easily; receiving help is the harder part.
strengths: You never make anyone feel like your rescuer or your helper on call.
weaknesses: To some people, turning down their help feels like turning down their love.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve brought your own umbrella, your own charger and a backup plan for getting home.
In a fight: You fix the problem alone, then wonder why they feel left out. Let them in on it.
tips: Say yes to one small offer of help this week. Letting someone in is a gift to them too.
match: Best with: Someone who respects your independence and offers rather than insists.
Green flag: They ask “want a hand?” and take “no” gracefully.
Careful with: Someone who helps in ways that make you feel small.

VeryLow.label: The Feelings-First Type
summaries: Love, for you, is felt, not done.

You’ve always handled your own errands, bills and bad days, and you like it that way. Love, for you, lives in talks, laughter and how someone makes you feel, not in who did the dishes. Help is kind; it just isn’t where your heart looks.
behaviors: A deep conversation beats a cleaned room for you, every time.
You don’t keep track of who did what around the house.
Unasked help can feel a little strange, like a fix you didn’t order.
strengths: You never turn love into a list of chores or a scoreboard.
weaknesses: Someone who shows love by doing things may feel unseen when you don’t notice.
realLife: On a first date: You forget to look at the menu because you’re deep in a talk about life.
In a fight: You want to talk about feelings, not about who forgot the groceries.
tips: Notice the small things they do for you and say thanks out loud. For some people, that’s how love speaks.
match: Best with: Someone who connects through talks, time and feelings.
Green flag: They ask what you need instead of assuming.
Careful with: Someone who does favours and then counts them later.

Undecided.label: The Fair Teammate
summaries: You share the load and notice who carries it.

For you, love includes the boring parts: groceries, bills, remembering to book the gas cylinder. You like a fair split and you notice effort, without keeping a strict score. Help is one of the ways you feel loved, not the only one.
behaviors: You’ll do the dishes if they cooked, without being asked.
You notice when they quietly handle something that was stressing you.
You like a relationship that runs like a good team.
strengths: You make shared life feel fair and easy.
weaknesses: Fairness can quietly turn into counting when you’re tired.
realLife: On a first date: You split the bill naturally, with no awkward dance about who pays.
In a fight: You want to sort out who’s doing what, calmly, like a plan.
tips: Ask for help before you’re tired and annoyed. “Can you take this one?” is easier than a fight later.
match: Best with: Someone who pulls their weight and says thanks.
Green flag: They step in when you’re swamped, without a speech about it.
Careful with: Someone who needs a reminder for everything, every time.

tests.title: Gift Giving
tests.subtitle: Thoughtfulness and symbols
tests.description: Measures how much symbolic gestures, thoughtful gifts, and surprises matter to you.
tests.whatYouLearn: Whether gifts/gestures make you feel seen.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps match people who share similar gesture expectations (so nobody feels ‘cheap’ or ‘wasteful’).

questions.text: Their birthday is in two weeks. You…

options.text: Will find something nice that week
Plan a great day. Gifts aren’t my thing
Started planning a month ago. There’s a list
Ask what they want and get exactly that

questions.text: They’re back from a work trip to Jaipur with a tiny keychain for you. You…

options.text: Put it on my keys that very day
Say thanks, and it goes in a drawer
Love it. They thought of me there
Find it cute and say a big thanks

questions.text: For your birthday, you’d rather get…

options.text: Something small they picked just for me
No gift. Just a really good day together

questions.text: Somewhere in your room, there’s…

options.text: A few special things, not much
A box of ticket stubs, cards and dried flowers
Nothing much. I’m not a keeper of stuff

questions.text: Diwali with someone new. What do you get them?

options.text: Nothing. We’ll light diyas together
A nice box of kaju katli
Something personal, wrapped, with a card
Kaju katli plus something personal

questions.text: They forget an anniversary gift but plan a lovely day. You…

options.text: Mind for a moment, then forget it
Feel a small sting. A token matters to me
Don’t notice. The day was the gift
Love the day, and tease them about the gift

questions.text: You see something perfect for them in a shop, no occasion. You…

options.text: Remember it for their birthday
Walk on. No occasion, no gift
Buy it. Reasons are overrated
Click a photo and send it to them

questions.text: Which gift would you remember longest?

options.text: A really good pair of headphones
A sketch of us they drew, however badly
Honestly, I don’t remember gifts much
Tickets to a show I’d mentioned once

tests.measures: how much thoughtful gifts and symbolic gestures mean to you

VeryHigh.label: The Memory Box
summaries: Every ticket stub, every card, kept forever.

Gifts are how love becomes something you can hold. You keep ticket stubs, dried flowers and birthday cards, and you give the kind of gifts that make people tear up. For you, a present is a small piece of someone’s attention, wrapped.
behaviors: You plan birthday gifts months ahead, with a running list in your notes.
A forgotten anniversary hurts more than you’ll easily admit.
Every fridge magnet they bring you gets a place of honour.
strengths: Your gifts show people exactly how well you know them.
weaknesses: You can read a missing gift as missing love, when it’s just a busy week.
realLife: On a first date: You wondered whether a gift on a first date was too much. You probably brought one anyway.
In a fight: A thoughtful little gift softens you, but you still need the real sorry.
tips: Tell them gifts matter to you, and that small and cheap is perfect. They can’t give what they don’t know you love.
match: Best with: Someone thoughtful who remembers the little details too.
Green flag: Their gifts, even tiny ones, show they listened.
Careful with: Someone who never notices your effort or the meaning behind it.

High.label: The Just-Because Giver
summaries: You saw it and thought of them. That’s enough.

You notice the little things people love and turn them into gifts: the book they mentioned, the snack from their hometown. To you, a present is proof of attention. You light up when someone does the same for you.
behaviors: You bring back a souvenir from every trip, even work trips.
A random gift on a Wednesday is your favourite kind.
You keep every card they’ve given you, somewhere safe.
strengths: You make people feel noticed in a way they can hold in their hands.
weaknesses: When gifts don’t come back, you might feel forgotten, even when you aren’t.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve brought a tiny something, a bar of their favourite chocolate, because they mentioned it once.
In a fight: You might turn up with their favourite sweets as a peace offering, plus a real sorry.
tips: Tell them it’s the thought you love, not the cost. It takes the pressure off and keeps the little gifts coming.
match: Best with: Someone who loves little surprises and gives them too.
Green flag: They remember what you said you liked and surprise you with it later.
Careful with: Someone who calls your gifts silly or a waste of money.

Moderate.label: The Occasion Keeper
summaries: Birthdays and anniversaries, always done right.

You never forget a special day, and you put real thought into it. Gifts matter to you on the days that matter, and you don’t need them in between. A thoughtful present on a birthday says everything; a random Tuesday can just be a Tuesday.
behaviors: Their birthday gift is chosen weeks in advance.
You love a surprise gift, but you don’t expect one every week.
You remember anniversaries, and quietly hope they do too.
strengths: Your special-day gifts are always on time and on point.
weaknesses: Gifts can turn into a calendar duty instead of a spontaneous joy.
realLife: On a first date: No gift needed, but you remember what they ordered, for next time.
In a fight: You don’t need a gift to make up, but a thoughtful gesture helps.
tips: Try one unplanned gift a year, just because. The surprise days are the ones people remember.
match: Best with: Someone who also celebrates the big days with care.
Green flag: They remember your important dates without reminders.
Careful with: Someone who forgets your birthday and makes it your fault for minding.

Low.label: The Wish-List Shopper
summaries: Tell me what you want. I’ll get exactly that.

Gifts are fine, but guessing feels like a gamble to you. You’d rather ask what someone needs and get it right than surprise them with something they’ll never use. Practical, honest and slightly allergic to clutter.
behaviors: You’ve asked “what do you want for your birthday?” three weeks early.
You love a useful gift: the good headphones, not the giant teddy bear.
You don’t keep cards or wrapping paper, and you hope that’s okay.
strengths: Your gifts get used every single day.
weaknesses: A gift they asked for can feel less personal to someone who loves surprises.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest the place with the best reviews and offer to split the bill.
In a fight: You don’t want a gift to fix it, just a straight conversation.
tips: Once in a while, skip the list and surprise them with something tiny that shows you listened.
match: Best with: Someone practical who enjoys useful, well-chosen gifts.
Green flag: They tell you what they’d like instead of making you guess.
Careful with: Someone who measures love by the price tag.

VeryLow.label: The Minimalist Heart
summaries: Moments over things, always.

You don’t need things to feel loved, and your room probably proves it. You’d rather have a good day, a long talk or a trip than anything wrapped in paper. Gifts make you a bit awkward, giving them and getting them.
behaviors: You’d swap any birthday present for a full day together.
You give experiences: a concert, a road trip, a pottery class.
Opening a gift in front of someone makes you a little shy.
strengths: Nobody ever has to impress you with money.
weaknesses: Someone who loves gifts may feel forgotten on special days.
realLife: On a first date: A long walk and street food, with no pressure to bring anything.
In a fight: A peace gift won’t move you. A real talk will, so ask for that.
tips: On their special days, give a small something anyway. It doesn’t need to be big, just chosen.
match: Best with: Someone who values experiences and memories over objects.
Green flag: They plan time together instead of trying to buy their way out of it.
Careful with: Someone who uses expensive gifts to skip apologies.

Undecided.label: The Occasion Keeper
summaries: Birthdays and anniversaries, always done right.

You never forget a special day, and you put real thought into it. Gifts matter to you on the days that matter, and you don’t need them in between. A thoughtful present on a birthday says everything; a random Tuesday can just be a Tuesday.
behaviors: Their birthday gift is chosen weeks in advance.
You love a surprise gift, but you don’t expect one every week.
You remember anniversaries, and quietly hope they do too.
strengths: Your special-day gifts are always on time and on point.
weaknesses: Gifts can turn into a calendar duty instead of a spontaneous joy.
realLife: On a first date: No gift needed, but you remember what they ordered, for next time.
In a fight: You don’t need a gift to make up, but a thoughtful gesture helps.
tips: Try one unplanned gift a year, just because. The surprise days are the ones people remember.
match: Best with: Someone who also celebrates the big days with care.
Green flag: They remember your important dates without reminders.
Careful with: Someone who forgets your birthday and makes it your fault for minding.

Change the subject, kindly

When their texts get shorter

tests.measures: how you support a partner during difficulty and stress

VeryHigh.label: The 2 am Person
summaries: The one everyone calls when it all falls apart.

When someone you love is hurting, you drop everything. You read moods before they’re spoken, you sit in hospital corridors, you stay up for the practice run. You give support with your whole heart, and it’s the most natural thing in the world to you.
behaviors: You’ve gone to a hospital at midnight for someone who didn’t even ask.
You remember the date of their big interview and call that morning.
Their bad day becomes your bad day, then your project.
strengths: With you around, nobody has to go through hard times alone.
weaknesses: You give so much that you forget to ask for anything back.
realLife: On a first date: They mention their mother has been unwell, and you’ve asked after her twice by the end of the evening.
In a fight: Even mid-fight, if they’re truly hurting, you stop and look after them first.
tips: Keep some of that care for yourself. You can’t be anyone’s 2 am person if you’re running on empty.
match: Best with: Someone who is as present for you as you are for them.
Green flag: They show up for you without being asked, even in small ways.
Careful with: Someone who only calls in a crisis and disappears when you have one.

High.label: The Steady Shoulder
summaries: You listen first, and you stay.

You’re the one people call when things go wrong, because you listen without judging and you stay until it’s better. You notice when someone’s off and check in gently. You care deeply, and it shows in how you turn up.
behaviors: You notice the shorter texts and ask, “Rough day?”
You listen to the whole story before you offer any advice.
You turn up with their favourite food when the week has been hard.
strengths: People feel safe falling apart in front of you.
weaknesses: You can hold their stress so closely that it becomes yours.
realLife: On a first date: They mention a rough week and you ask the questions nobody else thought to ask.
In a fight: You stay calm and try to understand them, even when you’re hurt yourself.
tips: Let someone hold you up for a change. Strong shoulders need rest too.
match: Best with: Someone who opens up and looks after you in return.
Green flag: They check in on you as often as you check in on them.
Careful with: Someone who leans on you every day and is never there when you need them.

Moderate.label: The Problem Solver
summaries: Feelings heard, then a plan on the table.

When someone you love is struggling, your brain goes straight to fixing it. You listen, you care, and then you want to do something useful: a plan, a call, a solution. You always show up, though sometimes with a spreadsheet when they wanted a shoulder.
behaviors: You’ve drafted a reply to their boss before they’ve finished the story.
You support them best when there’s something concrete to do.
You check in during hard weeks, though not always about feelings.
strengths: Problems get smaller when you’re around.
weaknesses: Sometimes they don’t want a fix, just someone to sit with them.
realLife: On a first date: They mention a work issue and you’ve shared three practical ideas before dessert.
In a fight: You jump to solutions. Pause and say “I get why you’re upset” first.
tips: Before you fix anything, ask: “Do you want advice or a hug?” Both are support, just different kinds.
match: Best with: Someone who loves a teammate in tough times and tells you what kind of help they want.
Green flag: They say “I just need to vent” or “help me fix this”, so you know which.
Careful with: Someone who brings the same problem every week and never wants to solve it.

Low.label: The Standby Hero
summaries: Not hovering, but always one call away.

You care, and you’re there if asked, but you don’t push your way into someone’s troubles. You think adults like to handle their own stuff, and you respect that. Emotional moments make you a little awkward, so you show up with practical help instead.
behaviors: You say “call me if you need anything” and mean every word.
You’re great in a crisis that needs doing, less sure in one that needs feeling.
You check in once, then wait for them to reach out.
strengths: In a real emergency you’re calm, quick and useful.
weaknesses: Waiting to be asked can look like not caring to someone who won’t ask.
realLife: On a first date: They mention a stressful week and you offer one good tip, then make them laugh.
In a fight: You’d rather solve it later than talk feelings now. Stay in the room a little longer than feels natural.
tips: Don’t wait for an invitation. A “thinking of you, want me to come over?” text is never too much.
match: Best with: Someone who says what they need and handles the rest.
Green flag: They ask for help directly, so you know exactly how to show up.
Careful with: Someone who tests you with silence to see if you’ll notice.

VeryLow.label: The Space Giver
summaries: You trust people to find their own feet.

You believe most people heal best with room to breathe, because that’s what works for you. You don’t crowd, you don’t pry, and you never make someone’s bad day about you. Big emotions can leave you unsure what to do, so you step back and wait.
behaviors: On a bad day you give them space, and assume they’ll ask if they need you.
You stay calm when things get emotional, sometimes calmer than they’d like.
When they do ask for help, you show up, no questions asked.
strengths: You never smother anyone, and you never make their bad day about you.
weaknesses: Your space can feel like absence to someone who needs company in hard times.
realLife: On a first date: When they mention a rough week, you listen politely, then steer things somewhere fun.
In a fight: You step away to cool off. Tell them you’re coming back, so it doesn’t feel like leaving.
tips: When they’re low, ask one simple question: “Do you want company or space?” Then do what they say.
match: Best with: Someone independent who handles their own storms and likes a calm place to come back to.
Green flag: They tell you clearly what they need instead of hoping you’ll guess.
Careful with: Someone who expects you to read their silence and holds it against you when you can’t.

Undecided.label: The Problem Solver

When someone you love is struggling, your brain goes straight to fixing it. You listen, you care, and then you want to do something useful: a plan, a call, a solution. You always show up, though sometimes with a spreadsheet when they wanted a shoulder.
behaviors: You’ve drafted a reply to their boss before they’ve finished the story.
You support them best when there’s something concrete to do.
You check in during hard weeks, though not always about feelings.
strengths: Problems get smaller when you’re around.
weaknesses: Sometimes they don’t want a fix, just someone to sit with them.

In a fight: You jump to solutions. Pause and say “I get why you’re upset” first.

Green flag: They say “I just need to vent” or “help me fix this”, so you know which.
Careful with: Someone who brings the same problem every week and never wants to solve it.

tests.measures: how much surprise, romance, and creative love expression matter to you

VeryHigh.label: The Hopeless Romantic
summaries: Rain dances, fairy lights, love like a story.

You believe love should feel like a story worth telling. You plan surprises on random Tuesdays, make playlists, notice sunsets, and you’d dance in the rain if the moment called for it. You don’t just want to be loved; you want to be swept away.
behaviors: You’ve planned a surprise date with clues hidden across the city.
Valentine’s Day, anniversaries, the day you first met: all celebrated.
Love without a spark feels to you like a film with the sound off.
strengths: You make ordinary life feel magical for the people you love.
weaknesses: Real life can feel flat next to the story in your head.
realLife: On a first date: You noticed the song playing when they walked in. You’ll remember it forever.
In a fight: You want a big, sincere make-up scene, ideally with flowers.
tips: Love the small, quiet moments too. Not every chapter needs fairy lights to be beautiful.
match: Best with: Someone who loves romance and gives as good as they get.
Green flag: They surprise you back, in their own way.
Careful with: Someone who calls romance “too much” and won’t meet you halfway.

High.label: The Playful Flirt
summaries: Teasing, laughing, and still flirting a year in.

For you, love should be fun. You tease, you flirt, you start flour fights and send terrible pickup lines just to get a reaction. Playfulness is how you keep closeness alive, and laughter is your favourite way to fall for someone.
behaviors: You still flirt with them like it’s the first month.
Inside jokes are your love letters.
You turn errands into games and boring evenings into silly challenges.
strengths: Nobody gets bored with you around.
weaknesses: You might joke when they actually need you to be serious.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve teased them about their order, challenged them to a game and made them laugh till they snorted.
In a fight: You try to break the tension with a joke. Wait for the right moment, or it can land badly.
tips: Know when to drop the jokes. Being serious once in a while makes your playful side even more fun.
match: Best with: Someone with a quick sense of humour who plays back.
Green flag: They laugh at your nonsense and add their own.
Careful with: Someone who calls your playfulness childish.

Moderate.label: The Weekend Romantic
summaries: Practical on weekdays, sweet when it counts.

You know when to bring the romance and when to just get on with life. Weekdays are for logistics; anniversaries, trips and slow Sundays are for candles and playlists. You enjoy both sides of love, and you switch between them easily.
behaviors: You plan a lovely birthday surprise, then go back to normal on Monday.
You flirt when life slows down, and don’t force it when it doesn’t.
You enjoy a cheesy moment, as long as it isn’t every moment.
strengths: You keep love both fun and functional.
weaknesses: Romance can slip down the list when work gets busy.
realLife: On a first date: A good restaurant you booked ahead, and a short walk after because the evening felt nice.
In a fight: You talk it through sensibly, then make up with a little gesture.
tips: Put one romantic thing in an ordinary week. The spark shouldn’t have to wait for occasions.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys a mix of fun and steady.
Green flag: They make an effort on special days and stay easy on normal ones.
Careful with: Someone who needs constant grand gestures to feel loved.

Low.label: The Low-Key Lover
summaries: Sweet in small doses, never over the top.

You’re not one for roses and big speeches, but you have your moments: a favourite snack picked up on the way, a private joke at dinner. Romance, for you, works best quiet and unplanned. Too much of it feels like a film you didn’t buy a ticket for.
behaviors: Your romance is subtle: a song shared, a hand squeezed, a look.
Valentine’s Day makes you a little shy, but you’ll still do something sweet.
You prefer cosy nights in to fancy dinners out.
strengths: Your sweetness feels real because it’s never overdone.
weaknesses: A big romantic might wish you’d go all out once in a while.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest your favourite little place and quietly hope they like it as much as you do.
In a fight: You make up with a shy gesture, like their favourite chai, and a quiet sorry.
tips: Go a little bigger once a year. You might enjoy being over the top more than you think.
match: Best with: Someone who loves quiet, cosy, everyday romance.
Green flag: They enjoy small gestures and don’t ask for big shows.
Careful with: Someone who measures love in roses and public posts.

VeryLow.label: The Grounded Heart
summaries: Romance? You prefer real life, done well.

You love in steady, practical ways: on time, honest, reliable. Grand gestures and cheesy lines feel a bit like a performance to you. For you, the most romantic thing is someone who is still there, still kind, on an ordinary Wednesday.
behaviors: Your idea of a surprise is fixing the thing they mentioned last week.
You’d rather skip Valentine’s and have a nice dinner on a quiet Thursday.
Your love feels safe, calm and very real.
strengths: No drama, no games: people always know where they stand with you.
weaknesses: Someone who loves romance may feel the spark is missing, even when the love is strong.
realLife: On a first date: A simple café, an honest conversation and a clear “I’d like to see you again.”
In a fight: You want to solve the problem, not make a scene. Keep it warm, not only logical.
tips: Plan one surprise a month, even a silly one. It costs little and reminds them there’s a spark.
match: Best with: Someone who finds steadiness romantic.
Green flag: They show love in daily ways instead of big shows.
Careful with: Someone whose grand gestures cover up small daily neglect.

Undecided.label: The Weekend Romantic
summaries: Practical on weekdays, sweet when it counts.

You know when to bring the romance and when to just get on with life. Weekdays are for logistics; anniversaries, trips and slow Sundays are for candles and playlists. You enjoy both sides of love, and you switch between them easily.
behaviors: You plan a lovely birthday surprise, then go back to normal on Monday.
You flirt when life slows down, and don’t force it when it doesn’t.
You enjoy a cheesy moment, as long as it isn’t every moment.
strengths: You keep love both fun and functional.
weaknesses: Romance can slip down the list when work gets busy.
realLife: On a first date: A good restaurant you booked ahead, and a short walk after because the evening felt nice.
In a fight: You talk it through sensibly, then make up with a little gesture.
tips: Put one romantic thing in an ordinary week. The spark shouldn’t have to wait for occasions.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys a mix of fun and steady.
Green flag: They make an effort on special days and stay easy on normal ones.
Careful with: Someone who needs constant grand gestures to feel loved.
