tests.measures: how much emotional availability and presence matter in how you feel loved

VeryHigh.label: The Lovebird
summaries: Two of you, one nest, always together.

For you, love means sharing life closely: daily plans, daily updates, decisions made as a pair. Being together feels like home, and being apart feels too quiet. You give your whole heart, and you hope for the same in return.
behaviors: You’d share locations, playlists and passwords in a heartbeat.
A weekend apart feels long, and you’ll probably call by noon.
You make most decisions together, from jobs to haircuts.
strengths: Your person always knows they’re part of your life, every single day.
weaknesses: When they need space, it can feel like a step away from you.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve talked for four hours and are already planning the next date before the bill comes.
In a fight: Distance after a fight is hard for you. Ask for a time to talk instead of chasing.
tips: Keep one thing that’s just yours. It gives you something new to bring back to the nest.
match: Best with: Someone who loves closeness and shares life as fully as you do.
Green flag: They include you naturally, without you having to ask.
Careful with: Someone who keeps big parts of their life hidden from you.

High.label: The We Person
summaries: Your plans quietly turned into our plans.

You love building a shared life: shared friends, shared jokes, shared Sunday routines. You still have your own world, but you’d rather bring them into it. When you’re close to someone, “I” naturally becomes “we”.
behaviors: You invite them to everything: your badminton group, your cousin’s wedding, your Sunday brunch.
You want to hear about their day, the small parts too.
You’re happiest when your friend circles mix.
strengths: People feel truly welcome in your life.
weaknesses: Someone independent may feel pulled in faster than they’d like.
realLife: On a first date: By the end, you’ve already planned to take them to your favourite momo place.
In a fight: You want to sort it out together right away. Give them a little time if they need it.
tips: Keep one thing just for you, a hobby or a night out with your people. It makes the “we” stronger.
match: Best with: Someone who loves a shared life as much as you do.
Green flag: They make room for you in their world too.
Careful with: Someone who keeps you in a separate box from the rest of their life.

Moderate.label: The Together-Apart Type
summaries: Close when you’re together, fine when you’re not.

You like a shared life with room to breathe in it. Some evenings together, some apart; some friends shared, some just yours. You don’t need every minute together and you don’t need to escape either, and that ease is rare.
behaviors: You share a lot, but keep a few things that are just yours.
You miss them on a trip, and you also enjoy your own time.
You ask for their opinion on big decisions and make the small ones alone.
strengths: You make both closeness and space feel safe.
weaknesses: With someone very independent or very close, you may adjust more than you notice.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their friends and hobbies and share yours, curious how your lives would fit.
In a fight: You take a short break, then come back together to sort it.
tips: Notice your own needs too, not just theirs. Say “I need a night in” or “I miss you” out loud.
match: Best with: Someone who wants a shared life with room to breathe.
Green flag: They tell you what kind of closeness feels good to them.
Careful with: Someone who swings from all-in to absent without warning.

Low.label: The Own Orbit
summaries: Close, but with your own path around the sun.

You love being with them, and you love coming back to your own space too. You keep your friendships, hobbies and quiet evenings alive, because they make you a better person to come home to. Two lives that meet often feel healthier to you than one merged life.
behaviors: You enjoy a few evenings a week together, and the rest are yours.
You’ll invite them to some things, not all of them.
You keep your own friends and gently encourage them to keep theirs.
strengths: You keep love fresh by staying interesting to yourself.
weaknesses: Someone close-knit may want more invitations into your world.
realLife: On a first date: A lovely evening, and you’re still happy to go home to your own space at the end of it.
In a fight: You need a quiet evening to sort your thoughts, then you come back ready to talk.
tips: Tell them your space isn’t about them. It helps them enjoy it with you instead of worrying.
match: Best with: Someone independent who likes coming back together.
Green flag: They’re happy to do things apart and excited to catch up after.
Careful with: Someone who sulks every time you make plans without them.

VeryLow.label: The Free Bird
summaries: You love best with the window open.

You have your own friends, your own plans and your own Saturdays, and love doesn’t change that. Space isn’t distance to you; it’s how you stay yourself and keep coming back with something to share. Being needed every minute would make you want to fly.
behaviors: You love them and still go on solo trips without a second thought.
You don’t need daily plans to feel secure together.
You like hearing about their life more than being in every part of it.
strengths: You never lose yourself in love, and you never ask them to lose themselves.
weaknesses: Someone who loves closeness may feel like a visitor in your life.
realLife: On a first date: You leave on time because you promised your gang you’d join them later.
In a fight: You need space to think. Say when you’ll be back, so it doesn’t feel like goodbye.
tips: Invite them into one part of your world on purpose. It tells them they belong there.
match: Best with: Someone with a full, happy life of their own.
Green flag: They have their own plans and are happy when you have yours.
Careful with: Someone who wants to know where you are every hour.

Undecided.label: The Together-Apart Type
summaries: Close when you’re together, fine when you’re not.

You like a shared life with room to breathe in it. Some evenings together, some apart; some friends shared, some just yours. You don’t need every minute together and you don’t need to escape either, and that ease is rare.
behaviors: You share a lot, but keep a few things that are just yours.
You miss them on a trip, and you also enjoy your own time.
You ask for their opinion on big decisions and make the small ones alone.
strengths: You make both closeness and space feel safe.
weaknesses: With someone very independent or very close, you may adjust more than you notice.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their friends and hobbies and share yours, curious how your lives would fit.
In a fight: You take a short break, then come back together to sort it.
tips: Notice your own needs too, not just theirs. Say “I need a night in” or “I miss you” out loud.
match: Best with: Someone who wants a shared life with room to breathe.
Green flag: They tell you what kind of closeness feels good to them.
Careful with: Someone who swings from all-in to absent without warning.

tests.measures: how quickly you express and deepen affection in relationships

VeryHigh.label: The All-In Heart
summaries: Zero to butterflies in one conversation.

You fall fast and you fall completely. One good conversation and your heart is already planning trips, and you’d rather feel everything than protect yourself from it. Your openness is brave and rare, even when it gets you hurt now and then.
behaviors: You knew you liked them before the first coffee was finished.
In week two, “I’m falling for you” feels perfectly normal to say.
Your friends get screenshots, updates and voice notes from day one.
strengths: Your courage to feel things fully makes people feel truly wanted.
weaknesses: You can fall for who you hope someone is before you know who they are.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve said “we should go to Goa together” before the starters arrive.
In a fight: You feel it all at once. Wait an hour before you send the long message.
tips: Enjoy the rush, and let time and actions confirm it. The right person will still be there in month three.
match: Best with: Someone open and expressive who loves an intense start.
Green flag: They share your excitement and are still around in month three.
Careful with: Someone who is all sweet words in week one and vague by week four.

High.label: The Quick Spark
summaries: You feel it early, and you let it show.

When you like someone, you know quickly and you don’t hide it. You text first, plan the next date before this one ends and tell your friends on day one. You’re open and brave with your feelings, though you still keep an eye on whether they feel the same.
behaviors: You text “I had so much fun” before you’ve even reached home.
One great conversation can tell you most of what you need to know.
You say “I really like you” early, and you mean it.
strengths: Nobody has to guess whether you’re interested.
weaknesses: A slower person may feel rushed by your enthusiasm.
realLife: On a first date: It went great, and you’ve already said so twice before the bill comes.
In a fight: You want to clear it up the same day, and you usually do.
tips: Let them catch up. Feelings shared at their speed land better than feelings sent at yours.
match: Best with: Someone open who enjoys an early spark as much as you do.
Green flag: They show interest back early, clearly and consistently.
Careful with: Someone who enjoys your attention but never returns it.

Moderate.label: The Mid-Tempo Heart
summaries: Not too fast, not too slow, just in tune.

You open up as things feel right, not by a timeline. You can feel excited early, but you like to see consistency before you go all in. You read the other person’s pace and adjust, which makes you easy to fall for.
behaviors: You text after a good date, but you won’t send a paragraph.
You tell your close friends after a few good dates, not before the first.
You’re ready for labels once it feels steady, usually in a month or two.

weaknesses: Following their pace can hide what you actually want.

In a fight: You want to talk once you’ve both cooled down a bit.
tips: Notice your own pace too. If you’re ready before them, it’s okay to say so.
match: Best with: Someone who moves at a natural, steady pace.
Green flag: They check how things feel for you, not just for them.
Careful with: Someone who rushes in, then suddenly pulls back.

Low.label: The Slow Burn
summaries: Steady warmth that builds, never rushed.

You feel things; you just like them to grow at their own pace. You show interest in small steps: a second date, a longer call, a shared song. Your feelings build quietly and deeply, and you trust what grows slowly more than what flares up overnight.
behaviors: You’d rather go on five chai dates than one intense weekend.
You say “I like you” once you’re sure, and not before.
Your affection grows week by week, quietly and steadily.
strengths: What you build lasts, because you built it carefully.
weaknesses: Your careful pace can be mistaken for low interest early on.
realLife: On a first date: Friendly, curious and a little guarded, with a “let’s do this again” text the next morning.
In a fight: You cool off first and come back calm. Tell them that’s the plan.
tips: Say your pace out loud: “I like you, I just take my time.” It turns your slowness into something they can trust.
match: Best with: Someone steady who enjoys getting to know you slowly.
Green flag: They’re consistent from week one, never hot and cold.
Careful with: Someone who pushes for big labels before you’ve had a second date.

VeryLow.label: The Dum Biryani
summaries: Slow, sealed, and absolutely worth the wait.

You don’t rush feelings, yours or anyone’s. You let trust build over months, through small kept promises and real-life moments, before you let your heart show. When you finally say “I love you”, it’s been cooking for a long time, and it’s real.
behaviors: You wait to feel sure before calling it anything, even to yourself.
Early “I miss you” texts make you smile, and also a little nervous.
Once you’re in, you’re in for the long run.
strengths: Your feelings, once shown, are rock solid.
weaknesses: Someone who moves faster may think you’re not interested when you’re just being careful.
realLife: On a first date: You enjoy it, keep your cards close, and wait a day or two before texting.
In a fight: You need time to think before you talk, so ask for it kindly.
tips: Give small signs while you’re still deciding. “I’m enjoying this” costs nothing and stops them guessing.
match: Best with: Someone patient who enjoys a slow build.
Green flag: They let things grow naturally and never pressure you to label it.
Careful with: Someone who says “I love you” in week one and expects it back.

Undecided.label: The Mid-Tempo Heart
summaries: Not too fast, not too slow, just in tune.

You open up as things feel right, not by a timeline. You can feel excited early, but you like to see consistency before you go all in. You read the other person’s pace and adjust, which makes you easy to fall for.
behaviors: You text after a good date, but you won’t send a paragraph.
You tell your close friends after a few good dates, not before the first.
You’re ready for labels once it feels steady, usually in a month or two.
strengths: You move at a pace that feels safe for both of you.
weaknesses: Following their pace can hide what you actually want.
realLife: On a first date: Warm, easy and a little flirty, happy to let the evening decide what’s next.
In a fight: You want to talk once you’ve both cooled down a bit.
tips: Notice your own pace too. If you’re ready before them, it’s okay to say so.
match: Best with: Someone who moves at a natural, steady pace.
Green flag: They check how things feel for you, not just for them.
Careful with: Someone who rushes in, then suddenly pulls back.

tests.title: Bond Strength
tests.subtitle: How quickly you form closeness
tests.description: This test shows how easily you feel emotionally connected and how much closeness you naturally seek. It helps the app predict pacing: some people bond fast, others need time and space.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your natural pace in getting close, and how quickly you invest emotionally.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Matching improves when two people have compatible pace: similar bonding speed reduces hot/cold dynamics.

options.text: Text your best friend: “I think I like this one”
Remind yourself it was one evening
Already miss them a little
Think “nice, I’d go again”

questions.text: How do you usually fall for someone?

options.text: Slowly. One day I notice I’ve liked them for weeks
Fast. A few good conversations and I’m in

options.text: Still open. It’s only been two weeks
Gone. I stopped replying after our first call
Still there, but fading fast

Sharing Maggi at 2 am and all our secrets
Friendly, with a few good late-night chats
Ordering food together every Friday

After a month or so of regular dates
Embarrassingly early. Week one

options.text: Send a warm wish at midnight
Already have a gift idea, maybe two
Wish them on the day, like anyone else

tests.measures: how quickly and deeply you form emotional bonds

VeryHigh.label: The Deep-End Diver
summaries: When it clicks, you’re all in by Thursday.

You don’t wade in, you dive. When the vibe is right, you feel close almost instantly, and you’re not shy about it. Your heart works fast and generously, which makes people feel wanted like nobody else can. It also means a short story can hurt like a long one.
behaviors: Three good chats and you’re thinking about them in the middle of a meeting.
You close the other chats early, because splitting your attention feels wrong.
A two-week fizzle can take you longer to get over than anyone would guess.
strengths: Your warmth is fearless. People never wonder if you like them.
weaknesses: You can fall for who you hope they are before you know who they are.
realLife: On a first date: You leave already missing them a little, and send a sweet text before you’re home.
In a fight: It feels big because they already mean a lot. Say “I care, that’s why this hurts.”
tips: Keep feeling fast, but decide slow. Give every big decision three more dates than your heart wants.
match: Best with: Someone just as expressive, or a calmer person who says clearly where they stand.
Green flag: Their actions keep up with their words, week after week.
Careful with: Big words in week one and very little follow-through by week four.

High.label: The Warm Welcome
summaries: A few good conversations and people feel close to you.

You open up quickly once you like someone, and people feel it. A few good conversations and they’re in your daily life: your memes, your chai breaks, your weekend plans. You’re not reckless, you just don’t see the point of holding back warmth you already feel.
behaviors: By the second date you know their sister’s name and their favourite momos place.
You start making small plans together early, and you enjoy every one.
When it fizzles, it stings for a few days, and then you’re hopeful again.
strengths: People feel chosen around you, and fast.
weaknesses: You can invest before you know whether they’re investing back.
realLife: On a first date: It runs an hour over, and you’ve already found a second place to try.
In a fight: You want to fix it quickly, because the bond already matters to you.
tips: Enjoy the fast start, and let their actions catch up with your feelings before you plan the next six months.
match: Best with: Someone who warms up quickly too, or a slower person who is clear and kind about it.
Green flag: They meet your energy and remember the small things you told them.
Careful with: Someone who enjoys your attention but never quite gives any back.

Moderate.label: The Steady Spark
summaries: Feels the spark early, lets it grow at its own pace.

You notice chemistry quickly, but you don’t build a whole future on it. You let a connection grow week by week, warm enough that people feel wanted and calm enough that nobody feels rushed. Your feelings tend to match what has actually happened between you.
behaviors: After a good date you’re excited, and you still sleep fine.
Around the one-month mark, you start saying “we” without noticing.
You can speed up for someone keen or slow down for someone careful.
strengths: Your pace feels easy to almost everyone, fast or slow.
weaknesses: Because you adjust so well, you sometimes forget to say what pace you actually want.
realLife: On a first date: Easy laughs, one deeper question, and a natural “let’s do this again”.
In a fight: You don’t panic and you don’t pull away. You ask what happened.
tips: Next time you like someone, say so a little earlier than feels comfortable. Your steadiness makes it land well.
match: Best with: Someone open about their feelings, so you can meet them where they are.
Green flag: Interest that grows steadily, date by date, without hot and cold weeks.
Careful with: Huge feelings early that vanish the moment real life arrives.

Low.label: The Low-Flame Chai
summaries: Takes its time, and is worth the wait.

You warm up gradually and on purpose. You like someone before you let yourself feel close, and you want to see a few weeks of them being who they said they were. It isn’t coldness. You just like your feelings to have something solid under them.
behaviors: You enjoy the talking stage without rushing to put a label on it.
By the fourth or fifth date the warmth starts to show, and then it doesn’t stop.
You’d rather go slow and be sure than go fast and be sorry.
strengths: You rarely get swept away by someone who was only good at the first week.
weaknesses: Your careful start can look lukewarm to someone who wears their heart on their sleeve.
realLife: On a first date: You pick a café you know, stay a comfortable two hours, and say yes to a second one.
In a fight: You want to talk it through calmly, and it teaches you a lot about who they are.
tips: Let them see the warmth before you’re fully sure. A “that was fun, let’s do it again” costs you nothing and means a lot.
match: Best with: Someone warm but unhurried, who is happy to let things simmer.
Green flag: They keep small promises: they call when they said they would.
Careful with: Pressure to define things before you’ve had time to feel them.

VeryLow.label: The Slow Bloom
summaries: Slow to put down roots, impossible to move once you do.

You don’t fall for people, you grow into them. It takes months of small proofs before you feel truly close, and you’re fine with that. The part nobody sees at first: once you’re attached, you stay, through boring Tuesdays and hard years.
behaviors: The first few dates feel like getting to know a nice colleague, and that’s okay with you.
You show interest by showing up, long before you say anything soft.
When you finally say “I really like you”, you’ve meant it for weeks.
strengths: Your feelings don’t fade after the first exciting months, because they never ran on them.
weaknesses: A fast faller can read your calm as “not interested” and leave before you warm up.
realLife: On a first date: You ask good questions, enjoy yourself, and go home without overthinking any of it.
In a fight: Early on, a fight makes you step back and watch. Later, you stay and work it out.
tips: Give one small, clear sign early, like “I’m enjoying this, I’m just slow.” It keeps good people around long enough for your roots to grow.
match: Best with: Someone patient who enjoys a slow build and doesn’t need fireworks by date three.
Green flag: They’re the same on date six as on date one: steady, curious, no pressure.
Careful with: Someone who says “I’ve never felt this way” in week one.

Undecided.label: The Steady Spark

You notice chemistry quickly, but you don’t build a whole future on it. You let a connection grow week by week, warm enough that people feel wanted and calm enough that nobody feels rushed. Your feelings tend to match what has actually happened between you.

You can speed up for someone keen or slow down for someone careful.

Green flag: Interest that grows steadily, date by date, without hot and cold weeks.
Careful with: Huge feelings early that vanish the moment real life arrives.

tests.subtitle: How safe intimacy feels
tests.description: Measures how comfortable you are with emotional and physical closeness when things become real.
tests.whatYouLearn: Whether intimacy feels safe, energizing, or overwhelming for you.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Pairs better when both people enjoy a similar level of closeness (too much/too little creates push-pull).

Ask them to please just use my name

tests.measures: how comfortable you are with emotional and physical closeness

VeryHigh.label: The Safe Harbour
summaries: Being close to you feels like coming home after a long day.

You’re completely at home with closeness. Being known inside out doesn’t scare you, it’s the whole point. You can sit with someone’s tears, say the big words when you feel them, and ask “are we okay?” without drama. People who have been hurt before often relax with you first.
behaviors: You say “I love you” back when you feel it, without a long pause.
When they’re sick, you’re at the door with dal-chawal and a phone charger.
A “where is this going” talk is one you’d happily start yourself.
strengths: You make intimacy feel safe for people who have never found it easy.
weaknesses: You can go deeper, faster, than a guarded person can follow.
realLife: On a first date: Two hours in, you’re both talking about what you were like at twelve.
In a fight: You reach for their hand halfway through, because the fight matters less than the two of you.
tips: Let guarded people come to you at their own pace. Your warmth works best when it waits at the door instead of pulling.
match: Best with: Someone who wants real closeness, or a careful person who is honest about learning it.
Green flag: They lean in when you open up, and open up back.
Careful with: Someone who enjoys your warmth but keeps every one of their own doors locked.

High.label: The Cosy Corner
summaries: Being close feels easy, and people relax around you.

You’re comfortable with closeness: the long talks, the hand-holding, the “how did the meeting go?”. You don’t see intimacy as a risk to manage, it’s one of the best parts of being with someone. You still keep a little corner of yourself, and you know that’s healthy too.
behaviors: You say “I miss you” when you miss them, no strategy involved.
When they open up, you move closer and put your phone away.
Talks about the future excite you more than they scare you.
strengths: People feel safe enough around you to be fully themselves.
weaknesses: You can take someone’s need for space as a sign they care less.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their family and their weird hobby, and they tell you more than they planned.
In a fight: You stay in the room and say “we’ll sort it”, and you mean it.
tips: When someone close needs space, give it warmly. Closeness that can breathe lasts longer.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys real closeness and says what they feel.
Green flag: They let you see their messy days, not only their good ones.
Careful with: Someone who goes cold every time things get real.

Moderate.label: The Shy Sweetheart
summaries: Warm all the way through, just shy at the big moments.

You enjoy closeness and you’re good at it: the check-ins, the cosy evenings, the inside jokes. It’s the big moments that make you blush and stall, like the first “I love you” or a talk about the future. Give you a minute and you come round, usually with something lovely to say.
behaviors: You love being looked after, right after the first “no no, I’m fine”.
A sudden “I miss you” gets a heart from you before you find the words.
Deep talks go well with you, with a joke or two to keep them breathing.
strengths: You make closeness feel light and safe, never heavy.
weaknesses: Your jokes can rescue you from a serious moment before it was finished.
realLife: On a first date: You laugh a lot, get flustered at one compliment, and want a second date.
In a fight: You soften fast, especially if they reach for your hand.
tips: When a big moment comes, stay in it ten seconds longer before the joke. Those ten seconds are where people feel close to you.
match: Best with: Someone gentle who gives you a second to find your words.
Green flag: They say the important things again when you’re ready to hear them.
Careful with: Someone who takes your shy pause as a final answer.

Low.label: The Door Ajar
summaries: Closeness, yes. With a way out, please.

You like being close to someone, in doses. A great evening together can be followed by a day where you want nobody at all, and that doesn’t mean anything is wrong. You let people in one room at a time, and you notice when they rush the hallway.
behaviors: You love a cosy evening in, then need a solo Sunday to feel like yourself again.
Sweet words make you shy, so you reply with a meme instead.
You open up more on walks and long drives than face to face.
strengths: You give space naturally, so nobody ever feels smothered by you.
weaknesses: Your sudden need for air can feel like a door closing to someone who just got close.
realLife: On a first date: You enjoy it, keep one or two stories for later, and leave on a high.
In a fight: You need a little distance first, then you can talk it out properly.
tips: When you need space, say why in one line: “Not you, I just need a quiet evening.” It keeps the door from looking shut.
match: Best with: Someone affectionate with a full life of their own.
Green flag: They’re warm without turning every moment into a big moment.
Careful with: Someone who reads every quiet day as a problem to solve.

VeryLow.label: The Walled Garden
summaries: Beautiful inside, and the gate takes a while to find.

You care deeply, but closeness can feel like a lot, so you keep a wall up and a gate you control. Somewhere along the way you learned that leaning on people was risky, or you just like your inner world tidy. People who make it inside find someone loyal, funny and surprisingly soft.
behaviors: A “where is this going” talk makes you suddenly very interested in the menu.
You show love by doing things: fixing their laptop, booking the cab, remembering the dentist.
After a very close day, even a lovely one, you need a lot of air.
strengths: You never fake closeness. When you let someone in, it’s real and it lasts.
weaknesses: Your wall can look like a “no” to someone who is only knocking gently.
realLife: On a first date: A walk or a game night, something side by side, is easier than eye contact over a candle.
In a fight: You go quiet and need distance. Say “give me an hour, I’m coming back”, and then come back.
tips: Next time someone wants to look after you, let them. Say yes to the khichdi. Small doses of being cared for make the gate easier to open.
match: Best with: Someone warm and patient, who doesn’t take your need for air personally.
Green flag: They let you set the pace of closeness, and notice when you step nearer.
Careful with: Someone who pushes for intensity fast, or teases you for being private.

Undecided.label: The Shy Sweetheart
summaries: Warm all the way through, just shy at the big moments.

You enjoy closeness and you’re good at it: the check-ins, the cosy evenings, the inside jokes. It’s the big moments that make you blush and stall, like the first “I love you” or a talk about the future. Give you a minute and you come round, usually with something lovely to say.

A sudden “I miss you” gets a heart from you before you find the words.
Deep talks go well with you, with a joke or two to keep them breathing.
strengths: You make closeness feel light and safe, never heavy.
weaknesses: Your jokes can rescue you from a serious moment before it was finished.
realLife: On a first date: You laugh a lot, get flustered at one compliment, and want a second date.
In a fight: You soften fast, especially if they reach for your hand.
tips: When a big moment comes, stay in it ten seconds longer before the joke. Those ten seconds are where people feel close to you.

Careful with: Someone who takes your shy pause as a final answer.

tests.title: Reassurance Need
tests.subtitle: How much confirmation you need
tests.description: Shows how often you need clear signs (texts, words, actions) to feel secure in the connection.
tests.whatYouLearn: How much reassurance you naturally need and what triggers insecurity.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps avoid mismatch where one person needs steady reassurance and the other provides too little.

options.text: Feel fine. The plans say it all
Keep wondering what they really think

“Are we really okay?”

options.text: Nothing. Let them enjoy it
A text or two, so I know I’m on their mind

A quick photo, so I feel part of it

options.text: Hearing “I’m not going anywhere”
A normal evening together, no speeches

options.text: Now and then, when it comes out on its own

Wonder a bit, then let it go

options.text: Prefer it that way. It’s our business
Drop a hint: “We look cute in this one”
Mind it. A post would make it feel real
Wouldn’t mind one, but it’s fine

tests.measures: how much verbal and emotional reassurance you need to feel secure

VeryHigh.label: The Tell-Me-Again Heart
summaries: You know they love you. You’d still like to hear it again.

You love wholeheartedly, and you want to feel it coming back in words, texts and little signs, all the time. Silence and vagueness are hard for you, and clear words settle you like nothing else. People who love saying it out loud find you the most rewarding person to love.
behaviors: A daily “I love you” never gets old for you.
Three months together with no photo of you online can quietly bother you.
After any little argument, you need a clear “we’re fine” before you can sleep.
strengths: You make love explicit, so nobody is ever left guessing.
weaknesses: When the words don’t come, your mind can write a sad story that isn’t true.
realLife: On a first date: You check your phone all the way home, hoping for a “that was lovely” text.
In a fight: You want to fix it tonight, with words, and a hug if possible.
tips: Keep a little list of things they’ve done that showed love. On a quiet day, read it before you ask again.
match: Best with: Someone warm and wordy, who finds saying it easy and fun.
Green flag: They reassure you before you ask, and never make you feel silly for asking.
Careful with: Hot and cold people who give warmth only when it suits them.

High.label: The Say-It-Out-Loud Type
summaries: Feelings count double for you when they’re said.

You like to know where you stand, clearly and often. You notice changes in tone, and a kind word calms you faster than anything else. That’s simply how you’re built: you feel love most when it’s spoken, and you speak it back generously.
behaviors: A heartfelt “I’m lucky to have you” can carry you through a whole bad week.
You’d rather ask “are we good?” than lie awake guessing.
You notice the day they stop saying the small sweet things.
strengths: You say what you feel, so the people you love always know it.
weaknesses: You can ask for reassurance so often that the words start to lose their magic.
realLife: On a first date: You’d love a clear “I want to see you again” before the night ends.
In a fight: You need to hear “we’re okay” before you can let it go.
tips: Before you ask “are we okay?”, look back at the last week. If they showed up, let that be the answer this time.
match: Best with: Someone expressive who enjoys saying the sweet things out loud.
Green flag: They tell you how they feel without being asked.
Careful with: Someone who goes quiet and expects you to just know.

Moderate.label: The Little Top-Up
summaries: Mostly fully charged. A sweet word now and then helps.

You’re secure most days, and you also like a small top-up: a “thinking of you” text, a hug after a rough day, a “we’re good” after a fight. You don’t need it constantly, but you notice when it’s been a while. Being honest about that makes you easy to love.
behaviors: After a small fight, a sweet text before bed settles you.
You love it when they say what they like about you, out of nowhere.
On a stressful week you might ask “are we okay?” once, and mean it lightly.
strengths: You know what you need, and you can ask for it without drama.
weaknesses: If the top-ups stop for a while, you might go quiet instead of saying so.
realLife: On a first date: A “had a great time” text that evening makes your whole week.
In a fight: You need one clear “we’re fine” at the end, and then you really are fine.
tips: When you need a top-up, ask in plain words: “Tell me something nice today.” It works better than waiting and hoping.
match: Best with: Someone who says kind things easily and means them.
Green flag: They check in after a fight without being asked.
Careful with: Someone who calls a simple request for reassurance “too much”.

Low.label: The Quiet Believer
summaries: Actions tell you most of what you need to know.

You feel secure most of the time, and you read people by what they do. A sweet word now and then is lovely, but you don’t keep count. You’d rather spend an ordinary evening together than hear a big speech about how much you matter.
behaviors: Plans, not promises, are what make you feel sure of someone.
You notice the little efforts: the cab booked for you, the extra cup of chai.
If something feels off, you ask once, then trust the answer.
strengths: You trust people to mean well, and it helps them relax.
weaknesses: You may miss that a more sensitive person needs words, not only actions.
realLife: On a first date: You notice whether they listened, not how many compliments they paid you.
In a fight: You want a clear sorry and a changed habit, not a long apology essay.
tips: Ask them once what makes them feel secure. Then do it, even if you’d never need it yourself.
match: Best with: Someone who shows love through effort and is fine with quiet days.
Green flag: They keep small promises without being reminded.
Careful with: Grand words with nothing behind them.

VeryLow.label: The Inner Compass
summaries: You know where you stand without being told.

Your sense of security comes from inside, not from texts or labels. If someone keeps showing up, that’s all the proof you need, and a quiet week doesn’t shake you. It makes you very easy to be with, and now and then a little hard to read.
behaviors: You can tell how they feel from how they act, so you rarely ask.
A busy week apart doesn’t make you wonder about the two of you.
You’re genuinely happy when they go out without you, and you don’t need updates.
strengths: You never make anyone prove themselves every single day.
weaknesses: Because you need so little reassurance, you can forget that they might need some.
realLife: On a first date: No overthinking afterwards. If it was good, you simply ask for the next one.
In a fight: Once it’s sorted, it’s sorted. You don’t need three follow-ups to feel okay.
tips: Say the warm thing out loud anyway. You may not need to hear it, but the person you’re with might.
match: Best with: Someone secure and low-drama, or a warmer person who tells you what they need.
Green flag: They’re consistent, so their actions say it all.
Careful with: Someone who mistakes your calm for not caring and starts testing you.

Undecided.label: The Little Top-Up
summaries: Mostly fully charged. A sweet word now and then helps.

You’re secure most days, and you also like a small top-up: a “thinking of you” text, a hug after a rough day, a “we’re good” after a fight. You don’t need it constantly, but you notice when it’s been a while. Being honest about that makes you easy to love.
behaviors: After a small fight, a sweet text before bed settles you.
You love it when they say what they like about you, out of nowhere.
On a stressful week you might ask “are we okay?” once, and mean it lightly.
strengths: You know what you need, and you can ask for it without drama.
weaknesses: If the top-ups stop for a while, you might go quiet instead of saying so.
realLife: On a first date: A “had a great time” text that evening makes your whole week.
In a fight: You need one clear “we’re fine” at the end, and then you really are fine.
tips: When you need a top-up, ask in plain words: “Tell me something nice today.” It works better than waiting and hoping.
match: Best with: Someone who says kind things easily and means them.
Green flag: They check in after a fight without being asked.
Careful with: Someone who calls a simple request for reassurance “too much”.

tests.title: Space Need
tests.subtitle: How much space you require
tests.description: Shows whether you recharge through independence or through closeness and frequent contact.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your natural need for space and how you react to daily contact.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Prevents misunderstandings: some people need daily closeness, others need quiet space to feel okay.

questions.text: A free Saturday with the person you’re seeing. Your ideal version:

options.text: Together, from breakfast to the midnight snack
Morning to myself, evening together
Same room, each doing our own thing
My day, my plans. Let’s meet on Sunday

options.text: A corner or a room that’s only mine
Every space shared, our stuff everywhere

options.text: Love it. The day goes faster
Find it hard to focus, and tell them
Like a few texts, not a running chat

options.text: Enjoy it, then hint you’ve got work
Love the surprise. Come in!
Feel caught off guard. I’d planned a quiet night
Happy, but a heads-up would be nice

options.text: Skip it. Five days without them sounds long
Go, and text them every evening
Go, and enjoy missing them a bit
Join for just the weekend

options.text: Send food and a sweet text, no need to talk
Come over and just be there
Let me sulk alone till I’m human again
Call, and let me rant for a bit

questions.text: Hobbies in a relationship should be…

options.text: Some shared, some just mine
Mostly mine. That’s where I recharge
Mostly shared. Couple badminton!

questions.text: Once things are serious, how many evenings a week together feels right?

options.text: One or two. The rest are mine
Every evening, ideally
Five, with a night off for my own stuff
Three or four

tests.measures: how much personal space and autonomy you need in relationships

VeryHigh.label: Pure Cat Energy
summaries: Affection on your own terms, and it’s worth it.

You need a lot of room: your own plans, your own weekends, sometimes your own city. That doesn’t mean you love less. It means you love from a place of freedom, and you come back because you want to. People who don’t need constant contact find you wonderfully easy.
behaviors: Seeing them once or twice a week feels close enough to you.
A trip on your own is your idea of a perfect holiday.
An unannounced visit can feel like someone walked into your quiet room.
strengths: You’re completely yourself in love, and you let them be too.
weaknesses: Your need for room can leave a warm person wondering if they matter.
realLife: On a first date: Somewhere easy to leave, and you’ll text the next day if it was good.
In a fight: You disappear to think. Leave a note first: “Need the night, not leaving.”
tips: Show up for the small rituals: a call on Sunday, a hello at night. A little rhythm makes your freedom feel safe to them.
match: Best with: Someone equally independent, with a big life of their own.
Green flag: They’re genuinely happy to see you, and genuinely fine without you.
Careful with: Someone who needs to know where you are every hour.

High.label: The Solo Recharger
summaries: Love you lots. Also, this evening is mine.

You love deeply, and you also need time that belongs only to you: a solo morning, a hobby, a quiet evening with a book or a game. It’s how you stay yourself, and you’re much better company when you are. You give people space as easily as you take it.
behaviors: A day apart feels like a breath, not a warning.
You prefer a few good texts over a chat that runs all day.
Surprise visits are sweet, but you like a heads-up first.
strengths: You never smother anyone, and you never need them to fill your day.
weaknesses: Your quiet evenings can look like distance to someone who shows love by being near.
realLife: On a first date: Lovely, and done by ten. You like leaving them wanting more, and getting your sleep.
In a fight: You go for a walk alone, then come back with clear words.
tips: When you take space, say when you’ll be back: “Alone tonight, call you tomorrow.” A clear return time makes space feel safe.
match: Best with: Someone with a full life of their own who enjoys a bit of room.
Green flag: They respect your solo time and don’t ask you to explain it.
Careful with: Someone who hears “I need an evening to myself” as a breakup speech.

Moderate.label: The Twin Orbit
summaries: Close together, each on your own path.

You want a shared life and a life of your own, and you don’t see a conflict between them. A morning to yourself, an evening together, a trip with your gang once a year. You read pretty well when it’s time to come close and when it’s time to drift a little.
behaviors: Three or four evenings a week together feels just right.
You like hearing about their solo plans and sharing yours.
A heads-up before a surprise visit makes the surprise even nicer.
strengths: You keep a relationship both close and breathable.
weaknesses: You can be so balanced that you forget to say when you need more of either.
realLife: On a first date: A good two hours, a clear plan for next time, and both of you home at a decent hour.
In a fight: You take an hour apart to think, then come back to talk.
tips: Say your rhythm out loud early: “I need one evening a week to myself.” It saves a lot of guessing.
match: Best with: Someone with their own interests who loves coming home to you.
Green flag: They have friends and plans, and still make time for you.
Careful with: All or nothing: glued to you one week, gone the next.

Low.label: The Easy Companion
summaries: Loves being near you, even when you’re both busy.

You like your person close: same room, same couch, each on a laptop if needed. You enjoy a few things of your own, but most of life feels better shared. You’re easy to live with, because your idea of space is quiet company, not a closed door.
behaviors: Working side by side on a Sunday counts as a date to you.
You love a trip with your old gang, as long as it’s short.
On a bad day, a call where you can rant helps more than being alone.
strengths: You make ordinary days feel like time together.
weaknesses: You may not notice when they need real alone time, not just quiet time.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest a second activity before the first one is over.
In a fight: You’d rather sit in the same room, a bit grumpy, than go to separate corners.
tips: When they ask for an evening alone, say “enjoy it” and mean it. Then plan something you enjoy too.
match: Best with: Someone who likes company and has a couple of hobbies you can join.
Green flag: They invite you into their routines, not just their weekends.
Careful with: Someone who disappears for days and calls it normal.

VeryLow.label: The Shared Umbrella
summaries: Life is better with two people under it.

For you, love means sharing the everyday: the commute, the groceries, the late-night snack. Time together isn’t something you schedule, it’s the default, and time apart feels like a draught in the room. You make the person you love feel wanted every single day.
behaviors: Your ideal Saturday is together from breakfast to the last episode.
A five-day trip without them sounds more lonely than fun.
You’d happily turn their hobby into your shared hobby.
strengths: Nobody ever feels like an afterthought with you.
weaknesses: Their wish for an evening alone can feel like rejection when it isn’t.
realLife: On a first date: It turns into dinner, then a walk, then “one more chai?”
In a fight: Distance hurts more than the fight, so you want to make up in the same room.
tips: Keep one thing that’s only yours: a class, a weekly game, a friend you meet alone. It makes the time together even sweeter.
match: Best with: Someone who loves a shared life as much as you do.
Green flag: They include you in their plans without being asked.
Careful with: Someone who keeps you at arm’s length and calls it “independence”.

Undecided.label: The Twin Orbit
summaries: Close together, each on your own path.

You want a shared life and a life of your own, and you don’t see a conflict between them. A morning to yourself, an evening together, a trip with your gang once a year. You read pretty well when it’s time to come close and when it’s time to drift a little.

You like hearing about their solo plans and sharing yours.
A heads-up before a surprise visit makes the surprise even nicer.
strengths: You keep a relationship both close and breathable.
weaknesses: You can be so balanced that you forget to say when you need more of either.
realLife: On a first date: A good two hours, a clear plan for next time, and both of you home at a decent hour.
In a fight: You take an hour apart to think, then come back to talk.
tips: Say your rhythm out loud early: “I need one evening a week to myself.” It saves a lot of guessing.
match: Best with: Someone with their own interests who loves coming home to you.
Green flag: They have friends and plans, and still make time for you.
Careful with: All or nothing: glued to you one week, gone the next.

tests.title: Fear of Rejection
tests.subtitle: Sensitivity to distance & silence
tests.description: Measures how strongly you react to signs of rejection (slow replies, distance, lack of enthusiasm).
tests.whatYouLearn: Your sensitivity to rejection cues and how you cope with uncertainty.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps match people who interpret signals similarly, reducing overthinking loops.

questions.text: You sent a sweet text at 6 pm. It’s 10 pm: two blue ticks, no reply. You…

options.text: Feel a small pinch, then get on with my evening
Reread my text for anything wrong
Assume they’re busy. They’ll reply
Check their last seen a few times

questions.text: They cancel tomorrow’s date: “So sorry, work blew up.” You…

options.text: Wonder if work is the real reason
Say “no worries, next week?”
Feel flat for a bit, then suggest a new day

options.text: “Did I do something?”
“They’ve got something going on”

questions.text: You finally say “I really like you.” They reply “aww, you’re sweet.” You…

options.text: Replay it all night
Feel exposed for a day, then shrug
Laugh. They’ll say it when they’re ready
Ask them the next day what they meant

options.text: Wait for Mummy to call. She always does
Feel like nobody cares
Assume everyone’s busy. Reactions will come
Send a funny follow-up to get a reaction

Enjoy my own evening. We’ve got the whole trip

Feel a little left out

options.text: “Not meant to be.” Delete and move on
“What was wrong with me?”
Feel low for a day, then let it go

tests.measures: how much worry and anxiety you experience about relationships

VeryHigh.label: The Big-Hearted Overthinker
summaries: You love big, so every silence feels loud.

You feel distance deeply. A slow reply, a cancelled plan or a vague answer can sink your evening, and you often wonder what you did wrong. Underneath is a loyal, generous heart that hates being left out. You deserve people who make you feel chosen, without a guessing game.
behaviors: Two hours of “we need to talk” silence can feel like two days.
A family chat that goes quiet after your news can hurt more than you show.
You often say sorry first, even when you’re not sure what for.
strengths: Your sensitivity makes you kind. You’d never leave anyone wondering.
weaknesses: Your fear can write a rejection story before anything has actually happened.
realLife: On a first date: You leave sure you talked too much, and then they ask for a second date.
In a fight: You may rush to fix it out of fear. Breathe first, then talk.
tips: When the fear starts, ask one clear question instead of reading ten signs: “Are we okay?” Then believe the answer.
match: Best with: Someone steady and openly affectionate, who never plays games with silence.
Green flag: They reassure you without being asked, and keep doing it.
Careful with: Anyone who enjoys keeping you guessing. You deserve clarity.

High.label: The Late-Night Rereader
summaries: Every quiet text gets a careful second look.

You care a lot about how people feel about you, so you notice everything: the shorter reply, the missing emoji, the plan that got moved. Your mind fills the gaps, and not always kindly to you. It’s the flip side of a big heart that wants to be chosen.
behaviors: A text read and left can send you back to reread your own message twice.
When they say “we need to talk”, your mind writes three endings before they call.
A little less attention on a group trip can feel like a lot less love.
strengths: You’re so tuned in that you catch hurt feelings before anyone says a word.
weaknesses: You can treat a busy week as proof that you don’t matter.
realLife: On a first date: You replay their goodbye on the way home to check how it sounded.
In a fight: The fear of losing them can be louder than the fight. Say that out loud, it helps.
tips: Before you read a silence, list three boring reasons for it: a meeting, traffic, a dead battery. It’s usually one of those.
match: Best with: Someone consistent and warm, who says “busy day, talk tonight” without being asked.
Green flag: They notice when you’ve gone quiet, and ask kindly.
Careful with: Someone who disappears and reappears without explaining.

Moderate.label: The Two-Minute Worrier
summaries: A quick wobble, then you’re fine. Like Maggi.

Silence or distance does get to you for a moment: the stomach drop, the quick check of their last seen. Then your good sense kicks in and you remember they have a life. You feel things, you just don’t let them cook for long.
behaviors: “We need to talk” makes your heart jump, and then you simply ask “all okay?”
A slow reply might get one extra look at your phone, not ten.
When they’re quiet, you wonder for a minute, then decide it’s probably work.
strengths: You feel the worry and still choose to trust.
weaknesses: On a tired day, the two minutes can stretch into a whole evening.
realLife: On a first date: You wonder for a second if they liked you, then see the “that was fun” text and relax.
In a fight: You worry briefly about what it means, then focus on what actually happened.
tips: When the wobble comes, give it a timer: two minutes, then do something with your hands. Most worries don’t survive the timer.
match: Best with: Someone who gives a quick heads-up when they’re going to be busy.
Green flag: They explain a late reply without you having to ask.
Careful with: Someone who goes silent after a fight to make a point.

Low.label: The Clear-Eyed Noticer
summaries: You notice the signals and don’t let them run the show.

You pick up on distance and changes in tone, but you don’t build a story around them. You ask if you need to, accept the answer and get on with your day. It probably took some living to get here, and it shows: you’re sensitive without being shaken.
behaviors: A quiet day from them gets a light “all okay?” and nothing more.
A cancelled plan stings for a minute, then you suggest another day.
You can say “I like you” first and survive a lukewarm answer.
strengths: You read people well and still assume the kind explanation first.
weaknesses: Sometimes you brush off a feeling that deserved a real conversation.
realLife: On a first date: You notice whether they’re into it, but you’re too busy enjoying yourself to obsess.
In a fight: You name what hurt, calmly, and you don’t assume the worst about them.
tips: When a feeling keeps coming back, say it once, kindly. Calm doesn’t have to mean quiet.
match: Best with: Someone open and steady, who doesn’t play hot and cold.
Green flag: When they’re busy, they say so before you have to wonder.
Careful with: Mixed signals that keep changing from week to week.

VeryLow.label: The Unbothered One
summaries: Silence is just silence. You sleep fine.

You don’t take distance personally. A slow reply, a cancelled plan or a quiet evening reads to you as someone’s busy life, not a verdict on you. That calm comes from knowing your own worth, and it makes you a very restful person to be close to.
behaviors: Blue ticks and no reply? You assume they’re in a meeting, and you’re usually right.
A cancelled date gets a “no worries, next week?” and no second thought.
If it doesn’t work out, you’re sad, not shattered, and you don’t blame yourself.
strengths: You never make someone pay for having a busy day.
weaknesses: You can miss real signs that something is off, because you expect the best.
realLife: On a first date: If they’re running late, you order a chai and enjoy the people-watching.
In a fight: You don’t panic about the relationship. You just deal with the issue.
tips: Now and then, check in even when you’re not worried. “All good with you?” shows you notice, not just that you’re calm.
match: Best with: Someone steady and honest, who tells you when something really is wrong.
Green flag: They say what they mean, so your calm is well placed.
Careful with: Someone who goes silent on purpose to see if you’ll chase.

Undecided.label: The Two-Minute Worrier
summaries: A quick wobble, then you’re fine. Like Maggi.

Silence or distance does get to you for a moment: the stomach drop, the quick check of their last seen. Then your good sense kicks in and you remember they have a life. You feel things, you just don’t let them cook for long.

A slow reply might get one extra look at your phone, not ten.
When they’re quiet, you wonder for a minute, then decide it’s probably work.
strengths: You feel the worry and still choose to trust.
weaknesses: On a tired day, the two minutes can stretch into a whole evening.
realLife: On a first date: You wonder for a second if they liked you, then see the “that was fun” text and relax.
In a fight: You worry briefly about what it means, then focus on what actually happened.
tips: When the wobble comes, give it a timer: two minutes, then do something with your hands. Most worries don’t survive the timer.
match: Best with: Someone who gives a quick heads-up when they’re going to be busy.
Green flag: They explain a late reply without you having to ask.
Careful with: Someone who goes silent after a fight to make a point.

tests.title: Trust Building
tests.subtitle: How you form trust over time
tests.description: Shows whether you trust quickly, cautiously, or only after consistent proof.
tests.whatYouLearn: How you build trust and what behaviors earn it.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Pairs best when trust-building speed aligns (fast trust vs slow trust).

questions.text: They said they’d call at 9. It’s 9:40, no call, and they’ve always been on time. You…

options.text: Think “here we go” and make a note
Assume something came up
Feel a flicker of doubt, then wait

questions.text: How long before you share your Netflix password with someone you’re seeing?

options.text: A couple of months
About a week. What’s the worst they’ll watch?
When we’re engaged

questions.text: Two months in, they ask to borrow ₹5,000 till payday. You…

options.text: Send it. They’re good for it
Find a polite way to say no

questions.text: Do you ever test someone, like going quiet to see if they notice?

options.text: More often than I’d admit
Never. If I want to know, I ask
Sometimes I wait to see who texts first
Once or twice, early on

questions.text: You were badly let down before. Now someone new is kind and steady. You…

options.text: Enjoy it, and keep one eye open
Wait for the catch
Relax a little more every month
Give them a clean page

questions.text: They tell you, “I’m serious about you.” When do you believe it?

options.text: After a few months of matching actions
Right away. Why would they lie?
When I’ve seen a year of it
Pretty soon, if it feels true

options.text: Quietly try to book them myself too
Leave it to them and get on with my day
Send a reminder at 9:55, just in case

questions.text: Six months of them being steady, kind and reliable. Your trust is…

options.text: Growing, with a little still held back
Still on probation, honestly
Full. They’ve earned it, and then some

tests.measures: how readily you let trust grow once someone shows they are reliable

VeryHigh.label: The Clean Slate
summaries: Everyone starts with your full trust, no deposit needed.

You give people a clean page, whatever happened before them. You believe what you’re told, you share easily, and testing someone would never cross your mind. It’s a generous way to love, and it means the right people feel at home with you instantly.
behaviors: Even after a past hurt, you don’t make the new person pay for it.
You’d lend money to someone you’ve been seeing for two months, no questions asked.
“I’m serious about you” is something you believe the first time you hear it.
strengths: You make people feel trusted, and it brings out their best.
weaknesses: You might miss a pattern that a more careful person would spot early.
realLife: On a first date: You tell them more than you planned, and you don’t regret it.
In a fight: You believe their apology and move on quickly, sometimes too quickly.
tips: Keep your clean slate, but ask one person you trust what they see. A second pair of eyes protects a big heart.
match: Best with: Someone honest to the core, who would never take your trust for granted.
Green flag: They protect your trust as carefully as you give it.
Careful with: Stories that change a little each time you ask. Notice that.

High.label: The Open Hand
summaries: You start with trust and let people keep it.

You believe people are mostly decent, and you treat them that way from the start. You don’t keep score of small slips or test anyone in secret. That openness makes people want to live up to it, and most of them do.
behaviors: If they say they’ll book the tickets, you leave it to them and go back to your chai.
A late call makes you think “traffic”, not “lies”.
You share small things, like passwords and plans, without making it a big step.
strengths: People feel safe and respected with you, never watched.
weaknesses: You can keep trusting someone a little after the evidence says stop.
realLife: On a first date: You believe their stories and ask for more of them.
In a fight: You assume they didn’t mean to hurt you, and you start from there.
tips: Keep your open hand, and keep your eyes open too. Trust what they do more than what they promise.
match: Best with: Someone honest and dependable who values being trusted.
Green flag: They’re open about their life without being asked.
Careful with: Someone who keeps asking you for “one more chance”.

Moderate.label: The Step-by-Step Truster
summaries: A fair chance at the start, more trust with every step.

You don’t assume the worst and you don’t hand over everything on day one. You start people with a fair amount of trust and let it grow as they show up. A single slip doesn’t undo months of good behaviour for you, but a pattern does.
behaviors: You believe kind words, and you believe them more when actions follow.
A late call gets a “what happened?” rather than a cold shoulder.
You trust them to book the tickets, and maybe you set one reminder.
strengths: You’re fair: generous at the start, clear about what matters.
weaknesses: You can forgive a slow pattern for too long, because each slip looks small.
realLife: On a first date: You take them at their word and simply enjoy the evening.
In a fight: You listen to their side before deciding what it means.
tips: Notice patterns, not moments. Three slips is information. One slip is just a Tuesday.
match: Best with: Someone reliable and open, who doesn’t mind a gentle question.
Green flag: Their words and actions say the same thing, month after month.
Careful with: Small broken promises that keep coming back with new excuses.

Low.label: The Key Keeper
summaries: You hand over trust one key at a time.

You’re not suspicious, just careful. You let people in step by step: first your plans, then your friends, then your worries. Every kept promise opens one more door, and you remember exactly who kept them.
behaviors: The Netflix password comes after a couple of months, not a couple of dates.
You give a fair chance, and you keep one eye open while you do.
A missed call at 9 makes you wonder for a while, even if they’ve always been on time.
strengths: Your trust is earned, so it holds up when life gets hard.
weaknesses: Your careful pace can make an honest person feel they’re on trial.
realLife: On a first date: Pleasant and polite, with the real warmth saved for the third or fourth date.
In a fight: You need to see the change, not just hear the sorry.
tips: Tell them what builds your trust: “Just do what you say, I’ll notice.” It turns your caution into a clear path.
match: Best with: Someone consistent who doesn’t rush you to trust them.
Green flag: They explain a slip before you have to ask.
Careful with: Someone who gets defensive when you ask a simple question.

VeryLow.label: The Watchful Gatekeeper
summaries: You read every promise twice before you sign.

Trust is the most valuable thing you own, so you don’t hand it out on a first date. Maybe you’ve been let down before, maybe you’re just careful by nature, but you need to see words and actions match for a long time. Whoever earns your trust gets someone fiercely loyal.
behaviors: Six good months can still feel like a probation period to you.
When they say “I’m serious about you”, you wait to see it in how they act.
A single missed promise stays in your head longer than ten kept ones.
strengths: You’re almost impossible to fool, and once you trust someone, it doesn’t wobble.
weaknesses: Good people can get tired of proving themselves again and again.
realLife: On a first date: You notice if they arrive when they said, and quietly give them a point for it.
In a fight: You want facts and a clear explanation, not just “trust me”.
tips: Try giving one small trust early, like letting them plan a whole evening. Small risks show you who deserves the big ones.
match: Best with: Someone patient and boringly reliable, in the best way.
Green flag: They do what they said, when they said, without making a show of it.
Careful with: Charm with gaps in the story. Trust your instinct there.

Undecided.label: The Step-by-Step Truster
summaries: A fair chance at the start, more trust with every step.

You don’t assume the worst and you don’t hand over everything on day one. You start people with a fair amount of trust and let it grow as they show up. A single slip doesn’t undo months of good behaviour for you, but a pattern does.
behaviors: You believe kind words, and you believe them more when actions follow.
A late call gets a “what happened?” rather than a cold shoulder.
You trust them to book the tickets, and maybe you set one reminder.
strengths: You’re fair: generous at the start, clear about what matters.
weaknesses: You can forgive a slow pattern for too long, because each slip looks small.
realLife: On a first date: You take them at their word and simply enjoy the evening.
In a fight: You listen to their side before deciding what it means.
tips: Notice patterns, not moments. Three slips is information. One slip is just a Tuesday.
match: Best with: Someone reliable and open, who doesn’t mind a gentle question.
Green flag: Their words and actions say the same thing, month after month.
Careful with: Small broken promises that keep coming back with new excuses.

tests.title: Emotional Regulation
tests.subtitle: Stability when triggered
tests.description: Measures how calm and self-controlled you stay when emotions spike in dating/relationships.
tests.whatYouLearn: How you handle triggers without spiraling or shutting down.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Improves matching by predicting how stressful moments will be handled together.

questions.text: They forgot to book the table for your anniversary dinner. At the restaurant door, you…

options.text: Go quiet the whole way home
Laugh and find a dhaba nearby
Say “you had one job” in front of the staff
Feel annoyed, breathe, make a new plan

questions.text: Midnight. You’ve typed a long, angry text. You…

options.text: Soften it, then send
Send it. They need to know now
Delete it and talk in the morning

questions.text: In front of friends, they make a joke at your expense. It stings. You…

options.text: Fire a sharper joke back
Laugh along, and tell them later it hurt
Go cold for the rest of the night
Say “not cool” right there, calmly

questions.text: When you’re upset with someone, you usually…

options.text: Take a little time before I talk
Have to say it right now

questions.text: Mid-argument, your mum calls. You…

options.text: Cut her off: “Ma, I’ll call you back!”
Pick up, sound normal, and come back calmer
Text “will call later” and carry on

questions.text: They’re 40 minutes late, phone off. When they finally arrive, you…

options.text: Let them have it, right there
Say a cold “we’ll talk later”
Ask if they’re okay first
Say you were annoyed, and also worried

questions.text: After a big fight, how long until you feel normal again?

options.text: Days. It replays in my head
An hour or two, once we’ve talked
A day. I need to sleep on it

questions.text: Your boss criticised your work in front of the team. That evening, with the person you’re seeing, you…

options.text: Vent for an hour, then feel better
Snap at them over nothing
Tell them about it, then enjoy dinner
Barely talk, stuck in my head

tests.measures: how well you manage your emotions when triggered in relationships

VeryHigh.label: The Unshakeable Oak
summaries: Last over, twelve to win, and you’re still smiling.

You stay grounded when things get messy. Big feelings come, and you can hold them, look at them and respond instead of react. People come to you in a crisis because you don’t add to it, and you bounce back from a bad day faster than anyone in the dressing room.
behaviors: A ruined reservation turns into a dhaba adventure and a story you both retell.
You can be hurt and still kind in the same sentence.
After a fight, you’re back to normal in an hour, once things are said.
strengths: You lower the temperature of any room you walk into.
weaknesses: You may expect others to calm down as quickly as you do.
realLife: On a first date: Late auto, spilled chai, wrong address: you laugh through all of it.
In a fight: You listen fully, say your part clearly, and don’t bring up old fights.
tips: Your calm is a gift. Don’t let it become the only calm in the relationship: make room for them to steady you too.
match: Best with: Someone open about their feelings who enjoys your steadiness.
Green flag: They feel safe enough with you to show their messy side.
Careful with: Someone who leans on your calm and never learns their own.

High.label: The Calm Pilot
summaries: Turbulence happens. Your voice stays steady.

When emotions run high, you feel them, and you still choose what to do next. You can pause, name what’s going on and talk without making it worse. It isn’t that nothing bothers you. You’ve just learned that most storms pass faster when someone keeps the plane level.
behaviors: When they’re 40 minutes late, you ask if they’re okay before you ask why.
You delete the midnight text and talk it through in the morning.
A sting in front of friends gets handled later, privately and clearly.
strengths: You make hard moments feel safe for both of you.
weaknesses: Staying calm can look like not caring to someone who shows feelings loudly.
realLife: On a first date: The table mix-up doesn’t faze you. You find a better place nearby.
In a fight: You say “I’m upset, give me ten minutes, then let’s talk”, and you mean ten.
tips: Let them see the feeling under your calm sometimes. “I was really hurt” isn’t losing control, it’s closeness.
match: Best with: Someone who values talking things out, even if they run hotter than you.
Green flag: They come back after a fight wanting to understand, not just to win.
Careful with: Someone who takes your calm as a reason to keep pushing.

Moderate.label: The Deep Breather
summaries: Usually makes it to ten. On bad days, to six.

You know the drill: breathe, count, don’t send the text. Most of the time it works, and you handle stress with more grace than you give yourself credit for. On a tired, hungry or hard day the count runs short, and you’re honest enough to say sorry after.
behaviors: Most nights, you soften an angry message before you send it.
A bad day at work comes home with you for an hour, then you let it go.
After a big fight, you need a night’s sleep to really feel okay.
strengths: You can pull yourself back from the edge, and you own it when you can’t.
weaknesses: Stress from outside the relationship makes your count shorter inside it.
realLife: On a first date: If something goes wrong, you sigh, then laugh, and the evening is fine.
In a fight: You get through the first round calmly. Ask for a pause before round two.
tips: Know your short-count days: hungry, tired, after a bad meeting. On those days, eat first and talk later.
match: Best with: Someone patient who gives you a minute when you need one.
Green flag: They say “let’s take five” instead of pushing through a hot moment.
Careful with: Someone who picks fights when you’re tired and hungry.

Low.label: The Simmering Pot
summaries: You hold it, hold it, and then comes the whistle.

You try hard to stay calm, and mostly you do, until it builds up and comes out all at once. Small things pile up quietly, then one tiny thing sets off the whistle. You care a lot about keeping the peace, which is exactly why the steam collects.
behaviors: You go quiet and cold for an evening before you say what’s really wrong.
A joke at your expense can sting for days without them knowing.
When it finally comes out, it’s about ten things, not the one in front of you.
strengths: You put up with a lot, and you rarely start a fight over nothing.
weaknesses: Holding it in makes the final whistle louder than the problem ever was.
realLife: On a first date: You’re easygoing and fun, and nobody would guess there’s any steam at all.
In a fight: It comes out all at once. Try saying the first small thing on the day it happens.
tips: Let a little steam out every day. One “that bothered me a bit” at dinner beats a blow-up on Sunday.
match: Best with: Someone who notices when you’ve gone quiet and asks gently.
Green flag: They make it safe to say small things before they become big things.
Careful with: Someone who calls your feelings “overreacting” instead of listening.

VeryLow.label: The Monsoon Storm
summaries: Loud, sudden, over fast, and the air is clearer after.

You feel everything at full volume, and it comes out before you’ve had time to sort it. A forgotten plan or a careless joke can set you off, and you say things you have to fix later. Underneath is someone passionate and honest, who never pretends to be fine when they’re not.
behaviors: A midnight angry text is out before you’ve finished reading it back.
You can go from furious to hugging them in the same evening.
When you’re hurt, everyone in the room knows, including your mum on the phone.
strengths: You’re never fake. People always know exactly where they stand with you.
weaknesses: Words said in the storm can stay with them long after it has passed for you.
realLife: On a first date: If the waiter gets your order wrong, they’ll see a flash of your fire. Laugh about it together.
In a fight: You blow up fast and cool down fast. Say sorry for the words, even if the feeling was fair.
tips: Make one rule: nothing sent and nothing decided while it’s hot. Write it, wait twenty minutes, then choose. You keep the honesty and lose the damage.
match: Best with: Someone calm and secure, who doesn’t take every thunderclap personally.
Green flag: They stay steady and say “let’s talk when we’re both calm”.
Careful with: Someone who meets your storm with one of their own. Two monsoons, one roof.
