behaviors: Most nights, you soften an angry message before you send it.
A bad day at work comes home with you for an hour, then you let it go.
After a big fight, you need a night’s sleep to really feel okay.
strengths: You can pull yourself back from the edge, and you own it when you can’t.
weaknesses: Stress from outside the relationship makes your count shorter inside it.
realLife: On a first date: If something goes wrong, you sigh, then laugh, and the evening is fine.
In a fight: You get through the first round calmly. Ask for a pause before round two.
tips: Know your short-count days: hungry, tired, after a bad meeting. On those days, eat first and talk later.
match: Best with: Someone patient who gives you a minute when you need one.
Green flag: They say “let’s take five” instead of pushing through a hot moment.
Careful with: Someone who picks fights when you’re tired and hungry.

tests.title: Consistency Need
tests.subtitle: How much routine contact matters
tests.description: Shows how important stable communication routines are for your emotional safety.
tests.whatYouLearn: Whether you need predictable contact or you’re fine with flexible rhythms.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Prevents hot/cold mismatches where one person needs routine and the other is random.

questions.text: For a month they’ve texted good morning every day. Today, nothing by noon. You…

options.text: Honestly wouldn’t notice
Notice straight away and check in
Clock it, and wait to see

questions.text: Calls with the person you’re seeing: which sounds better?

options.text: Whenever we both feel like it
A call every night at 10

questions.text: They promised to visit on Sunday. Saturday night: “Can we do next Sunday instead?” You…

options.text: Feel let down. A plan is a promise
Sure! Next Sunday it is
Okay, but it takes some shine off the week

questions.text: Weekends with someone you’re seeing. What feels best?

options.text: A rough idea, details on Saturday
Our standing Saturday thing, every week
Decide that morning. Maybe a road trip
Plan it by Thursday

questions.text: Exam season for them: they can only talk every two or three days. You…

options.text: Miss them, but manage fine
Ask for a fixed five-minute call, even daily
Totally fine. We’ll talk after the exams

questions.text: Someone being on time and calling when they said they would feels like…

options.text: Nice, but I don’t keep count
Respect. It matters a lot
Not a big deal. Life happens
Important for big things, not small ones

questions.text: They’re sweet and fun, but text in bursts: three days of chat, then two of silence. You…

options.text: Ask them for a steadier rhythm
Love the bursts, don’t mind the gaps
It would wear me out over time
Enjoy it, though steadier would be nice

questions.text: Your family has had the same Sunday morning call for years. Rituals like that are…

options.text: A bit much. I’d rather call when I feel like it
Sweet, as long as they’re not rules
My favourite thing. I’d want one with my person too

tests.measures: how much routine contact and predictable behavior you need from a partner

VeryHigh.label: The Clockwork Romantic
summaries: Steady, predictable love is the most romantic thing there is.

For you, consistency is respect. Calls when they said, plans that stay put, the same warm hello every morning. Hot-and-cold contact drains you, even when the hot days are lovely. You give the same steadiness you ask for, and people always know they can count on you.
behaviors: A good-morning text that hasn’t come by noon puts your whole morning a little off.
A standing date night that nothing moves sounds like a dream to you.
You remember the plan, the time and the place, and you expect the same back.
strengths: You’re the most dependable person anyone could hope to love.
weaknesses: Real life is messy, and you can read a busy week as a change of heart.
realLife: On a first date: Fixed time, fixed place, and they’re there five minutes early. You’re already charmed.
In a fight: Pick a time to talk and stick to it. Open-ended silence is the hardest part for you.
tips: Build one or two rituals together and let the rest flex. A few fixed points can hold a lot of chaos.
match: Best with: Someone organised and warm, who likes knowing the plan too.
Green flag: They keep the small promises, every time, without being reminded.
Careful with: Someone who calls your need for consistency “too much”.

High.label: The Ritual Keeper
summaries: Little rituals are how you know you’re loved.

You feel close through rhythm: the good-night text, the Saturday plan, the call on the drive home. When a routine breaks without a word, you feel it. It’s not about control. Regular contact is simply how love feels real and safe to you.
behaviors: A daily good-morning text matters more to you than a big gift.
A last-minute change of plan takes some of the shine off your week.
You’d rather have a short call every day than a long one once a week.
strengths: You build rituals that make a relationship feel like home.
weaknesses: One broken routine can feel bigger to you than it was ever meant to be.
realLife: On a first date: On time, as planned, and a “home safe?” text afterwards. Perfect.
In a fight: You want to settle on a time to talk, so the silence doesn’t feel endless.
tips: When a routine breaks, ask about it once, kindly, before deciding what it means. Usually it’s just life.
match: Best with: Someone reliable who enjoys a rhythm as much as you do.
Green flag: They tell you before the pattern changes, not after.
Careful with: Hot for a week, gone for three days, back like nothing happened.

Moderate.label: The Soft Schedule
summaries: Steady on the big things, easy on the small ones.

You like reliability where it counts: show up for the important dinner, call when you said you would. The rest can flex. You notice patterns without tracking them, and you’d rather talk about a change than stew over it.
behaviors: A changed plan is fine with notice, and less fine at the last minute.
A rough weekly rhythm feels nice: a few calls, one proper date.
If they go quiet for a few days, you notice, then ask lightly.
strengths: You give stability without turning it into a rulebook.
weaknesses: You might not mention that a change bothered you, because it only bothered you a bit.
realLife: On a first date: You confirm the time, and you’re happy if the place changes on the way.
In a fight: You want a clear plan for when you’ll talk, not an open-ended “later”.
tips: Say which things matter: “Move dinner if you need to, but call if you’re late.” Clear priorities make flexibility easy.
match: Best with: Someone reliable who still enjoys the odd spontaneous plan.
Green flag: They keep their word on the big things and tell you early when plans change.
Careful with: Plans that keep moving, with a new reason every time.

Low.label: The Easy Breeze
summaries: Relaxed about rhythm, warm when you’re there.

You like a bit of regular contact, but you don’t need it on a timetable. Plans can move, replies can wait, and you take it in your stride. Your relaxed way of loving makes busy people feel understood.
behaviors: Exam season with calls every few days? You miss them and manage fine.
A good-morning streak that ends doesn’t worry you.
You like making Saturday plans on Thursday, not a week ahead.
strengths: You adapt to someone’s busy life without making it about you.
weaknesses: You may forget that small routines matter more to them than to you.
realLife: On a first date: You’re fine with “let’s figure it out when we meet”.
In a fight: You don’t need it sorted on a schedule, just sorted.
tips: Ask early what rhythm makes them feel safe. You can give a little more routine easily, and it will mean a lot.
match: Best with: Someone warm and flexible, with a life as full as yours.
Green flag: They keep in touch through busy weeks, even in small ways.
Careful with: Someone who disappears completely and calls it being flexible.

VeryLow.label: The Road-Trip Soul
summaries: The best plans are made that morning.

You like connection that happens on its own: a call because you felt like it, a plan made an hour before. Fixed routines can feel like homework to you, even sweet ones. You’re easy about changes and gaps, and nobody ever feels trapped with you.
behaviors: A rescheduled date gets a cheerful “sure!” and you’ve already made other plans.
Three days of chat and two days of quiet is a normal week to you.
Your best memories together are the unplanned ones.
strengths: You never make anyone feel guilty for a busy week.
weaknesses: Your easy rhythm can feel unpredictable to someone who needs to know when you’ll call.
realLife: On a first date: Planned for coffee, it became street food and a long walk.
In a fight: You’re fine taking a day to cool off. Just tell them when you’ll be back.
tips: Pick one small ritual to keep, like a Sunday call. It costs you nothing and gives a steadier person a lot.
match: Best with: Someone spontaneous who loves a last-minute plan.
Green flag: They say yes to the sudden road trip, and to the quiet week after.
Careful with: Someone who turns every missed call into a trust issue.

Undecided.label: The Soft Schedule

You like reliability where it counts: show up for the important dinner, call when you said you would. The rest can flex. You notice patterns without tracking them, and you’d rather talk about a change than stew over it.
behaviors: A changed plan is fine with notice, and less fine at the last minute.
A rough weekly rhythm feels nice: a few calls, one proper date.
If they go quiet for a few days, you notice, then ask lightly.
strengths: You give stability without turning it into a rulebook.
weaknesses: You might not mention that a change bothered you, because it only bothered you a bit.

In a fight: You want a clear plan for when you’ll talk, not an open-ended “later”.

match: Best with: Someone reliable who still enjoys the odd spontaneous plan.
Green flag: They keep their word on the big things and tell you early when plans change.
Careful with: Plans that keep moving, with a new reason every time.

tests.title: Vulnerability
tests.subtitle: How easily you open up
tests.description: Measures how comfortable you are with opening up emotionally and showing your real self.
tests.whatYouLearn: How easily you share feelings and needs without fear.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Compatibility improves when both people have similar openness (or can gently meet in the middle).

questions.text: You didn’t get the promotion you’d hoped for. That night they ask, “How was your day?” You…

options.text: Give the short version and move on
Tell them everything, even that I nearly cried
Say “long day” and leave it there
Tell them tomorrow, once I’ve calmed down

questions.text: Something they said last week hurt you. They have no idea. You…

options.text: Let it go. Not worth a fuss
Bring it up as a joke
Tell them gently: “That stung a bit”

questions.text: Crying in front of the person you’re seeing feels…

options.text: Impossible. I’ll cry in the bathroom
Fine. They should see the real me

questions.text: On a long drive, they ask: “What was growing up like for you?” You…

options.text: Tell the real story, messy bits too
Keep it to “normal, nothing special”
Share the funny stories, skip the hard ones

questions.text: You’re scared about something big, like moving cities for a new job. You…

options.text: Talk about the plan, not the fear
Keep it to myself till it’s sorted
Mention it, then change the topic fast
Tell them “I’m scared” in those words

options.text: Ask: “Can you just hold me for a bit?”
Put a sad song on my status
Get through it alone
Hope they notice and offer

options.text: Admit it, but play it down
Change the subject fast
Say it honestly: “I’m a bit sensitive about that”

questions.text: Six months in. How much of your inner world do they know?

options.text: The highlights. The rest is mine
A lot, with a few locked drawers
Almost everything, even the weird bits
More than anyone else does

tests.measures: how easily you open up and let yourself be seen

VeryHigh.label: The Heart-on-Sleeve
summaries: What you feel, they’ll know. Usually within minutes.

You don’t do hidden. Your joys, fears, soft spots and tears are all part of how you love, and you share them easily with people you trust. It takes real courage to be this open, and it gives everyone around you permission to be human too.
behaviors: You cry at films, at weddings, sometimes on video calls, and you don’t hide it.
When you need comfort, you simply say “just hold me for a bit”.
Six months in, they know your weird bits, your old wounds and your big dreams.
strengths: Around you, people stop pretending.
weaknesses: You can hand your feelings to people before they’ve earned them.
realLife: On a first date: You laugh, you share a lot, and you know exactly how you feel by dessert.
In a fight: You say exactly how you feel, tears included, and you want to fix it tonight.
tips: Keep your heart open and your timing wise. Let someone earn your deepest stories over a few months.
match: Best with: Someone warm, emotionally brave and careful with what you give.
Green flag: They treat your soft spots carefully and show you theirs.
Careful with: Someone who goes quiet whenever you get real.

High.label: The Real-Talker
summaries: You say what you feel, even the soft stuff.

You let people see the real you: the hard days, the worries, the things that hurt. It doesn’t come without fear. You just decided that being known is worth the risk. People open up around you because you go first.
behaviors: “I’m scared about this job” comes out of you in exactly those words.
You tell them gently when something they said stung.
You can ask for a hug when you need one, without apologising.
strengths: You make honesty feel safe, so the relationship gets real fast.
weaknesses: You can share more than a private person is ready to hold.
realLife: On a first date: You tell them one real thing about your family, and it changes the whole evening.
In a fight: You say “that hurt me” instead of attacking, and it usually softens them.
tips: Notice how much they share back. Match their pace a little, so your openness feels like a gift, not a flood.
match: Best with: Someone emotionally honest who shares back.
Green flag: They match your openness, a little at a time.
Careful with: Someone who listens to everything and shares nothing.

Moderate.label: The Chapter-by-Chapter
summaries: You open up one chapter at a time.

You can be open, and you choose when. Hard days, family stuff, worries: you share them once you’ve sorted your thoughts a little and feel safe. You’re honest without spilling everything at once, which makes people feel trusted as each new chapter comes.
behaviors: You’ll tell them about the missed promotion, once you’ve had a night to think.
You show a soft spot, then quietly make it sound smaller than it is.
Six months in, they know a lot, and you still have a few stories saved for later.
strengths: You share with care, so what you share always means something.
weaknesses: Waiting until you’ve sorted things out can mean they miss the moment to support you.
realLife: On a first date: A good mix: light stories and one real thing about your life.
In a fight: You say what hurt once you’ve had time to find the words.
tips: Now and then, share before it’s sorted. “I don’t know how I feel yet” is a full sentence.
match: Best with: Someone open but patient, who doesn’t push for the next chapter.
Green flag: They remember what you shared and handle it gently.
Careful with: Someone who wants your whole life story on date two.

Low.label: The Velvet Curtain
summaries: Hard shell, soft inside, and worth the effort.

You come across as calm and a little closed, but you’re soft inside, and you know it. You open up slowly, to people who’ve shown they’re safe, and usually with a joke as a shield. Once you trust someone, they see a side of you most people never do.
behaviors: You tell the funny family stories long before the hard ones.
A hurt gets mentioned as a joke first, to test if it’s safe.
When you’re low, you’d rather they noticed than have to ask.
strengths: You’re steady and you don’t overshare, so people feel safe trusting you too.
weaknesses: Your jokes can hide the very moment they could have comforted you.
realLife: On a first date: Charming and fun, with one surprisingly honest line near the end.
In a fight: You need a minute and a soft start before the real feeling comes out.
tips: Next time you joke about something that hurts, add “but honestly, it did hurt a bit.” That second line is where closeness lives.
match: Best with: Someone warm and observant, who can read a quiet day.
Green flag: They take the hint inside your joke seriously, and gently.
Careful with: Someone who laughs off the one serious thing you finally said.

VeryLow.label: The Locked Diary
summaries: Full of stories, and you keep the key.

Your inner world is rich and very private. You handle hard things alone first, and by the time you mention them, they’re usually solved. Life may have taught you that keeping things in was safer, or you simply like your feelings to stay yours. The few people who get to read a page or two never forget it.
behaviors: “Long day” can mean anything from a missed bus to a missed promotion.
You’d rather cry in the bathroom than in front of them, at least for the first year.
You show love by doing, not telling: the fixed tap, the remembered date.
strengths: You’re strong in a crisis and never make your mood someone else’s job.
weaknesses: They can feel shut out of your life, even while you’re sitting right beside them.
realLife: On a first date: You ask great questions, and somehow, by the end, they know almost nothing about you.
In a fight: You go quiet rather than say what hurt. Try one sentence: “That stung.”
tips: Share one small true thing a week, like a worry about work. Opening up is a muscle, and small reps count.
match: Best with: Someone gentle and patient who doesn’t pry and is happy to go first.
Green flag: They share their own soft stuff without expecting yours straight away.
Careful with: Someone who uses what you share against you later. Walk away.

Green flag: They remember what you shared and handle it gently.
Careful with: Someone who wants your whole life story on date two.

tests.subtitle: Independence inside connection
tests.description: Shows if you can keep your identity while staying connected, without fear or control.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your balance between independence and togetherness.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Best matches happen when both people respect autonomy without feeling rejected.

tests.measures: how well you keep your own identity and give a partner freedom without fear or control

VeryHigh.label: The Open Sky
summaries: Love with room for two whole lives in it.

You love fully and hold lightly. You want them to have big dreams, close friends and time of their own, and you keep all of yours too. Distance, trips and separate Diwalis don’t shake you, because your security comes from the bond itself, not from keeping watch.
behaviors: A job in another city? You say “go” and start looking up weekend trains.
Their cricket Sundays are your Sundays to do exactly what you want.
You’re each other’s favourite person, and neither of you is the other’s whole world.
strengths: You make love feel like freedom, which is rare and very attractive.
weaknesses: Someone who needs closeness might read your calm as not needing them.
realLife: On a first date: Two people with full lives, enjoying an evening because they want to, not because they need to.
In a fight: You never use space as a punishment. You take a breath, then come back to it.
tips: Freedom is your gift. Now and then, lean on them: ask for help, admit a bad day. Being needed makes people feel loved.
match: Best with: Someone secure and curious, with a life as full as yours.
Green flag: They cheer for your plans, even the ones that don’t include them.
Careful with: Someone who wants you to shrink your world to fit theirs.

High.label: The Long-String Kite
summaries: Free to fly, and never far from the hand that holds the string.

You can love deeply and still stay yourself. Their trips, friends and evenings alone don’t scare you, and your own life keeps going while you’re in love. You stay connected by choice, not by fear, and that makes being with you feel light.
behaviors: Their week away is your week to catch up with your own people.
“I need an evening to myself” gets an “enjoy!” and no second thoughts.
You go to the wedding out of town alone and send them the best photos.
strengths: People feel free with you, so they keep choosing you.
weaknesses: You can be so relaxed that a more sensitive person wonders if you’d even miss them.
realLife: On a first date: Easy and fun, and you both go home to full, happy lives.
In a fight: You give space without disappearing, and you come back when you said you would.
tips: Say “I missed you” out loud when they get back. Your freedom feels even safer when they know you noticed they were gone.
match: Best with: Someone independent and affectionate, who gives as much freedom as they get.
Green flag: They have their own passions and love hearing about yours.
Careful with: Someone who treats every evening apart as a problem.

Moderate.label: The Gentle Grip
summaries: Secure most days, with the odd little pang.

You’re happy for them to have their own life, and you keep yours. Most of the time it feels easy. Now and then a trip or a night out leaves you with a small pang, and you’re honest enough to notice it rather than act on it.
behaviors: You say “go” to their big job offer, and admit you’re scared of the distance.
Their weekly night out is fine, and you might send one “have fun” text.
A year in, you’ve kept your essentials: your gang, your hobby, your Sunday.
strengths: You hold someone close without holding them back.
weaknesses: You might hide a pang to look relaxed, and it leaks out later.
realLife: On a first date: You enjoy it fully, and you don’t spend the next day waiting by the phone.
In a fight: You can give them space, and you ask for a clear time to talk again.
tips: When a pang comes, say it lightly: “I’ll miss you this weekend.” Pangs you name stay small.
match: Best with: Someone secure with a full life, who keeps you in the loop.
Green flag: They’re free and still thoughtful: a photo from the trip, a call on the way home.
Careful with: Someone who treats every bit of freedom as a test of your patience.

Low.label: The Close Keeper
summaries: You like them close, and you’re learning to loosen your grip.

You love being part of someone’s everyday, and their separate plans can leave you feeling a little outside. You don’t try to control them, but you notice every evening they choose something else. Your loyalty is real, and so is the effort you put into giving them room.
behaviors: You say “have fun” about their cricket Sunday, then check your phone more than usual.
A Diwali apart can feel like a sign, even when it’s just two families.
You’d happily skip a wedding out of town if they can’t come.
strengths: You make the person you love feel like a priority, every day.
weaknesses: Small pangs about their freedom can come out as sulking instead of words.
realLife: On a first date: You love it when they suggest the next date before you have to.
In a fight: You can feel pushed away when they ask for space. Ask when they’ll be back, then trust it.
tips: When they go out without you, plan something lovely for yourself that night. Their freedom gets easier when yours is fun too.
match: Best with: Someone affectionate who includes you and still has a world of their own.
Green flag: They tell you their plans early and invite you into some of them.
Careful with: Someone vague about where they are and who they’re with.

VeryLow.label: The Tight Hug
summaries: You love with both arms, and letting go is hard.

When you love someone, you want to be part of everything: their plans, their evenings, their big days. Time apart can feel like losing your place, and their independence can feel like a door closing. It all comes from a big, loyal heart that’s afraid of being left behind.
behaviors: A week-long trip without you feels like a week of not knowing where you stand.
If they need an evening alone, your first thought is “what’s wrong?”
A year in, your weekends and theirs have quietly become one calendar.
strengths: Your devotion is total. Nobody you love ever doubts they’re wanted.
weaknesses: Holding tight can make someone want room, which makes you hold tighter.
realLife: On a first date: Before the bill comes, you’re already wondering when the next one is.
In a fight: The fear of losing them takes over. Say “I just need to know we’re okay” instead of holding on harder.
tips: Build one thing of your own this month: a class, a weekly game, a friend you see alone. The more you have, the less letting go hurts.
match: Best with: Someone warm and steady who reassures you and gently keeps their own life.
Green flag: They come back from every trip happy to see you, and say so.
Careful with: Someone who uses your fear of distance to control you. That isn’t love.

Careful with: Someone who treats every bit of freedom as a test of your patience.

tests.measures: how directly and clearly you express your needs and feelings

VeryHigh.label: The Straight Shooter
summaries: If you want it, you say it. Same day.

Hints confuse you and guessing games bore you. You say what you want when you want it, and you expect the same back. It keeps life simple and honest, and it can startle people who grew up being careful with every word.
behaviors: You’ll ask “so, are we a thing?” by the third date.
You’d rather have one awkward talk than three weeks of wondering.
When something bugs you, they know before dinner is over.
strengths: Nobody has to decode you. You save everyone hours of overthinking.
weaknesses: Your speed can feel like pressure to someone who needs a day to find their words.
realLife: On a first date: Halfway through, you tell them you’re having a really good time. They blush.
In a fight: Everything is on the table in the first five minutes. Give them a minute to catch up.
tips: Ask before you say it: “Is now a good time?” Your truth lands better when they’re ready for it.
match: Best with: Someone secure who likes clarity and isn’t scared of a direct question.
Green flag: They answer your direct questions directly, even the awkward ones.
Careful with: Someone who calls you “too much” for simply saying what you need.

High.label: The Plain Speaker
summaries: Clear asks, kind words, no guessing games.

You say what you need without making a show of it. To you, clear is kind: it saves everyone from guessing. You can ask, say no and change plans with a smile, and people trust your yes because they’ve heard your no.
behaviors: You say “I’d love a call tonight” instead of waiting to see if they call.
You ask the awkward question early: “Are we exclusive?”
Your “I’m fine” actually means you’re fine.
strengths: Your yes means yes and your no means no. People find that restful.
weaknesses: Not everyone answers as clearly. Their hesitation isn’t always a no.
realLife: On a first date: You say “I don’t drink, but you go ahead” before the waiter even arrives.
In a fight: You say exactly what upset you, once, without bringing up last year.
tips: Leave a little room after you speak. Not everyone finds their words as fast as you do.
match: Best with: Someone who answers clearly and doesn’t hear a plain ask as a demand.
Green flag: They say what they want back, plainly, without you having to dig.
Careful with: Vague, sulky replies when something’s wrong, and “nothing” when you ask.

Moderate.label: The After-Dinner Talker
summaries: You say it all, once the moment feels right.

You’re clear about the big things and gentle with the small ones. You read the room first, choose your moment, and then say what you mean. It keeps things calm, though some things wait longer than they need to while you look for the perfect time.
behaviors: You bring up the hard topic after dinner, never during it.
Small annoyances you let go. Real needs you say out loud, eventually.
You can ask for what you want, but sometimes you wait to be asked first.
strengths: Good timing. When you say something, people are ready to hear it.
weaknesses: The perfect moment rarely comes. Some things stay unsaid while you wait for it.
realLife: On a first date: You let them pick the place, but you’re clear about the time you need to leave.
In a fight: You hold it until you’re both calm, then say it properly.
tips: If you’ve waited three days for the right moment, this is it. Say it now, kindly.
match: Best with: Someone steady who makes it easy to bring things up at any time.
Green flag: They tell you what they need too, so it never feels one-sided.
Careful with: Someone whose mood decides when anything can be discussed.

Low.label: The Hint Dropper
summaries: You say it in clues and hope they solve it.

You do tell people what you need, just in code: a sigh, a sad song on your story, a long tale about how your cousin’s husband plans every anniversary. Saying it plainly feels too exposed, so you leave a trail and see who follows it. The ones who do, you keep for life.
behaviors: You’ll mention a café five times instead of saying “take me there”.
A song on your story is often a message for one person.
When they finally get it, you feel truly seen. When they don’t, you feel invisible.
strengths: Tact. You never make anyone feel cornered.
weaknesses: Most people are bad at clues. Missing your hint doesn’t mean they don’t care.
realLife: On a first date: You say “I’m not that hungry” while eyeing their fries. They’d better offer.
In a fight: You get quieter and drier, waiting for them to ask what’s wrong.
tips: Swap one hint for one sentence this week: “I’d love it if you…” Watch how fast you get what you were hoping for.
match: Best with: Someone attentive who notices small changes and gently asks what’s up.
Green flag: They ask “is something on your mind?” and wait for the answer.
Careful with: Someone who teases you for being “complicated” instead of asking what you meant.

VeryLow.label: The Anything-Is-Fine
summaries: You keep the peace, even when it costs you.

You notice everything and say very little of it. Somewhere along the way you learned that keeping things calm matters more than getting your way, so your needs wait their turn, sometimes forever. People find you easy to be around; fewer know what you actually want.
behaviors: You’ll eat at their favourite place for the fifth time and call it lovely.
You hope they’ll notice you’re upset, and feel lonely when they don’t.
When you finally say something, it’s been building for months, so it comes out bigger.
strengths: You’re easy to be with, and you never make a scene out of small things.
weaknesses: Silence reads as “all good”, so the people who love you miss what you need.
realLife: On a first date: They ask where you want to eat. You say “anything is fine” and quietly hope for dosa.
In a fight: You say “it’s fine.” Inside, it is very much not fine, and it will come out later.
tips: Start tiny: one small want a day, out loud. “I’d like the window seat.” It gets easier, and the people who love you will be glad to know.
match: Best with: Someone patient and curious who asks “what do you want?” and waits for the real answer.
Green flag: They ask your opinion first, and sometimes actually go with it.
Careful with: Someone who always decides and never notices you didn’t get a say.

Undecided.label: The After-Dinner Talker

Small annoyances you let go. Real needs you say out loud, eventually.
You can ask for what you want, but sometimes you wait to be asked first.

In a fight: You hold it until you’re both calm, then say it properly.

Careful with: Someone whose mood decides when anything can be discussed.

tests.subtitle: Warmth vs coldness in talks
tests.description: Measures whether your communication tone is warm/supportive or cold/sharp under stress.
tests.whatYouLearn: How your tone feels to a partner during serious talks.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Avoids mismatch where one needs softness and the other communicates too harshly.

Say “That joke hurt. Can we talk?”

Laugh: “Yes, Ma. Dal chawal. Love you.”

questions.text: In a heated moment, people can tell you’re upset because…

options.text: My voice goes calm, polite and ice-cold
I say “I’m upset” in my normal voice
I get loud, then quiet, then say sorry

tests.measures: how warm or cold your tone becomes during serious conversations

VeryHigh.label: The Soft Landing
summaries: Even your angriest words land gently.

Your voice stays kind when everything else gets loud. You know a hard talk can leave marks, so you choose words that tell the other person they’re still safe with you. People come out of a fight with you feeling closer, which is rare.
behaviors: You start a hard talk with what you love about them, then the problem.
You reach for their hand halfway through an argument.
Even when you’re hurt, you check whether they’re okay.
strengths: Fights with you end in a hug, not a cold war.
weaknesses: You might swallow real anger to keep things soft, and it has to go somewhere.
realLife: On a first date: The place is overbooked and they’re mortified. You turn it into an adventure at the momo stall next door.
In a fight: Your voice stays low and your words stay kind, even when you’re shaking inside.
tips: Your anger is allowed in the room too. Say “I’m really angry” in your soft voice. Nothing will break.
match: Best with: Someone who treasures your gentleness and gives it back on hard days.
Green flag: They thank you when you stay kind in a tough moment.
Careful with: Someone who uses your softness to avoid ever hearing a hard truth.

High.label: The Warm Chai
summaries: Hard talks with you still feel warm.

Even when you’re annoyed, your voice stays kind. You believe how you say something matters as much as what you say, and you’d rather be gentle than win. People bring you their hard news because they know you won’t make them feel small.
behaviors: You can say “that hurt me” without it sounding like an attack.
Even on deadline days it’s “call you at 8, miss you”, not just “busy”.
You apologise for your tone, even when you were right about the point.
strengths: People can argue with you and still feel respected.
weaknesses: So much warmth can hide how serious you are. Sometimes they miss the point.
realLife: On a first date: They knock water onto your lap. You laugh, dab it off, and tell them it’s good luck.
In a fight: You say “I’m upset, and I still love you,” and mean both.
tips: When it really matters, say plainly “this is serious for me.” Your warmth can make big things sound small.
match: Best with: Someone who answers softness with softness and never mistakes it for weakness.
Green flag: They keep their voice kind when they’re upset too.
Careful with: Someone who gets meaner the calmer you stay.

Moderate.label: The Warm Kettle
summaries: Warm most days, one loud whistle under pressure.

You’re warm by nature and you try hard to stay that way in a tough talk, and most of the time you manage. When the pressure builds, a sharp line or a long sigh escapes. You usually catch it and say sorry before the evening is over.
behaviors: You start every hard talk kindly. It’s near the end that your tone slips.
You hear yourself get clipped and say “sorry, that came out wrong”.
Stressful weeks show in your voice before they show anywhere else.
strengths: You catch yourself. Your apologies for tone come fast and real.
weaknesses: One sharp line at the end can undo an hour of kind talking.
realLife: On a first date: Traffic made you twenty minutes late and flustered. By the time the starters arrive, you’re laughing about it.
In a fight: You start kind, get louder by round three, then stop and say “okay, let me try that again”.
tips: Learn your whistle: the moment your sentences get short. That’s your cue to pause, sip some water and slow down.
match: Best with: Someone calm who forgives a slip and doesn’t keep a list of them.
Green flag: They notice when you’re stressed and slow the talk down for you.
Careful with: Someone who picks heavy topics on your most stressful days.

Low.label: The Cold Front
summaries: When you’re upset, the temperature drops.

You don’t shout. When something hurts, you go cool, polite and very short, and the warmth comes back only once you feel safe again. It’s how you protect yourself. The people around you feel the chill even when you say nothing at all.
behaviors: Your flat “it’s fine” is the loudest thing you say.
Stress turns your replies into one word, even with people you love.
You warm up again once you feel heard, not a minute before.
strengths: You rarely say something cruel. Your cool keeps you from words you’d regret.
weaknesses: Cold can hurt as much as loud. Your silence can land like punishment, even when it isn’t.
realLife: On a first date: Long day, short answers. Say it out loud: “I’m tired, give me ten minutes to warm up.”
In a fight: You go quiet and formal. Inside, you’re waiting for them to make it safe to thaw.
tips: Say the feeling, not just the temperature: “I’m hurt and I need a bit of time.” It turns a cold wall into an open door.
match: Best with: Someone gentle and patient who can sit near you without forcing the talk.
Green flag: They notice the chill and ask kindly, instead of going cold back.
Careful with: Someone who goes cold right back. Then nobody makes the first move.

VeryLow.label: The Green Chilli
summaries: Hot words, cold silences, and a big heart under both.

When you’re hurt, your words get sharp or your voice goes ice-cold, and both happen fast. It isn’t that you don’t care; you care so much that it comes out as heat. The people who stay close learn that the sting passes and the loyal, honest you is still there.
behaviors: A forgotten plan can get a “don’t bother” before they’ve even explained.
Sarcasm is your first language when you feel let down.
Once you cool down, you’re fiercely sweet, and a little embarrassed.
strengths: You’re never fake. People always know exactly how you feel.
weaknesses: Words said in heat stay with people long after the heat is gone.
realLife: On a first date: The waiter gets your order wrong. You catch your tone halfway and finish with a big smile.
In a fight: The sharpest line comes out first. Five minutes later, you wish you could take it back.
tips: When you feel the heat rising, say “give me ten minutes” and walk around the block. Then say the same thing, softer.
match: Best with: Someone steady who doesn’t take your first sharp line personally, and tells you when one lands.
Green flag: They stay calm when you flare up, and still tell you when a line hurt.
Careful with: Someone who matches your fire line for line. Two chillies make a very hot kitchen.

Undecided.label: The Warm Kettle
summaries: Warm most days, one loud whistle under pressure.

You’re warm by nature and you try hard to stay that way in a tough talk, and most of the time you manage. When the pressure builds, a sharp line or a long sigh escapes. You usually catch it and say sorry before the evening is over.

You hear yourself get clipped and say “sorry, that came out wrong”.
Stressful weeks show in your voice before they show anywhere else.

weaknesses: One sharp line at the end can undo an hour of kind talking.

In a fight: You start kind, get louder by round three, then stop and say “okay, let me try that again”.
tips: Learn your whistle: the moment your sentences get short. That’s your cue to pause, sip some water and slow down.
match: Best with: Someone calm who forgives a slip and doesn’t keep a list of them.
Green flag: They notice when you’re stressed and slow the talk down for you.
Careful with: Someone who picks heavy topics on your most stressful days.

tests.title: Listening
tests.subtitle: How well you hear and validate
tests.description: Measures active listening, validation, and whether you truly hear a partner (not just reply).
tests.whatYouLearn: Your ability to listen without defensiveness.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Strong listening creates emotional safety and reduces repetitive fights.

questions.text: They’re telling you about office drama. It’s the last over of the match. You…

options.text: Nod along, one eye on the score
Ask “sorry, what?” once the over ends
“One sec, last over!” Then all ears
Mute the TV and turn to face them

options.text: Let them finish, rehearsing your reply
Jump in: “That’s not what happened”
Let them finish, then ask what hurt most

questions.text: Last week they mentioned a big interview on Thursday. It’s Thursday morning. You…

options.text: Remember it at night and ask how it went
Text “All the best today! Tell me after?”
Thursday? What was Thursday?
Remember only when they bring it up

questions.text: In a group conversation, you’re usually the one…

options.text: Asking “wait, then what happened?”
With an even better story ready

questions.text: They’re hurt you didn’t invite them to your team dinner. You think it’s silly. You…

options.text: Explain why it really wasn’t a big deal
Say sorry and quickly move on
Say “That makes sense. I’d feel left out too.”
Tell them they’re overthinking it

options.text: Glance, then right back to them
Reply fast: “Go on, I’m listening!”
Flip it face down without looking
Read it and lose the thread a bit

questions.text: Turns out you misheard them and argued about the wrong thing for ten minutes. You…

options.text: Move on quietly like it never happened
Laugh: “Oh no, I totally misheard. Sorry!”
Say “Well, you weren’t very clear”
Ask them to explain again so you get it right

questions.text: They’re venting about their boss for the third time this week. You…

options.text: Scroll Instagram while saying “haan, haan”
Listen a bit, then steer to something lighter
Listen, but your mind drifts to dinner
Ask for today’s episode and settle in

tests.measures: how well you truly hear and validate what your partner communicates

VeryHigh.label: The Human Diary
summaries: You remember the interview date, and ask how it went.

When someone talks to you, they get all of you: phone down, eyes up, full attention. You hear the words and the feeling under them, and you remember both for weeks. People open up to you without meaning to, and leave feeling understood.
behaviors: You text “all the best” on the morning of their big interview, without a reminder.
You notice when today’s “I’m fine” sounds different from yesterday’s.
You can say “I got that wrong, tell me again” without a second of pride.
strengths: People feel truly heard around you, which is rarer than it should be.
weaknesses: You hold everyone’s stories, and sometimes nobody asks for yours.
realLife: On a first date: Two hours in, you know their childhood nickname, their sister’s exams and their fear of pigeons.
In a fight: You repeat back what they said before you answer. They calm down halfway through.
tips: Your attention is a gift. Make sure there’s someone in your life who gives you the same one.
match: Best with: Someone who listens back and remembers your things the way you remember theirs.
Green flag: They ask you real follow-up questions, not just “and you?”
Careful with: Someone who only calls when they need a listener.

High.label: The Then-What-Happened
summaries: Invested in every story, right up to the plot twist.

You love people’s stories and you show it: you ask the next question, you remember the names, you turn away from the screen. You let people finish before you speak, and you can hear someone out even when you see it differently.
behaviors: You remember their colleague’s name and ask how the office feud is going.
You mute the match when they start a story that matters.
You say “that makes sense” before you give your side.
strengths: People feel interesting when they talk to you.
weaknesses: You’re so good at asking that you forget to share your own stuff.
realLife: On a first date: They mention their dog once. Twenty minutes later you’ve seen forty photos and asked about each one.
In a fight: You let them finish, then ask “what hurt most?” It changes the whole fight.
tips: Take your turn too. Tell them your story and let them ask the questions. Being known is part of being close.
match: Best with: Someone who loves telling stories and asks you just as many questions back.
Green flag: They remember what you told them last week, too.
Careful with: Someone who treats every chat as an audience for their monologue.

Moderate.label: The Gist Catcher
summaries: You get the story, if not always the feeling under it.

You’re a good listener on a good day and a distracted one on a bad one. You catch the main point and can repeat it back, but the feeling underneath sometimes slips past. When you’re rested and the phone is away, you’re surprisingly good at this.
behaviors: You listen beautifully over chai and less well during a cricket match.
You remember the big dates, if not the small ones.
You catch what they said, and sometimes miss why it mattered.
strengths: You get to the main point fast and rarely get lost in details.
weaknesses: Sometimes the detail was the point, and the gist misses it.
realLife: On a first date: You’re listening well until the waiter arrives, then lose the thread. “Sorry, where were we?” works.
In a fight: You get the point of their complaint, but miss how much it hurt.
tips: Ask one question about the feeling, not the facts: “How did that feel?” It turns good listening into great.
match: Best with: Someone who says “I don’t need advice, just listen” when that’s what they need.
Green flag: They’re patient when you ask them to repeat something.
Careful with: Someone who saves big talks for when you’re clearly busy or tired.

Low.label: The Ready Reply
summaries: Your answer is loading before they’ve finished.

You’re quick and you love a good conversation, so your mind races ahead to what you’ll say next. You hear the words, but your reply is often ready before the other person is done. It comes from enthusiasm, not from not caring.
behaviors: You jump in to correct a detail while they’re still mid-story.
Their bad day reminds you of yours, and you tell them all about it.
You finish their sentences, sometimes right, sometimes not.
strengths: Conversations with you never go flat. You always have something to add.
weaknesses: Waiting to talk isn’t the same as listening, and people can feel the difference.
realLife: On a first date: You have a great story for every one of theirs. Try one “and then what?” instead.
In a fight: You’re answering point one while they’re still on point three.
tips: Before you reply, repeat back one thing they said: “So the worst part was…” It slows you down in the best way.
match: Best with: Someone confident who will happily say “let me finish” and laugh about it.
Green flag: They tell you when they just need you to hear them out.
Careful with: Someone who goes quiet instead of telling you they felt cut off.

VeryLow.label: The Hundred Tabs
summaries: A busy mind, a big heart, and a phone that keeps buzzing.

Your head is always running: work, plans, the match, the next thing. You care about people a lot, but your attention jumps around, so stories reach you in pieces. When something is truly big you show up; it’s the everyday listening that slips through.
behaviors: You catch the headline of their day and miss the bit that mattered most.
Your “haan, haan” sometimes does the listening while your mind is elsewhere.
When they say “you never listen”, you’re honestly surprised, and a little guilty.
strengths: You bring energy and ideas to every conversation.
weaknesses: Half-listening feels like not caring to the person talking, even when you care a lot.
realLife: On a first date: Your phone buzzes three times. Put it in your bag before the starters arrive and watch the date change.
In a fight: You answer what you think they said. Ask “wait, can you say that again?” It saves twenty minutes.
tips: Pick one conversation a day for full attention: phone away, eyes up, one follow-up question. That’s all it takes to feel close.
match: Best with: Someone easygoing who can say “phone down, this one matters” without a fight.
Green flag: They tell you plainly when they need your full attention.
Careful with: Someone who quizzes you on what they said instead of just asking for your attention.

Undecided.label: The Gist Catcher

You remember the big dates, if not the small ones.
You catch what they said, and sometimes miss why it mattered.

In a fight: You get the point of their complaint, but miss how much it hurt.

Green flag: They’re patient when you ask them to repeat something.
Careful with: Someone who saves big talks for when you’re clearly busy or tired.

tests.title: Conflict Talk
tests.subtitle: Do you talk problems through
tests.description: Shows whether you can discuss problems directly or avoid until things explode.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your comfort with hard conversations.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps predict if issues get solved early or become long-term resentment.

questions.text: They’re late again, the third time this month. You’ve been waiting 40 minutes. You…

options.text: Make a joke about it and hope it lands
Say nothing now, and explode on the fifth time
Calmly: “Can we talk about you running late?”
Say nothing. It’s not worth a fight

questions.text: They text “We need to talk.” Your stomach drops. You…

options.text: Suddenly remember an urgent call
Reply “Okay. Call now?”
Reply “Is it bad?” and brace yourself

questions.text: A small thing bugs you. You usually…

options.text: Let it go. Most things pass
Mention it while it’s still small

questions.text: Your parents bring up “settling down” at every single meal. You…

options.text: Answer with jokes until they drop it
Change the topic to your cousin’s new car
Say “Not now, Ma” every time
Sit them down and talk about it properly

questions.text: The argument is going in circles and it’s nearly 1 am. You…

options.text: Keep talking. You’re not sleeping on this
Say “You’re right, whatever” to end it
Suggest a pause: “Let’s finish this at 7 tomorrow”
Go to sleep and hope it’s gone by morning

questions.text: Your best friend has been weirdly distant all week. You…

options.text: Ask them straight: “Did I do something?”
Ask a mutual friend what’s going on
Give it a week and see
Get distant back

questions.text: A colleague presents your idea as theirs in a meeting. You…

options.text: Vent about it at chai, never to them
Say “building on my idea from last week…” next time
Talk to them after: “That was mine. What happened?”
Never share an idea with them again

questions.text: They spend much more freely than you, and it’s starting to worry you. You…

options.text: Bring it up on a calm Sunday: “Can we talk money?”
Hope it sorts itself out with time
Mention it in passing and watch their reaction
Make comments every time they buy something

tests.measures: how well you discuss problems and disagreements directly

VeryHigh.label: The Never-Sleep-Angry
summaries: No fight goes to bed with you. Ever.

You believe almost anything can be fixed by talking, and you’re willing to stay in the room until it is. Discomfort doesn’t scare you; silence does. You name problems early and stay with them, which keeps your relationships honest and very rarely stuck.
behaviors: You’d rather talk until 1 am than sleep on a fight.
You raise things the day they happen, kindly but clearly.
Silent treatments don’t survive around you. You knock on the door.
strengths: Nothing gets swept under the rug. Your relationships stay clean and current.
weaknesses: Some people need space before they can talk. Pushing now can make it harder.
realLife: On a first date: You ask what they’re looking for and how they handle fights. On date one. They’re impressed, mostly.
In a fight: You keep going until it’s sorted. Check whether they need a breather first.
tips: Let some talks wait till morning. A rested “let’s fix this” often works better than a tired one at midnight.
match: Best with: Someone who feels safe in honest talks and doesn’t shut down when it gets heavy.
Green flag: They stay at the table when it gets uncomfortable.
Careful with: Someone who goes silent for days and calls it “keeping the peace”.

High.label: The Sunday Sit-Down
summaries: Problems get a proper talk, not a silent week.

When something’s off, you’d rather sit down and talk it through than let it hang in the air. You can stay in an uncomfortable conversation without attacking or running, and you care more about fixing the problem than winning the argument.
behaviors: You bring up the money worry on a calm Sunday, not in the middle of a fight.
You ask “did I do something?” instead of waiting for things to feel normal.
If a talk goes in circles, you suggest a break and actually come back to it.
strengths: Problems around you get solved while they’re still small.
weaknesses: Not everyone is ready to talk when you are. Some people need a day first.
realLife: On a first date: They make a joke that lands wrong. You say so lightly, they apologise, and the date gets better.
In a fight: You say “let’s pause and finish this at 7”, and at 7, you’re there.
tips: Ask “is now a good time?” before a hard talk. People listen better once they’ve said yes.
match: Best with: Someone who would rather solve a problem together than win it.
Green flag: They come back to a paused talk without being reminded.
Careful with: “I don’t want to talk about it”, about everything, forever.

Moderate.label: The Battle Picker
summaries: The big stuff gets a talk. The small stuff gets a shrug.

You don’t fight about everything and you don’t dodge everything either. You’ve learned to tell which problems will grow and which will fade, and you speak up for the first kind. Your judgement is usually good, though sometimes a ‘small’ one turns out to be big.
behaviors: You’ll talk about money and family, and let the toothpaste cap go.
You raise things with a joke first, and get serious if the joke doesn’t land.
You can stay in a hard talk, but you need a break if it passes the hour mark.
strengths: You save your energy for what matters, so when you raise something, people listen.
weaknesses: What feels small to you might be big to them, and they may be waiting for you to ask.
realLife: On a first date: They’re fifteen minutes late. You let it go. If it happens again on date three, you’ll say something.
In a fight: You stick to the main issue and refuse to drag in last Diwali.
tips: Every few weeks, ask: “Anything small bugging you?” Small things are easiest to fix early.
match: Best with: Someone who also knows which hills are worth climbing.
Green flag: They tell you when something small to you is big to them.
Careful with: Someone who wants to talk out every single thing, every single day.

Low.label: The Wait-and-See
summaries: You hope it passes. Sometimes it does.

You’d rather give a problem time than talk about it right now. Plenty of small things do fade, so your patience often works. The ones that don’t fade stay inside, stacking up quietly, until one small thing brings all of them out at once.
behaviors: You let the third late arrival slide, and the fifth one gets everything.
You ask a mutual friend what’s wrong before you ask them.
You do talk about problems, usually a few weeks late.
strengths: Patience. You don’t make drama out of passing moods.
weaknesses: Waiting too long turns a five-minute talk into a three-hour fight.
realLife: On a first date: The food is cold and you eat it anyway. You’ll mention it to your sister later.
In a fight: A small thing sets it off, and three weeks of stored-up stuff comes out together.
tips: Try a 48-hour rule: if it still bugs you after two days, say it, calmly and small.
match: Best with: Someone calm who notices when you’re holding something and invites it out.
Green flag: They ask “is everything okay with us?” now and then, and mean it.
Careful with: Someone who also waits. Months can pass without a single real talk.

VeryLow.label: The Escape Artist
summaries: Hard talk incoming? You’ve already left the room.

You can feel a conflict coming from a mile away, and you’re gone before it lands: a joke, a new topic, a sudden call. It comes from wanting things to stay nice. The trouble is that problems wait for you, and they don’t get smaller while they wait.
behaviors: “We need to talk” makes you suddenly, urgently busy.
You’ll go along with a plan you hate rather than discuss it.
Things feel peaceful for months, until one day they very much don’t.
strengths: You keep everyday life light and easy. Nobody walks on eggshells around you.
weaknesses: Avoided talks don’t disappear. They come back bigger, usually at the worst time.
realLife: On a first date: They ask about your ex. You make a joke and somehow end up talking about pani puri.
In a fight: You say “whatever you think” and take a very long shower. The fight waits for you outside.
tips: Try a small one: “Can I tell you something that bothered me? It’s tiny.” Small talks are practice for the big ones.
match: Best with: Someone gentle who brings things up softly and keeps hard talks short and safe.
Green flag: They raise problems calmly, without blame, one issue at a time.
Careful with: Someone who turns every small talk into a big fight. It teaches you to run further.

Undecided.label: The Battle Picker
summaries: The big stuff gets a talk. The small stuff gets a shrug.

You don’t fight about everything and you don’t dodge everything either. You’ve learned to tell which problems will grow and which will fade, and you speak up for the first kind. Your judgement is usually good, though sometimes a ‘small’ one turns out to be big.
behaviors: You’ll talk about money and family, and let the toothpaste cap go.
You raise things with a joke first, and get serious if the joke doesn’t land.
You can stay in a hard talk, but you need a break if it passes the hour mark.

weaknesses: What feels small to you might be big to them, and they may be waiting for you to ask.
realLife: On a first date: They’re fifteen minutes late. You let it go. If it happens again on date three, you’ll say something.
In a fight: You stick to the main issue and refuse to drag in last Diwali.

match: Best with: Someone who also knows which hills are worth climbing.
Green flag: They tell you when something small to you is big to them.
Careful with: Someone who wants to talk out every single thing, every single day.

tests.title: Texting Style
tests.subtitle: Pacing, clarity, reply energy
tests.description: Measures how you use texting: fast replies vs slow, clarity vs dryness, emotional signal vs minimal.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your texting rhythm and how much meaning you attach to it.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Prevents mismatch: one sees slow replies as disrespect, the other sees it as normal.

questions.text: They text “Reached home safe 🙂” at 11:40 pm. You…

options.text: Reply in a minute: “Yay! Sleep well 😴”
Heart it and go to sleep
Reply in the morning
Leave it on seen. It didn’t need a reply

questions.text: Your texts are usually…

options.text: Long paras and voice notes
One-liners, maybe a 👍

questions.text: Busy workday. The person you’re talking to sends a meme at 11 am. You…

options.text: Send one back right away. Work can wait thirty seconds
React 😂 now, reply properly at lunch
Reply in the evening when you’re free
It was just a meme. No reply needed

questions.text: They read your text wrong and replied “ok.” You…

options.text: Send a voice note straight away to clear it up
Text “that came out wrong, I meant…”
Wait and see if it was really a problem
Reply “ok” back. Two can play

questions.text: How do you start the day with someone you’re getting to know?

options.text: A good-morning text and a photo of my chai
A quick “gm” if I remember
I wait for them to text first
Mornings are not for texting

questions.text: When you reply late, it usually means…

options.text: Something came up, and I’ll say what
Nothing. I reply when I reply

questions.text: You’re upset with them. Over text you…

options.text: Say it: “That bothered me. Can we talk tonight?”
Keep texting normally and save it for when you meet
Get shorter and drier until they notice
Go quiet for a while

questions.text: Your ideal texting rhythm with someone you like:

options.text: All day: memes, updates, the little things
One proper chat every evening
A few texts a day, calls for real talk
Only to make plans. Talking is for meeting

tests.measures: how you use texting as a communication and connection tool

VeryHigh.label: The Voice-Note Poet
summaries: You text like you talk: warm, quick, never just “ok”.
For you, texting isn’t admin. It’s how closeness grows between dates. You notice small things, send them on, and reply fast because you want to. A dry “k” can quietly ruin your evening.
behaviors: You share the small stuff: the auto driver’s argument, your lunch, the sunset from the office window.
You read tone in every message, so warmth matters to you.
A reply that takes all day can feel like a mood, even when it isn’t.
strengths: Nobody wonders where they stand with you.
weaknesses: You can read silence as rejection when they’re just busy.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve sent three “almost there!” updates before you arrive.
In a fight: You’d rather send a long, honest voice note than wait till morning.
tips: Tell them in week one what rhythm feels good to you. It saves a hundred overthought evenings.
match: Best with: Someone who loves a chatty phone as much as you, or who tells you their rhythm in week one.
Green flag: They send voice notes back.
Careful with: Hot and cold replies that keep you guessing.

High.label: The Good-Morning Texter
summaries: Steady, warm, and first to check in.
You like someone to know they’re on your mind, so you check in, reply fast and explain when you can’t. Texting is part of how you care. You notice when it’s not returned.
behaviors: Good-morning and good-night texts feel natural to you.
You clear up a misread message the same day.
You remember to ask how their big meeting went.
strengths: People never wonder whether you care.
weaknesses: A slow reply can sting more than it should.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve sent “running five minutes late, sorry!” before anyone even asked.
In a fight: You want to sort it the same day, ideally by voice.
tips: Let a slow reply just be a slow reply. Ask when you meet instead of guessing at 1 am.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys a daily chat, or a slower texter who tells you their rhythm upfront.
Green flag: They reply with questions, not just reactions.
Careful with: Replies that turn warm only when they want something.

Moderate.label: The Balanced Replier
summaries: Warm when it matters, quiet when it doesn’t.
You text enough to stay close and not so much that it runs your day. You can be chatty with the right person and brief when life is busy. Most people find your rhythm easy.
behaviors: You reply when you can, and say so when you can’t.
You enjoy a good chat, but you won’t text through dinner with friends.
You match their energy rather than set the pace.
strengths: You adapt: chatty with chatty people, calm with calm ones.
weaknesses: Matching their energy can mean nobody makes the first move.
realLife: On a first date: One “see you at 7?” and a “here!” when you arrive.
In a fight: You’ll text that you’re upset and talk it out properly later.
tips: Now and then, text first. You don’t always have to wait to match their energy.
match: Best with: Almost anyone who says clearly what they like.
Green flag: They’re easy to read: warm texts, clear plans.
Careful with: Hot one day, gone the next, with no explanation.

Low.label: The Call-Me Type
summaries: Texts for plans, voice for feelings.
You keep texting practical and let real feelings happen on a call or in person. You’re warm, just not in writing. A whole relationship in chat bubbles sounds tiring to you.
behaviors: You’ll text “free tonight?” and say the sweet stuff when you meet.
You’d rather call for two minutes than type for twenty.
You don’t read much into their reply speed, and hope they don’t read into yours.
strengths: You don’t overthink texts, so small things stay small.
weaknesses: Your short replies can look like low interest to a chatty partner.
realLife: On a first date: You confirm with one text and keep the stories for the date.
In a fight: You’ll say “can we talk on call?” and you’re usually right.
tips: Add one small warm text a day, even just a photo. It costs you ten seconds and tells them they’re on your mind.
match: Best with: Someone who likes calls and plans more than all-day chat.
Green flag: They pick up when you call and are fine with quiet days.
Careful with: Someone who reads every slow reply as a sign.

VeryLow.label: The Seen-Zone Monk
summaries: Minimal texter, full presence in person.

Your phone is a tool, not a hangout. You save your attention for real conversations, and you mean every word you do send. People who know you don’t read your short replies as cold; people who don’t, sometimes do.
behaviors: You’d rather plan the next chai date than chat until 2 am.
A long silence from you rarely means anything is wrong.
When you show up in person, you’re all there, phone face down.
strengths: No mind games: your texts mean exactly what they say.
weaknesses: A one-word reply can feel like a closed door to someone who loves texting.
realLife: On a first date: You arrive on time, without a single “on my way” text.
In a fight: You go quiet to think. Tell them it’s thinking, not punishing.
tips: Say your rhythm out loud early: “I’m not a texter, but I’m all in when we meet.” It changes how every short reply reads.
match: Best with: Someone calm who likes meeting more than messaging.
Green flag: They make plans and keep them, without needing daily texts.
Careful with: Someone who keeps score of reply times.

Undecided.label: The Balanced Replier
summaries: Warm when it matters, quiet when it doesn’t.
You text enough to stay close and not so much that it runs your day. You can be chatty with the right person and brief when life is busy. Most people find your rhythm easy.
behaviors: You reply when you can, and say so when you can’t.
You enjoy a good chat, but you won’t text through dinner with friends.
You match their energy rather than set the pace.
strengths: You adapt: chatty with chatty people, calm with calm ones.
weaknesses: Matching their energy can mean nobody makes the first move.
realLife: On a first date: One “see you at 7?” and a “here!” when you arrive.
In a fight: You’ll text that you’re upset and talk it out properly later.
tips: Now and then, text first. You don’t always have to wait to match their energy.
match: Best with: Almost anyone who says clearly what they like.
Green flag: They’re easy to read: warm texts, clear plans.
Careful with: Hot one day, gone the next, with no explanation.

tests.title: Boundaries Talk
tests.subtitle: Can you set limits without drama
tests.description: Measures whether you can set boundaries clearly and respectfully (time, privacy, needs).
tests.whatYouLearn: Your ability to communicate limits without guilt or aggression.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Boundaries reduce jealousy, resentment, and control issues.

Say okay, but check in a few times

Lie awake fuming and say nothing
Pop out: “Guys, can we wrap up by 12? Early day.”

questions.text: They keep planning your weekends with their family without asking you. You…

options.text: Go along every time. It’s easier
Say yes to some, invent plans for others
Go, but be grumpy the whole day
Say “I love your family, but check with me first?”

tests.measures: how clearly and calmly you communicate personal boundaries

VeryHigh.label: The Calm Gatekeeper
summaries: Clear lines, open heart, zero drama.

You know exactly where your lines are, you say them calmly and early, and you respect other people’s just as easily. Saying no doesn’t make you feel guilty, and hearing no doesn’t make you feel attacked. People feel safe with you because nothing is hidden.
behaviors: You say what you’re comfortable with in week one, kindly and without a speech.
Their “I need a night alone” gets an “enjoy it” while you order your own biryani.
You never need to control them to feel secure.
strengths: Resentment doesn’t build up around you, because nothing goes unsaid.
weaknesses: Your ease with limits can feel cool to someone still learning to say theirs.
realLife: On a first date: You say you’d like to take things slow, and that you’d love a second date. Both land perfectly.
In a fight: “I won’t be spoken to like that. Let’s talk when we’re calmer.” You leave the door open.
tips: When someone is new to limits, explain yours once, warmly. Your calm makes it easier for them to find theirs.
match: Best with: Someone secure who likes clear lines and doesn’t read them as distance.
Green flag: They respect your no the first time, without a sulk.
Careful with: Someone who treats every limit you set as a puzzle to get around.

High.label: The Gentle No
summaries: You say no kindly, and people still feel loved.

You can say what you’re okay with and what you’re not, without guilt and without a fight. You learned somewhere that a clear no protects a relationship better than a bitter yes. And when someone sets a limit with you, you hear it without taking it personally.
behaviors: You say “not tonight, I’m wiped. Tomorrow?” and nobody feels rejected.
When they need a night alone, you say “of course” and mean it.
You offer what you can give when you say no to what you can’t.
strengths: People trust your yes, because they know you can say no.
weaknesses: Your calm no can feel abrupt to someone who grew up with lots of explaining.
realLife: On a first date: They suggest a horror film. You say “not my thing, but I’d love the comedy” and they happily switch.
In a fight: You say “I need ten minutes, then I’ll come back,” and you do.
tips: Add one warm line to every no: “I can’t do Saturday, but I’d love Sunday.” Your no becomes an invitation.
match: Best with: Someone who says their limits as clearly as you do.
Green flag: They thank you for saying what you need instead of making them guess.
Careful with: Someone who calls every limit you set “selfish”.

Moderate.label: The Flexible Fence
summaries: Firm on the big stuff, bendy on the rest.

You have limits and you can say them, just not always. With people you trust you’re clear; with bosses, elders and new people you bend more than you’d like. You decide case by case, which keeps things smooth and sometimes leaves you a little short-changed.
behaviors: You’ll say no to live location, and yes to every single family lunch.
You give space when they ask, though you check in a little more than needed.
You set a limit kindly, then wonder all evening if you were too harsh.
strengths: You bend without breaking. People find you easy to plan with.
weaknesses: Case by case can slowly become never, especially with people who push.
realLife: On a first date: You tell them you need to leave by 10. At 10:40 you’re still there, by choice.
In a fight: You hold your line for a while, then soften the moment they look hurt.
tips: Pick your three non-negotiables and say them early. Then bend freely on the rest.
match: Best with: Someone who respects your no the first time, so you don’t have to repeat it.
Green flag: They ask before they assume, about your time, your space and your plans.
Careful with: Someone who goes cold when you set a limit, until you take it back.

Low.label: The Polite Dodger
summaries: You don’t say no. You say “maybe, let’s see”.

You know your limits; you just find it hard to say them plainly. So you dodge: a joke, an excuse, a sudden deadline, and now and then a slammed door when it all gets too much. You don’t want to hurt anyone, but it leaves people unsure where your lines really are.
behaviors: You invent a busy weekend instead of saying you need one alone.
You say yes out loud and grumble about it to your sibling later.
When you finally push back, it comes out sharper than you meant.
strengths: Tact. You can wriggle out of almost anything without a scene.
weaknesses: Excuses work once. After that, people learn your words don’t match what you feel.
realLife: On a first date: They order for both of you. You don’t love it, but you eat it and call it delicious.
In a fight: You say “it’s fine” and then close a few cupboards rather loudly.
tips: Next time, skip the excuse and try the short version: “I can’t this time.” No reason needed. Watch how little happens.
match: Best with: Someone easygoing who takes a plain no well, so you can practise saying one.
Green flag: They say their own limits plainly, which shows you it’s safe to do the same.
Careful with: Someone who pushes past every “maybe” until it turns into a yes.

VeryLow.label: The Always-Yes
summaries: Your yes comes fast. Your no rarely comes at all.

You hate letting people down, so the yes is out before you’ve checked if you have the time, money or energy. People love how generous you are. The cost shows up later, in tired weekends and quiet resentment you’re too kind to say out loud.
behaviors: You share your location, your Sundays and your last samosa, even when part of you wants to say no.
You go to every family lunch they plan, then feel strangely drained.
When it finally gets too much, it comes out all at once and surprises everyone, you included.
strengths: Generosity. People feel welcome in your life from day one.
weaknesses: A yes you don’t mean slowly turns into resentment nobody saw coming.
realLife: On a first date: At 11 pm they suggest a second place. You’re exhausted. You hear yourself say “sure!”
In a fight: You give in to end it fast, then feel worse than if you’d argued.
tips: Practise one sentence: “Let me check and tell you tomorrow.” It buys you time to find out what you actually want.
match: Best with: Someone who asks “are you sure?” and really wants the honest answer.
Green flag: They make it easy to say no, and don’t sulk when you do.
Careful with: Someone who keeps asking for a little more, because you never say no.

Undecided.label: The Flexible Fence
summaries: Firm on the big stuff, bendy on the rest.

You have limits and you can say them, just not always. With people you trust you’re clear; with bosses, elders and new people you bend more than you’d like. You decide case by case, which keeps things smooth and sometimes leaves you a little short-changed.

You give space when they ask, though you check in a little more than needed.
You set a limit kindly, then wonder all evening if you were too harsh.
