options.text: Only when something hurts
When the office sponsors one
Booked every year. I actually read the reports

tests.measures: how much healthy habits, self-care and a steady daily rhythm matter to you

VeryHigh.label: The Green-Juice Regular
summaries: Your routine is your superpower, and you never skip it.

Health isn’t a phase for you; it’s a way of life. You plan your meals, track your sleep and treat workouts like meetings you can’t miss. You do it because it makes you feel strong, clear and in charge of your day, and it shows.
behaviors: You want someone who takes care of themselves as seriously as you do.
Your dream weekend is a trek, a fresh juice and an early night.
You show love by caring about their health, sometimes a little too much.
strengths: Your discipline is inspiring, and people quietly copy your habits.
weaknesses: Strict rules can make a relaxed person feel judged at every meal.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest a morning hike, and you’ve packed snacks for both of you.
In a fight: You hit the gym first, then come back calm and clear.
tips: Leave room for the odd cheat day with someone you love. A shared plate of jalebis is good for the heart, too.
match: Best with: Someone as disciplined as you, or one who loves joining your routine.
Green flag: They work out with you and cheer your personal bests.
Careful with: Someone who tempts you off your plan every single time.

High.label: The Early Riser
summaries: Up with the sun, asleep before the reels get good.

You’ve built habits that make you feel good: decent sleep, real food, regular movement. You’re not obsessive about it, but you notice quickly when life knocks you off track. Taking care of yourself is how you take care of everything else.
behaviors: You’d love someone who joins your Sunday morning walk.
You notice their sleep and water, and gently say so.
You plan dates that leave you both feeling better, not just fuller.
strengths: You bring energy, steadiness and good habits into any relationship.
weaknesses: You can sound preachy when you’re just excited about a new habit.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest breakfast, not dinner, and arrive glowing from your run.
In a fight: You need a walk to clear your head. Tell them it’s a walk, not an exit.
tips: Invite, don’t instruct. The best way to share a healthy habit is to make it look fun.
match: Best with: Someone who values health and has their own rhythm.
Green flag: They respect your early mornings and join you sometimes.
Careful with: Someone who mocks your routine or keeps pulling you off it.

Moderate.label: The Weekend Warrior
summaries: Healthy most days, happily off track on some.

You care about your health, and you also care about pani puri. You work out when life allows, eat well most of the week and don’t lose sleep over a big Sunday lunch. Balance, for you, is a lifestyle, not a diet chart.
behaviors: You’ll happily plan a trek and end it with a big meal.
You can join their routine or their binge, whatever the day needs.
You never make food or fitness a point of tension.
strengths: You make healthy feel easy and fun, never strict.
weaknesses: Your routine can vanish for weeks when life gets busy.
realLife: On a first date: A Saturday morning walk that turns into a long breakfast.
In a fight: You go for a walk to cool off, then come back ready to talk.
tips: Anchor one habit that never moves, like a weekly game or a Sunday swim. It holds the rest together.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys a run and a feast in the same weekend.
Green flag: They suggest active dates and still order dessert.
Careful with: Someone at either extreme who wants you to follow their rules.

Low.label: The Comfort Seeker
summaries: You like your sleep long and your Sundays slow.

You take care of yourself in a cosy way: good food, lots of rest, nothing too strict. You’ll go for a walk if the weather is nice and skip the gym if it isn’t. You know health matters; you just don’t want it to feel like homework.
behaviors: Your idea of a perfect date ends on a couch with good snacks.
You’ll join their morning walk sometimes, if there’s chai after.
You keep things relaxed and never make anyone feel judged.
strengths: You make people feel calm and unpressured, in body and mind.
weaknesses: A fitness-focused person might wish you’d join them more often.
realLife: On a first date: A cosy café, a comfortable chair, and you order the hot chocolate.
In a fight: You need a snack and a nap before you can be reasonable, and that’s fair.
tips: Find one active thing you enjoy: dance, badminton, a long walk. Health sticks best when it feels like fun.
match: Best with: Someone easy-going who loves comfort as much as you.
Green flag: They invite you to move with them and are happy whether you say yes or no.
Careful with: Someone who turns every meal into a lecture.

VeryLow.label: The Midnight Snacker
summaries: Life is short, so you order the extra cheese.

You live for the good stuff: late nights, great food, last-minute plans. Rules about sleep and diet feel like they belong to someone else’s life. You’re easy to be around because you never make anyone feel guilty about the second dessert.
behaviors: You’re the one who says “one more episode” and means three.
Your best dates involve food, laughter and zero calorie counting.
You’ll never judge their plate, their bedtime or their snack drawer.
strengths: You make ordinary moments feel like a celebration.
weaknesses: Someone with a strict routine may feel you pull them off it.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve already ordered starters for both of you, and dessert is non-negotiable.
In a fight: You’d rather sort it out over a plate of momos than a long, serious talk.
tips: Pick one small habit, like a walk after dinner, and keep it for a month. It makes the good life last longer.
match: Best with: A fellow foodie who loves a late night and a lazy morning.
Green flag: They share their fries without being asked.
Careful with: Someone who comments on everything you eat.

Undecided.label: The Weekend Warrior
summaries: Healthy most days, happily off track on some.

You care about your health, and you also care about pani puri. You work out when life allows, eat well most of the week and don’t lose sleep over a big Sunday lunch. Balance, for you, is a lifestyle, not a diet chart.
behaviors: You’ll happily plan a trek and end it with a big meal.
You can join their routine or their binge, whatever the day needs.
You never make food or fitness a point of tension.
strengths: You make healthy feel easy and fun, never strict.
weaknesses: Your routine can vanish for weeks when life gets busy.
realLife: On a first date: A Saturday morning walk that turns into a long breakfast.
In a fight: You go for a walk to cool off, then come back ready to talk.
tips: Anchor one habit that never moves, like a weekly game or a Sunday swim. It holds the rest together.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys a run and a feast in the same weekend.
Green flag: They suggest active dates and still order dessert.
Careful with: Someone at either extreme who wants you to follow their rules.

tests.title: Money Mindset
tests.subtitle: Spending, saving, security
tests.description: Measures whether you’re a saver, spender, planner, or spontaneous with money.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your money behavior and security needs.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Money mismatch kills relationships; this helps predict conflict points early.

questions.text: Salary day. The first thing you do:

options.text: Treat myself. I earned it
Pay the bills and see what’s left
Split it: bills, a SIP, a little fun
Move savings first, then breathe

questions.text: Half-price sale on sneakers you don’t really need. You…

options.text: Add to cart and sleep on it
Buy them. Half price is basically free
Close the app. Don’t need, don’t buy

questions.text: Talking money with someone you’re getting serious about:

options.text: Awkward. Let’s keep it romantic
Early and open: salaries, loans, goals
When it comes up naturally

questions.text: A last-minute Goa trip with the gang, this weekend. You…

options.text: In, if it fits this month’s budget
I’m in. Memories over money
Out. It wasn’t in the plan
Yes, and I’ll sort the money later

questions.text: Your emergency fund is…

options.text: Six months of expenses, untouched
Me. I am the emergency fund
Something, though I’ve dipped into it

questions.text: Their birthday is next week. Your gift plan:

options.text: Whatever feels right when I see it
A thoughtful gift within the limit I set
A little more than I planned. It’s them

questions.text: Dream wedding, or the down payment on a flat?

options.text: The flat. A wedding is one day
The wedding. We only do it once

questions.text: How do you keep track of your spending?

options.text: The bank app, now and then
A spreadsheet, every rupee
A rough budget in my head
I don’t. My UPI history scares me

tests.measures: how you approach money, spending, and financial planning in relationships

VeryHigh.label: The Rupee Strategist
summaries: Every rupee has a job, and you know them all.

You play the long game with money: budgets, SIPs, emergency funds and goals with dates on them. Financial security is how you feel free, and you’ve worked hard for it. Friends come to you before any big purchase, and they should.
behaviors: You want to talk salaries, savings and goals before things get serious.
Your idea of romance includes a shared plan for the future.
You feel most cared for when someone respects your budget.
strengths: You turn dreams into dates and numbers, and then make them happen.
weaknesses: Your rules can feel like control to someone who loves spontaneity.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve checked the menu online, and you still say yes to dessert.
In a fight: You open the spreadsheet. Open your heart first, then the file.
tips: Keep one line in the budget called “because life”. Joy is part of a good plan.
match: Best with: Another planner, or a spender who truly wants to learn the game.
Green flag: They know their own numbers and share them without fuss.
Careful with: Someone who hides debts or refuses to talk money at all.

High.label: The Cushion Builder
summaries: A little set aside, every month, without fail.

You like knowing there’s a cushion. You save regularly, think before big purchases and feel calmer when your plan is on track. You still enjoy life; you just like to enjoy it with your bills paid and your future looked after.
behaviors: You’ll plan a beautiful date and know exactly what it costs.
You want money talk early, because surprises later aren’t romantic.
You show love by building security for the two of you.
strengths: You make people feel safe about tomorrow.
weaknesses: A spontaneous person may feel you say no to fun too often.
realLife: On a first date: You choose a lovely place you could afford twice, because you’re hoping for a second date.
In a fight: You bring the numbers. Bring warmth too. It helps the numbers land.
tips: Budget a little “yes” fund for spontaneous fun. Planned spontaneity still counts.
match: Best with: Someone responsible with money who still knows how to celebrate.
Green flag: They’re open about their finances and have a plan of their own.
Careful with: Someone who spends as if the bill will never come.

Moderate.label: The Choosy Spender
summaries: Saves most days, splurges on purpose.

You’ve found a rhythm with money: bills paid, something saved, and room for the things that make you happy. You don’t track every rupee, but you know roughly where they go. You can say yes to a trip and no to a sale, and mean both.
behaviors: You can split bills fairly and still surprise them with something nice.
You’re happy to talk money when it matters, without making it heavy.
You can meet a saver or a spender halfway.
strengths: You enjoy money without letting it run your life.
weaknesses: Your “roughly” can turn into “no idea” in a busy month.
realLife: On a first date: You pick a place with great food and fair prices, and happily split or treat.
In a fight: You look for the fair middle: a budget with room for fun.
tips: Check your money once a month, over chai. Ten minutes keeps “roughly” from becoming “oops”.
match: Best with: Someone open about money who likes a mix of plans and treats.
Green flag: They talk about money easily and spend on what matters to them.
Careful with: Someone who hides their spending or their debts.

Low.label: The Experience Collector
summaries: Concerts, trips and good food are your investments.

You spend on what makes life rich: trips, concerts, dinners with your people. You know saving matters and you do some of it, but you’d rather have the memories now than a perfect plan for later. Money, to you, is a ticket, not a trophy.
behaviors: You’ll book the weekend getaway while they’re still thinking about it.
You remember the experiences, not the price tags.
You’d choose a shared adventure over an expensive gift.
strengths: You make sure life is lived, not just planned.
weaknesses: Big goals can drift away while you collect great weekends.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest a live gig, and you already have two tickets.
In a fight: You want to move on quickly and plan something fun to reset.
tips: Keep a separate fund just for adventures. You’ll enjoy them more knowing the rent is safe.
match: Best with: Someone who loves experiences and keeps a gentle hand on the plan.
Green flag: They say yes to adventures and help you put a little aside.
Careful with: Someone who makes you feel guilty for every treat.

VeryLow.label: The Bill Grabber
summaries: Money comes, money goes, memories stay.

You see money as something to enjoy and share, not to hoard. You’re the first to pick up the bill, book the trip or buy the gift, and you’d rather have a great story than a perfect bank balance. Life feels too short to spend it in spreadsheets.
behaviors: You spoil the people you love, often and without warning.
Your dates are generous, spontaneous and a little over budget.
You’d rather talk about dreams than about budgets.
strengths: Your generosity makes people feel truly celebrated.
weaknesses: A planner may feel anxious watching money leave so easily.
realLife: On a first date: You insist on paying, order the dessert special and suggest a second place after.
In a fight: You’d rather buy a peace offering than sit with a budget sheet.
tips: Set up one automatic saving for the day your salary lands. Your generous heart deserves a cushion too.
match: Best with: Someone generous too, or a calm planner who loves your spark.
Green flag: They enjoy your surprises and gently help you plan the big things.
Careful with: Someone who keeps a running tab of who paid for what.

Undecided.label: The Choosy Spender
summaries: Saves most days, splurges on purpose.

You’ve found a rhythm with money: bills paid, something saved, and room for the things that make you happy. You don’t track every rupee, but you know roughly where they go. You can say yes to a trip and no to a sale, and mean both.
behaviors: You can split bills fairly and still surprise them with something nice.
You’re happy to talk money when it matters, without making it heavy.
You can meet a saver or a spender halfway.
strengths: You enjoy money without letting it run your life.
weaknesses: Your “roughly” can turn into “no idea” in a busy month.
realLife: On a first date: You pick a place with great food and fair prices, and happily split or treat.
In a fight: You look for the fair middle: a budget with room for fun.
tips: Check your money once a month, over chai. Ten minutes keeps “roughly” from becoming “oops”.
match: Best with: Someone open about money who likes a mix of plans and treats.
Green flag: They talk about money easily and spend on what matters to them.
Careful with: Someone who hides their spending or their debts.

tests.title: Roles & Expectations
tests.subtitle: Views on duties and fairness
tests.description: Measures how you view relationship roles, responsibilities, and fairness (50/50 vs traditional roles).
tests.whatYouLearn: Your expectation of duties and role balance.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps align expectations early and reduce resentment.

questions.text: Moving in together. How do you split the housework?

options.text: The way it was always done at home
Sit down and split it by who likes what
Fifty-fifty on everything, strictly
It’ll sort itself out, no need to discuss

questions.text: Who earns, who runs the home: in your future marriage, that’s…

options.text: Already clear in my head
Flexible, with a few things I’d need
Ours to decide together, traditional or not

questions.text: They get a big job in another country. You’d have to pause your career. You…

options.text: Let the bigger salary decide
Talk it through. Careers can take turns
Stay. My career isn’t the one that pauses
Go, if they’d do the same for me later

questions.text: They’re down with fever for a week. At home you…

options.text: Handle the essentials, the rest can wait
Call family or order in. Some jobs aren’t mine
Take over everything they usually do

questions.text: Festival lunch at your family’s home. Who helps in the kitchen?

options.text: Everyone, guests included
Whoever the elders ask
Whoever enjoys cooking, and the rest clean up
The same people as every year. It works

questions.text: Talking about who does what, before marriage, is…

options.text: Smart. A clear talk now saves fights later
Unromantic. Love figures it out

questions.text: A year in, the split you planned isn’t working anymore. You…

options.text: Tweak a few things, keep the rest
Stick to it. We decided once
Redo it. Life changed, so can the plan

questions.text: Planning dates, remembering birthdays, booking tickets: who does it?

options.text: Them. They’re better at that stuff
Mostly one of us, with a thank-you every time
We take turns, so nobody gets tired

tests.measures: how fair, flexible and open to discussion you are about sharing roles and duties

VeryHigh.label: The Co-Pilot
summaries: Either of you can fly the plane, and you love that.

You believe roles should fit the people, not the other way round. You’ll cook, earn, care, plan or step back, whatever the season of life asks, and you expect the same openness in return. Traditional or modern doesn’t matter to you, as long as both of you chose it.
behaviors: You’re happy with any setup, traditional or new, if it’s chosen together.
You swap roles easily when one of you is busy, sick or chasing a dream.
You talk about duties and money openly, and it brings you closer.
strengths: You adapt to whatever life throws, and you keep it fair for both.
weaknesses: Your flexibility can wear you out if the other person never offers the same.
realLife: On a first date: You offer to split, to treat or to be treated, whatever feels right to them.
In a fight: You put every option on the table, then pick one together.
tips: Keep asking what they need, and say what you need too. Flexible works best when it goes both ways.
match: Best with: Someone who sees fairness as a living thing, not a fixed rule.
Green flag: They pause their plans for yours sometimes, and you do the same for them.
Careful with: Someone who wants you to bend while they never do.

High.label: The Team Player
summaries: You split life by strengths, not by script.

You see a relationship as a team: whoever is better at something does it, and whoever has more time that week picks up more. You’re happy to talk roles openly and change them when life changes. Fairness, for you, means both people feel looked after.
behaviors: You’ll cook if you love cooking, and happily hand over the bills if they love numbers.
You talk about who does what early, and it never feels heavy.
You notice when they’re stretched and quietly take more on.
strengths: You make a home feel like a team where everyone wins.
weaknesses: You might take on extra without saying, then feel tired and unseen.
realLife: On a first date: You take turns choosing the place, and you’ve already planned round two.
In a fight: You ask “what would make this fair for you?” and mean it.
tips: Say it when you’re carrying more. A good team needs to hear when someone is tired.
match: Best with: Someone who sees love as teamwork and says what they need.
Green flag: They step in when you’re swamped, without being asked.
Careful with: Someone who thinks some jobs are beneath them.

Moderate.label: The Fair Splitter
summaries: Fair is fair, and you like it in equal halves.

You care a lot about fairness, and you like it clear: half the bills, half the chores, turns for everything. You’re open to other setups, but you need to see that nobody is carrying more. Underneath the maths is a big heart that hates anyone feeling used.
behaviors: You split the bill without being asked, and expect the same.
You notice when the balance tips, even a little.
You’re open to new arrangements, once they feel fair to you.
strengths: With you, nobody gets taken for granted.
weaknesses: Keeping things exactly equal can turn into quietly keeping score.
realLife: On a first date: You offer to split the bill before it even arrives.
In a fight: You list who did what. Start with how you feel, then the list.
tips: Fair doesn’t always mean equal. Some months one of you will carry more, and that can be love, not a debt.
match: Best with: Someone who values fairness and doesn’t mind talking it through.
Green flag: They do their share without being reminded.
Careful with: Someone who assumes you’ll pick up their slack.

Low.label: The Habit Keeper
summaries: You like your roles familiar, and you bend when it counts.

You have a fairly set idea of how things should be split, and you like routines that don’t need talking about. When life throws a curveball, you adjust, though you’d rather go back to normal soon after. You value stability, and you give it generously.
behaviors: You settle into roles quickly and do your part reliably.
Long talks about chores aren’t your thing. Doing feels simpler than discussing.
You step up in a crisis, then hope things go back to how they were.
strengths: You’re dependable. What’s yours gets done, every time.
weaknesses: Not talking about roles can let resentment build quietly, on either side.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest your usual place, because you know it’s good.
In a fight: You want things back to normal fast. Ask what normal should look like now.
tips: Every few months, ask: “Is the way we split things still working for you?” Small check-ins keep big resentments away.
match: Best with: Someone steady who likes clear routines and kind check-ins.
Green flag: They tell you when something isn’t working, gently and early.
Careful with: Someone who keeps changing the plan without warning.

VeryLow.label: The Clear Blueprint
summaries: You know the home you want, down to who makes the chai.

You carry a clear picture of how a home should run, often from the one that raised you, and that picture feels safe and right. You like knowing who does what, without long discussions. Change can feel like losing something precious, so you hold on to what you know works.
behaviors: You know what you’ll bring to a home, and what you hope they’ll bring.
You’d rather follow a familiar pattern than invent a new one.
A surprise in who does what can unsettle you more than you show.
strengths: You bring certainty and order. In your home, nobody wonders what’s expected.
weaknesses: Your picture can feel like a script the other person never got to read.
realLife: On a first date: You already know who’s paying, how you’ll get home and what you’ll order.
In a fight: You go back to “this is how it should be.” Try asking “how do you see it?”
tips: Say your picture out loud early and ask for theirs. A plan you both chose holds better than one you assumed.
match: Best with: Someone who shares your picture of home, or loves the clarity you bring.
Green flag: They ask about your expectations and share theirs openly.
Careful with: Someone who says “we’ll figure it out” about everything, and never does.

Undecided.label: The Fair Splitter
summaries: Fair is fair, and you like it in equal halves.

You care a lot about fairness, and you like it clear: half the bills, half the chores, turns for everything. You’re open to other setups, but you need to see that nobody is carrying more. Underneath the maths is a big heart that hates anyone feeling used.
behaviors: You split the bill without being asked, and expect the same.
You notice when the balance tips, even a little.
You’re open to new arrangements, once they feel fair to you.
strengths: With you, nobody gets taken for granted.
weaknesses: Keeping things exactly equal can turn into quietly keeping score.
realLife: On a first date: You offer to split the bill before it even arrives.
In a fight: You list who did what. Start with how you feel, then the list.
tips: Fair doesn’t always mean equal. Some months one of you will carry more, and that can be love, not a debt.
match: Best with: Someone who values fairness and doesn’t mind talking it through.
Green flag: They do their share without being reminded.
Careful with: Someone who assumes you’ll pick up their slack.

tests.title: Loyalty
tests.subtitle: Commitment, privacy, boundaries
tests.description: Measures how strongly you value loyalty, exclusivity, and privacy boundaries in relationships.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your loyalty expectations and boundary strictness.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Prevents mismatch: one is very open/social, other expects strict exclusivity behavior.

questions.text: Two weeks of great chats with someone new. Your other chats on the app?

options.text: Still open. It’s two weeks, not a ring
Closed. One person at a time, always
Open until we talk about being exclusive
There, but I’ve stopped replying

questions.text: You’re seeing someone. A charming colleague invites you to a one-on-one dinner.

options.text: Suggest a team lunch instead
Go. It’s a colleague, not a date
Go, and mention it at home first

questions.text: You had a fight with the person you’re seeing. Who hears about it?

options.text: My closest person, for advice
The whole gang, the same night
Nobody. What happens between us stays between us

questions.text: You’re taken, and someone attractive is flirting with you at a party. You…

options.text: Banter a little. It’s harmless fun
Stay friendly and mention the person I’m with
Shut it down kindly: “I’m with someone”
Find my people and change the scene

questions.text: Your phone, once you’re in a relationship:

options.text: An open book. Nothing on it I’d hide
My space. Trust means not checking

questions.text: Your friends start joking about the person you’re seeing, behind their back. You…

options.text: Laugh along. They’d laugh too
Change the topic, then tell them later
Stop them, right there and then

questions.text: Where does cheating start, for you?

options.text: Hiding things, or anything physical
A secret emotional bond with someone else
Only when something physical happens

questions.text: Staying friends with an ex while you’re seeing someone new:

options.text: Not for me. When it ends, it ends
Totally normal. Some exes become family
Fine, with clear limits

tests.measures: how deeply you value loyalty, commitment, and privacy in relationships

VeryHigh.label: The Ride-or-Die
summaries: Once you’re in, you’re all in.

Your loyalty is fierce. You defend the people you love in every room, keep their secrets like your own and draw firm lines around your relationship. For you, commitment isn’t a mood; it’s a promise you keep on the hard days too.
behaviors: Once you choose someone, other options stop existing.
You’d defend them in a room full of their critics, and expect the same.
Exes stay in the past. Firmly.
strengths: Your loyalty is unshakeable, and people feel it.
weaknesses: Your strict lines can feel like a cage to someone with a freer style.
realLife: On a first date: You’re honest that you want something real, and you watch how they react.
In a fight: You never take it outside. It stays between the two of you, even when you’re hurt.
tips: Let loyalty be a promise, not a rulebook. Trust them with a little freedom: that’s how loyalty comes back to you.
match: Best with: Someone just as committed who sees loyalty as love.
Green flag: They stand up for you even when you’re not there.
Careful with: Someone who wants all of your loyalty and gives half of theirs.

High.label: The Lighthouse
summaries: With you, they never have to wonder.

Loyalty is one of your deepest values. You keep private things private, you don’t play games, and once you’re in, you’re in. People feel safe with you because your words and your actions always line up.
behaviors: You close other chats as soon as someone matters.
Your relationship problems never become group-chat material.
You keep a respectful distance from anything that could look like more.
strengths: You make people feel chosen, every single day.
weaknesses: You may expect the same strict lines from someone who never learned them.
realLife: On a first date: You give them your full attention and notice how they talk about their exes.
In a fight: You keep it between the two of you, always.
tips: Say your lines out loud early. Loyalty is easier to return when people know what it looks like to you.
match: Best with: Someone who values commitment and privacy as much as you.
Green flag: They introduce you proudly and keep your secrets.
Careful with: Someone who calls flirting “harmless” while you’re standing right there.

Moderate.label: The Honest Balancer
summaries: Clear lines, warm heart, no drama.

You take loyalty seriously without turning it into rules for everyone. You keep your friendships, old ones included, with clear lines, and you’re open about where you are and who you’re with. You expect honesty more than restrictions.
behaviors: You don’t do secret chats, and you don’t check theirs.
Once you’re exclusive, you close other doors without fuss.
You share enough that they never have to wonder.
strengths: You’re trustworthy without being controlling.
weaknesses: You might assume your lines are obvious when they aren’t to everyone.
realLife: On a first date: You’re fully present, phone away, and honest about what you’re looking for.
In a fight: You want honesty first. Everything else can be worked out.
tips: Talk about boundaries in the first months, not after something hurts. Steady love needs a clear map.
match: Best with: Someone honest and secure who keeps their word.
Green flag: They mention their plans before you have to ask.
Careful with: Someone vague about where they were and who with.

Low.label: The Live-and-Let-Live
summaries: Loyal at heart, relaxed about the rules.

You’re loyal where it counts, but you don’t need strict rules to prove it. Friends of every kind, a friendly ex, a little banter at a party: none of it feels like a threat to you. You trust easily and expect to be trusted back.
behaviors: You commit when it’s real, and you don’t need a rulebook to stay.
You give them plenty of freedom and expect the same.
You’ll mention a friendly chat with an ex, because to you it’s nothing.
strengths: You make love feel easy, light and free of suspicion.
weaknesses: What feels harmless to you can feel like a crossed line to them.
realLife: On a first date: You’re relaxed, curious and not already planning the wedding.
In a fight: You keep it calm and practical. Make sure they feel heard, not brushed off.
tips: Ask what makes them feel safe, and do a few of those things. Light love can still have a few clear lines.
match: Best with: Someone secure who doesn’t need constant proof.
Green flag: They trust you without checking, and tell you their own boundaries.
Careful with: Someone who reads every friendship as a threat.

VeryLow.label: The Breezy Heart
summaries: You love freely and hold on lightly.

You believe love works best with the windows open. You stay friends with exes, enjoy a bit of harmless banter and keep your options open until something is clearly decided. To you, trust isn’t built with rules; it’s shown by giving people room.
behaviors: You don’t check phones, track locations or keep tabs, and you hope for the same.
Early on, you keep a few doors open until one feels right.
You’re relaxed about their friendships, old flames included.
strengths: You never smother anyone. People feel free around you.
weaknesses: Someone who needs clear signs of loyalty may feel unsure where they stand.
realLife: On a first date: You enjoy it fully, with no big expectations, and see where it goes.
In a fight: You say “you’re reading too much into it.” Ask what they need instead.
tips: Ask early what loyalty looks like to them. Your easy way is lovely, but their lines might sit closer than yours.
match: Best with: Someone secure and easy-going who loves freedom as much as you.
Green flag: They say clearly what they need, so you know where the lines are.
Careful with: Someone who expects silent rules you were never told.

Undecided.label: The Honest Balancer
summaries: Clear lines, warm heart, no drama.

You take loyalty seriously without turning it into rules for everyone. You keep your friendships, old ones included, with clear lines, and you’re open about where you are and who you’re with. You expect honesty more than restrictions.
behaviors: You don’t do secret chats, and you don’t check theirs.
Once you’re exclusive, you close other doors without fuss.
You share enough that they never have to wonder.
strengths: You’re trustworthy without being controlling.
weaknesses: You might assume your lines are obvious when they aren’t to everyone.
realLife: On a first date: You’re fully present, phone away, and honest about what you’re looking for.
In a fight: You want honesty first. Everything else can be worked out.
tips: Talk about boundaries in the first months, not after something hurts. Steady love needs a clear map.
match: Best with: Someone honest and secure who keeps their word.
Green flag: They mention their plans before you have to ask.
Careful with: Someone vague about where they were and who with.

tests.title: Social Circle
tests.subtitle: Friends, parties, community life
tests.description: Measures how much you value social life, friends, and community energy.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your preferred social lifestyle pace.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Avoids mismatch: homebody vs party/social person.

Live for it: every function, every dance
Go for the main days, skip a few

options.text: Two or three
One. That’s all I need
Easily ten

options.text: Week two. The gang needs to approve
My love life and my crowd stay separate

options.text: On silent. The weekend is mine
One plan, confirmed
Fifteen plans across five group chats

Join the committee. I love this stuff
Show up for the evening programme

options.text: Brunch with a big group, then a party
Just the two of us, phones away

tests.measures: how important friends, community, and social life are to you

VeryHigh.label: The Life of the Party
summaries: Where you go, a crowd follows.

People give you energy, and you give it right back. Weddings, festivals, house parties, community events: you’re there, you’re dancing and you know everyone by the end of the night. Life, for you, is meant to be lived together, loudly and with a lot of food.
behaviors: You want someone who’ll dance at every sangeet with you.
Your love is out loud: photos, stories and introductions to everyone.
A quiet night in is lovely, about once a month.
strengths: You make everyone around you feel welcome and part of something.
weaknesses: A private person may feel overwhelmed by the crowd that comes with you.
realLife: On a first date: You bump into three people you know before the starters arrive.
In a fight: You want to talk now, even at a party. Find a quiet corner first.
tips: Ask them how much crowd they enjoy, and protect some quiet for them. Love grows in the quiet moments too.
match: Best with: Someone who loves people as much as you, or a calm soul who enjoys the show.
Green flag: They light up around your people and hold your hand in the crowd.
Careful with: Someone who slowly tries to shrink your world down to just the two of you.

High.label: The Group-Chat Admin
summaries: You make the plans, and everyone shows up.

You’re the one who makes things happen: the dinner booking, the trip plan, the reunion nobody else would organise. Friends and community matter deeply to you, and your calendar shows it. You’re happiest when your people are together.
behaviors: You want them in your circle early, and you want to know theirs.
Your weekends together usually include other people.
You love planning double dates and group trips.
strengths: You build community wherever you go.
weaknesses: The person you’re with may want you to themselves more than your calendar allows.
realLife: On a first date: You’ve picked the place everyone recommends, and you know the owner.
In a fight: You want it sorted before the weekend plans. Slow down; they come first.
tips: Block one evening a week for just the two of you. Your crowd will survive a night without you.
match: Best with: Someone social who loves being part of a big circle.
Green flag: They get along with your people and bring their own into the mix.
Careful with: Someone who makes you feel guilty for seeing your people.

Moderate.label: The Selective Socialite
summaries: Great at parties, even better at leaving them.

You can light up a room and you can also leave it early without guilt. You love your people and a good night out, but you pick your plans carefully and keep some evenings just for you. Your social life is busy enough to be fun and quiet enough to stay yours.
behaviors: You’ll bring them to the good parties and skip the boring ones together.
You balance nights out with nights in, and enjoy both.
You like them meeting your crowd, at the right time.
strengths: You fit into any room and know when to head home.
weaknesses: People may not know which version of you is showing up tonight.
realLife: On a first date: Drinks somewhere lively, then a walk somewhere quiet.
In a fight: You talk privately, and soon, so it doesn’t spill into plans with others.
tips: Tell them your rhythm, like “two nights out, two nights in.” It saves a lot of guessing.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys both a party and a quiet Sunday.
Green flag: They ask if you’re in the mood for people before making plans.
Careful with: Someone at either extreme who expects you to live their way.

Low.label: The Small-Circle Soul
summaries: Few people, deep roots, long chai sessions.

You have a handful of people you’d trust with your life, and that’s plenty. You enjoy a gathering now and then, but your favourite evenings are small: a few close faces, good food, real talk. You’re choosy with your time because you give it fully.
behaviors: You’ll introduce them to your inner circle when it’s serious, and that’s a big deal.
You prefer dinner for four over a party for forty.
You go to their big events for them, and slip away once you’ve done your bit.
strengths: Your friendships last decades, and so does your love.
weaknesses: A very social person may read your no to parties as a no to them.
realLife: On a first date: A tiny café you love, and you tell them it’s your secret spot.
In a fight: You talk it through in private, never in front of others.
tips: Say yes to one of their big plans each month. A little stretch shows how much you care.
match: Best with: Someone with a close circle of their own who loves a cosy plan.
Green flag: They respect your energy and plan small things with you.
Careful with: Someone who drags you to every event and sulks when you leave early.

VeryLow.label: The Secret Garden
summaries: A small, beautiful world, by invitation only.

You guard your peace and your privacy, and you’re good at both. A quiet evening, one trusted person and no audience is your idea of a full life. People who make it past your garden gate feel truly chosen, because you don’t let many in.
behaviors: You want a love that lives between two people, not in front of a crowd.
You’d rather have one deep conversation than ten parties.
You keep your relationship off social media, and you like it that way.
strengths: When you let someone in, they get all of you.
weaknesses: A social person may feel shut out of your world, or kept hidden in it.
realLife: On a first date: A quiet corner table, no crowd, and a conversation that runs past closing time.
In a fight: You need quiet before you talk. Tell them it’s space, not distance.
tips: Let one or two of your people meet them early. It shows they’re welcome in your world, not just in your evenings.
match: Best with: Someone who loves quiet nights and doesn’t need an audience.
Green flag: They’re happy to skip the party and stay in with you.
Careful with: Someone who posts every moment of your relationship online.

Undecided.label: The Selective Socialite
summaries: Great at parties, even better at leaving them.

You can light up a room and you can also leave it early without guilt. You love your people and a good night out, but you pick your plans carefully and keep some evenings just for you. Your social life is busy enough to be fun and quiet enough to stay yours.
behaviors: You’ll bring them to the good parties and skip the boring ones together.
You balance nights out with nights in, and enjoy both.
You like them meeting your crowd, at the right time.
strengths: You fit into any room and know when to head home.
weaknesses: People may not know which version of you is showing up tonight.
realLife: On a first date: Drinks somewhere lively, then a walk somewhere quiet.
In a fight: You talk privately, and soon, so it doesn’t spill into plans with others.
tips: Tell them your rhythm, like “two nights out, two nights in.” It saves a lot of guessing.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys both a party and a quiet Sunday.
Green flag: They ask if you’re in the mood for people before making plans.
Careful with: Someone at either extreme who expects you to live their way.

tests.title: Growth & Learning
tests.subtitle: Self-development priorities
tests.description: Measures how much you value growth: learning, self-improvement, therapy, skill-building.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your growth mindset in love and life.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Pairs better when both want growth (or at least respect it).

questions.text: Someone you’re close to says, “You get defensive when I bring things up.” You…

options.text: Feel hurt, then think it over later
That’s just how I am, and that’s okay
Ask for an example and really think about it

questions.text: What’s on your nightstand right now?

options.text: My phone, and the next episode
Three half-read self-help books
A novel I’m slowly enjoying

questions.text: New Year’s resolutions:

options.text: One or two things I actually want to try
A list, a tracker and monthly reviews
Resolutions? I like me as I am

questions.text: Talking to a counsellor to understand yourself better is…

options.text: Not for me. I sort things out my way
Useful for others. Not sure about me yet
Something I’ve done, or would, happily

questions.text: A free Saturday, all yours. You’d rather…

options.text: Learn something new: pottery, a language, guitar
Rest and recharge, guilt-free

questions.text: You notice you’ve made the same mistake in love twice. You…

options.text: Note it and try to do better
Journal it and find the pattern
Shrug. Some things are just luck
Ask a close friend what they see

questions.text: Someone who’s always working on themselves sounds…

options.text: Inspiring. Let’s grow together
Nice, as long as they don’t try to fix me
Exhausting. Love me as I am

questions.text: An old school friend says, “You haven’t changed at all!” You feel…

options.text: Proud. Still the same me
A little worried. I’ve worked so hard on me
Happy, though I hope I’ve grown a bit

tests.measures: how much you value personal growth, learning, and self-improvement

VeryHigh.label: The Ever-Evolving
summaries: Next year’s you is already in progress.

You see yourself as a work in progress, and that excites you. Courses, books, counselling, hard conversations: you treat life as a school you never want to graduate from. You change a lot, and the people around you often grow just by being near you.
behaviors: You want someone who grows with you, not someone who stays the same.
You love honest feedback, and you give it, sometimes too freely.
Your idea of a deep date is a long talk about who you’re both becoming.
strengths: You never stop getting better, and you inspire others to try.
weaknesses: The person you love may wonder if they’re enough, just as they are.
realLife: On a first date: You ask what they’re learning right now, and you’ve brought a book suggestion.
In a fight: You want to analyse it right away. Sometimes they just need a hug first.
tips: Love them as they are today, not as who they could become. Growth feels best when it’s invited, not assigned.
match: Best with: Someone just as hungry to grow, who loves deep conversations.
Green flag: They work on themselves and cheer you on in your own growth.
Careful with: Someone who mocks self-work or refuses to ever change.

High.label: The Curious Mind
summaries: Always learning, always asking why.

You love learning: about the world, about people, about yourself. You read, you try new things and you actually listen when someone tells you something hard. Growing is part of how you enjoy life, not a chore you tick off.
behaviors: You ask real questions and remember the answers.
You want a relationship where both people keep growing.
You can say “you’re right, I’ll work on it” and mean it.
strengths: You learn from every relationship, and keep getting better at love.
weaknesses: You might treat the person you love like a project, or yourself like one.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their favourite book, and actually write it down.
In a fight: You want to understand the pattern, not just win the round.
tips: Let some days be just for enjoying each other, no lessons. Growing together also means resting together.
match: Best with: Someone curious who loves learning as much as you.
Green flag: They take feedback well and give it kindly.
Careful with: Someone who won’t talk about anything deeper than the weather.

Moderate.label: The Slow Grower
summaries: Always growing, never in a hurry.

You like getting better, but you won’t turn your life into a self-improvement project. You read a bit, reflect a bit and change what truly needs changing. To you, growth is a slow plant, not a crash course.
behaviors: You’re open to feedback, when it comes with kindness.
You enjoy learning new things together, at a gentle pace.
You change for the relationship when it makes sense, not to win approval.
strengths: You grow without losing yourself.
weaknesses: To someone in a hurry, going slow can look like not trying.
realLife: On a first date: You both order a dish you’ve never tried, and you’re both a little brave.
In a fight: You listen, take a day and come back with one real change.
tips: Choose one thing to work on each year, and tell them. Shared goals turn growth into a team sport.
match: Best with: Someone curious and patient who grows alongside you.
Green flag: They try new things with you, without needing them to be perfect.
Careful with: Someone who wants you to change faster than feels right.

Low.label: The School-of-Life Grad
summaries: You learn from life, not from self-help books.

You grow, just not on a schedule. Life teaches you its lessons through people, mistakes and good days, and you pick them up in your own time. Workshops and journals aren’t really you; a long chat with someone wise is.
behaviors: You learn about love by living it, not by reading about it.
You’ll change for someone when it matters, without making it a project.
You prefer easy togetherness to “let’s work on our relationship” talks.
strengths: Your growth is natural and unforced, so it actually lasts.
weaknesses: You might brush off feedback that’s actually worth hearing.
realLife: On a first date: You swap life stories, and the best ones are lessons learned the hard way.
In a fight: You need time to think, and you come back having actually thought.
tips: When someone gives you honest feedback, sleep on it before deciding it’s wrong. The best lessons often come from people who love you.
match: Best with: Someone practical and warm who doesn’t push self-improvement.
Green flag: They share what they learn without lecturing.
Careful with: Someone who corrects you constantly in the name of growth.

VeryLow.label: The Original Edition
summaries: No updates needed. You came complete.

You know who you are, and you like it. You don’t feel the need to keep reinventing yourself; you’re busy living as the person you already are: steady, familiar, comfortable in your skin. People always know what they’re getting with you, and that’s a gift.
behaviors: You want to be loved as you are, quirks included, and you offer the same.
You don’t try to change people, and you hope they won’t try to change you.
Heavy talks about “working on us” make you want to run for chai.
strengths: You’re consistent. The person they fell for is the person they’ll get.
weaknesses: A growth-minded person may feel alone in the work of growing together.
realLife: On a first date: You’re exactly yourself from the first minute, no performance.
In a fight: You say “this is who I am.” Try adding “but I hear you.”
tips: Pick one small thing they ask of you and try it, just for them. Staying yourself and growing a little can go together.
match: Best with: Someone who loves a simple, steady version of life.
Green flag: They accept your quirks without a list of improvements.
Careful with: Someone who sees you as a project.

Undecided.label: The Slow Grower

You like getting better, but you won’t turn your life into a self-improvement project. You read a bit, reflect a bit and change what truly needs changing. To you, growth is a slow plant, not a crash course.
