tests.measures: how jealous you get about your partner's friendships and social interactions

VeryHigh.label: The Safe Space
summaries: With you, people can finally breathe.

You understand that everyone needs a room of their own, even in love. You never ask for passwords, proof or a full account of their day, because to you, trust and privacy go together. Being with you feels like coming home: warm, open, and never watched.
behaviors: Their phone could ring all night. You’d hand it to them without a glance.
You encourage their friendships, their hobbies and their alone time.
They share their past with you slowly, because you never pushed.
strengths: You make people feel completely trusted, and that brings out their best.
weaknesses: Some people read your easy respect as not caring. Show them that you do.
realLife: On a first date: You don’t ask a single prying question, and somehow they end up telling you their life story.
In a fight: You never use privacy as a weapon, theirs or yours. You talk it out, then give space.
tips: Your respect is a gift. Pair it with curiosity about their day, their people and their past, so it never feels like distance.
match: Best with: Someone who gives you the same room and doesn’t mistake space for distance.
Green flag: They tell you what they need and ask what you need, kindly.
Careful with: Someone who wants full access to your life while keeping theirs locked.

High.label: The Trust Keeper
summaries: Their privacy is safe in your hands.

You know that loving someone doesn’t mean owning their phone, their past or their Sundays. You give people room without making them earn it, and you ask questions out of interest, not suspicion. People relax with you, and they end up sharing more.
behaviors: You don’t touch their phone, even when it buzzes on the table.
Their alone time is theirs, and you use yours happily.
You ask about their past once, gently, and let them take it from there.
strengths: People feel free with you, and free people tend to stay close.
weaknesses: You may respect their space so well that you forget to ask for the closeness you want.
realLife: On a first date: They dodge a question about their ex. You smile, change the topic, and enjoy the evening.
In a fight: You ask honest questions and accept honest answers, even short ones.
tips: Respecting their space is lovely. Make sure they know what you want too: “I’d love to meet your gang someday” isn’t intruding.
match: Best with: Someone who also values privacy and gives as much room as they get.
Green flag: They share openly because they want to, not because they have to.
Careful with: Someone who checks your phone, when you’d never check theirs.

Moderate.label: The Polite Knocker
summaries: You knock before you walk in, most of the time.

You believe everyone needs some private space, and you try to respect it, even when it makes you curious. You ask questions rather than dig, and you mostly accept the answers. On a bad day you might feel shut out, but you’d still rather knock than push the door.
behaviors: You’re fine with their alone time, as long as you get your time too.
You’d ask about a strange name on their screen, not search for it.
Their old gang can have their Sundays. You’d just like an invite sometimes.
strengths: You balance closeness and privacy well. People feel safe and wanted with you.
weaknesses: When you feel left out, you may not say it, and it can sour quietly.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their family and friends, and notice which topics they skip, without pushing.
In a fight: You ask what’s going on and accept “I need a bit of time”, as long as the talk does come.
tips: When their space makes you feel left out, say it plainly: “I miss you on Sundays.” A need said out loud is easier to meet than one swallowed.
match: Best with: Someone who shares a lot and tells you clearly what they keep for themselves.
Green flag: They respect your privacy too, without needing to be told.
Careful with: Someone who treats every question as an attack.

Low.label: The Little Detective
summaries: Curiosity sometimes walks in without knocking.

You respect privacy in theory, and mostly in practice too. But when something feels unclear, curiosity gets the better of you: a peek at a preview, a quick search for the ex, one question too many. You’re not trying to control anyone. You just hate not knowing.
behaviors: You’ve looked up their ex at least once, and you’re not sorry.
Their alone time is fine, though you’d love to know what they did with it.
You ask lots of questions, mostly out of love, sometimes out of worry.
strengths: You’re interested in every part of them, and people feel noticed by you.
weaknesses: A little peek can turn into a bigger worry that you then can’t mention.
realLife: On a first date: Their phone buzzes on the table. You don’t look, but you really, really want to.
In a fight: You may ask five questions at once. Pick the one that matters and ask it softly.
tips: When you feel like peeking, ask instead. “Who was that?”, said kindly, is better for both of you than a secret look you can’t talk about.
match: Best with: Someone open and easygoing, who shares freely and laughs at your questions.
Green flag: They tell you about their day without being asked.
Careful with: Someone vague about simple things. That puts your curiosity on overtime.

VeryLow.label: The No-Secrets Soul
summaries: You want love with no locked doors.

For you, closeness means nothing hidden: passcodes, plans, past, all of it. When something is kept private, your mind fills the gap with a secret, and that hurts. It comes from wanting to be truly let in. But to the other person, it can feel like they have no room left of their own.
behaviors: A locked phone or a quiet evening alone can feel like a door shut on you.
You want to know their friends, their past and their plans, completely.
When you feel let in, you’re the most open, generous person in the room.
strengths: You’re all in. You share everything yourself and hide nothing from the people you love.
weaknesses: Needing to see everything can leave the other person no room to breathe, or to choose you freely.
realLife: On a first date: You share your whole story by the first date, and hope to hear theirs by the second.
In a fight: You may want answers right now. Ask yourself first: am I asking to understand, or to check?
tips: When they want privacy, say “okay” and wait one day before asking anything. Notice that the love is still there. Space and closeness can live together.
match: Best with: Someone naturally open and patient, who shares a lot and gently explains what they keep to themselves.
Green flag: They tell you things before you ask, and explain kindly when they need space.
Careful with: Someone who keeps big secrets. That would feed your worst fears.

weaknesses: When you feel left out, you may not say it, and it can sour quietly.

In a fight: You ask what’s going on and accept “I need a bit of time”, as long as the talk does come.

Careful with: Someone who treats every question as an attack.

tests.subtitle: How much attention you require
tests.description: Measures how much attention and prioritization you expect from a partner to feel secure.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your attention baseline in relationships.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Prevents mismatch where one needs high attention and the other is more independent.

options.text: A bit forgotten, honestly
Fine, but I miss our long chats
Totally fine. I’m busy too
Fine. We’ll catch up on the weekend

options.text: Catch their eye now and then and smile
Make new friends of my own at the snack table
Wish they’d pull me into the chat
Join in for a bit, then find my own people

questions.text: Your idea of a perfect Sunday together:

options.text: Just us, phones away, all day
Same room, each doing our own thing

options.text: Happy. Their team deserves a party too
A little hurt I wasn’t first
Fine, as long as our celebration is special
A bit left out, but I won’t say it

options.text: Whenever. No fixed need
Through the day: updates, memes, “ate lunch?”
Once or twice, a quick hello
One proper chat in the evening

Dinner somewhere quiet, just the two of us

Breakfast in bed, then the whole day together

options.text: Sit on the remote till they look at me
Let them watch. I’ll tell it at the break
Tease them: “Hello, I’m also here!”
Feel a bit unheard and go quiet

questions.text: When someone shows love, what counts more to you?

options.text: How they show up when it really matters
How often they show up, day to day

tests.measures: how much attention and prioritization you need from a partner to feel secure

VeryHigh.label: The Sunflower
summaries: You bloom when they turn towards you.

You thrive on being chosen, and you feel it in your whole body when you are. Undivided time, daily check-ins and big gestures make you light up, and a distracted evening can make you wilt a little. You love loudly and openly, and you want love that shows up just as clearly.
behaviors: Phones away, all day, just the two of you: that’s your perfect Sunday.
You want to be their first call, for good news and bad.
When attention drops, you feel it right away, sometimes as hurt.
strengths: You love with full attention. Being with you feels like being the only one in the room.
weaknesses: When their focus is elsewhere for a while, you can read it as love fading.
realLife: On a first date: They put their phone away for the whole evening, and you’re already half charmed.
In a fight: Feeling ignored hurts you most. Say, gently, “I need you here with me for this.”
tips: Keep a few things that fill you up on your own: a hobby, your gang, a solo walk. Then their attention becomes a joy, not your only sunshine.
match: Best with: Someone openly affectionate who loves giving attention as much as you love getting it.
Green flag: They make you a priority without being asked, and it shows.
Careful with: Someone who gives attention in bursts, then disappears.

High.label: The Little-Things Lover
summaries: Small attentions are how you know you’re loved.

For you, love lives in the small daily stuff: a meme at lunch, a good-night text, a hand that finds yours at a party. You notice when the little things stop, sometimes before they do. It isn’t neediness. Attention is simply how you feel close, and you give it back generously.
behaviors: You feel loved when they check in during a busy day.
You notice quickly when they’re distracted, even if you don’t say it.
You’re generous with attention, and you hope for the same back.
strengths: You make people feel seen. Nothing they do goes unnoticed by you.
weaknesses: A busy week on their side can feel like a cold week to you.
realLife: On a first date: They remember your coffee order from your chats, and you’re charmed.
In a fight: You want them to turn towards you, not away. Ask for a hug before the talk.
tips: Tell them which small things fill you up, like a lunch text or a hand on your back. People love a clear map, and you won’t have to hope they guess.
match: Best with: Someone affectionate and attentive who enjoys daily closeness.
Green flag: They remember small details and act on them.
Careful with: Someone who calls a simple need for attention “too much”.

Moderate.label: The Sweet Spot
summaries: Not too much, not too little, just right.

You like attention the way you like your chai: regular, warm, and not overdone. A daily check-in and some focused time make you feel loved, but you don’t need to be the centre of every room. You notice when things get too quiet, and you say so.
behaviors: A hello during the day and a proper chat at night feel just right.
A quiet dinner for two means more to you than a big party.
You’ll tease them for attention long before you’d sulk for it.
strengths: You know your needs, and they’re easy to meet. Being loved by you feels simple.
weaknesses: You might adjust to someone else’s rhythm and forget to ask for yours.
realLife: On a first date: A “reached home?” text afterwards, a reply, and you’re happy.
In a fight: You want the problem looked at soon, not days later.
tips: When a busy phase leaves you running low, say it simply: “I miss you. Can we keep one evening this week?” Clear asks get clear answers.
match: Best with: Someone steady and warm who keeps in touch without being asked.
Green flag: They remember small things and check in without a reminder.
Careful with: Someone who makes you ask for every bit of time together.

Low.label: The Easy Company
summaries: Warm, relaxed, and happy with a little.

You enjoy attention, but you don’t need a steady stream of it to feel secure. A good chat in the evening, a proper weekend together, and you’re content. You give the people you love room to have busy days without feeling guilty about it.
behaviors: A busy week is fine, as long as you catch up properly on the weekend.
You like a little check-in, but you don’t count them.
At a party, you’re happy to mingle and find each other later.
strengths: You’re easy to love: warm when together, relaxed when apart.
weaknesses: You might not notice when someone else needs more contact than you.
realLife: On a first date: You enjoy the evening and send one nice text afterwards. No overthinking.
In a fight: You’re fine taking a breather and sorting it out the next day.
tips: Ask early how much contact they like. If they need more than you, a quick midday text is an easy way to meet them halfway.
match: Best with: Someone who likes closeness without needing constant attention.
Green flag: They make real time for you, even in a busy week.
Careful with: Someone who keeps score of who texted first.

VeryLow.label: The Happy Cactus
summaries: You need very little water, and you still bloom.

You feel loved without daily proof. A quiet week, a forgotten good-night text or a busy partner doesn’t shake you, because your sense of connection doesn’t run on constant contact. You have your own life, your own people and your own hobbies, and you like it that way.
behaviors: You can go a day or two without talking and feel just as close.
Big gestures make you a bit shy. A sweet text is plenty.
You show love in solid, practical ways more than constant check-ins.
strengths: You’re restful to be with. Nobody ever feels they’re failing to keep you happy.
weaknesses: Your easy independence can look like low interest to someone who needs more contact.
realLife: On a first date: You don’t text much before or after, and you’re fully there in between.
In a fight: You want space to think. Tell them when you’ll be back, so the space doesn’t feel like a punishment.
tips: Your low needs are a gift, but say out loud that you care. A random “thinking of you” costs nothing and means a lot to most people.
match: Best with: Someone with a full life of their own who also loves easy, no-pressure closeness.
Green flag: They respect your quiet days and are warm when you reconnect.
Careful with: Someone who reads every gap as rejection and needs constant proof.

tests.title: Past Wounds
tests.subtitle: Old pain affecting trust
tests.description: Measures how much past experiences (betrayal, abandonment, disrespect) affect your current jealousy triggers.
tests.whatYouLearn: How much the past lives in your present reactions.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps match partners who can handle sensitivity gently (or people with similar healing stage).

options.text: Get angry with them before they’ve even explained
Order a cold coffee and wait. Probably traffic
Feel my chest go tight, then text “all okay?”
Assume the worst, the way it happened before

options.text: Brace for them to disappear too
Feel the old pinch, and remind myself it’s not them
Hear it as just a sentence. New person, new story
Tell them, lightly, that it’s a sore spot for me

questions.text: When you think about your last big heartbreak today, it feels…

options.text: Still close. Some days it’s right there
Like a chapter. I learnt, and I moved on

options.text: I want to say no, but I’m not sure anymore
No. Most people are decent
Yes. It’s just a matter of time
Some would, so I keep my eyes open

options.text: Snap at them, then feel bad later
Mention it calmly, and explain why it bugs me
Laugh it off. They’re not my ex
Go quiet and distant for the evening

options.text: “Maybe a little, sometimes”
“Ha, not true. That chapter’s closed”
“That hurt, because it’s true”
“I do, but I’m trying not to”

options.text: Make a joke of it so it doesn’t sting
Tell it simply, with no bitterness
Feel the old anger come back as I tell it
Give the short version and change the topic

questions.text: A new relationship is going really well. Deep down, you…

options.text: Enjoy it, with a small voice saying “careful”
Wait for the moment it falls apart
Enjoy it. Good things can last
Hold back a little, so it hurts less if it ends

tests.measures: how much past relationship pain affects your current trust and jealousy

VeryHigh.label: The Healed Heart
summaries: Every new person gets a fresh start with you.

Whatever happened before, you’ve made peace with it. It taught you things, and then you let it go. You don’t carry old suspicions into new rooms, and you meet people as they are, not as someone else once was. That kind of openness is rare, and people feel lighter around you.
behaviors: A late reply is just a late reply. It doesn’t remind you of anyone.
You can talk about your past easily, without bitterness or drama.
You believe good things can last, and you let them.
strengths: You love without baggage. New people never pay for old mistakes with you.
weaknesses: You might not get why someone else can’t just let go, and push them too soon.
realLife: On a first date: You arrive curious, with zero assumptions. They feel it within five minutes.
In a fight: You never drag in old hurts, theirs or yours. Today’s fight stays today’s.
tips: If someone you love still carries old hurt, don’t tell them to get over it. Ask what helps. Your calm is a gift when it comes with patience.
match: Best with: Someone who wants to build something fresh, without old ghosts in the room.
Green flag: They let you see their past honestly, and leave it there.
Careful with: Someone still deep in an old story, who isn’t ready for a new one.

High.label: The Page-Turner
summaries: The past is a chapter, not the whole book.

You’ve been through things, and you’ve done the work of moving on. The past taught you what you want and what you won’t accept, and it mostly stays in its place. When something does stir an old memory, you notice it, smile at how far you’ve come, and turn the page.
behaviors: You judge each new person on their own story, not your old one.
You can mention an ex without any heat in your voice.
You know your sore spots and can explain them calmly.
strengths: You give new people a fair chance, and you’re hard to scare off.
weaknesses: You may expect others to have moved on as easily as you did.
realLife: On a first date: The ex question comes up. You answer in two warm lines and ask about their favourite food.
In a fight: You keep it to this relationship and this problem. Old ghosts aren’t invited.
tips: Be patient with someone whose past is louder than yours. Your calm shows them that moving on can be done, and that’s worth more than advice.
match: Best with: Someone emotionally honest who has made peace with their own past.
Green flag: They’re curious about your past without digging for drama.
Careful with: Someone who still brings up their ex every second sentence.

Moderate.label: The Lesson Keeper
summaries: You kept the lessons, and dropped most of the pain.

Your past left a few marks, and you’ve made peace with most of them. Now and then an old memory stirs, a late reply or a familiar line, but you can usually tell the past from the present. You carry lessons, not grudges, and you’re still learning to put the last few down.
behaviors: You feel an old pinch sometimes, and remind yourself this is someone new.
You can talk about your exes calmly, with a small sigh here and there.
You trust, with a little caution you earned the hard way.
strengths: You learn from what happened, so you choose better each time.
weaknesses: A small, unhealed bit can still flare up on a stressful day.
realLife: On a first date: A song from an old relationship plays in the café. You feel it for a second, then ask about their playlist.
In a fight: You notice when an old feeling sneaks in, and you say so. It clears the air.
tips: When an old feeling flares, name it: “That’s from before, not from you.” Saying it, to yourself or to them, keeps the past where it belongs.
match: Best with: Someone kind and open, who’s done some growing of their own.
Green flag: They talk about their own past honestly, without bitterness.
Careful with: Someone with the very same habits that hurt you before.

Low.label: The Guarded Romantic
summaries: You want love, and you keep one hand on your shield.

You’ve been hurt before, and you learnt from it, maybe a little too well. You’re open to love, but you watch for the signs that once came before pain. Most days you manage it well. Some days, an old memory gets there before you do.
behaviors: Habits that remind you of an ex bother you more than they should.
You let people in slowly, one tested layer at a time.
Good things make you happy and a little nervous, both at once.
strengths: You’re wise about people. You spot real problems that others miss.
weaknesses: Your shield can stay up even when the person in front of you is safe.
realLife: On a first date: You enjoy it, and you quietly note how they treat the waiter. Old lessons.
In a fight: You may reach for your shield. Try telling them: “This reminds me of something old.”
tips: Make a short list of the habits that stir old memories, and share it when it feels right. Someone who knows your sore spots can avoid pressing them.
match: Best with: Someone steady and honest, who earns trust patiently and doesn’t rush you.
Green flag: They’re the same person on day fifty as on day one.
Careful with: Someone who gets annoyed that you need time to trust.

VeryLow.label: The Healing Heart
summaries: Still sore in places, and still brave enough to love.

Something in your past hurt you deeply, and parts of it still feel fresh. Certain words, a late reply or a familiar habit can bring it all back in a second, and your guard goes up before you can think. That isn’t weakness. It’s a heart that remembers, and the fact that you’re still open to love says a lot about your courage.
behaviors: Some ordinary moments can feel like a replay of something painful.
You may expect the ending before the story has really begun.
When someone is gentle and steady with you, you notice, and it means everything.
strengths: You know pain, so you’re deeply kind about other people’s hurts.
weaknesses: A new person can end up paying for an old person’s mistakes.
realLife: On a first date: You like them, and you still keep one foot near the door. That’s allowed.
In a fight: Old fear can make you say more than you mean. Pause and ask: is this about them, or about before?
tips: Tell the story that still hurts to someone you trust, a close friend or a counsellor. Said out loud, old pain slowly loosens its grip on new love.
match: Best with: Someone patient and consistent, who doesn’t take your guard personally.
Green flag: They keep small promises, over and over, without making a show of it.
Careful with: Someone who uses your past against you in an argument.

You trust, with a little caution you earned the hard way.

Green flag: They talk about their own past honestly, without bitterness.
Careful with: Someone with the very same habits that hurt you before.

tests.title: Independence & Trust
tests.subtitle: Freedom without fear
tests.description: Measures whether you can trust when you’re not together and allow independence without fear.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your trust capacity with distance and freedom.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Best matches when both allow independence without control.

Glad. I’ll make my own plans

questions.text: Trust, for you, comes from…

options.text: Who they are, wherever they are

tests.measures: how well you balance giving your partner independence with trusting them

VeryHigh.label: The Roomy Heart
summaries: Love with room to fly, and a place to land.

You trust the person, not their location. Distance, solo trips, new people and days without a word don’t shake you, because you believe in who they are. You give people the whole sky, and that’s exactly why they keep flying back to you.
behaviors: A long-distance year sounds doable to you, maybe even romantic.
You cheer when they plan a trip with their gang.
You never ask where they are. They usually tell you anyway.
strengths: You make freedom and love feel like the same thing.
weaknesses: Someone who needs more contact may feel you don’t miss them enough.
realLife: On a first date: They’re off to Ladakh solo next week. You’re thrilled for them, not worried.
In a fight: You stay calm and curious, and you never make them account for every hour.
tips: Your trust is rare and lovely. Let them see that you miss them too: a “come home soon” now and then keeps the sky warm.
match: Best with: Someone just as independent, who also believes trust doesn’t need tracking.
Green flag: They come back from every trip happy to see you.
Careful with: Someone who uses your trust as cover, staying vague and distant.

High.label: The Breathing-Room Giver
summaries: You give love room to breathe, and it comes back to you.

You believe two full lives make a stronger couple than one shared calendar. Their trips, their gang and their new hobbies feel like good news to you, and you’re busy with your own. Unease visits sometimes, but it rarely stays long.
behaviors: You enjoy your quiet week when they travel, and their stories when they’re back.
Their new people are welcome, and you look forward to meeting them.
You don’t need daily updates to feel close.
strengths: With you, people never have to choose between love and their own life.
weaknesses: You might be so relaxed that they wonder whether you missed them at all.
realLife: On a first date: They have to leave early for a cousin’s party. You say “have fun” and plan the next date.
In a fight: You never make it about their freedom. You talk about what actually went wrong.
tips: Tell them you missed them, out loud, even when you were fine. Freedom feels even better with a warm welcome home.
match: Best with: Someone with their own passions, who loves coming home to you.
Green flag: They bring their world home to you and share it.
Careful with: Someone who mistakes your easy trust for not caring.

Moderate.label: The Warm Thread
summaries: You trust them out there, as long as the thread stays warm.

You’re happy for them to have trips, friends and plans of their own, and you have yours. What keeps you easy is a warm thread between you: a call, a photo, a “miss you”. When the thread goes quiet for too long, you feel it, and you say so.
behaviors: A week apart is fine, with a few calls in between.
You like meeting their new people, just to put faces to names.
A silent day makes you restless, but you don’t panic.
strengths: You balance freedom and closeness, and people feel both with you.
weaknesses: On a low day, one missed call can feel bigger than it is.
realLife: On a first date: They say they travel a lot for work. You ask where to, and quietly hope they’re a good texter.
In a fight: You say what you need to feel connected, simply, and listen to what they need too.
tips: Settle on a simple rhythm for time apart, like one call a day. Knowing it’s coming lets you relax in between.
match: Best with: Someone independent who still sends a photo from wherever they are.
Green flag: They stay in touch on trips without being reminded.
Careful with: Someone who vanishes when they’re away and acts surprised you noticed.

Low.label: The Stay-Close Type
summaries: You love freedom in theory, and closeness in practice.

You believe people should have their own lives, and you try to live by it. But when they’re away for long, or busy with new people, a small unease creeps in. You’re happiest with plenty of togetherness and a clear, regular way of staying in touch.
behaviors: You’re fine with their plans, as long as you hear from them along the way.
A new group of people in their life makes you curious, and a bit uneasy.
Long distance sounds hard to you, and you’d want a strong routine for it.
strengths: You keep the connection strong. Nobody drifts away from you by accident.
weaknesses: Wanting regular contact can feel like a check-in schedule to a freer spirit.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their weekend plans, partly curious, partly hoping to be in them soon.
In a fight: You may push for more time together. Ask instead what would help you both feel close.
tips: Try one weekend fully on your own plans while they’re on theirs. Notice that you’re still close on Monday. It gets easier every time.
match: Best with: Someone who also loves lots of time together and doesn’t mind a nightly call.
Green flag: They include you in their world and introduce you to their people.
Careful with: Someone who keeps big parts of their life completely separate from you.

VeryLow.label: The Homesick Heart
summaries: When they’re away, a part of you is too.

You feel safest when the people you love are close, and distance makes your heart restless. A work trip, a weekend with cousins or a quiet day offline can fill your head with questions. It isn’t that you think they’re doing wrong. Being apart just feels like losing a little piece of home.
behaviors: Their trips can feel long, even when they call every night.
You feel calmer when you know where they are and who they’re with.
When they come back, your relief is real, and so is your joy.
strengths: You love closely and devotedly. Nobody ever wonders whether you miss them.
weaknesses: Your unease can make their time apart feel like something they have to apologise for.
realLife: On a first date: You love that they live close by, and you’re already hoping the next date is soon.
In a fight: If the fight is about time apart, say the feeling, “I miss you and I get scared”, not a rule.
tips: Build a life you love on your own too: a class, a weekend ritual, your own gang. The fuller your days, the shorter their trips will feel.
match: Best with: Someone warm and communicative, who keeps in touch naturally when they’re away.
Green flag: They share their plans and check in without being asked.
Careful with: Someone who goes silent for days and calls it “freedom”.

Undecided.label: The Warm Thread
summaries: You trust them out there, as long as the thread stays warm.

You’re happy for them to have trips, friends and plans of their own, and you have yours. What keeps you easy is a warm thread between you: a call, a photo, a “miss you”. When the thread goes quiet for too long, you feel it, and you say so.
behaviors: A week apart is fine, with a few calls in between.
You like meeting their new people, just to put faces to names.
A silent day makes you restless, but you don’t panic.
strengths: You balance freedom and closeness, and people feel both with you.
weaknesses: On a low day, one missed call can feel bigger than it is.
realLife: On a first date: They say they travel a lot for work. You ask where to, and quietly hope they’re a good texter.
In a fight: You say what you need to feel connected, simply, and listen to what they need too.
tips: Settle on a simple rhythm for time apart, like one call a day. Knowing it’s coming lets you relax in between.
match: Best with: Someone independent who still sends a photo from wherever they are.
Green flag: They stay in touch on trips without being reminded.
Careful with: Someone who vanishes when they’re away and acts surprised you noticed.

tests.subtitle: How much you’re building a home
tests.description: Measures how much you value family building, stability, and home life.
tests.whatYouLearn: Whether you’re oriented to building a home and long-term stability.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Avoids mismatch between ‘freedom’ phase and ‘build family’ phase.

questions.text: Cousin’s wedding. An aunty corners you at the dessert counter: “So, when is your turn?” You say…

options.text: “Not for a few years. Life first, Aunty.”
“Soon, I hope. I’m actually looking.”
“When the right person comes, Aunty.”
Laugh, grab a gulab jamun, change the topic

options.text: A full passport and no fixed address
A home, one person, Sunday lunches

questions.text: Third date. They say, “I’m looking for something serious, heading to marriage.” You feel…

options.text: A little flattered, a little cornered
Relieved. Finally, someone who says it
Like asking for the bill
Curious. Let’s see if it’s us

questions.text: Mum forwards a biodata to your WhatsApp: “Just see once.” You…

options.text: Send “Ma, not now 🙏” and mute the chat
Read it properly. Twice
Reply “Let’s see” and leave it there

questions.text: Midnight scrolling. You keep landing on…

options.text: Home tours and wedding reels
Cheap flights to anywhere
Couple memes, then flight deals

questions.text: Three months in, they ask, “Where do you see us in a year?” You say…

options.text: “Still together, figuring it out”
“A year? I plan weekends, not years”
“Meeting each other’s families, I hope”
“Honestly, I need a minute with that one”

questions.text: You’ve just moved flats. A month later you have…

options.text: Mostly unpacked. The rest can wait
A mattress, a charger and no regrets
Curtains, plants and a proper dinner set

questions.text: Being someone’s person, every day, for years. That sounds…

options.text: A lot to take on, for now
Like the whole point

tests.measures: how ready and oriented you are toward building a family and home life

VeryHigh.label: The Forever Seeker
summaries: Ready for the keys, the person and the Sunday lunches.

You know what you want: a home, a person, a life you build together, and you want it soon. You’ve had your fun and your freedom, and someone to come home to now feels like the next great adventure. You don’t play games, because you’re not here to play.
behaviors: You say it early: “I’m looking for something that leads to marriage.”
You notice how they talk to their parents, and how they talk about the future.
A slow “let’s see” from someone you like can feel like a very long wait.
strengths: Total clarity. Nobody has to guess what you’re looking for.
weaknesses: Wanting it this much can make you skip the part where you get to know them.
realLife: On a first date: You ask what they’re looking for before the starters arrive, kindly but clearly.
In a fight: You jump to “what does this mean for us?”. One fight is not the end of the future.
tips: Ready is beautiful. Still let three months be three months: forever goes better with someone you really know.
match: Best with: Someone who’s also ready now, not someday, and says so.
Green flag: They introduce you to their people and talk about next year with you in it.
Careful with: “I’m not sure what I want” after six months. Believe them.

High.label: The Nest Builder
summaries: Already saving a spot for someone.

You’re not in a hurry, but you’re clearly headed somewhere: a home, a person, a life with a shape. You date with intention and notice who could fit. Freedom is nice; building something lasting feels nicer.
behaviors: By the third date, you’ve noticed whether they talk about the future too.
You like a plan for the two of you: the next trip, the next step, the next big holiday.
You’d rather invest in one good person than keep your options open.
strengths: People feel safe with you, because you’re clearly here to build.
weaknesses: You can size up someone’s future before you’ve properly met their present.
realLife: On a first date: You’re having fun, and somewhere at the back of your mind you’re asking: could this be home?
In a fight: You fight for the relationship, not for the point. You want to fix it, not win it.
tips: Enjoy the first few months as months, not as an interview for forever. The right one will still be right.
match: Best with: Someone who wants the same kind of life and enjoys building it slowly.
Green flag: They make plans with you weeks ahead, and keep them.
Careful with: Someone who loves the idea of you but goes vague when you say “future”.

Moderate.label: The Maybe-Soon
summaries: Ready when it’s right, not before.

You’re not chasing a wedding and you’re not running from one. If the right person walked in tomorrow, you’d make room; if they don’t, your life is full anyway. You’ve made peace with not knowing the timing.
behaviors: You date with an open mind: it could be a summer, it could be forever.
You’ll talk about the future, but the present has to feel right first.
Meeting the family doesn’t scare you, as long as you got there naturally.
strengths: You can go either way without panic, so people relax around you.
weaknesses: Being open to everything can look like wanting nothing in particular.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their family and their travel list with the same interest.
In a fight: When the future comes up, you say “I’m open”. Then say what you’d actually like.
tips: Open is good. Now name one thing you’d love in five years. It turns “maybe” into a direction.
match: Best with: Someone steady and honest who lets things unfold at a human pace.
Green flag: They’re clear about what they want and kind about where you are.
Careful with: Someone who keeps you in the “we’ll see” zone for years.

Low.label: The Someday Settler
summaries: Love now, nest later.

You do want a home and a person one day, you just don’t want to start on it this year. Right now you’re in the good middle: serious about people, light about timelines. You’ll know when you’re ready, and you won’t let anyone else announce it.
behaviors: You can be in a real, loyal relationship without a five-year plan attached.
Big future questions make you smile and say “let’s get there first”.
You’d plan a trip with someone long before you’d plan a home.
strengths: You let love grow at its own speed, so it rarely feels forced.
weaknesses: “Someday” can stay someday for a very long time if you never give it a shape.
realLife: On a first date: You talk travel and favourite food, and dodge “so what are you looking for?” with a grin.
In a fight: If they push for a timeline, you say “soon”. Give them a rough when, not just a shrug.
tips: Give “someday” a rough shape, like “in two or three years”. It helps the right person wait without worrying.
match: Best with: Someone patient who wants a future too, but isn’t in a rush to start it.
Green flag: They enjoy where you are now and talk about later without pressure.
Careful with: Someone who sets deadlines for your heart: “by Diwali we should know”.

VeryLow.label: The Not-Yet Nester
summaries: Life first. The nest can wait.

You’re building yourself right now: the career, the cities, the people, the mistakes worth making. A home and a family might come one day, but not because a calendar or an aunty says so. You’d rather arrive there whole than be rushed into it.
behaviors: You date for the joy of it, and you’re honest that forever isn’t on the table yet.
Wedding talk on the third date makes you look for the exit.
You’re generous with your time and your adventures, just not with promises.
strengths: You never promise what you can’t give, so nobody is left waiting on you.
weaknesses: Someone falling hard may hear “not yet” as “not you”. Say which one you mean.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest a new place across town and stay out much later than planned.
In a fight: When it turns to “where is this going?”, you go quiet. Answer honestly, even if it’s “I don’t know yet”.
tips: Say your season out loud early: “I’m not ready for forever yet.” The right people will stay for the now.
match: Best with: Someone with big plans of their own who isn’t counting down to a wedding.
Green flag: They’re happy in the present and don’t treat your freedom as a phase to fix.
Careful with: Someone who says “casual is fine” while quietly planning the mehendi.

Undecided.label: The Maybe-Soon
summaries: Ready when it’s right, not before.

You’re not chasing a wedding and you’re not running from one. If the right person walked in tomorrow, you’d make room; if they don’t, your life is full anyway. You’ve made peace with not knowing the timing.

You’ll talk about the future, but the present has to feel right first.
Meeting the family doesn’t scare you, as long as you got there naturally.
strengths: You can go either way without panic, so people relax around you.

In a fight: When the future comes up, you say “I’m open”. Then say what you’d actually like.

Green flag: They’re clear about what they want and kind about where you are.
Careful with: Someone who keeps you in the “we’ll see” zone for years.

Smile nervously and pray they don’t cry

Kids jumping on the bed, asking for parathas

questions.text: Is there a baby name saved somewhere in your Notes app?

options.text: One, half as a joke
No. And there won’t be
Three, ranked, with meanings

questions.text: On a flight, a toddler kicks your seat for an hour. You…

options.text: Play peekaboo over the seat
Smile at the tired parent, put on headphones
Quietly thank yourself for your life choices

questions.text: Second date. They say, “I don’t see kids in my future.” You…

options.text: Exhale. Same here
Feel a little sad. Kids are in mine
Want to talk about it. It’s early, people change
Like them, but make a mental note. It matters

options.text: Start a new group for the rest of us
Heart a few, scroll past the rest
Love it. Keep them coming

options.text: “The cool aunt or uncle. That’s my calling”
“The one who knows every teacher’s name”
“The fun one, I hope. If it happens”
“Honestly? I’ve never pictured it”

questions.text: Someone says, “Kids change everything.” You think…

options.text: “Exactly. That’s why I want them”
“Exactly. That’s why I don’t”
“True. The hard bits and the lovely bits”

tests.measures: how you feel about having children and what role parenthood plays in your future

VeryHigh.label: The Baby-Name Keeper
summaries: The names are picked. The person is next.

Being a parent is one of the things you want most from life, and you’re not shy about it. You light up around kids, you’ve thought about the bedtime stories, and there’s probably a name or two saved somewhere. A home full of noise sounds like the best kind of home to you.
behaviors: Kids come up by date two, because you can’t picture a future without them.
Watching someone play with a little cousin makes you fall a bit harder.
You’d pick a loud family Sunday over a fancy trip, most weeks.
strengths: Your warmth with kids shows exactly what kind of home you’d make.
weaknesses: You can love the dream of a family so much that you hurry past the person.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their family, and by dessert you know if kids are a yes.
In a fight: You take it hard if they waver on kids. Ask what’s behind it before deciding what it means.
tips: Ask early, then listen to the answer they give, not the one you’re hoping for.
match: Best with: Someone who wants children as much as you do and says so early.
Green flag: They have their own ideas about raising kids and love talking about them.
Careful with: Someone who says “maybe” about kids just to keep you around.

High.label: The Future Parent
summaries: Kids in the picture, not on the clock.

You do see children in your future, and you think about the kind of parent you’d like to be. You’re not in a hurry, though: the right person and a steady life come first. Somewhere in you there’s already a list of things you’d do differently from your own parents.
behaviors: You bring up kids once things get serious, because it matters to you.
You notice how someone is with a niece or nephew, and it counts.
You’d build a steady home first, then make room for little ones.
strengths: You think ahead about the family you’d build, so it isn’t left to chance.
weaknesses: You may picture someone as a parent before you’ve got to know them as a person.
realLife: On a first date: You notice how they wave back at the toddler at the next table. It tells you a lot.
In a fight: If the future comes up, you need to know you’re on the same page about kids. Ask calmly, not mid-fight.
tips: Ask about kids before you’re in too deep, kindly and directly. It saves two hearts a lot of hurt.
match: Best with: Someone who wants kids too and is happy to get there at a calm pace.
Green flag: They light up around kids and talk about family plans without flinching.
Careful with: “I’ll decide about kids later” from someone who keeps not deciding.

Moderate.label: The Happy Either Way
summaries: A family would be lovely. So would life without one.

You’re genuinely open: if it happens with the right person, you’d be all in, and if it doesn’t, your life is still full. Kids don’t scare you and they don’t define your future. You let the relationship decide more than any plan does.
behaviors: You’d happily raise kids with the right person, or happily travel with them instead.
You don’t rule people out over kids. You talk about it.
You enjoy other people’s children without counting down to your own.
strengths: You can meet almost anyone halfway on the biggest question in love.
weaknesses: Going along with what they want can hide what you actually want.
realLife: On a first date: Kids come up, you say “I’m open”, and you mean it.
In a fight: You try to see both sides. Make sure your own side gets said out loud too.
tips: Open is lovely. Still tell them which way you lean, even slightly. It helps them know you.
match: Best with: Someone with a clear view on kids who loves you for your openness.
Green flag: They’re honest about their own wish and don’t push you to match it.
Careful with: Someone who decides the kids question for both of you, without asking.

Low.label: The Big Maybe
summaries: Kids? Ask me again in a few years.

You haven’t decided, and you’re not going to fake an answer. Some days you can picture it, most days you like your life just as it is. You’d need the right person and the right moment before it ever felt like a yes.
behaviors: When kids come up, you say “I genuinely don’t know yet”, and mean it.
You’d rather figure it out together than tick a box on date one.
Someone who already has names picked makes you a little nervous.
strengths: You don’t pretend. Your honesty keeps the big conversation real.
weaknesses: A maybe can sit untouched for years while life decides for you.
realLife: On a first date: If kids come up, you laugh, say “ask me in a few years”, and ask about their dog.
In a fight: When they push for a yes or no, say “I need time, and I will come back to you on this.” Then do it.
tips: Ask yourself one real question this year: is it fear of the change, or no wish at all? The answer helps.
match: Best with: Someone also unsure, or someone who wants kids and can wait for a real answer.
Green flag: They ask how you feel about kids, then actually listen.
Careful with: Someone sure they want three children by thirty-two.

VeryLow.label: The Plant Parent
summaries: Plenty of love. Just not for a nursery.

You know what your life looks like, and kids aren’t in it. That isn’t coldness: you give your care to people, pets, plants and the work you love, and you like choosing how your days go. You’d rather be the favourite aunt or uncle than a parent you never wanted to be.
behaviors: You say it early and kindly: “I don’t want children.” It saves everyone years.
Your idea of family can be two people, a dog and a lot of travel.
You bring the best gifts to every kid’s birthday party, and leave by seven.
strengths: You’re honest about a big thing early, which is rarer and kinder than it sounds.
weaknesses: You may expect pushback and get defensive before anyone has pushed.
realLife: On a first date: When kids come up, you say “not for me” and watch their face. Relief is a lovely sign.
In a fight: If kids come up again, you stand firm. Say it gently: it lands better than a debate.
tips: Say it by the second date. The right person will hear it as good news, not bad.
match: Best with: Someone who is truly child-free too, not just “not yet”.
Green flag: They respect your choice without a lecture or a “you’ll change your mind”.
Careful with: Someone who hopes you’ll come round. You won’t, and that isn’t fair on either of you.

Undecided.label: The Happy Either Way
summaries: A family would be lovely. So would life without one.

You’re genuinely open: if it happens with the right person, you’d be all in, and if it doesn’t, your life is still full. Kids don’t scare you and they don’t define your future. You let the relationship decide more than any plan does.

You don’t rule people out over kids. You talk about it.
You enjoy other people’s children without counting down to your own.

In a fight: You try to see both sides. Make sure your own side gets said out loud too.
tips: Open is lovely. Still tell them which way you lean, even slightly. It helps them know you.

Green flag: They’re honest about their own wish and don’t push you to match it.
Careful with: Someone who decides the kids question for both of you, without asking.

tests.subtitle: Family involvement tolerance
tests.description: Measures how you handle relatives/in-laws: closeness, boundaries, and influence.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your tolerance for family involvement and your boundary style.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Prevents huge fights about parents and interference.

options.text: Say hi, then mostly lurk
Tell your person, gently, it’s a bit soon
Send a good-morning flower GIF by day two
Mute it and heart the birthday wishes

options.text: Festivals and birthdays
Once a month or so
Every Sunday. I’ll bring dessert

options.text: Lovely to visit, not to live in
Warm. More people, more food, more love

options.text: Smile, and secretly mourn your lazy Saturday
Put the chai on. Love a surprise

Welcome them, and ask for a call next time

options.text: The sangeet and the main day
The reception, briefly, with a good gift
All five, in outfits that match theirs

Accept with a hug. Family helps family

Squeeze your person’s hand under the table: help
Laugh: “Aunty, you’ll be the first to know”
Say kindly that it’s private

tests.measures: how you handle family involvement and in-law relationships

VeryHigh.label: The More-the-Merrier
summaries: More people, more food, more love.

For you, family is a big, loud, warm thing, and loving someone means loving all of them. A house full of voices feels like home, an elder’s opinion feels like care, and you’d rather have too many people at the table than too few. You grew up knowing that family shows up.
behaviors: You’d happily live with their parents, at least for a while.
You want to be part of their family rituals, not a guest at them.
The family WhatsApp group doesn’t scare you. You’re its most active member.
strengths: You make everyone feel at home, from the grandparents to the littlest cousin.
weaknesses: With everyone involved, your person may struggle to find the two of you.
realLife: On a first date: You talk about your family for twenty minutes. Watch their face: it tells you a lot.
In a fight: You may want to call your mum for advice. Ask your person first if that’s okay.
tips: Keep one ritual that’s only yours as a couple. A big family stays sweet when the couple stays close.
match: Best with: Someone from a close family who wants that warmth at home too.
Green flag: Their family welcomes you as one of their own from day one.
Careful with: Someone who wants to keep their family at arm’s length forever.

High.label: The Favourite In-Law
summaries: Their mum already saves you the last laddoo.

Families like you, and you like them back. You remember birthdays, you ask after an uncle’s knee, you actually enjoy the long lunches. You still want your own space, but you see a partner’s family as a bonus, not a test.
behaviors: You call their parents on your own, just to say hi.
Family functions with them feel like fun, not duty.
You listen to advice from their side, and sometimes even follow it.
strengths: You make two families feel like one. That’s a rare gift.
weaknesses: You can say yes to every family plan and run out of steam without saying so.
realLife: On a first date: You ask their mum’s name. By the third date, you know her favourite sweet.
In a fight: You keep both families out of your fights, and you expect the same from them.
tips: Being loved by their family is lovely. Keep a few evenings a week that are only yours anyway.
match: Best with: Someone with a warm family who’s glad you fit right in.
Green flag: They’re just as warm with your family as you are with theirs.
Careful with: Someone who leans on your closeness with their family to skip their own share.

Moderate.label: The Bridge Builder
summaries: Close to the family, clear about the two of you.

You love a family lunch and you love your own front door, and you’ve found a way to have both. You can sit with an aunty for an hour and still answer an opinion with “we’ll think about it”. People on both sides tend to trust you.
behaviors: You’re happy at family functions, and just as happy when it’s just you two.
You take family advice seriously, then decide together.
You’re the one who smooths things over when the families first meet.
strengths: You keep both families close without letting either one take over.
weaknesses: Keeping everyone happy can mean swallowing your own wishes.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their family and trade a funny story about yours.
In a fight: You look for the middle: “Let’s go for lunch, and leave by four.” It usually works.
tips: Settle your rules as a couple before a family event, not in the car on the way there.
match: Best with: Someone who loves their family and knows where the line is.
Green flag: They stand by you in front of their family, and by their family in front of you.
Careful with: Someone who can’t say no to their parents, ever.

Low.label: The Festival Guest
summaries: Warm on the big days, private on the rest.

You genuinely like family, in measured doses. You’ll dress up for the festival, laugh at the uncle jokes and carry the sweets, then you’ll want your own home and your own Sunday back. Closeness, for you, works best with a door you can close.
behaviors: You’re lovely with their parents at events, and glad to go home after.
You prefer a phone call on birthdays to weekly drop-ins.
You’ll go to the wedding, just maybe not all five days of it.
strengths: You’re warm without being swallowed up, so you never resent the family.
weaknesses: Some families measure love in hours spent. Yours may look rationed to them.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their family and enjoy the stories, especially the short ones.
In a fight: You ask for a bit less family time. Offer what you will do, not just what you won’t.
tips: Call their parents once on your own, for no reason. One unprompted call is worth five dutiful visits.
match: Best with: Someone close to their family who’s happy with a few big gatherings a year.
Green flag: They protect your weekends without turning their parents into villains.
Careful with: Expectations of daily calls you never signed up for.

VeryLow.label: The Private Island
summaries: Love the family. From a comfortable distance.

You’re respectful with family, theirs and yours, but your home and your relationship are a country of two. You like visits planned, opinions invited and decisions made by the people who live with them. That isn’t coldness: it’s how you keep love from getting crowded.
behaviors: You’d rather live in your own place, even a smaller one, than share with parents.
Your fights, your money and your plans stay between you two.
You’ll show up for the big days, and keep the rest of the week for yourselves.
strengths: You protect the relationship from outside noise, so it stays yours.
weaknesses: Too much distance can read as disrespect to a family that shows love by showing up.
realLife: On a first date: They mention the family group chat. You ask how many members, slightly scared.
In a fight: If their family comes up, you ask that the final call stays with you two. Say it calmly, not as an ultimatum.
tips: Pick two family things you’ll always show up for. Doing those warmly buys you all the space you need.
match: Best with: Someone who also wants their own home and handles their own family kindly.
Green flag: They tell their parents “we’ll decide”, and “we” means the two of you.
Careful with: Someone who runs every decision past home first.

Undecided.label: The Bridge Builder

You love a family lunch and you love your own front door, and you’ve found a way to have both. You can sit with an aunty for an hour and still answer an opinion with “we’ll think about it”. People on both sides tend to trust you.
behaviors: You’re happy at family functions, and just as happy when it’s just you two.
You take family advice seriously, then decide together.
You’re the one who smooths things over when the families first meet.

weaknesses: Keeping everyone happy can mean swallowing your own wishes.

In a fight: You look for the middle: “Let’s go for lunch, and leave by four.” It usually works.
tips: Settle your rules as a couple before a family event, not in the car on the way there.
match: Best with: Someone who loves their family and knows where the line is.
Green flag: They stand by you in front of their family, and by their family in front of you.
Careful with: Someone who can’t say no to their parents, ever.

tests.title: Home Routines
tests.subtitle: Daily life structure at home
tests.description: Measures how much you value routines, home comfort, cleanliness, and shared household rhythm.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your home-life rhythm (structured vs flexible).
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Home routines mismatch creates daily friction, even with love.

questions.text: Your ideal Sunday morning at home:

options.text: Whatever happens. No plan is the plan
Clean the flat, big breakfast, plants watered
Sleep in, then a slow tidy-up

questions.text: Dishes in the sink at 11 pm. You…

options.text: Wash them now. I can’t sleep otherwise
Leave them. Morning me will handle it

questions.text: Most weeknights, dinner at your place is…

options.text: Home-cooked, at the table, around the same time
Swiggy at whatever o’clock, on the bed
Half cooked, half ordered
Something quick on the sofa, with a show

questions.text: Open your fridge right now. There’s…

options.text: Ketchup, ice and one sad lemon
The basics, and Maggi for emergencies
Labelled boxes, chopped veggies, tomorrow’s lunch

questions.text: First time at their place. Clothes on the chair, bed unmade. You…

options.text: Feel right at home
Notice it, and don’t mind
Fight the urge to fold one shirt
Don’t notice until they apologise

questions.text: A ritual you’d love to share with someone at home:

options.text: A weekly movie night, if we’re both free
No rituals. Every day different
Evening chai on the balcony, every day

questions.text: Sharing a home with someone. Chores should be…

options.text: Roughly fair, no chart needed
On a list, split fairly, done on time
Whoever notices, does it. Eventually

questions.text: Friday night after a long week. You’d rather…

options.text: Be anywhere but home
Be home: blanket, comfort food, own bed
One drink out, then home by eleven
See where the night takes me

tests.measures: how much you value shared domestic routines and home-building habits

VeryHigh.label: The Heart of the Home
summaries: You don’t live in a house. You make a home.

For you, home is where life really happens: the masala dabba is labelled, dinner is at the table, and Friday night means your own blanket. Routines don’t feel like rules to you, they feel like love you can repeat every day. People who visit don’t want to leave.
behaviors: Your idea of romance is cooking together on a Tuesday.
Your home has to feel calm and clean for you to feel calm.
Small rituals, like cooking to the same old playlist, beat grand gestures for you.
strengths: You build homes that people feel safe in. That’s a real gift.
weaknesses: You might redo their chores without a word, then feel nobody noticed.
realLife: On a first date: You’d secretly love a cooking-class date, and you notice if they rinse their glass.
In a fight: You go quiet and start cleaning. Say what’s wrong before the kitchen sparkles.
tips: Let some mess be. A lived-in home with a happy person in it beats a perfect one.
match: Best with: A fellow homebody who loves routines as much as you do.
Green flag: They’re happy to stay in on a Friday and help you make dinner.
Careful with: Someone who never wants to be home before midnight.

High.label: The Sunday Reset
summaries: Clean sheets, dinner at eight, a home that works.

Home is your happy place, and you look after it. You like dinner at a proper time, a weekly clean-up and a few rituals that make ordinary days feel good. A messy kitchen can sour your mood; a tidy one makes the whole week better.
behaviors: You show love with home things: a cooked meal, fresh towels, a made bed.
You’d rather host a dinner than go to a loud bar.
A shared routine, like an evening walk, makes you feel close.
strengths: People feel cared for in your home before you say a word.
weaknesses: Your standards can feel like rules to someone more relaxed.
realLife: On a first date: You’re on time, and already wondering whether they’d like your cooking.
In a fight: You’ll bring up the wet towel on the bed. Bring it up once, kindly, then let it go.
tips: Let one corner of the home be theirs to keep however they like. It saves a hundred small fights.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys home life and does their share without reminders.
Green flag: They notice what you do at home, and thank you for it.
Careful with: Someone who treats your home like a hotel.

Moderate.label: The Cosy Realist
summaries: A warm home, a few habits, no strict rules.

You like your home warm and working: clean sheets, a couple of rituals, food that isn’t always ordered. You also know life happens, so the dishes can wait a night and Sunday can be lazy. It’s a home people can actually live in.
behaviors: You like a few shared habits, like Sunday breakfast, without a timetable.
You notice mess, but you don’t make it a big deal.
You’re as happy staying in as going out, depending on the week.
strengths: You make a home that works for tidy people and messy ones.
weaknesses: You may let small habits slide until one of you is annoyed.
realLife: On a first date: You pick a cosy café and stay till they start stacking the chairs.
In a fight: You’re fair about it: “You cook, I clean” is your kind of peace deal.
tips: Choose one ritual together, like Sunday breakfast, and protect it. Small habits make a home feel like yours.
match: Best with: Someone who wants a warm home, not a perfect one.
Green flag: They pull their weight at home without being asked twice.
Careful with: Someone who leaves every chore to “whoever notices”.

Low.label: The Easy Flatmate
summaries: Relaxed at home, tidy enough for guests.
You like a comfortable home, not a perfect one. You clean before people come over, cook when you feel like it and order without guilt when you don’t. Routines are nice ideas you visit now and then.
behaviors: You’re easy to live with: no lectures about where the towels go.
You’d rather go out for dinner than plan a weekly menu.
You tidy in bursts, usually right before their parents visit.
strengths: You keep home light and easy, so it never feels like a job.
weaknesses: What looks relaxed to you can look like “I do everything” to them.
realLife: On a first date: You’re flexible about the place and the time. They pick, you show up happy.
In a fight: When chores come up, you say “I’ll do it”. Do it that same evening, and it’s over.
tips: Ask which one thing at home matters most to them, and make that your thing.
match: Best with: Someone who likes a relaxed home but cares about the basics.
Green flag: They handle mess with a joke, not a sigh.
Careful with: Someone who wants every evening planned around the kitchen.

VeryLow.label: The Happy Chaos
summaries: Home is wherever the charger is.

Your home is lived in, loudly. Dinner happens when you’re hungry, the laundry chair has seen things, and no two days look the same. You’d rather spend your energy on people and plans than on folding fitted sheets, and honestly, you’re rarely home anyway.
behaviors: You’re the one who suggests eating on the floor because the table is covered.
A chore chart can feel like a school timetable to you.
You bring life into a home, just not always the tidy kind.
strengths: Nothing at home stresses you, so you’re great to live with in a crisis.
weaknesses: Your “I’ll do it later” can turn into their “I always do it”.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest a street-food crawl instead of a sit-down dinner, and stay out late.
In a fight: If it’s about the dishes, it’s rarely about the dishes. Do them, then talk.
tips: Pick one chore that’s fully yours and never let it slide. One reliable thing changes how the rest is seen.
match: Best with: Someone relaxed about mess, or someone who loves tidying and doesn’t keep score.
Green flag: They laugh at the pile of clothes, and help you sort it once.
Careful with: Someone who measures love by how the kitchen looks.

Undecided.label: The Cosy Realist

You like your home warm and working: clean sheets, a couple of rituals, food that isn’t always ordered. You also know life happens, so the dishes can wait a night and Sunday can be lazy. It’s a home people can actually live in.

You notice mess, but you don’t make it a big deal.
You’re as happy staying in as going out, depending on the week.

tests.title: Caregiving Energy
tests.subtitle: How nurturing you are
tests.description: Measures whether you naturally care for loved ones during sickness, stress, or hard seasons.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your caregiving tendency and emotional reliability.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps match partners who expect strong support vs those who prefer independence.

questions.text: They text: “101 fever, dying 🤒.” You…

options.text: Send “Rest well, call if you need anything”
Show up with khichdi, a thermometer and a blanket
Order soup to their door and check in at night
Call once in the evening to see how it’s going

questions.text: Your flatmate gets bad news and starts crying in the kitchen. You…

options.text: Stay, though you don’t know what to say
Freeze a bit. Fixing is easier than feeling
Move closer: tissues, water, a hand on theirs

questions.text: A parent needs care for a month after surgery. You’d…

options.text: Arrange the best help and visit when possible
Move back home for the month, no question
Split it with siblings: shifts, a nurse, a plan

questions.text: Being really needed by someone feels…

options.text: A bit much. I love people who manage
Good. It’s how I know I matter

questions.text: A friend asks you to keep their dog for a week. You…

options.text: Say yes and send daily photos
Say yes, if they leave instructions
Help them find a good sitter instead

questions.text: They come home after an awful day and drop onto the sofa. You…

options.text: Give them space, check in later
Let them be. They’ll say if they need something
Make their favourite food without asking
Sit down and ask what happened

questions.text: They mentioned a dentist appointment last week. That morning you…

options.text: Remember later and ask how it went
Text “All the best, brave one 🦷”
Wouldn’t remember, honestly

questions.text: You’re hosting. You’re the one who…

options.text: Points to the kitchen: “Help yourselves”
Makes sure everyone has a drink
Keeps refilling plates until they beg you to stop

tests.measures: how nurturing and caring you are in a domestic context

VeryHigh.label: The Human Blanket
summaries: Warm, steady, and there before anyone asks.

Caring for people isn’t something you do, it’s who you are. You’re the one at the hospital bedside, the one who knows everyone’s medicines, the one who keeps refilling plates. Being needed feels right to you, and people feel safe in your hands.
behaviors: You’d take leave to look after them, and not think twice.
You feel closest when you’re caring for each other in small ways.
Their bad day becomes your project, with food, a plan and a blanket.
strengths: Nobody feels alone around you. Ever.
weaknesses: You may care for everyone except yourself, and burn out without telling anyone.
realLife: On a first date: You check they got home safe, then ask if they drank enough water.
In a fight: You’ll want to soothe their hurt before your own. Say what hurt you, too.
tips: Ask for help once a week, for anything at all. Being cared for is a skill, and you deserve to practise it.
match: Best with: Someone gentle who loves being looked after, and looks after you right back.
Green flag: They insist on caring for you when you’re the one who’s sick.
Careful with: Someone who lets you carry everything and calls it love.

High.label: The Soup Bringer
summaries: Fever? Bad day? A dabba is already on its way.

Taking care of people is one of your favourite ways to love them. You remember the doctor’s appointment, bring the khichdi, sit through the sad film. You also know when to step back, which is exactly why people let you care for them.
behaviors: When they’re sick, you’re at the door with food before they ask.
You remember the small stresses in their week and ask how they went.
Looking after them feels good, as long as they look after you too.
strengths: You make people feel held when life gets heavy.
weaknesses: You can give so much that you forget to ask for anything back.
realLife: On a first date: You hear they skipped lunch and order them a starter before your own drink arrives.
In a fight: Even upset, you’ll ask if they’ve eaten. Then you’ll talk.
tips: Let them take care of you sometimes. Being cared for is part of the deal too.
match: Best with: Someone who receives care with gratitude, and gives it back.
Green flag: They notice when you’re tired and make the chai for once.
Careful with: Someone who only calls when they need looking after.

Moderate.label: The Steady Helper
summaries: There when it counts, not hovering in between.

You show up when it matters: the hospital visit, the long call after a breakup, the soup on a sick day. In between, you trust people to run their own lives. Your care isn’t constant, but it’s reliable, and people know it.
behaviors: You check in when they’re ill and drop by if they want you to.
You’re a rock in a crisis, a little less tuned in to small daily worries.
You like caring for each other without needing to be needed.
strengths: People can count on you in a real crisis, without feeling smothered day to day.
weaknesses: You may miss the quiet bad days that don’t look like a crisis.
realLife: On a first date: You ask a real question about their family, and listen properly to the answer.
In a fight: You stay calm and fair, and you check on them afterwards.
tips: Notice the small days too. A two-line text on an ordinary bad day counts as much as a hospital visit.
match: Best with: Someone independent who’s glad to lean on you when it really counts.
Green flag: They care for you back, in their own way, without keeping score.
Careful with: Someone who treats every bad mood as an emergency.

Low.label: The Practical Fixer
summaries: Less hugging, more booking the doctor.

Your care looks like action: you book the appointment, find the right medicine, sort the paperwork. Long emotional talks make you a little restless, but nobody gets things done in a crisis like you. You love people with solutions.
behaviors: When they’re stressed, you make a plan before you make tea.
You’d rather fix their laptop than talk feelings for an hour.
You remember the practical stuff: the insurance, the spare key, the charger.
strengths: In a crisis, you’re the calm one with a plan and the right phone number.
weaknesses: Sometimes they don’t want a fix. They want you to sit and listen.
realLife: On a first date: You notice they’re cold before they do, and swap seats so they’re out of the draught.
In a fight: You jump to solutions. Ask first: “Do you want me to fix this, or just hear it?”
tips: Next time they’re upset, try ten minutes of listening before any solution. It will feel slow. It works.
match: Best with: Someone who sees a fixed tap as love, because it is.
Green flag: They thank you for the practical things, not just the romantic ones.
Careful with: Someone who needs constant emotional rescue and calls it romance.

VeryLow.label: The Gentle Delegator
summaries: You love people by trusting them to stand.

You care, you just don’t hover. When someone’s down you give them room, a clear offer of help and the respect of handling their own life. Nursing, fussing and big emotional scenes don’t come naturally, and you’d rather be honest about that than fake it.
behaviors: When they’re sick, you’ll send food and let them sleep, not sit by the bed.
You like someone who has their own life and doesn’t need managing.
You show love by being steady and fair, not by fussing.
strengths: You never smother anyone. People feel respected around you.
weaknesses: On a really bad day, your space can feel like absence. Ask what they need.
realLife: On a first date: You don’t ask about their worst year. You let them bring it up if they want.
In a fight: You step back to let things cool. Say “I’m still here” before you leave the room.
tips: When they’re low, ask one simple question: “Company or space?” Then give exactly that.
match: Best with: Someone independent who gets through a cold with a blanket and a playlist, alone.
Green flag: They tell you clearly when they need you, so you don’t have to guess.
Careful with: Someone who expects you to read their mood and rescue them every time.

Undecided.label: The Steady Helper
summaries: There when it counts, not hovering in between.

You show up when it matters: the hospital visit, the long call after a breakup, the soup on a sick day. In between, you trust people to run their own lives. Your care isn’t constant, but it’s reliable, and people know it.
behaviors: You check in when they’re ill and drop by if they want you to.
You’re a rock in a crisis, a little less tuned in to small daily worries.
You like caring for each other without needing to be needed.
strengths: People can count on you in a real crisis, without feeling smothered day to day.
weaknesses: You may miss the quiet bad days that don’t look like a crisis.

In a fight: You stay calm and fair, and you check on them afterwards.
tips: Notice the small days too. A two-line text on an ordinary bad day counts as much as a hospital visit.
match: Best with: Someone independent who’s glad to lean on you when it really counts.
Green flag: They care for you back, in their own way, without keeping score.
Careful with: Someone who treats every bad mood as an emergency.

tests.title: Career vs Family
tests.subtitle: Balancing ambition with home
tests.description: Measures how you balance career growth with family/home responsibilities.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your priority balance under time pressure.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps align expectations about time, ambition, and home responsibilities.

questions.text: A promotion with 12-hour days, or your current role with evenings free?

options.text: The promotion. This is my building decade
Evenings free. Time is the real salary

questions.text: Your sister’s engagement falls on the day of your biggest client pitch this year. You…

options.text: Pitch in the morning, reach by the evening
Go to the engagement. Someone else can pitch
Pitch. She’ll understand, and I’ll make it up
Ask to move the pitch, then decide

options.text: Excuse yourself and open the laptop
Reply once dinner’s done
Type a quick reply under the table
See it at 9:30, answer at 9 am

options.text: Half family, half my own trips
Nothing much. I barely take them
Family: weddings, visits, festivals at home

questions.text: Your dad’s 60th birthday falls on a Wednesday afternoon. You…

options.text: Call in the morning, celebrate at the weekend
Take the day off. Obviously
Leave early and log back in at night

options.text: “Dinner with my people, most nights”
“My name on something big”
“A good role, and Sundays that are sacred”

Volunteer, happily
Find help so neither of us has to
