Morning on the project, evening with family
With family, phone on silent. It can wait
Mostly on it, with a family lunch in between

tests.measures: how you balance career ambition with family and home life

VeryHigh.label: The Family-First Heart
summaries: Work is what you do. Family is why.

For you, family isn’t something you fit around work. It’s the reason you work at all. You’d skip the big pitch for a sister’s engagement, take the slower path for evenings at home, and never feel you lost anything. You measure a good life by who’s at your table.
behaviors: Your evenings are for home, and you guard them.
You’d slow down at work in a heartbeat if the family needed you.
Someone who never switches off from work would worry you.
strengths: People feel like your priority, because they are.
weaknesses: Giving up too much at work can leave you feeling stuck later.
realLife: On a first date: You talk about your family within ten minutes, with pride.
In a fight: You defend family time fiercely. Make sure you hear their ambitions too.
tips: Keep growing at work, even slowly. A family-first person with a bit of fire gets the best of both.
match: Best with: Someone family-centred who sees home time as the real success.
Green flag: They choose family events over work without thinking twice.
Careful with: Someone who always says “next time” to family plans.

High.label: The Sunday-Lunch Loyalist
summaries: Ambitious, but family wins the tie.

You care about your work and you’re good at it, but when it clashes with family, family usually wins. You’d take a smaller title for evenings at home, and you don’t see that as giving up. For you, a career supports the life; it isn’t the life.
behaviors: Your phone stays away at dinner, and you hope theirs does too.
You plan work around family festivals, not the other way round.
You want someone who’s proud of their work and still home on time.
strengths: You know what matters, and you keep it at the centre.
weaknesses: You may undersell your own ambition, even to yourself.
realLife: On a first date: You leave work on time for it, and your phone stays in your bag all evening.
In a fight: If work starts eating your evenings together, you raise it early and kindly.
tips: Keep one ambition just for you, however small. Family-first works best when you’re growing too.
match: Best with: Someone who values home time as much as you and works smart.
Green flag: They switch off from work for family, without being asked.
Careful with: Someone who calls you “not ambitious” for leaving at six.

Moderate.label: The Calendar Juggler
summaries: Career and home, both in the calendar.

You want both, a career you’re proud of and a home life you love, and you work hard to have them. Some weeks lean one way, some the other. You make it work with plans, phone alarms and a colour-coded calendar.
behaviors: You’ll leave work early for a special dinner, and log back in after.
You want someone who shares the juggling, not just watches it.
Your weekends are sacred. Mostly.
strengths: You keep a lot of plates spinning and rarely drop the important ones.
weaknesses: Giving everything to both can leave nothing for you.
realLife: On a first date: It’s in your calendar with two alarms, and you’re genuinely excited.
In a fight: You pull out the calendar to find a fair split. Ask how they feel first.
tips: Choose together the few things that never move: a birthday, a Sunday lunch. Everything else can flex.
match: Best with: Someone organised who is juggling career and home too.
Green flag: They share the planning, the chores and the calendar.
Careful with: Someone who leaves all the juggling to you.

Low.label: The Hustler With a Heart
summaries: Work first, most days. Family on the big ones.

You’re ambitious and you’re not sorry about it, but you never miss the moments that really count. Work gets most weekdays; birthdays, weddings and emergencies get all of you. You’re still working out exactly where the line sits.
behaviors: You’ll miss a random Tuesday, but never the anniversary.
You might answer one work email on holiday. Or three.
You want someone who respects your drive and reminds you to switch off.
strengths: You build a career without losing the people who matter.
weaknesses: Ordinary days add up. Big days alone don’t make up for many missed small ones.
realLife: On a first date: You squeeze it in after work, then stay much longer than you planned.
In a fight: You say “I’ll make it up to you”. Name the day you will, right there.
tips: Pick two ordinary evenings a week to be home, properly home. The small days are where love lives.
match: Best with: Someone with their own ambitions who also knows how to drag you to dinner.
Green flag: They plan around your busy weeks without making you feel guilty.
Careful with: Someone who wants all of your evenings from day one.

VeryLow.label: The Go-Getter
summaries: This decade is for building. Home can wait.

You’re in your building years and you know it: the career, the skills, the name. You love your family, but right now ambition gets the best hours of your day. You’d rather be honest about that than promise evenings you can’t give.
behaviors: You fall for people who get excited about your work, not jealous of it.
The late-night glow on your face is often the laptop, not their texts.
You plan dates around deadlines, and when you do show up, you’re all there.
strengths: You go after what you want, and that drive is magnetic.
weaknesses: “After this launch” can turn into five years of launches.
realLife: On a first date: You arrive straight from a meeting, on time, and talk about your work with stars in your eyes.
In a fight: If it’s about time, don’t defend the job. Offer one fixed evening a week, and keep it.
tips: Block one evening a week that work can never touch. It keeps the people you love in the story.
match: Best with: Someone just as ambitious who’s happy with fewer, better evenings.
Green flag: They cheer your wins and have big plans of their own.
Careful with: Someone who counts every late night as proof you don’t care.

Undecided.label: The Calendar Juggler
summaries: Career and home, both in the calendar.

You want both, a career you’re proud of and a home life you love, and you work hard to have them. Some weeks lean one way, some the other. You make it work with plans, phone alarms and a colour-coded calendar.
behaviors: You’ll leave work early for a special dinner, and log back in after.
You want someone who shares the juggling, not just watches it.
Your weekends are sacred. Mostly.
strengths: You keep a lot of plates spinning and rarely drop the important ones.
weaknesses: Giving everything to both can leave nothing for you.
realLife: On a first date: It’s in your calendar with two alarms, and you’re genuinely excited.
In a fight: You pull out the calendar to find a fair split. Ask how they feel first.
tips: Choose together the few things that never move: a birthday, a Sunday lunch. Everything else can flex.
match: Best with: Someone organised who is juggling career and home too.
Green flag: They share the planning, the chores and the calendar.
Careful with: Someone who leaves all the juggling to you.

tests.title: Traditions & Holidays
tests.subtitle: How much rituals matter
tests.description: Measures how much you value celebrating holidays, traditions, rituals, and creating family memories.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your emotional value for rituals and celebration.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Compatibility improves when both value similar tradition intensity.

questions.text: Your family’s big festival morning. You…

options.text: Show up for the meal and the photos
Wake early: new clothes, prayers, the full routine
Sleep in. It’s a holiday after all
Call the family, eat well, keep it simple

questions.text: Nani has a festival recipe that only she knows. You…

options.text: Film her making it, just in case
Order from the best sweet shop when it’s time
Already learning it, notebook and all

questions.text: The person you’re seeing doesn’t celebrate your festivals. You’d want them to…

options.text: Do whatever feels right. It doesn’t matter
Join in fully, rituals and all
Come for the food and the fun, no pressure

questions.text: Your birthday, ideally:

options.text: Dinner with my people, nothing fixed
Cake at midnight, a family call, the same café every year
Just another day. No fuss

questions.text: A couple ritual, like the same restaurant every anniversary, sounds…

options.text: Boring. Surprise me every time
Romantic. Same place, every year

questions.text: Your own wedding, in an ideal world:

options.text: Court marriage, then a great dinner
Every ritual, every function, all the relatives
A small ceremony, only the rituals that mean something
The key rituals, then a big party

questions.text: Your family wants a small prayer before you move into your new flat. You…

options.text: Skip it politely. Not my thing
Go along with it, for them
Plan it with them. It feels right

questions.text: Every year your family gathers in the hometown for the same festival. This year you…

options.text: Booked my tickets in July
Go if work allows
Skip it and video-call

tests.measures: how much value you place on traditions, holidays, and family rituals

VeryHigh.label: The Torchbearer
summaries: You carry the family’s traditions forward.

Traditions aren’t a hobby for you, they’re roots. You know the recipes, the prayers, the dates and the stories behind them, and you want them alive in your own home one day. A festival done properly, with everyone there, makes you feel deeply connected.
behaviors: You want someone who’ll keep the traditions with you, not just watch.
Your year is planned around festivals, family dates and rituals.
A wedding with no rituals would feel like something was missing.
strengths: You keep a family’s memory alive. That’s a quiet kind of greatness.
weaknesses: Your traditions can feel like rules to someone from a different home.
realLife: On a first date: You talk about your family’s festival plans with so much joy that they want an invite.
In a fight: You hold firm on rituals. Decide which ones you’d share and which you could bend.
tips: Invite them in, and let them bring a tradition of their own. The best families keep adding rituals.
match: Best with: Someone who shares your traditions, or loves learning them with you.
Green flag: They ask about your rituals and want to learn the recipes too.
Careful with: Someone who calls your traditions “old-fashioned” and means it.

High.label: The Occasion Maker
summaries: Festivals are the highlights of your year.

You love the rituals, the lights, the special food and the whole family under one roof. Festivals and birthdays are where your best memories live, and you put real effort into making them special. If you’re doing it, you’re doing it properly.
behaviors: You remember every anniversary and plan something every time.
You’d love them at your family festivals, dressed for the occasion.
Couple traditions make you feel close, the more the better.
strengths: You turn days into memories people keep for years.
weaknesses: When someone shrugs at a festival, you can take it personally.
realLife: On a first date: If a festival is near, you’re already wondering whether to invite them.
In a fight: If they skip a family function, you’re hurt. Tell them why it mattered.
tips: Leave room for their traditions too. Two families’ festivals are twice the fun.
match: Best with: Someone who loves celebrations and family gatherings as much as you.
Green flag: They remember your festival dates and ask how to join in.
Careful with: Someone who calls traditions “a waste of time”.

Moderate.label: The Keeper of a Few
summaries: You keep the traditions that mean something.

You don’t do every ritual, but the ones you keep, you keep with your whole heart. Maybe it’s the first lamp of Diwali, midnight mass at Christmas or a grandparent’s Eid biryani. You pick what matters and let the rest go without guilt.
behaviors: You’d love to start a couple tradition, as long as it feels real.
You join their family festivals and bring a bit of your own.
You care about the meaning more than getting every step right.
strengths: You keep traditions alive by keeping them meaningful.
weaknesses: What you choose to skip may be what their family holds most dear.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their family traditions and share your one favourite.
In a fight: You offer to keep one tradition their way and one yours. Fair trade.
tips: Start one ritual that’s only yours as a couple. It becomes the tradition your future family remembers.
match: Best with: Someone who treasures a few traditions and is curious about yours.
Green flag: They want to make a few traditions of your own, together.
Careful with: Someone who mocks the rituals that matter to you.

Low.label: The Festival Foodie
summaries: In it for the sweets and the people.

You love a festival for the food, the noise and seeing everyone, and you’re less fussed about the steps. You come home for the big ones when you can, eat the sweets and leave the rituals to the experts in the family. Traditions are nice; they’re not your compass.
behaviors: You’ll gladly join their family festival, mostly for the food.
You keep couple traditions loosely, like takeaway and a film on birthdays.
Missing a festival one year doesn’t feel like a big deal to you.
strengths: You bring fun and ease to every family festival, minus the stress.
weaknesses: Treating a ritual as optional can look careless to someone who holds it dear.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their favourite festival food and plan the next date around it.
In a fight: If they want more effort at a festival, give it this once. Then ask why it matters.
tips: Ask an elder to teach you one ritual. You may find you like it more than the sweets.
match: Best with: Someone who enjoys festivals but doesn’t need them done perfectly.
Green flag: They welcome you in without making you feel you did it wrong.
Careful with: Someone who turns every festival into a test you have to pass.

VeryLow.label: The Any-Day Celebrator
summaries: Why wait for a date on the calendar?

Rituals don’t move you much, and you don’t pretend they do. You’d rather celebrate a random Tuesday with someone you love than go through the motions on a big day. You respect other people’s traditions; you just don’t need them to feel close.
behaviors: Your idea of an anniversary is a surprise trip, never the same place twice.
You’ll join their festival for the people, and skip the parts you don’t feel.
Couple rituals sound sweet to you, for about a year.
strengths: You make ordinary days feel special, no occasion needed.
weaknesses: Skipping their family rituals can hurt more than you realise.
realLife: On a first date: You pick a random weekday and somehow make it feel like an occasion.
In a fight: If they’re hurt that you skipped a family festival, listen. It wasn’t about the festival.
tips: Find one tradition that matters to them and go all in on it. It means more than you think.
match: Best with: Someone easygoing about festivals who loves a spontaneous plan.
Green flag: They don’t need a big day to show they care.
Careful with: Someone who measures love by how much of every ritual you do.

Undecided.label: The Keeper of a Few
summaries: You keep the traditions that mean something.

You don’t do every ritual, but the ones you keep, you keep with your whole heart. Maybe it’s the first lamp of Diwali, midnight mass at Christmas or a grandparent’s Eid biryani. You pick what matters and let the rest go without guilt.
behaviors: You’d love to start a couple tradition, as long as it feels real.
You join their family festivals and bring a bit of your own.
You care about the meaning more than getting every step right.
strengths: You keep traditions alive by keeping them meaningful.
weaknesses: What you choose to skip may be what their family holds most dear.
realLife: On a first date: You ask about their family traditions and share your one favourite.
In a fight: You offer to keep one tradition their way and one yours. Fair trade.
tips: Start one ritual that’s only yours as a couple. It becomes the tradition your future family remembers.
match: Best with: Someone who treasures a few traditions and is curious about yours.
Green flag: They want to make a few traditions of your own, together.
Careful with: Someone who mocks the rituals that matter to you.

tests.title: Financial Planning
tests.subtitle: Budgeting, stability, planning
tests.description: Measures how much you value planning, saving, and building financial security for a future family.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your stability planning mindset.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps match partners with similar financial responsibility levels.

questions.text: Salary day. The first thing you do:

options.text: Treat myself. I earned it
Move money to savings before anything else
Pay the bills, see what’s left
Clear the credit card, then vibes

questions.text: Do you know roughly what you spent last month?

options.text: Roughly, give or take a few thousand
No, and I’d rather not look
To the rupee. There’s a spreadsheet

questions.text: A surprise bonus lands in your account. You…

options.text: Plan a trip. This weekend
Save half, spend half on something nice
Put it straight into savings or investments

questions.text: A dream wedding, or a down payment on a flat?

options.text: The flat. Small wedding, big future
The wedding. You only do it once

questions.text: When would you talk money with someone you’re serious about?

options.text: When something comes up
Never, ideally. It kills the romance
Early: salaries, loans, goals, all of it
Once we’re thinking of moving in

questions.text: Your phone dies. You need a new one tomorrow. You…

options.text: No-cost EMI, obviously
Pay from the emergency fund. That’s what it’s for
Use savings and skip eating out for a month

questions.text: A colleague starts talking about retirement plans at 25. You…

options.text: Make a mental note to look into it
Take notes. Started mine last year
Laugh. I’m still planning Friday

questions.text: Sharing a home with someone. Money would work like…

options.text: A shared budget and a joint account for the house
Whoever has it pays. It evens out
Split rent and bills, the rest is ours

tests.measures: how much you value financial planning and budgeting for family stability

VeryHigh.label: The Spreadsheet Soul
summaries: There’s a sheet for that. And a backup sheet.

You know where every rupee goes and where it’s going next year. Emergency fund, investments, a plan for the house, maybe even a retirement plan at 25. Planning isn’t stress for you, it’s peace: when the money is sorted, your heart can relax.
behaviors: You’d want to talk salaries, loans and goals before you get serious.
A shared budget feels weirdly romantic to you.
You notice how someone handles money by the second date.
strengths: With you, the future is planned and the bad days are covered.
weaknesses: Too much planning can make a spontaneous person feel watched.
realLife: On a first date: You enjoy every minute, and you already know what it cost.
In a fight: You bring numbers to a feelings fight. Lead with the feeling, then show the sheet.
tips: Build a fun fund that needs no reason. A planner who can splurge is a planner people love living with.
match: Best with: Another planner, or a free spirit who trusts you with the sheets.
Green flag: They ask about your money goals and share their own.
Careful with: Someone who calls every money talk “too much” and changes the subject.

High.label: The Quiet Saver
summaries: Your future self is already grateful.

You plan, you save and you think ahead, but you’re not tight about it. You like knowing there’s a cushion for bad days and a plan for the big ones: a home, a family, a dream trip. Money, for you, is how you make life feel safe.
behaviors: You bring up money once it’s serious, because it matters to you.
You’d choose the flat over the fancy wedding, probably.
You like someone who saves too, and you notice when they don’t.
strengths: People feel secure with you. The future feels handled.
weaknesses: You can worry about tomorrow so much that you forget to enjoy today.
realLife: On a first date: You have a lovely evening, and glance at the bill before you split it.
In a fight: Money worry makes you sharp. Say the fear, not just the number.
tips: Plan a guilt-free spend into every month. Joy is part of the plan too.
match: Best with: Someone steady with money who shares your bigger goals.
Green flag: They know their own numbers and talk about them openly.
Careful with: Someone with big spending and vague answers.

Moderate.label: The Sensible Splurger
summaries: Save first, then enjoy it properly.
You save, you spend, and you know which is which. You put money aside every month and then enjoy a good holiday without guilt. Your planning is real, but it doesn’t run your life.
behaviors: You like to talk money once it’s getting serious, not on date one.
You’d save up for a trip together and enjoy every rupee of it.
You split fairly, and you’re generous when it counts.
strengths: You balance security and joy, which is harder than it looks.
weaknesses: You might skip the deeper money talks because things seem fine.
realLife: On a first date: You pick a nice place within budget and enjoy every bite.
In a fight: You look for the middle: a bit more saving, a bit less guilt.
tips: Pick one shared money goal with them, like a trip. It makes money talk feel like planning for joy.
match: Best with: Someone who saves too, and also knows how to have fun.
Green flag: They’re open about money and generous without being reckless.
Careful with: Someone who hides spending or debts.

Low.label: The Ballpark Budgeter
summaries: Roughly fine, mostly.

You keep a loose eye on money: you know roughly what comes in, roughly what goes out, and the bills get paid on time. Detailed plans bore you a little, and you’d rather enjoy today than calculate the next decade. You’re careful when it counts and relaxed the rest of the time.
behaviors: You split the bill without a calculator, and don’t mind if it’s uneven.
Big money plans feel like a later conversation to you.
You’d rather spend on an experience together than save for something far off.
strengths: Money doesn’t stress you out, so it rarely stresses your relationship.
weaknesses: “Roughly” can hide a slow leak until a big expense shows up.
realLife: On a first date: You go wherever they suggest and don’t check the menu prices first.
In a fight: If they want a budget, don’t brush it off. Ask what would make them feel safe.
tips: Look at your spending once a month, with chai. Ten minutes, no guilt. It’s enough.
match: Best with: Someone organised who doesn’t lecture you about it.
Green flag: They make planning feel like a fun goal, not a budget meeting.
Careful with: Someone even more casual with money than you, with a bigger credit card.

VeryLow.label: The Big-Hearted Spender
summaries: Money is for living, and you live well.

You see money as something to enjoy: good food, last-minute trips, treating the people you love. Spreadsheets and five-year plans feel like a weight you don’t need yet. You’re generous, spontaneous and, somehow, it usually works out.
behaviors: You book the surprise dinner without checking the bill first.
You’re the first to pay for everyone, and the last to check your balance.
Money talk on a date feels like homework to you.
strengths: You make life feel abundant, whatever’s in the account.
weaknesses: One big surprise expense can hit hard when there’s no cushion.
realLife: On a first date: You insist on paying, then suggest dessert somewhere else too.
In a fight: If money comes up, you may go quiet. Listen for the worry under their words.
tips: Set up one automatic saving for the day your salary lands, even a small one. Then spend the rest with zero guilt.
match: Best with: Someone who loves your generosity and quietly keeps a small safety net.
Green flag: They talk about money without making you feel judged.
Careful with: Someone who keeps a running tab of who paid for what.

Undecided.label: The Sensible Splurger
summaries: Save first, then enjoy it properly.
You save, you spend, and you know which is which. You put money aside every month and then enjoy a good holiday without guilt. Your planning is real, but it doesn’t run your life.
behaviors: You like to talk money once it’s getting serious, not on date one.
You’d save up for a trip together and enjoy every rupee of it.
You split fairly, and you’re generous when it counts.
strengths: You balance security and joy, which is harder than it looks.
weaknesses: You might skip the deeper money talks because things seem fine.
realLife: On a first date: You pick a nice place within budget and enjoy every bite.
In a fight: You look for the middle: a bit more saving, a bit less guilt.
tips: Pick one shared money goal with them, like a trip. It makes money talk feel like planning for joy.
match: Best with: Someone who saves too, and also knows how to have fun.
Green flag: They’re open about money and generous without being reckless.
Careful with: Someone who hides spending or debts.

tests.title: Stability Need
tests.subtitle: Consistency, predictability, calm
tests.description: Measures how much you need predictability, stable routines, and low chaos for home life.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your need for predictability vs flexibility.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Mismatch causes stress: one wants stable, other wants constant change.

questions.text: Saturday noon. They cancel your plan and suggest a surprise road trip instead. You…

options.text: Already packing. Best text all week
Go, after a minute of re-planning in your head
Feel thrown. I’d planned my day around it

questions.text: Your order at your favourite restaurant:

options.text: The same thing for five years. Why risk it
Never the same twice
The usual, unless something looks amazing

questions.text: A steady job with yearly hikes, or a startup that could go either way?

options.text: Startup. I want the ride
Steady job. Peace of mind is pay too

questions.text: You’ve lived in the same flat for four years. That feels…

options.text: Good, though I browse flat listings for fun
Perfect. It’s home now
Way too long. Time for a new place
Comfortable, maybe a bit too comfortable

questions.text: In a relationship, what makes you feel safest?

options.text: A few rituals and lots of room
Still being surprised by them
Knowing exactly what our week looks like
Them being the same person every day

questions.text: New city, new job and a new relationship, all in one year. Sounds…

options.text: Hard, but I’d manage
A lot. One at a time, please
Like my dream year

questions.text: How often do you rearrange your room?

options.text: Never. Everything has its place
Once a year, maybe
Every few weeks. I get bored

questions.text: A home where something is always happening: guests, noise, plans changing. You’d…

options.text: Love it. Quiet homes feel empty
Enjoy it on weekends, not every day
Mostly enjoy it, with headphones handy
Need a quiet corner, fast

tests.measures: how much you need consistency, predictability, and calm in your home life

VeryHigh.label: The Deep Roots
summaries: Steady as a rock, and proud of it.

You need life to be calm, predictable and steady, and you’re very good at making it so. You like the same order, the same chair, the same people, because that’s where you feel safe. Big changes all at once feel like a storm, and you’d rather sail around it.
behaviors: You want to know where they’ll be, when, and that they’ll be there.
Last-minute changes can unsettle your whole day.
You build a home where everyone knows they can count on you.
strengths: People trust you completely. You’re the same person every single day.
weaknesses: Holding on too tight to routine can make life feel smaller than it is.
realLife: On a first date: You arrive early at the place you picked weeks ago, and order your usual.
In a fight: Sudden fights shake you. Ask to talk at a set time, and stick to it.
tips: Try one new thing a month, on your terms. Small changes you choose make the big ones less scary.
match: Best with: Someone calm and consistent who loves a quiet, steady life.
Green flag: They keep their word, and give you a heads-up when plans change.
Careful with: Someone whose plans, moods and promises change every week.

High.label: The Slow-and-Steady
summaries: You like knowing what tomorrow looks like.

You do best when life is calm and you know what’s coming. Plans, routines and people who keep their word make you feel safe. You can handle change, but you’d rather it came with a heads-up and some time to adjust.
behaviors: You love someone whose texts, plans and moods are steady.
A sudden change of plan takes you a minute to accept.
You show love by being consistent, day after day.
strengths: You’re the calm in other people’s storms.
weaknesses: Too much caution can make you miss a lovely surprise.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest a place you know and love, so all your attention can go to them.
In a fight: You want calm before talking. Say “give me an hour”, then come back.
tips: Say yes to one small surprise a month. Your calm will still be there when you get back.
match: Best with: Someone reliable who loves a peaceful home.
Green flag: They do what they say, when they say.
Careful with: Someone who cancels at the last minute, again and again.

Moderate.label: The Weekend Adventurer
summaries: Roots that bend, and a heart that likes both.
You like a calm, predictable base with the odd surprise on top. Your week has a shape, but you’ll gladly break it for something good. You handle change well, as long as it doesn’t all arrive at once.
behaviors: You like a few fixed rituals and room for spontaneous plans.
You can roll with a cancelled plan after a minute of re-planning.
You’re happiest in a steady relationship that still surprises you.
strengths: You can be someone’s calm and their adventure, both.
weaknesses: You might not say which one you need more on a given day.
realLife: On a first date: You plan the dinner and leave the after-dinner to chance.
In a fight: You stay steady, and you’re open to trying a fresh approach.
tips: Tell them which kind of day you need: steady or new. It’s a small question with a big pay-off.
match: Best with: Someone who likes a steady life with the occasional plot twist.
Green flag: They’re reliable, and still know how to surprise you.
Careful with: Someone who keeps life in chaos and calls it fun.

Low.label: The Restless Explorer
summaries: A home base, and a bag always half-packed.
You like having a base, but you get restless when every week looks the same. New places, new plans and small changes keep you happy. You can settle, as long as settling doesn’t mean standing still.
behaviors: You like routine in small doses: Sunday breakfast, yes; every evening planned, no.
You’re the one who says “let’s try the new place” instead of the usual.
A slow, predictable month makes you itch for a weekend trip.
strengths: You bring freshness to a relationship without shaking its base.
weaknesses: You may push for change when they just need things to stay put.
realLife: On a first date: You pick a place neither of you has tried. That’s half the fun.
In a fight: You want to fix it with a change of scene. Sometimes they need to stay and talk.
tips: Ask what they need to stay the same, then keep that steady. Everything else you can shake up together.
match: Best with: Someone steady who enjoys the occasional adventure.
Green flag: They’re up for new things, and give you a calm home to come back to.
Careful with: Someone who sees every change as a threat.

VeryLow.label: The Plot-Twist Lover
summaries: Same old? Not on your watch.
You come alive when things change: new cities, new plans, a new dish on the menu. Routine makes you restless and a surprise makes your week. You can build a life anywhere, as long as it keeps moving.
behaviors: You love someone who texts “pack a bag” on a Friday.
A fixed weekly date night can feel like a timetable to you.
You keep a relationship fresh, sometimes a little too fresh for a calm person.
strengths: You handle change with a smile while others panic.
weaknesses: Your love of change can feel unsettling to someone who needs calm.
realLife: On a first date: You change the plan halfway through, and somehow it’s better.
In a fight: You want to move on fast. Give them time to settle before the next twist.
tips: Give them one thing that never changes, like a nightly call. It lets them enjoy all your surprises.
match: Best with: Someone adventurous who enjoys a plot twist as much as you.
Green flag: They say yes to last-minute plans and bring surprises of their own.
Careful with: Someone who wants every weekend planned a month ahead.

Undecided.label: The Weekend Adventurer
summaries: Roots that bend, and a heart that likes both.
You like a calm, predictable base with the odd surprise on top. Your week has a shape, but you’ll gladly break it for something good. You handle change well, as long as it doesn’t all arrive at once.
behaviors: You like a few fixed rituals and room for spontaneous plans.
You can roll with a cancelled plan after a minute of re-planning.
You’re happiest in a steady relationship that still surprises you.
strengths: You can be someone’s calm and their adventure, both.
weaknesses: You might not say which one you need more on a given day.
realLife: On a first date: You plan the dinner and leave the after-dinner to chance.
In a fight: You stay steady, and you’re open to trying a fresh approach.
tips: Tell them which kind of day you need: steady or new. It’s a small question with a big pay-off.
match: Best with: Someone who likes a steady life with the occasional plot twist.
Green flag: They’re reliable, and still know how to surprise you.
Careful with: Someone who keeps life in chaos and calls it fun.

tests.subtitle: Moving for family/opportunity
tests.description: Measures how flexible you are about relocating for partner, career, or family goals.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your willingness to move and adapt.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps match couples on future geography and lifestyle flexibility.

questions.text: Your dream job offer arrives, 2,000 km from home. You…

options.text: Visit the city first, then decide
Ask if it can be remote. I’m staying
Take it, with a plan to come back in two years
Pack this weekend

options.text: Ask them to find something here
Move, if your work can come along
Start reading about visas that night
Try long distance first, then decide

questions.text: The place you grew up is…

options.text: Home. Always will be
Where I’m from. Home is wherever I live

questions.text: After marriage, living in the same city as your parents feels…

options.text: Non-negotiable. Same city
Nice, not necessary
Important. A short trip away at most

questions.text: Moving somewhere you don’t speak the language. You think…

options.text: “Scary, but doable”
“Not for me. I need to feel at home”
“Exciting. I’ll learn”

questions.text: Leaving your friends behind for a move would feel…

options.text: Like leaving a piece of me
Hard. I’d need a strong reason
Sad, but they’re a call away

questions.text: They want to move back to their small hometown to be near family. You say…

options.text: “Let’s try it. A new kind of life”
“Maybe, for a few years”
“I’d miss my city too much”

questions.text: A new city every few years. That life sounds…

options.text: Like an adventure I’d sign up for
Exhausting. I like my lanes and my people
Fun for a while, then I’d want roots

tests.measures: how willing you are to relocate for family, career, or opportunity

VeryHigh.label: The Suitcase Soul
summaries: Home is a person, not a pin code.

You could live anywhere, and you probably will. New cities, new languages and new starts feel like the best part of life to you. Home isn’t a place on a map: it’s the people you choose and the life you build, wherever that is.
behaviors: You’d follow the right person across the world, happily.
Living far from your parents feels natural to you, not sad.
Long distance is a puzzle you’re happy to solve.
strengths: You can build a life anywhere, and bring joy to every new place.
weaknesses: Moving often can make it hard for people to believe you’ll stay.
realLife: On a first date: You name three countries you’d love to live in. They add a fourth. Perfect.
In a fight: If they’re scared of moving, slow down. Show them how home can come along.
tips: Ask early: “Could you see yourself living somewhere else?” It saves a lot of maybes.
match: Best with: A fellow wanderer, or someone whose work can travel.
Green flag: They get excited when you talk about where you could live next.
Careful with: Someone who will never leave their city, whatever happens.

High.label: The Open Map
summaries: New city? Let’s look at the map together.

You’re ready to move for the right job, the right person or the right life. New cities excite you more than they scare you, and you settle in faster than most. You love your roots, and you know you can carry them with you.
behaviors: You’d move for them if the plan made sense for both of you.
Long distance doesn’t scare you, as long as it ends somewhere.
You see a move as an adventure you take together.
strengths: You adapt fast, and you make any city feel like home.
weaknesses: You may say yes to a move before asking what you’ll miss.
realLife: On a first date: You swap stories about cities you’ve lived in and cities you’d like to.
In a fight: You push for the move. Remember their roots may run deeper than yours.
tips: Before any big move, list three things you’ll miss. Then bring them along: a ritual, a recipe, a call.
match: Best with: Someone curious who’s also open to new places.
Green flag: They talk about cities they’d like to try, with you in the plan.
Careful with: Someone who expects you to move every time, and never moves for you.

Moderate.label: The Right-Reason Mover
summaries: Show you a good reason, and you’ll pack.

You’re open to moving, for love, work or family, but only when it really makes sense. You’d visit first, weigh it up and want a plan. Home matters to you, and so do the chances that live somewhere else.
behaviors: You’d move for them, after a few honest talks about why.
Ideally, you’d want both your families within reach.
You’re happy to talk about where to live, as long as it’s a real conversation.
strengths: You make thoughtful moves, so you rarely regret them.
weaknesses: Weighing every option can stall a decision that needs making.
realLife: On a first date: You ask where they see themselves living, and share your own short list.
In a fight: If a move divides you, you make a pros and cons list. Add how each of you feels to it.
tips: Decide your must-haves now: near family, good work, a city you like. It makes the big call easier later.
match: Best with: Someone flexible who still plans before they leap.
Green flag: They ask where you want to live, instead of telling you.
Careful with: Someone who picks a city without you.

Low.label: The Homing Pigeon
summaries: You can fly far, but you always come back.

You’d move for a few years for something special, but home stays home. You love trips and new experiences, and you also want to live near your people in the long run. Your heart has a pin code, and it’s an old one.
behaviors: You’d try a new city with them, with a plan to come back.
Being a few hours from family matters to you more than you say.
You’d take a slightly smaller job in your city over a big one far away.
strengths: You’re open to adventure without losing your roots.
weaknesses: “A few years” can turn into a very long time. Be honest with yourself.
realLife: On a first date: You swap travel stories, and talk about the one place you’ll always go back to.
In a fight: When moving comes up, say what you need: a return plan. It makes yes easier for both.
tips: Tell them your hometown is your compass. The right person will plan the adventures around it.
match: Best with: Someone who loves trips but also wants to settle near family.
Green flag: They respect your roots and visit your family with you.
Careful with: Someone who wants to settle far away forever, no return.

VeryLow.label: The Banyan Tree
summaries: Deep roots, wide shade, not going anywhere.

Your city, your people and your family are part of who you are, and you’re not looking to leave them. You know every lane, every food stall, every aunty on the street. You’d rather grow deeper where you are than start over somewhere new.
behaviors: You hope to find love close to home, and build a life right there.
A long-distance or move-abroad plan would be a big ask for you.
You make your city feel like home to anyone you love.
strengths: You give people a steady place to belong.
weaknesses: Saying no to every move can close doors your person dreams about.
realLife: On a first date: You take them to your favourite old spot, where the owner knows your order.
In a fight: If a move comes up, you dig in. Hear their dream out before you say no.
tips: Be clear early that you’re staying. Someone who wants roots with you will find you faster.
match: Best with: Someone who loves your city and wants to stay too.
Green flag: They’re rooted in the same place, or happy to plant themselves there.
Careful with: Someone already planning their move abroad on date two.

Undecided.label: The Right-Reason Mover
summaries: Show you a good reason, and you’ll pack.

You’re open to moving, for love, work or family, but only when it really makes sense. You’d visit first, weigh it up and want a plan. Home matters to you, and so do the chances that live somewhere else.
behaviors: You’d move for them, after a few honest talks about why.
Ideally, you’d want both your families within reach.
You’re happy to talk about where to live, as long as it’s a real conversation.
strengths: You make thoughtful moves, so you rarely regret them.
weaknesses: Weighing every option can stall a decision that needs making.
realLife: On a first date: You ask where they see themselves living, and share your own short list.
In a fight: If a move divides you, you make a pros and cons list. Add how each of you feels to it.
tips: Decide your must-haves now: near family, good work, a city you like. It makes the big call easier later.
match: Best with: Someone flexible who still plans before they leap.
Green flag: They ask where you want to live, instead of telling you.
Careful with: Someone who picks a city without you.

tests.subtitle: How you approach long-term bonds
tests.description: Shows how you commit: cautious, balanced, or fast and strong.
tests.whatYouLearn: Whether you commit slowly, steadily, or fast and intense.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps align expectations about exclusivity, pace, and stability.

options.text: A strong feeling in the first few dates
Months of them showing up the same way

questions.text: Two months in, they ask, “So, what are we?” You…

options.text: Say you like where it’s going, no label yet
Say it: “I’m in. Let’s make it official”
Change the subject. Labels make you itchy

questions.text: You promised to help them shift flats on Saturday. Your college gang plans a Goa trip that weekend. You…

options.text: Ask if the shifting can move a week
Help them shift. A promise is a promise
Go to Goa and send pizza to the new flat
Help on Saturday, join the gang a day late

questions.text: A year in, a quiet doubt shows up: “Is this it?” You…

options.text: Talk it through with them
Take it as a sign. Feelings don’t lie
Remember why you chose them and let it pass
Start wondering what else is out there

Stick with the same ones for years

questions.text: Your friends would describe you in a relationship as…

options.text: Loyal, once I’ve made up my mind
All in at first, then slowly drifting
Hard to pin down
The same in month ten as in week one

tests.measures: how steady and reliable your commitment is over time

VeryHigh.label: The Evergreen
summaries: Deep roots, wide shade, here for the long haul.

You’re the steady one: once you choose someone, you keep choosing them through busy months and boring Tuesdays. Consistency isn’t a chore for you; it’s how love grows. People feel safe around you because you are exactly who you were yesterday.
behaviors: A passing doubt doesn’t shake you. You know feelings move and commitment stays.
You book the birthday trip four months ahead without a second thought.
Your loyalty shows in small, repeated things, like the call after their big meeting, every time.
strengths: People can build their lives around your word.
weaknesses: You can stay loyal to something long after it stopped being good for you.
realLife: On a first date: On time, phone away, and already curious about who they’ll be in five years.
In a fight: You stay calm and stay put. A fight is a problem to fix, never a reason to go.
tips: Loyalty is your gift. Give it to someone who gives it back, and check now and then that you’re still happy, not just still there.
match: Best with: Someone equally steady who values showing up over showing off.
Green flag: They keep small promises without being reminded.
Careful with: Someone who loves your steadiness but never offers any of their own.

High.label: The Slow Yes
summaries: Takes time to say yes, then means it for years.

You don’t hand out commitment like free samples. You watch how someone behaves over weeks and months, and once you’re sure, you’re loyal and consistent. People who earn your yes rarely have to wonder about it again.
behaviors: You believe what you see on ordinary days more than anything said on a good one.
Once you’re exclusive, you act exclusive: the swiping stops, the backup chats go.
You keep plans, remember promises and turn up the same in month ten as in week one.
strengths: Reliability. Your yes doesn’t expire.
weaknesses: Your slow start can look like low interest to someone who moves faster.
realLife: On a first date: Warm, attentive, a little careful. You’re enjoying it and still taking notes.
In a fight: You stay and work it through. Leaving over one fight isn’t how you’re built.
tips: Tell them you’re slow but sure. “I take my time, and then I stay” saves a lot of guessing.
match: Best with: Someone consistent and patient who’s happy to build trust step by step.
Green flag: Their actions and their words tell the same story, week after week.
Careful with: Big declarations in week two with nothing to back them up.

Moderate.label: The Honest Maybe
summaries: Committed for real, and honest about the wobbles.

Your yes is real, but you don’t pretend it’s carved in stone. Most weeks you’re fully in; now and then a quiet “what if” knocks, and you notice it rather than hide it. That honesty makes you easy to trust, as long as you keep talking.
behaviors: You keep your word on the big things and sometimes wobble on the small plans.
You need the relationship to keep feeling good, not just to look good on paper.
When a doubt shows up, you think it through before you act on it.
strengths: You never fake certainty, so your commitments are real when you make them.
weaknesses: Your occasional “what if” can feel like a giant question mark to someone more certain.
realLife: On a first date: Relaxed and curious. You’re seeing if it feels right, and you’re upfront about that.
In a fight: You might step back to think. Say how long you need, so it doesn’t feel like goodbye.
tips: When a doubt comes, give it a week and a conversation before you give it a decision.
match: Best with: Someone patient and secure who doesn’t take your thinking out loud as a threat.
Green flag: They make it easy to bring up a doubt without it turning into a crisis.
Careful with: Someone who wants forever promises in month two.

Low.label: The Spark Chaser
summaries: All in at the start, testing it once it settles.

You love the rush of something new and you dive in with your whole heart. Then the calm arrives, and a small voice asks if the fire is going out. You’re not fickle; you just haven’t yet learned to trust the quieter kind of love.
behaviors: You can go from first coffee to “we should do Goa together” in two weeks.
Month four is your tricky month, when the butterflies settle and the doubts arrive.
Big gestures come easily to you; the boring, steady ones take more effort.
strengths: You make people feel chosen, fully and fast.
weaknesses: You can mistake calm for the end, when it’s really the start of something deeper.
realLife: On a first date: You’re funny, open and already a little smitten by the time the bill comes.
In a fight: You feel it all at once and might say “maybe this isn’t working”. Sleep on it first.
tips: When the spark dips, don’t look elsewhere. Plan something new together. Fresh experiences relight old fires.
match: Best with: Someone warm and playful who keeps a little adventure going long after the start.
Green flag: They plan small surprises in month eight, not just in month one.
Careful with: Someone who goes hot and cold. It feeds your rush and starves your trust.

VeryLow.label: The Open Road
summaries: Loves big, hates cages, still learning to land.

You fall fast and feel everything, and the moment something feels fixed, a part of you starts looking for the window. It isn’t that you can’t love; freedom has simply felt safer than promises so far. Landing is a skill, and you’re allowed to learn it slowly.
behaviors: The beginning is your favourite part: the first texts, the 2 am calls, the not-knowing.
When things start to feel routine, you catch yourself wondering what else is out there.
Plans months ahead make you itchy. Next weekend is about as far as you like to see.
strengths: You bring real spark to a start, and you never fake feelings you don’t have.
weaknesses: You can leave right at the point where it was about to get deep.
realLife: On a first date: Great stories, great energy, and you’re already planning a trip, maybe with them.
In a fight: Your first thought is the exit. Your better move is to stay in the room ten more minutes.
tips: Next time you want to leave, wait one week before you decide. Restless feelings pass. Good people are rarer.
match: Best with: Someone secure and unhurried, who gives you room and doesn’t panic when you need air.
Green flag: They stay calm when you go quiet, and they’re still warm when you come back.
Careful with: Someone as restless as you. Two open windows make a very draughty house.

Undecided.label: The Honest Maybe
summaries: Committed for real, and honest about the wobbles.

Your yes is real, but you don’t pretend it’s carved in stone. Most weeks you’re fully in; now and then a quiet “what if” knocks, and you notice it rather than hide it. That honesty makes you easy to trust, as long as you keep talking.

You need the relationship to keep feeling good, not just to look good on paper.
When a doubt shows up, you think it through before you act on it.

realLife: On a first date: Relaxed and curious. You’re seeing if it feels right, and you’re upfront about that.
In a fight: You might step back to think. Say how long you need, so it doesn’t feel like goodbye.
tips: When a doubt comes, give it a week and a conversation before you give it a decision.
match: Best with: Someone patient and secure who doesn’t take your thinking out loud as a threat.
Green flag: They make it easy to bring up a doubt without it turning into a crisis.
Careful with: Someone who wants forever promises in month two.

tests.whatYouLearn: Your marriage attitude and seriousness level.

options.text: “Eventually, with the right person”
“Not sure yet. Let’s see where this goes”
“Yes, that’s why I’m here”
“Honestly, no. But I want something real”

questions.text: Your cousin’s wedding: five days, three outfits, one very loud sangeet. Watching the couple, you think…

options.text: Lovely for them. I’ll see about me
Is the food counter open yet?
That’ll be me one day, and I can’t wait
Sweet, but a ceremony isn’t what makes love real

options.text: Okay, but when’s the wedding?
Depends on what they both want

Losing a little freedom

Change the topic. I don’t know what I want yet
Say I’ll find my own person, but yes, someday
Tell them gently that marriage may not be for me

tests.measures: how you view marriage as a life goal

VeryHigh.label: The Forever Vow
summaries: Marriage isn’t a box to tick. It’s the whole plan.

For you, marriage is the heart of a good life: two people, two families, one promise kept for decades. Arranged or love, you care less about how you meet and more about whether they’re ready for forever. You’d rather be clear early than waste anyone’s time, including your own.
behaviors: You say “I’m looking for marriage” in week one, and you’re proud of it.
Meeting someone through family doesn’t scare you. Good marriages start in many ways.
A wedding, to you, is the start of the real love story, not the end of one.
strengths: Total clarity. Nobody wonders what you’re looking for.
weaknesses: Your eye on forever can rush the getting-to-know-you part.
realLife: On a first date: You’re warm and fun, and by dessert you’ve gently asked how they feel about marriage.
In a fight: You fight like someone who plans to stay married: firm, fair, never with exit talk.
tips: Your clarity is a gift. Let the person unfold for a few months before you start the guest list.
match: Best with: Someone who wants marriage as much as you do and is ready to build it.
Green flag: They talk about marriage with warmth, not fear.
Careful with: Someone who calls marriage “just paper” and hopes you’ll change your mind.

High.label: The Someday Spouse
summaries: Marriage is in the picture. The timing is flexible.

You see yourself married one day, and the idea makes you happy rather than nervous. You’re not in a rush, but you’re not here to waste time either. Whether it starts with a biodata or a brunch, you hope it ends with a home together.
behaviors: By month three you’re quietly asking yourself if this person could be family.
You notice how they talk about their own family and their own future.
The talking stage feels easier when you both know marriage is on the table.
strengths: You’re clear about your direction and still relaxed about the pace.
weaknesses: You can start picturing the wedding before you really know the person.
realLife: On a first date: You enjoy the date, and somewhere in your head a question hums: could this be family?
In a fight: You fight for the long run, because you’re already picturing one.
tips: Ask about marriage early and lightly: “Is it something you see for yourself?” It can save you both a year.
match: Best with: Someone who wants marriage too, in their own time and their own way.
Green flag: They talk about the future with “we”, and mean it.
Careful with: Someone who dodges every question about where things are going.

Moderate.label: The Open Door
summaries: Not sure yet, and honest about it.

Marriage might be in your future, and you’re genuinely open to it: arranged, love or something in between. You just won’t pretend to know the timing or the shape yet. You’d rather meet the right person first and find out what you want with them.
behaviors: You answer “do you want marriage?” with “maybe, with the right person”, and you mean it.
A biodata and a profile both get a fair look from you, no strong rules either way.
You let the relationship tell you what it wants to become.
strengths: You come to love without a script, so you see the actual person.
weaknesses: Staying open for too long can leave the other person unsure where you’re headed.
realLife: On a first date: Curious, open and a little playful about the “so what are you looking for?” question.
In a fight: If it’s about the future, you ask for time to think, and you actually use it to think.
tips: Open is good, vague isn’t. Give yourself a rough answer for a year from now, and share it.
match: Best with: Someone patient who wants to see where it goes, without a countdown.
Green flag: They ask what you want and don’t rush the answer.
Careful with: Someone who needs a firm yes or no on marriage in week one.

Low.label: The Paperless Promise
summaries: Commitment, yes. The certificate is optional.

You take love seriously; you just don’t think a ceremony is what makes it serious. You could marry for the right person or to make your families happy, but it isn’t the dream you’re chasing. For you, the promise lives in how two people treat each other.
behaviors: You care more about how a couple treats each other than about the wedding date.
You’d marry for the right person, or for your families, but you’re not counting down.
When everyone talks wedding venues, you’re the one asking how the couple is actually doing.
strengths: You keep the focus on the relationship, not the ceremony.
weaknesses: Your easygoing view can sound unserious to someone who really wants marriage.
realLife: On a first date: Easy, curious and in no rush. You want to know the person before the plan.
In a fight: When marriage comes up in a fight, you explain your view calmly instead of dodging it.
tips: Say where you stand on marriage by the third date. “Open, but not chasing it” is a real answer.
match: Best with: Someone committed and relaxed, who sees marriage as a choice, not a deadline.
Green flag: They’re clear about where they stand on marriage, and open to talking about it.
Careful with: Someone with a wedding timeline who hasn’t asked what you want.

VeryLow.label: The No-Ring Romantic
summaries: All in on love, not sold on marriage.

You believe in love, loyalty and showing up; you just don’t see why it needs a wedding to count. Freedom matters to you, and so does choosing someone for real, every day, not once on a stage. You’re not against anyone’s marriage; it just isn’t your map.
behaviors: You can be deeply committed with no plans for a wedding at all.
Rishta talk at home makes you change the subject, politely.
You’d rather say “marriage isn’t my plan” early than lead anyone on.
strengths: Your commitment is a daily choice, not a contract, and it shows.
weaknesses: Someone who dreams of marriage may hear “not for me” as “not with you”.
realLife: On a first date: You talk about travel, books and big dreams. Weddings don’t come up, and you like it that way.
In a fight: If marriage becomes the fight, you stay honest instead of making promises you can’t keep.
tips: Say it kindly and early: “I want something real, I’m just not sure about marriage.” The right person will hear the first half too.
match: Best with: Someone who wants a real, lasting bond and doesn’t need a wedding to feel sure of it.
Green flag: They respect your view of marriage without trying to change it.
Careful with: Someone who says they don’t mind but keeps hoping you’ll come around.

Undecided.label: The Open Door

Marriage might be in your future, and you’re genuinely open to it: arranged, love or something in between. You just won’t pretend to know the timing or the shape yet. You’d rather meet the right person first and find out what you want with them.

You let the relationship tell you what it wants to become.

VeryHigh.label: The Same-Page Seeker
summaries: Chemistry is great. Same life plans are essential.

You want to build the same future, not just enjoy the same evenings. Work, home, kids, money, where you’ll live at 40: you’d rather know early than find out late. You’ve seen great love stories crack over different dreams, and you don’t plan to be one of them.
behaviors: You ask the big questions early, and you respect people who ask them back.
Strong chemistry with someone heading the other way feels like a beautiful mistake to you.
Talking about the future together is romantic to you, not a buzzkill.
strengths: You rarely waste years on something that was never going to fit.
weaknesses: Your list can close the door on someone who would have grown into your life.
realLife: On a first date: Charming, curious, and by the second chai you know where they want to live.
In a fight: You go straight to the root: “Is this about today, or about where we’re headed?”
tips: Keep your must-haves to three. Everything else, let them surprise you.
match: Best with: Someone clear about their goals who enjoys big conversations early.
Green flag: Their plans are specific, and they ask about yours with real interest.
Careful with: Someone who says “we’ll see” to every big question.

High.label: The Road-Map Romantic
summaries: Love, plus a shared idea of where it’s going.

For you, love feels safest when you both know where it’s heading. You enjoy talking about the future together: the city, the work, the home, the family. It isn’t about control; you just know chemistry lasts longer when two people are walking the same road.
behaviors: You like the “where do you see yourself in five years” talk, maybe a bit too much.
Clear long-term direction lets you relax and enjoy the present.
A big mismatch on kids or career cools you down, however good the chemistry.
strengths: You build relationships that don’t fall apart over a surprise in year three.
weaknesses: You can rule people out for plans they haven’t really made yet.
realLife: On a first date: You enjoy the banter, then steer it, gently, toward what they want from life.
In a fight: You calm down once you remember you want the same future. You say it, and it helps.
tips: Plans at 25 change by 30. Look for someone who plans with you, not only someone whose plans already fit.
match: Best with: Someone who knows roughly what they want and enjoys planning it with you.
Green flag: They bring up the future themselves, and they’re specific.
Careful with: Endless “let’s see”, with no answer even after a year.

Moderate.label: The Compass Checker
summaries: Same direction, please. The details can wait.

You don’t need someone’s five-year plan, but you do want to know you’re facing the same way. Kids or no kids, big city or small town, ambition or ease: you check the big direction, then relax. That makes you practical in love without turning it into a checklist.
behaviors: By month three you’ve gently found out where they stand on the big things.
Different hobbies, careers and habits are fine with you, as long as the destination matches.
You enjoy the present more once you know the future isn’t a fight waiting to happen.
strengths: You catch the big mismatches early without killing the romance.
weaknesses: A quick check-in about the future can feel like a test to someone more go-with-the-flow.
realLife: On a first date: Fun first. Somewhere near dessert, you’ve casually asked where they see themselves living.
In a fight: You bring it back to the big picture: “Are we still heading the same way?”
tips: Ask about the future lightly and often, not once with a list. It feels like curiosity, not a test.
match: Best with: Someone who can talk about the future easily, without needing it all decided.
Green flag: They answer big questions honestly, even when the answer is “I don’t know yet”.
Careful with: Someone who changes the subject every time the future comes up.

Low.label: The Plan Bender
summaries: Feelings first, and plans that can bend.

You care about where life is going; you just believe strong feelings can bridge a lot of differences. Plans change, cities change, jobs change, and you’d rather pick someone you love and adjust together. You’re easy to build a life with, because you bend.
behaviors: You’d move cities for the right person, and you’ve probably already thought about it.
You talk about the future when it comes up, never as a checklist.
Different goals feel like something to work out, not a reason to stop.
strengths: You adapt, so two different lives can actually become one.
weaknesses: You can bend so much that your own plans quietly disappear.
realLife: On a first date: Easy and open. If they mention a big plan, you’re curious, not worried.
In a fight: You look for the compromise first, sometimes before you’ve said what you want.
tips: Bending is a gift. Before you bend, say out loud what you’d want if you didn’t have to.
match: Best with: Someone with clear goals who still leaves plenty of room for yours.
Green flag: They ask what you want too, not just how you’ll fit into their plan.
Careful with: Someone who takes your flexibility for granted.

VeryLow.label: The Heart-First Leaper
summaries: Falls for the person. The plans can catch up later.

You fall for a laugh, a voice, the way someone talks to the waiter, and the five-year plan can wait. You believe two people who really want each other will find their way through the logistics. Some call it risky; you call it believing in people.
behaviors: Kids, cities and careers rarely come up in your first few months, and you like it that way.
You’ve fallen for people whose plans looked nothing like yours.
Big questions on early dates make you feel like you’re being interviewed.
strengths: You see the person, not the résumé.
weaknesses: A big difference you skipped in month two can turn up as a big fight in year two.
realLife: On a first date: You talk about films, food and childhood stories. Five-year plans aren’t invited.
In a fight: When plans clash, you say “we’ll figure it out”. Try figuring out one small step tonight.
tips: Keep leading with your heart, and ask one big question by month three: kids, city or work. Your heart can handle the answer.
match: Best with: Someone warm and flexible who’d rather build plans together than arrive with them.
Green flag: They’re curious about your dreams instead of checking them against a list.
Careful with: Someone with a fixed plan who expects you to bend into it.

Undecided.label: The Compass Checker
summaries: Same direction, please. The details can wait.

You don’t need someone’s five-year plan, but you do want to know you’re facing the same way. Kids or no kids, big city or small town, ambition or ease: you check the big direction, then relax. That makes you practical in love without turning it into a checklist.
behaviors: By month three you’ve gently found out where they stand on the big things.
Different hobbies, careers and habits are fine with you, as long as the destination matches.
You enjoy the present more once you know the future isn’t a fight waiting to happen.
strengths: You catch the big mismatches early without killing the romance.
weaknesses: A quick check-in about the future can feel like a test to someone more go-with-the-flow.
realLife: On a first date: Fun first. Somewhere near dessert, you’ve casually asked where they see themselves living.
In a fight: You bring it back to the big picture: “Are we still heading the same way?”
tips: Ask about the future lightly and often, not once with a list. It feels like curiosity, not a test.
match: Best with: Someone who can talk about the future easily, without needing it all decided.
Green flag: They answer big questions honestly, even when the answer is “I don’t know yet”.
Careful with: Someone who changes the subject every time the future comes up.

tests.title: Growth Partner
tests.subtitle: Do you build each other up
tests.description: Measures whether you see a partner as someone you build life with and grow with (not just romance).
tests.whatYouLearn: Your desire for growth-based partnership.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Pairs better when both want growth and teamwork, not only feelings.

options.text: Feel judged. I want to be liked as I am
Thank them. I’d rather know
Laugh it off, then quietly watch for it

options.text: Cheer them on and bring the snacks
Sign up too. Two beginners, one pool
Say “nice!” and leave it to them

questions.text: In love, what matters more to you?

options.text: Being loved exactly as I am
Becoming better people together

questions.text: Late-night talk. They ask what you’d like to change about yourself this year. You…

options.text: Have a list ready, and ask for theirs
Laugh: “Nothing, I’m perfect. Pass the chips”
Think, then share one honest thing

questions.text: Your person starts reading self-help books and sends you a quote every morning. You…

options.text: Mute the quotes, keep the person
Read along. Book club for two
Heart them, read them never
Skim them and try a tip or two

questions.text: Last week’s fight is over and you’ve made up. Now you…

options.text: Quietly try to do better next time
Talk about what each of us learnt
Move on. No post-mortem needed

questions.text: Ten years from now, you’d love your relationship to be…

options.text: The same easy us, just older
Some new chapters, same core
Two people who’ve grown a lot, side by side

questions.text: They suggest a 6 am gym routine, together. You…

options.text: In. Accountability buddy for life
You go. I’ll have chai ready when you’re back

tests.measures: how much you value mutual growth and building each other up in a relationship

VeryHigh.label: The Rise-Together Type
summaries: Love should make you both better, every year.

You see a relationship as two people building better versions of themselves, side by side. Learning, pushing, trying, talking it through: that’s when you feel closest. A love that stays exactly the same for ten years sounds like a missed chance to you.
behaviors: You’ll happily do a 6 am run, a language course or a money plan together.
After a fight, you want to talk about what each of you learnt.
A deep talk about who you’re both becoming is your idea of a great night.
strengths: You make growth feel like a team sport, not a chore.
weaknesses: Some days your person wants to be loved, not improved, and that’s okay.
realLife: On a first date: You talk goals, books and dreams, and leave with two new ideas and a big smile.
In a fight: You want a proper debrief. Give them a day to cool down before you ask “what did we learn?”
tips: Plan one lazy day a week with no goals at all. Rest is part of growing too.
match: Best with: Someone curious and driven who sees love as a journey, not a finish line.
Green flag: They take feedback with grace and give it with kindness.
Careful with: Someone who wants you to grow but never wants to change a thing themselves.

High.label: The Cheerleader
summaries: Their loudest fan, and happy to be pushed too.

You want someone who makes you better and lets you return the favour. You show up for their goals with real energy, from interview prep to the first 5 km run, and you like a little honest push in return. Love, for you, should leave both people stronger.
behaviors: You remember their big deadline and send a “you’ve got this” at 9 am.
You like honest feedback, as long as it comes with kindness.
You’re happiest when you’re both working on something, even different things.
strengths: People become braver around you.
weaknesses: Your encouragement can tip into pushing on days they just want to rest.
realLife: On a first date: By the end you know their dream job, and you’ve already told them to go for it.
In a fight: You want to know what you can both do better next time, not just to make up.
tips: Ask before you coach: “Do you want ideas or just a hug?” Half the time, it’s the hug.
match: Best with: Someone with goals of their own who enjoys cheering as much as being cheered.
Green flag: They ask how your goals are going, and remember the details.
Careful with: Someone who enjoys your support but never asks about your plans.

Moderate.label: The Quiet Grower
summaries: Open to growing together, at a natural pace.

You believe people should grow in a relationship, but you don’t make it a project. You’ll take feedback, try new things together and change over the years, just without schedules and speeches. Growth, for you, happens like a plant: quietly, then all at once.
behaviors: You’ll join their new hobby for a month and keep the bits you like.
Feedback lands better with you over chai than in the middle of a fight.
You notice how much you’ve both changed only when you look back a year.
strengths: You grow without drama, and you let them grow too.
weaknesses: A very driven person may want more pushing and planning than you offer.
realLife: On a first date: You’d happily try their favourite odd little café, and tell them honestly if you hated it.
In a fight: You need a day, and then you quietly do better. Tell them that’s what you’re doing.
tips: Say your growth out loud sometimes: “I’ve been working on that.” They’ll love seeing it.
match: Best with: Someone curious and kind who likes trying things together without pressure.
Green flag: They suggest new things to do together and are fine when you say “maybe later”.
Careful with: Someone who measures love by how much you’ve improved.

Low.label: The Comfortable Constant
summaries: Supportive, relaxed, allergic to lectures.

You love the people you love as they are, and you hope for the same. You’ll grow, of course, just in your own time and not as a couple’s project. Your relationships feel easy because nobody in them is being pushed.
behaviors: You cheer their goals from the sidelines and mean every word.
You’d rather share chai and gossip than a joint vision board.
You change when it matters to you, not because someone sent you a podcast.
strengths: Being with you is restful. Nobody feels judged.
weaknesses: When they’re in a growth phase, your calm can look like you’re not interested.
realLife: On a first date: Relaxed and curious, happy to hear their big plans without pitching any of your own.
In a fight: You want to make up and move on, not analyse what went wrong.
tips: Ask about their goals once a month and really listen. Support is a way of growing together too.
match: Best with: Someone warm and steady who doesn’t need every year to be a level-up.
Green flag: They share their goals without making them your homework.
Careful with: Someone who keeps sending you courses you never asked for.

VeryLow.label: The Come-As-You-Are
summaries: Love is a soft place to land, not a project.

You work hard at life all day; love is where you get to stop trying. You want to be accepted with your quirks, and you give the same easy acceptance back. A relationship that keeps grading you feels more like an office than a home.
behaviors: You don’t need a self-improvement plan to feel close to someone.
Their flaws don’t bother you much, and you hope yours don’t bother them.
Your idea of a perfect evening involves zero lessons and lots of comfort.
strengths: People relax around you, because you don’t try to fix them.
weaknesses: Gentle feedback can feel like criticism to you, even when it’s meant as care.
realLife: On a first date: Comfortable, funny and very much yourself. No performance, no pitch.
In a fight: You want to be heard, not coached. Say so: “I need you to listen, not fix.”
tips: Accepting is your gift. Now and then, let one piece of feedback in. Growing a little doesn’t mean you weren’t enough.
match: Best with: Someone easygoing who loves you on your lazy days too.
Green flag: They laugh at your quirks instead of trying to correct them.
Careful with: Someone who treats you like a renovation project.

Undecided.label: The Quiet Grower
summaries: Open to growing together, at a natural pace.

You believe people should grow in a relationship, but you don’t make it a project. You’ll take feedback, try new things together and change over the years, just without schedules and speeches. Growth, for you, happens like a plant: quietly, then all at once.
behaviors: You’ll join their new hobby for a month and keep the bits you like.
Feedback lands better with you over chai than in the middle of a fight.
You notice how much you’ve both changed only when you look back a year.
strengths: You grow without drama, and you let them grow too.
weaknesses: A very driven person may want more pushing and planning than you offer.
realLife: On a first date: You’d happily try their favourite odd little café, and tell them honestly if you hated it.
In a fight: You need a day, and then you quietly do better. Tell them that’s what you’re doing.
tips: Say your growth out loud sometimes: “I’ve been working on that.” They’ll love seeing it.
match: Best with: Someone curious and kind who likes trying things together without pressure.
Green flag: They suggest new things to do together and are fine when you say “maybe later”.
Careful with: Someone who measures love by how much you’ve improved.

tests.title: Patience & Stability
tests.subtitle: Consistency over excitement
tests.description: Measures your ability to stay stable and patient when the relationship is calm and routine (no drama).
tests.whatYouLearn: Your tolerance for routine vs chasing intensity.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Predicts whether you’ll keep bond strong after the honeymoon phase ends.

questions.text: Eight months in. Friday plan: home, dal chawal, the same show again. You feel…

options.text: Restless. Are we old already?
Happy. This is the good stuff
Fine, if next Friday is something new

options.text: Big highs, big lows, never boring
Calm and steady, few highs, few lows

options.text: Plan something big to bring it back
Feel closer. The butterflies were the trailer
Wonder if the feeling is gone
Miss the butterflies a little, but stay cosy

options.text: Good, as long as we still laugh a lot

We’re good at this

New experiences together, now and then
Kindness, in the same small ways every day
