options.text: Goals
Sweet, but I want more sparks than that

tests.measures: how comfortable you are with the calm, steady side of a long relationship

VeryHigh.label: The Steady Flame
summaries: Not fireworks. A flame that lasts all night.

You know the difference between excitement and love, and you choose love. Calm, routine and quiet evenings don’t worry you; they feel like proof that it’s working. You build closeness through consistency and care, and that kind of steadiness is rarer than any spark.
behaviors: Butterflies fading feels like the real relationship starting, not ending.
Comfortable silence on a long drive is one of your favourite feelings.
Your love lives in daily habits: the chai made just right, the call at lunch.
strengths: You make people feel safe enough to stop performing.
weaknesses: Your contentment can miss that your person needs a little more novelty than you.
realLife: On a first date: No big show. Just good conversation, and you notice whether they’re kind to the waiter.
In a fight: You stay calm and look for the fix. Drama doesn’t pull you in, and that steadies them.
tips: Your calm is a gift. Add one new shared experience each season so your person feels the flame too.
match: Best with: Someone grounded who sees peace as a gift, not a warning sign.
Green flag: They stay kind on boring days, not just exciting ones.
Careful with: Someone who picks fights to feel close. That’s a pattern, not passion.

High.label: The Easy Sunday
summaries: Peace isn’t boring to you. It’s the point.

You enjoy the quiet, steady stretches of a relationship more than most people do. Routine doesn’t dim your attraction; it gives it somewhere to live. You still like some fun along the way, but you never confuse calm with the end of love.
behaviors: Reached-home texts, the same chai order, the usual Sunday: you love all of it.
The end of the honeymoon phase feels like settling in, not like losing something.
You show love through small, reliable things, again and again.
strengths: You keep love warm long after the butterflies have flown off.
weaknesses: You might not notice when your person is craving a bit more excitement.
realLife: On a first date: A quiet café, a long chat, and within an hour you can tell if it feels easy.
In a fight: You keep it calm and short. You want peace back, not a win.
tips: Every few months, say yes to their wild idea. Your calm can handle a little adventure.
match: Best with: Someone warm and dependable who enjoys a quiet life as much as you do.
Green flag: They show up the same way on ordinary days as on special ones.
Careful with: Someone who keeps creating drama to feel something.

Moderate.label: The Calm With Sprinkles
summaries: Steady love, with a little fun on top.

You like a relationship you can rely on, and you also like it to surprise you now and then. Routine is comfortable, but too much of it goes flat for you. You’re the type who loves the same Friday plan, as long as once a month it turns into something new.
behaviors: You love your little routines together, and a weekend trip every few months.
Calm weeks are fine, as long as you’re still laughing.
You notice when things go flat, and you nudge them back to life.
strengths: You keep love steady and alive at the same time.
weaknesses: When life gets busy, both the calm and the fun can slip without you noticing.
realLife: On a first date: A café you know, then a walk somewhere you don’t. Comfortable, with a little surprise.
In a fight: You want peace back fast, and you’re happy to make up over something fun.
tips: Put one small new thing on the calendar every month. It keeps your calm from turning flat.
match: Best with: Someone reliable who can also be talked into the occasional adventure.
Green flag: They’re dependable on weekdays and playful on weekends.
Careful with: Someone who mistakes a dull relationship for a stable one.

Low.label: The Surprise Planner
summaries: Keeps love exciting, gets itchy in the routine.

You love the person, and you also love it when life with them feels like an adventure. Routine weeks make you restless, so you’re the one booking the weekend trip or the new restaurant. You keep relationships fresh, as long as you don’t read every quiet spell as trouble.
behaviors: You plan surprise dates because the usual Friday makes you itchy.
Long calm stretches make you restless, even when nothing is wrong.
A new experience together recharges you more than any long talk.
strengths: You keep love from going stale. Life with you is never on autopilot.
weaknesses: You can get restless just when things are finally settling into something good.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest the new rooftop place or the board game café, never the usual.
In a fight: You want it sorted quickly so you can both get back to the fun part.
tips: Enjoy one boring evening a week, on purpose. Calm is where trust grows, and you’ll still get your adventures.
match: Best with: Someone grounded who loves your surprises and enjoys a slow Sunday too.
Green flag: They say yes to your wild plans, and sometimes come up with their own.
Careful with: Someone hot and cold. The not-knowing can feel like excitement, but it isn’t.

VeryLow.label: The Firework
summaries: Loves loud, feels big, bored by beige.

You feel love at full volume, and when it goes quiet you start to wonder if it’s still there. Big emotions make you feel alive, and you bring that colour to everyone around you. Calm stretches are your hard part, not because you love less, but because quiet feels like distance to you.
behaviors: The chase, the 2 am talks, the grand gestures: that’s when you feel most in love.
Three quiet weeks in a row can leave you wondering if the spark is gone.
You’d rather have a dramatic make-up than a calm month of nothing much.
strengths: Nobody is ever bored with you. You make ordinary days feel like an event.
weaknesses: You can mistake peace for the end of love, and stir things up to feel it again.
realLife: On a first date: Big energy, big laughs, and you’re secretly hoping it ends with a story worth telling.
In a fight: It gets loud fast, and making up is half the point for you. Try skipping the loud part once.
tips: When it feels too calm, plan a new experience together instead of starting a fight. Same spark, much less damage.
match: Best with: Someone steady and playful who can be your calm and still say yes to adventures.
Green flag: They keep surprising you in small ways, long after the start.
Careful with: Someone who creates drama to keep you hooked. That’s a fire, not a spark.

Undecided.label: The Calm With Sprinkles
summaries: Steady love, with a little fun on top.

You like a relationship you can rely on, and you also like it to surprise you now and then. Routine is comfortable, but too much of it goes flat for you. You’re the type who loves the same Friday plan, as long as once a month it turns into something new.
behaviors: You love your little routines together, and a weekend trip every few months.
Calm weeks are fine, as long as you’re still laughing.
You notice when things go flat, and you nudge them back to life.
strengths: You keep love steady and alive at the same time.
weaknesses: When life gets busy, both the calm and the fun can slip without you noticing.
realLife: On a first date: A café you know, then a walk somewhere you don’t. Comfortable, with a little surprise.
In a fight: You want peace back fast, and you’re happy to make up over something fun.
tips: Put one small new thing on the calendar every month. It keeps your calm from turning flat.
match: Best with: Someone reliable who can also be talked into the occasional adventure.
Green flag: They’re dependable on weekdays and playful on weekends.
Careful with: Someone who mistakes a dull relationship for a stable one.

tests.subtitle: Planning vs living day-to-day
tests.description: Measures whether you like planning and making decisions together (moving, finances, timelines).
tests.whatYouLearn: Your future planning mindset as a couple.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Reduces mismatch where one wants clarity and the other avoids it forever.

Laugh: “A year? I don’t know what’s for dinner”

options.text: Decide on gut feeling, fast
Talk it over for a few evenings, then decide
Sit down with pros, cons and a timeline

tests.measures: how much you plan for the future versus living day-to-day

VeryHigh.label: The Colour-Coder
summaries: The future has tabs, and you made them.

You plan far ahead: money, moves, milestones, maybe even the names of future pets. Not knowing where things are going sits badly with you, and a good plan feels like love made practical. Your decisions today are quietly building tomorrow.
behaviors: You have a rough five-year plan, and you’d love someone to make it a shared one.
Big decisions get pros, cons and a timeline, even the exciting ones.
“Let’s see where life takes us” is the least romantic sentence you know.
strengths: With you, the future feels safe. People know there’s a plan.
weaknesses: Not everything good can be scheduled, including the person in front of you.
realLife: On a first date: You arrived ten minutes early, with a backup plan in case it rained.
In a fight: You want a clear next step. Ask for one, then let it be enough for tonight.
tips: Plan the big picture together, then leave space for surprises. The best memories rarely make it onto a list.
match: Best with: Someone who loves a shared plan and keeps their side of it.
Green flag: They open the shared spreadsheet and actually fill it in.
Careful with: Someone who keeps saying “later” to every future talk.

High.label: The Calendar Keeper
summaries: Knows the dates, books the tickets, likes to know.

You think ahead because it makes life calmer, not because you need control. Clear timelines help you relax, and you like to make big decisions with a little time and thought. You’re the one everyone trusts to remember the anniversary and the rent date.
behaviors: You like talking about where you’ll be next year, and you mean actual places.
Vague answers about the future make you uneasy, even early on.
You plan the trip, the budget and the backup, and you’re rarely caught out.
strengths: Life with you runs smoothly. Things get done, on time.
weaknesses: Your plans can arrive before the other person has had time to dream.
realLife: On a first date: Booked, confirmed, and you know exactly where you’ll park.
In a fight: You want a plan to fix it, not just a hug. Sometimes the hug comes first.
tips: Leave one weekend a month completely unplanned. It’s good for you, and they’ll love seeing you loosen up.
match: Best with: Someone reliable who enjoys planning, or at least loves that you do.
Green flag: They give you clear answers and keep the plans they make.
Careful with: Someone who calls all planning “controlling” and won’t talk about the future.

Moderate.label: The Pencil Planner
summaries: Plans the big things, in pencil, eraser handy.

You like a direction, and you like room to change it. You plan the important things, like money, moves and milestones, and let the small ones happen. Your plans are real; they just aren’t carved in stone.
behaviors: You can talk about next year happily, and drop the plan if life changes.
You book the big trip early and leave the days inside it open.
You meet planners and free spirits halfway, which most people find easy.
strengths: You make plans without making them a cage.
weaknesses: Sitting in the middle, you can let the louder person set the pace.
realLife: On a first date: You picked the place in advance and left the rest of the evening open.
In a fight: You look for the version of the plan you can both live with.
tips: Say which kind of planner you are early: “Big things yes, small things let’s see.” It saves a lot of friction.
match: Best with: Almost anyone who can talk about the future openly and change their mind kindly.
Green flag: They make plans with you, not for you.
Careful with: Someone who either refuses to plan anything or plans everything without asking.

Low.label: The Wing-It Optimist
summaries: Some plans, and lots of trust that it’ll work out.
You do think about the future, just not in spreadsheets. You trust that things usually work out, and so far they mostly have. You’d rather keep life light and flexible than plan away the fun.
behaviors: You have rough hopes for the future and very few deadlines.
You plan the big things when they’re close, not years ahead.
You’re great company on a trip that goes off script.
strengths: You stay calm when plans fall apart, because you never held them too tightly.
weaknesses: Your easy “we’ll figure it out” can worry someone who needs to see the plan.
realLife: On a first date: You booked nothing, found a great place anyway, and it became the story of the night.
In a fight: You say “it’ll work out”, and sometimes they need to hear how, not just that.
tips: When they ask about the future, give one concrete detail. “Maybe Pune in two years” beats “let’s see” every time.
match: Best with: Someone organised but relaxed, who plans the big things and lets the rest flow.
Green flag: They plan enough to feel safe, without planning the fun out of life.
Careful with: Someone who calls every flexible answer “not serious”.

VeryLow.label: The No-Plan Plan
summaries: Today is the plan. Tomorrow can introduce itself later.

You live in the present, and you’re good at it. Long-range plans feel heavy or pointless to you, because life has a habit of changing them anyway. You deal with things as they come, often better than the people who planned for them.
behaviors: “Where do you see us in five years?” makes you want to change the topic, or the table.
You’re brilliant at last-minute plans: tonight’s dinner, tomorrow’s road trip.
Your love feels fresh because it isn’t following a script.
strengths: You’re fully here. People feel how present you are with them.
weaknesses: A planner can hear your “let’s see” as “I don’t see us”.
realLife: On a first date: It started as coffee and became dinner, a walk and a street food detour. Unplanned, obviously.
In a fight: If it’s about the future, you go quiet. Try one small, honest sentence about what you want.
tips: You don’t need a five-year plan. Try a six-month one: one trip, one goal. It reassures them and costs you little.
match: Best with: Someone easygoing who enjoys today with you and doesn’t need a road map to feel safe.
Green flag: They make room for spontaneity and don’t panic when plans change.
Careful with: Someone who wants the next five years locked before you know their middle name.

Undecided.label: The Pencil Planner
summaries: Plans the big things, in pencil, eraser handy.

You like a direction, and you like room to change it. You plan the important things, like money, moves and milestones, and let the small ones happen. Your plans are real; they just aren’t carved in stone.
behaviors: You can talk about next year happily, and drop the plan if life changes.
You book the big trip early and leave the days inside it open.
You meet planners and free spirits halfway, which most people find easy.
strengths: You make plans without making them a cage.
weaknesses: Sitting in the middle, you can let the louder person set the pace.
realLife: On a first date: You picked the place in advance and left the rest of the evening open.
In a fight: You look for the version of the plan you can both live with.
tips: Say which kind of planner you are early: “Big things yes, small things let’s see.” It saves a lot of friction.
match: Best with: Almost anyone who can talk about the future openly and change their mind kindly.
Green flag: They make plans with you, not for you.
Careful with: Someone who either refuses to plan anything or plans everything without asking.

tests.title: Monogamy Values
tests.subtitle: Exclusivity and boundaries
tests.description: Measures how strongly you value exclusivity, boundaries, and commitment rules long-term.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your exclusivity expectations and boundaries.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps align trust expectations and reduces jealousy conflicts.

questions.text: Three weeks of talking to someone. Are you still chatting with others?

options.text: Until we say we’re exclusive, yes
No. One person at a time, always
Yes, and I don’t see why that has to change

questions.text: Your person keeps up a flirty banter with a colleague. You…

options.text: Nothing. A little flirting is harmless
Let it go if it stays light and out in the open
Tell them it bothers me. Flirting is for us

questions.text: In a serious relationship, exclusivity is…

options.text: Something each couple decides for itself
Non-negotiable

questions.text: Your person wants to stay close to an ex. Coffee every few months. You…

options.text: Totally fine. People can stay in each other’s lives
Not comfortable. Exes belong in the past
Fine, if I can tag along sometimes

questions.text: Six months in, they still swipe now and then, “just to look”. You…

options.text: Find it odd, and ask why
Shrug. Looking isn’t doing
Need a serious talk, tonight
Ask them, calmly, to stop

questions.text: The person you’re seeing brings up an open relationship. You…

options.text: Want to understand what they mean first
Feel relieved. I’ve thought about it too
Say no, and probably walk away
Hear them out, but it’s not for me

questions.text: Their best friend is exactly their type. You think…

options.text: Lucky them. A good friend is a good friend
That friendship needs some clear lines

questions.text: What counts as cheating to you?

options.text: Only breaking what the two of us decided
Even a secret flirty chat
Anything physical, or lying about it

tests.measures: how strongly you value exclusivity and monogamy in relationships

VeryHigh.label: The One-and-Only
summaries: One person, all in, no grey areas.

For you, exclusivity isn’t a rule; it’s the ground everything else stands on. You give one person all of your loyalty and expect the same back, from the talking stage onward. Grey areas make you uneasy, because to you love is the one place where things should be simple.
behaviors: You stop talking to others the moment you’re really interested in someone.
A secret flirty chat counts as cheating in your book, no debate.
You’re loyal in small things too: your jokes, your attention and your late-night calls are theirs.
strengths: Your loyalty is total. The person you love never has to wonder.
weaknesses: Your strict lines can make innocent friendships look like a threat.
realLife: On a first date: You’re fully present, and by the end you’ve gently asked if they’re seeing anyone else.
In a fight: If trust is touched, it’s the only topic. You need the truth before anything else.
tips: Your loyalty is rare. Trust it to be returned, and give their friendships a little room.
match: Best with: Someone just as devoted, who sees exclusivity as a gift, not a cage.
Green flag: They’re open with their phone and their plans, without being asked.
Careful with: Someone with “just friends” whose messages they’ll never show you.

High.label: The Clear-Lines Keeper
summaries: Exclusive means exclusive, and you say so.

You value loyalty and clear boundaries, and you live by them yourself. When you’re with someone, the swiping stops, the flirting stops and the exes stay in the past. You don’t do it out of fear; you just think trust grows best inside clear walls.
behaviors: Once you’re together, you stop flirting elsewhere, and you expect the same.
Secret chats, even innocent ones, bother you more than the chat itself.
Your loyalty is quiet and steady. You don’t need to announce it.
strengths: People always know where they stand with you.
weaknesses: Your lines can feel strict to someone who grew up with looser ones.
realLife: On a first date: Charming and attentive. Your phone stays face down, and you notice if theirs does too.
In a fight: You go straight to honesty: “Just tell me everything, and we’ll fix it.”
tips: Share your lines early and kindly. Clear boundaries feel safe; surprise ones feel like rules.
match: Best with: Someone loyal who likes clear boundaries as much as you do.
Green flag: They tell you about the awkward message before you have to ask.
Careful with: Someone who calls your boundaries “insecure” instead of respecting them.

Moderate.label: The Trust-But-Talk Type
summaries: One person, clear lines, no paranoia.

You prefer being exclusive and you expect honesty about it, but you’re not rigid or suspicious. You’d rather talk about where the lines are than assume them. Friendships, exes and the odd harmless flirt are fine with you, as long as nothing is hidden.
behaviors: You go exclusive when it’s said out loud, and then you mean it.
When something feels off, you ask questions instead of making accusations.
You and your person have actually talked about what counts as too far.
strengths: You make boundaries a conversation, not a rulebook.
weaknesses: If you assume your lines are obvious, you may not say them until they’re crossed.
realLife: On a first date: Open and easy. You won’t ask about exclusivity yet, but you will by date five.
In a fight: You want the full story, calmly, and then you decide how you feel.
tips: Have the “what counts as cheating for us?” talk early. It’s awkward for five minutes and useful for years.
match: Best with: Someone honest who likes having clear conversations about trust.
Green flag: They mention a coffee with an ex before you hear about it from someone else.
Careful with: Someone who gets defensive whenever you ask a simple question.

Low.label: The Easy Truster
summaries: Trusts first, doesn’t need a rulebook.

You prefer one person, but you don’t police the edges. Friends of every kind, a harmless flirt at a party, an old ex at a wedding: none of it rattles you much. You trust people until they give you a real reason not to.
behaviors: Your person’s close friendships don’t worry you; you have your own.
A bit of flirting at a party is just fun to you, not a threat.
You’d rather trust and be wrong once than watch and be tense always.
strengths: People feel trusted around you, and most of them rise to it.
weaknesses: Your easy trust can miss signs that someone more watchful would spot.
realLife: On a first date: Relaxed and fun. You don’t mind their phone buzzing, as long as they’re present.
In a fight: You’d rather talk it out than lay down rules.
tips: Easy trust is lovely. Still say your one or two real lines out loud, so nobody has to guess them.
match: Best with: Someone secure who enjoys a big social life and doesn’t keep tabs.
Green flag: They’re open about their life, so your trust never feels foolish.
Careful with: Someone who uses your easygoing trust as permission to hide things.

VeryLow.label: The Unlabelled Heart
summaries: Love without fences, built on honesty.

You don’t believe love has to mean owning someone. Closeness, honesty and freedom matter more to you than a fixed set of rules, and you’d rather two people write their own. What you can’t stand isn’t openness; it’s lying.
behaviors: You’re relaxed about exes, close friends and harmless flirting, yours and theirs.
You’d rather talk honestly about what you both want than assume the usual rules.
Jealousy isn’t how you measure love, and you don’t want yours measured that way.
strengths: You’re honest about what you want, even when it isn’t the usual answer.
weaknesses: Not everyone hears “I’m open” the way you mean it. Some hear “I’m not serious”.
realLife: On a first date: Easygoing and frank. If the topic comes up, you say what you think, kindly.
In a fight: You want the real feeling on the table, not a rule quoted at you.
tips: Say what you want early, in plain words. The right person will respect the honesty, even if their answer is different.
match: Best with: Someone secure and honest who wants to set the rules together, not just inherit them.
Green flag: They talk about boundaries openly, without shame or sulking.
Careful with: Someone who says they’re fine with it, then keeps score in secret.

Undecided.label: The Trust-But-Talk Type
summaries: One person, clear lines, no paranoia.

You prefer being exclusive and you expect honesty about it, but you’re not rigid or suspicious. You’d rather talk about where the lines are than assume them. Friendships, exes and the odd harmless flirt are fine with you, as long as nothing is hidden.

When something feels off, you ask questions instead of making accusations.
You and your person have actually talked about what counts as too far.
strengths: You make boundaries a conversation, not a rulebook.
weaknesses: If you assume your lines are obvious, you may not say them until they’re crossed.
realLife: On a first date: Open and easy. You won’t ask about exclusivity yet, but you will by date five.
In a fight: You want the full story, calmly, and then you decide how you feel.
tips: Have the “what counts as cheating for us?” talk early. It’s awkward for five minutes and useful for years.
match: Best with: Someone honest who likes having clear conversations about trust.
Green flag: They mention a coffee with an ex before you hear about it from someone else.
Careful with: Someone who gets defensive whenever you ask a simple question.

tests.title: Conflict Tolerance
tests.subtitle: Can you handle hard seasons
tests.description: Measures whether you stay and work through problems or quit fast when difficulties appear.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your endurance in hard seasons of relationships.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Predicts long-term survivability after the first big fight or life crisis.

questions.text: Your third big fight this month. Late at night, you think…

options.text: Maybe this just isn’t working
We’re in a bad patch. We’ll get through it
I’m done. Love shouldn’t be this hard
Something has to change. Let’s talk tomorrow

questions.text: Which do you believe more?

options.text: If it’s right, it shouldn’t feel this hard
Love is a choice you keep making

questions.text: They lose their job and turn quiet and grumpy for months. You…

options.text: Feel it dragging you down, and start pulling away
Stay close and ride it out with them
Support them, but ask for some warmth back

questions.text: Mid-fight, words fly. Has “maybe we should break up” ever come out of your mouth?

options.text: Once or twice, and I regretted it
Yes. When I say it, I usually mean it
Never. I don’t use it as a weapon

questions.text: Work means a year of long distance. You…

options.text: End it kindly. Distance never works
Give it a fair go and see how it feels
Make it work: calls, visits, a countdown

questions.text: A year in, their family still isn’t warming up to you. You…

options.text: Ask my person to step in more
Wonder if it’s worth all this
Keep showing up, kind and patient

questions.text: Your friends say, “You two fight too much. Just leave.” You…

options.text: Take it as the push I needed
Hear them out, then decide myself
Thank them, but this is ours to fix
Start to wonder if they’re right

questions.text: When a relationship gets hard, your first instinct is to…

options.text: Wonder if it’s time to go
Roll up my sleeves

tests.measures: how well you handle difficult seasons and repeated conflict in long-term relationships

VeryHigh.label: The Monsoon-Proof Heart
summaries: Storms come. You stay and wait for the sun.

You believe love is a choice you keep making, especially on the hard days. Job losses, long distance, difficult families, a bad year: you see them as seasons to get through together, not reasons to leave. That kind of staying power is rare, and the people you love feel it.
behaviors: A string of fights tells you it’s a bad patch, not a bad relationship.
You’ve stuck with someone through a hard season and come out closer.
You don’t take advice to leave from anyone who isn’t in the relationship.
strengths: When life gets hard, you’re the one who stays.
weaknesses: You can stay too long in something that keeps hurting you. Staying is only brave when both are trying.
realLife: On a first date: You’re easy company, and quietly impressed when they talk about sticking with hard things.
In a fight: You never threaten to leave. You say “we’ll fix this” and start working.
tips: Your staying power is a gift. Give it to someone who’s working too, and never stay where you feel unsafe.
match: Best with: Someone just as committed, who fights for the relationship, not against you.
Green flag: They stay calm in a crisis and lean in, not away.
Careful with: Someone who leans on your loyalty but never changes anything.

High.label: The Patch-Up Pro
summaries: Hard seasons don’t scare you off. You stitch.

You know every couple goes through rough stretches, and you don’t take them as a sign it’s over. When things get messy, you lean in, talk it through and work on repair. People feel safe with you, because one bad week won’t make you vanish.
behaviors: You make the first move to make up, even when you’re still a bit hurt.
Breakup talk stays out of your fights. It’s just not your weapon.
When they’re struggling, you stay close instead of stepping back.
strengths: You turn rough patches into stronger foundations.
weaknesses: You can work so hard at fixing it that you forget to check if they’re working too.
realLife: On a first date: If something goes wrong, like rain or a closed café, you laugh and find plan B together.
In a fight: You stay in the room, lower your voice and look for the fix.
tips: Repair is your talent. Make sure it’s a two-person job, and ask them to hold the other end of the thread.
match: Best with: Someone who repairs as willingly as you do.
Green flag: They come back after a fight ready to understand, not just to win.
Careful with: Someone who leaves all the fixing to you.

Moderate.label: The Second-Chance Giver
summaries: You’ll stay and fix it, as long as it’s fixing.

You don’t run at the first sign of trouble, and you don’t stay forever in something stuck either. You give hard seasons a fair try and watch for progress. If things get better, you’re all in; if nothing changes, you slowly make peace with leaving.
behaviors: You’ve worked through a rough patch before, and you’re glad you did.
One bad month won’t end it for you; a bad year might.
You need to see effort from both sides to keep giving yours.
strengths: You’re fair. You give real chances and keep honest limits.
weaknesses: Keeping track of progress can make the other person feel like they’re on probation.
realLife: On a first date: Easy and open. You don’t expect perfection, just honesty when something goes wrong.
In a fight: You want to solve it, and you want to see that they want to solve it too.
tips: Tell them what progress looks like to you. “I need us to fight less about money” is easier to work on than a feeling.
match: Best with: Someone who shows effort when things get hard, not just promises.
Green flag: They say “let’s fix this” and then actually change something.
Careful with: Someone who apologises beautifully and changes nothing.

Low.label: The Breathing-Room Type
summaries: You stay, but heavy stretches make you need air.

You care deeply, and you can handle a rough patch, but long heavy seasons drain you fast. When things stay hard, you pull back to breathe, and sometimes the pulling back turns into leaving. It isn’t a lack of love; you simply feel the weight of things more than most.
behaviors: You need space after a fight, and you come back calmer.
A long, heavy month makes you quietly wonder about the exit.
Small, visible improvements keep you going more than big promises.
strengths: You know your limits, and you protect your energy.
weaknesses: Your quiet pulling away can feel like goodbye before you’ve decided anything.
realLife: On a first date: Warm and easy. If it gets awkward, you change the topic, and it works.
In a fight: You need a break. Say when you’ll be back, so the break doesn’t look like the end.
tips: When you need air, say “I’m stepping back to breathe, not to leave.” One sentence changes everything for them.
match: Best with: Someone patient who gives you space and doesn’t chase you when you step back.
Green flag: They fix things in small, visible ways, not just with words.
Careful with: Someone who stays sad or angry for weeks and expects you to carry it.

VeryLow.label: The Peace Protector
summaries: When love starts to hurt, you choose your peace.

You’ve learned that you can’t control how others behave, only whether you stay. So when a relationship turns heavy, you’d rather leave cleanly than suffer slowly. That instinct has kept you safe, though sometimes it leaves before a fixable problem gets its chance to be fixed.
behaviors: Repeated fights make you check out long before you say anything.
You believe the right love should feel mostly easy, and you hold out for that.
When you say it’s over, you usually decided days ago.
strengths: You don’t stay where you’re unhappy. Your self-respect is strong.
weaknesses: Every couple has hard seasons. Leaving at the first one can mean missing the good one after it.
realLife: On a first date: You’re lovely company, and quietly watching how they handle a small hiccup, like a wrong order.
In a fight: You feel the urge to walk out. Say “I need an hour” instead of “I’m done”.
tips: Before you leave, ask one question: is this a bad person, or a bad month? Leave the first. Give the second a real try.
match: Best with: Someone calm and kind who keeps fights small and repairs them fast.
Green flag: They apologise quickly and mean it, so things rarely pile up.
Careful with: Someone who keeps the drama going. You’ll leave, and you’ll be right, but it’ll hurt.

Undecided.label: The Second-Chance Giver
summaries: You’ll stay and fix it, as long as it’s fixing.

You don’t run at the first sign of trouble, and you don’t stay forever in something stuck either. You give hard seasons a fair try and watch for progress. If things get better, you’re all in; if nothing changes, you slowly make peace with leaving.

One bad month won’t end it for you; a bad year might.
You need to see effort from both sides to keep giving yours.

weaknesses: Keeping track of progress can make the other person feel like they’re on probation.
realLife: On a first date: Easy and open. You don’t expect perfection, just honesty when something goes wrong.
In a fight: You want to solve it, and you want to see that they want to solve it too.
tips: Tell them what progress looks like to you. “I need us to fight less about money” is easier to work on than a feeling.
match: Best with: Someone who shows effort when things get hard, not just promises.
Green flag: They say “let’s fix this” and then actually change something.
Careful with: Someone who apologises beautifully and changes nothing.

tests.title: Adventure vs Settle
tests.subtitle: Lifestyle pace long-term
tests.description: Measures whether you want calm settled life or ongoing adventure and travel long-term.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your long-term lifestyle pace preference.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Helps align weekend style, travel, and daily life energy long-term.

questions.text: A long weekend is coming. Your dream plan:

options.text: A short trip, home by Sunday night
A last-minute bus to the hills, nothing booked
Home, slow mornings, a long family lunch

questions.text: In ten years, you’d rather have…

options.text: Passport stamps from thirty countries
A home with your name on the door

questions.text: Your person gets an offer to move to Berlin for two years. You…

options.text: Go, as long as we come back after
Start packing. I’ve been waiting for this
Hesitate. My whole life is here
Ask if they could do it from here

questions.text: Same flat, same job, same chai stall for five years. That sounds…

options.text: Like a slow cage
Fine, with a trip or two each year
Like heaven
Okay, but I’d change the job at least

questions.text: You picture your future home together as…

options.text: A base we keep, with lots of trips out of it
Somewhere new every few years
A flat near family, with a balcony full of plants

questions.text: A friend quits their job to travel for a year. You feel…

options.text: Happy for them, glad it isn’t me
Inspired. I’d do it in a heartbeat
A bit jealous, but I’d miss home

questions.text: Your ideal Sunday morning, years from now:

options.text: Somewhere I’ve never been
Same café, same order, the owner knows my name

questions.text: Your weeknights, ideally, look like…

options.text: Out somewhere: a gig, a new place, a class
A mix: two nights out, the rest at home
Home by seven, cook, call my parents, sleep
Whatever the day throws up

tests.measures: whether you prefer a settled or an adventurous lifestyle long-term

VeryHigh.label: The Neighbourhood Regular
summaries: Same café, same order, same people. Bliss.

You know exactly what makes you happy: a home that stays put, your people nearby and days you can predict. Constant change drains you more than it thrills you. You’d rather go deep in one place than skim across fifty, and you build a life that holds.
behaviors: Five years in the same flat with the same chai stall sounds like a dream to you.
A big move would need a very good reason, and a lot of time to say goodbye.
Your idea of romance is a shared routine you both love.
strengths: You build a stability the people you love can lean on for years.
weaknesses: Your love of the familiar can turn every new idea into a no before you’ve tried it.
realLife: On a first date: Your usual spot, your usual order, and you watch whether they seem at home there.
In a fight: You want things back to normal quickly. Normal is your happy place.
tips: Let one small new thing in each month: a new dish, a new route home. It keeps your steady life from going stiff.
match: Best with: Someone who loves home and routine as much as you do.
Green flag: They’re rooted too: close to their people, happy in their place.
Careful with: Someone always planning the next move, the next city, the next everything.

High.label: The Nest Maker
summaries: Home is your favourite place, and you make it lovely.

You love a settled life: your own space, your people nearby, your routines just right. Adventure is nice now and then, but you’re always glad to get home. You put your energy into building a place where life feels warm and steady.
behaviors: You love cooking at home, plants on the balcony and a familiar Sunday.
Trips are fun, and getting back to your own bed is the best part.
You picture a home near family, with room for everyone at festivals.
strengths: You make home feel like the safest place in the world.
weaknesses: Saying no to too many adventures can make an adventurous person feel caged.
realLife: On a first date: Your favourite café, the one where they know your order. You want them to see your world.
In a fight: You want to sort it at home, over chai, not in a crowded place.
tips: Say yes to one adventure a year that you wouldn’t pick yourself. Your nest will feel even better after.
match: Best with: Someone warm and homely who also brings in a little fresh air.
Green flag: They light up when they talk about the home they want to build.
Careful with: Someone who wants to live out of a suitcase forever.

Moderate.label: The Home-Base Explorer
summaries: Roots and wings, in roughly equal measure.

You want a home that feels like yours, and you want to leave it often enough to miss it. Some seasons of your life are for exploring, others for building, and you’re good at both. Most people find your pace easy to share.
behaviors: A cosy home and one big trip a year is your idea of balance.
You can enjoy a quiet month and still say yes to a sudden road trip.
You adjust to their pace without losing your own.
strengths: You can be happy almost anywhere: on the road or on the sofa.
weaknesses: Being flexible, you can drift toward their pace and forget what you wanted.
realLife: On a first date: A favourite old place, then a new one you spotted on the way.
In a fight: You want peace back, and you’re open to their way of getting there.
tips: Every few months, check the balance together: “More home or more road this season?” It keeps you both happy.
match: Best with: Someone who loves home and the occasional adventure in roughly the same mix.
Green flag: They’re happy to stay in and happy to go, and they ask what you feel like.
Careful with: Someone at one extreme who wants you to live there too.

Low.label: The Weekend Wanderer
summaries: A home base, and a bag always half-packed.

You like having a place that’s yours, but staying in it every weekend makes you restless. Short trips, new cafés and the odd big move keep you feeling alive. You can settle, as long as settling doesn’t mean standing still.
behaviors: You plan a getaway every month or two, and you’d love some company.
You’d move cities for the right job or person, without too much drama.
Routine is fine on weekdays; weekends are for something new.
strengths: You bring fresh air into a relationship without blowing the roof off.
weaknesses: A homebody can read your restlessness as a sign they’re not enough.
realLife: On a first date: Somewhere new to both of you, with a plan B in case it’s closed.
In a fight: You need to get out of the house to cool down. A walk fixes half of it.
tips: Tell them your rhythm: “One trip every couple of months keeps me happy.” Then they can plan around it instead of worrying.
match: Best with: Someone grounded who still says yes to the weekend bus.
Green flag: Sometimes they plan the trip, instead of just saying yes to yours.
Careful with: Someone who calls every trip a waste of money and time.

VeryLow.label: The Backpack Soul
summaries: Home is wherever the next adventure starts.

You come alive on the move: new cities, new food, new people, a 5 am bus to somewhere you can’t pronounce. Settling down sounds a bit like giving up on something important to you. You want love that travels, not love that waits at home.
behaviors: Your idea of a great date is a train ticket and no return plan.
Someone who wants to stay in every weekend slowly dims your light.
You’d rather share a hostel bunk with the right person than a mansion with the wrong one.
strengths: Life with you is a story worth telling. You make the world feel big.
weaknesses: You can treat every settled plan as a cage, even the ones that would make you happy.
realLife: On a first date: You suggest the new Burmese place across town, then a walk to somewhere neither of you has been.
In a fight: You want a long walk or a drive to sort it out. Moving helps you think.
tips: Keep exploring, and build one small home ritual too. Even a backpack needs a hook to hang on.
match: Best with: Someone curious and flexible who packs light and says yes.
Green flag: They already have a travel list, and they want to tick it off with you.
Careful with: Someone who loves your stories but wants you to stop making new ones.

Undecided.label: The Home-Base Explorer
summaries: Roots and wings, in roughly equal measure.

You want a home that feels like yours, and you want to leave it often enough to miss it. Some seasons of your life are for exploring, others for building, and you’re good at both. Most people find your pace easy to share.
behaviors: A cosy home and one big trip a year is your idea of balance.
You can enjoy a quiet month and still say yes to a sudden road trip.
You adjust to their pace without losing your own.
strengths: You can be happy almost anywhere: on the road or on the sofa.
weaknesses: Being flexible, you can drift toward their pace and forget what you wanted.
realLife: On a first date: A favourite old place, then a new one you spotted on the way.
In a fight: You want peace back, and you’re open to their way of getting there.
tips: Every few months, check the balance together: “More home or more road this season?” It keeps you both happy.
match: Best with: Someone who loves home and the occasional adventure in roughly the same mix.
Green flag: They’re happy to stay in and happy to go, and they ask what you feel like.
Careful with: Someone at one extreme who wants you to live there too.

tests.title: Legacy Build
tests.subtitle: Building something meaningful together
tests.description: Measures whether you want to build legacy: business, family, projects, impact — with a partner as a team.
tests.whatYouLearn: Your desire for ‘build together’ partnership energy.
tests.howItHelpsMatch: Pairs better when both want to build (or at least respect the builder mindset).

questions.text: Late-night talk. They ask, “What do you want to leave behind one day?” You say…

options.text: Good memories and people who felt loved
Nothing much. I want to enjoy now
Something with our name on it

questions.text: Money left over at the end of the year goes to…

options.text: Building something: land, a business, a fund
Experiences: a trip, a great dinner, a concert

questions.text: Your person dreams of opening a small bakery together someday. You…

options.text: Love the idea, as a someday dream
Start naming it tonight
Happy to taste-test, not to run it

questions.text: Your grandparents’ old house: the family wants to keep it for the next generation. You…

options.text: Sell it and let everyone enjoy the money now
Absolutely. Some things should stay in the family
Nice idea, if someone actually lives in it

questions.text: You imagine your life at 60 with someone. You see…

options.text: Still laughing at the same jokes, wherever we are
A cosy home and enough saved to travel
What we built: a home, a business, a big family table

questions.text: They suggest starting something for your neighbourhood: a little library, a clean-up drive. You…

options.text: Help out when I can
Yes. I want us to matter beyond us
Prefer to keep our time just for us

questions.text: Your first festival season in your own home. You want to…

options.text: Celebrate however we feel that year
Start a tradition we’ll keep for forty years

questions.text: They’re building their own company, and it eats their evenings. You see it as…

options.text: A lot of today traded for a maybe tomorrow
Our future. I’ll help however I can
Their dream. I’ll cheer, and keep my evenings
Fine for a year or two, not forever

tests.measures: how much you think about building something lasting together

VeryHigh.label: The Legacy Architect
summaries: Thinks in decades, builds for the next generation.

You want your love to add up to something bigger than two people: a home that stays in the family, a business with your name on it, traditions the next generation will keep. You think in decades, and you light up around people with vision. For you, love is a foundation.
behaviors: You’ve already imagined the house, the business and the big family table.
A shared mission attracts you more than a shared playlist.
Keeping family roots alive matters to you, even at 25.
strengths: You build things that last, and people trust you with the future.
weaknesses: Your eye on forever can skip right past a lovely Tuesday evening.
realLife: On a first date: By the second hour you’re talking about what you both want to build, and it feels thrilling.
In a fight: You remind yourself what you’re building together, and the fight shrinks.
tips: Your vision is a gift. Leave room for joy with no purpose at all. The best builders also know how to rest.
match: Best with: Someone ambitious and warm who wants to build a legacy, not just a life.
Green flag: They have a vision and the patience to build it slowly with you.
Careful with: Someone who calls every long-term plan “too serious”.

High.label: The Bricklayer
summaries: Building a life together is the romance.

You want your relationship to be part of something that lasts: a home, a family, a shared project. You think in years, not weekends, and you’re drawn to people with a vision. Love, for you, is two people laying bricks side by side.
behaviors: You get excited talking about the home, the business or the family you could build.
You’ll give up a few weekends for something that will last.
Someone with no plans for the future makes you a little uneasy.
strengths: You turn love into something solid that outlives a mood.
weaknesses: You can be so busy building the house that you forget to enjoy it.
realLife: On a first date: You end up talking about their big dream, and you’re already thinking of ways to help.
In a fight: You think about the long game. One fight doesn’t shake the foundation.
tips: Schedule fun the way you schedule goals. The best things you build should include a few good memories too.
match: Best with: Someone with vision who wants to build with you, not just beside you.
Green flag: They talk about the future with plans, not just wishes.
Careful with: Someone who loves your ambition but never adds a brick.

Moderate.label: The Patient Gardener
summaries: Plants a little each year. No grand vision needed.

You care about the future in a practical way: some savings, a home one day, a few traditions worth keeping. You don’t need a grand vision, but you like knowing you’re slowly growing something. Security matters to you more than glory.
behaviors: You’d put half the bonus away and spend half on something fun.
You like small rituals that slowly become yours as a couple.
You’ll support their big dream, as long as it doesn’t eat every evening.
strengths: You build quietly and steadily, and it adds up.
weaknesses: Big dreamers might want more fire from you than steady watering.
realLife: On a first date: Relaxed and real. You talk about what you’re working toward, without a sales pitch.
In a fight: You look for the practical fix, and you’re patient while it grows.
tips: Name one thing you’re building together, even a small one. It turns ordinary years into a story.
match: Best with: Someone practical and warm who likes building a little at a time.
Green flag: They save a bit, enjoy a bit, and talk about both.
Careful with: Someone who wants to risk everything on a grand plan in month three.

Low.label: The Light Packer
summaries: Travels light through life, and likes it that way.

You think about the future, but you don’t want it to weigh you down. Big projects and legacy talk feel heavy to you; you’d rather keep life simple, flexible and enjoyable. You’ll build what you need, not a monument.
behaviors: You like a cosy home, but you don’t dream of an empire.
Shared projects sound fun for a weekend, less so for a decade.
You’d rather have free evenings together than a side business.
strengths: You keep life light, so love has room to breathe.
weaknesses: Your easy pace can look like low ambition to someone who dreams big.
realLife: On a first date: Easy, unhurried, no big pitch. Just a good evening.
In a fight: You want it settled simply. Long post-mortems aren’t your style.
tips: Choose one small thing to build together, like a tradition or a savings jar. Light things can last too.
match: Best with: Someone grounded who enjoys a simple life and doesn’t need to prove anything.
Green flag: They’re content with enough, and they know what enough means.
Careful with: Someone who measures love by what you build together.

VeryLow.label: The Moment Collector
summaries: Life is for living now, not saving for someday.

You’d rather have a great year than a great five-year plan. Trips, dinners, concerts and long talks are your treasures, and you don’t need anything with your name on it. To you, a life well lived is the legacy.
behaviors: You’d spend the bonus on a trip together before you’d put it into a plot of land.
Grand “let’s build an empire” talk leaves you a little cold.
Your love story is a camera roll, not a balance sheet.
strengths: You make today count. People feel more alive around you.
weaknesses: A builder can hear your “let’s enjoy now” as “I don’t see a future”.
realLife: On a first date: You pick the place with the best view or the best music, and stay till they close.
In a fight: You want to make up and get back to enjoying things. Life is short.
tips: Keep collecting moments, and put one small thing aside for later. Future you will love the memories and the safety net.
match: Best with: Someone who loves experiences and knows how to enjoy an ordinary Tuesday.
Green flag: They plan the next adventure, not the next asset.
Careful with: Someone who keeps postponing happiness until the house is bought.

You care about the future in a practical way: some savings, a home one day, a few traditions worth keeping. You don’t need a grand vision, but you like knowing you’re slowly growing something. Security matters to you more than glory.
